severity_rubric.critical: moves money incorrectly, loses data, or bypasses a security/permission control
severity_rubric.high: a displayed number is wrong, or a user-facing action silently does nothing
severity_rubric.medium: dead code, missing audit entry, inconsistent behaviour

findings.title: commitCashRepayment() writes off driver cash debt with no permission check
findings.detail: The opener recordCashRepayment (L12188) checks requirePerm('process_payouts') and requirePagePerm('wallets','cash_repayment'). The commit function checks neither: it reads the owed amount, zeroes DB.driverCashDebt[driverId] and logs cash_debt_repaid.
findings.impact: Same commit-vs-opener asymmetry as #3. An outstanding balance a driver owes the platform is cleared to zero with no authorisation check on the line that performs the write.

findings.title: commitSettlement() books a rider refund and a driver payout with no permission check
findings.detail: openSettlement (L3640) checks requirePerm('manage_subscriptions'), but the commit function does not. commitSettlement reads the selected reason, computes the settlement, sets sub.status='Cancelled' and logs settle_subscription with the rider refund amount, the rider method, the driver payout and the amount Eyvar keeps. It then queues a driver payout notification.
findings.impact: Directly violates the design rule stated at L3117: 'One choke point per action, placed on the COMMIT function (the line that actually mutates DB), never on buttons'. Any path that reaches commitSettlement without going through openSettlement - a console call, a future UI entry point, or the gate re-invocation path - cancels a subscription and moves money with no authorisation.

findings.title: commitUserSwitch() is a total RBAC bypass - any operator can become the Owner
findings.detail: The acting-user switch has no requirePerm, no requirePagePerm and no guardAction registration. Its only rejection is status==='Invited'. Entry points are the top-bar avatar (L578) and the My Account permissions panel button (L3085), both ungated. Verified by reading the whole function body.
findings.impact: A Support operator holding 3 permissions clicks the avatar, picks Sarah Al-Rashid and instantly holds all 13 - including manage_settings, manage_team, process_payouts and release_escrow. Every other guard in the panel is downstream of CURRENT_USER_ID, so this single ungated write defeats the entire permission model. The switch_user audit entry records it but nothing prevents it.

findings.title: Impersonation attributes actions to the impersonated user, the opposite of what the gate promises
findings.detail: impersonate(userId) stashes window.__realUserId, then sets CURRENT_USER_ID=userId at L21071 BEFORE calling logAction at L21072. logAction resolves actorId and actorName from CURRENT_USER_ID (L3134, L3138). Every subsequent action, and even the impersonation_started entry itself, is therefore recorded against the impersonated user. The guardAction copy at L21095 states the reverse.
findings.evidence: consequences:['You will see exactly what they see, and be blocked where they are blocked.', 'Any action you take is recorded against your name, not theirs.',
findings.impact: An operator is explicitly told the audit trail will protect them and that the record will name them, and the system does the opposite - it frames the person being impersonated. Any investigation reading the Activity Log attributes the impersonator's actions to the wrong operator. This is a stated safety property that is inverted in code.

findings.title: No export is permission-gated, including the audit log itself
findings.detail: Thirteen export entry points contain no requirePerm or requirePagePerm: exportRiders (L7607), exportDrivers (L7611), exportSubscriptions (L7615), exportPayments (L7619), exportAuditLog (L7623), exportInbox (L7627), exportPushLog (L7631), exportEmailLog (L7634), exportSnapshots (L7665), exportContacts (L15056), exportIntegrity (L18617), exportRequestsSnapshot (L9766) and doExport (L9204). Twelve route through downloadCSV, which logs export_data at L7604, or through doExport, which logs at L9215. exportRequestsSnapshot writes a JSON blob of every ride request and subscription request and only toasts - it is the one bulk export that calls neither requirePerm nor logAction.
findings.impact: A Support user with three permissions and no view_finance can download the complete payments table, the rider and driver rosters with phone numbers, and the entire tamper record. exportAuditLog in particular lets any operator take the audit trail off-platform, and exportRequestsSnapshot exfiltrates the full request book leaving no trace at all.

findings.title: recordRefund() moves money with no permission check and no audit entry
findings.detail: The function that actually issues a refund reads the full body from L3176 to L3202: it validates only that amount>0, builds a REF- entry with status 'Processed', unshifts it onto DB.refunds, and calls issueCreditNote() to reverse the VAT on the original tax invoice. There is no requirePerm call and no logAction call anywhere in the function. It stamps processedBy onto the record but never writes to DB.auditLog. It is confirm-gated via guardAction at L17901, which is the only control on it.
findings.impact: Money leaves the platform and a VAT-reversing credit note is issued by anyone who can reach a refund button, regardless of role - and the Activity Log contains no record of it. The gate copy itself states 'Money leaves Eyvar and returns to the rider's payment method'. This contradicts the doc's own claim (section 5.4) that no DB-mutating function is unaudited; that scan looked only for removals.

findings.title: Settlement records the decision but moves no money
findings.detail: commitSettlement computes riderBack, driverPay and eyvarKeeps via computeSettlement, then performs exactly one DB mutation: sub.status='Cancelled'. It never calls recordRefund, creditRiderWallet or any payout function, unlike confirmCancelSub which does both at L5560-L5561. The rider refund/credit and the driver payout are described in the audit line, the toast and the ops notification, but nothing executes them.
findings.impact: An early-termination settlement looks complete in the audit log and the notification centre while no refund, wallet credit or driver payout ever happens; the money silently stays with the platform.

findings.title: sendRiderChangeNotif reassigns a driver with no permission check and no audit
findings.detail: The 'Send notification now' button in the notify-rider modal writes t.driver and t.driverStatus='moving' directly. It is a second path to the same write that confirmReassign() guards behind requirePerm('manage_subscriptions'), and unlike finalizeReassign it produces no audit entry at all.
findings.impact: An operator without manage_subscriptions can reassign any upcoming subscription trip's driver, and nothing in the activity log records that it happened or who did it.

findings.title: Approving a KYC document bypasses the permission check and the audit log
findings.detail: setDocStatus's 'ok' branch writes a.docs[key]='✓ Verified', deletes any prior rejection note, toasts and re-renders — with no requirePerm call and no logAction call. The 'rej' branch, by contrast, routes through a reason modal into confirmDocReject which calls requirePerm('approve_drivers') and logs a full before/after audit entry. Any operator who can open the applicant detail page can therefore mark every identity, licence and insurance document verified, leaving no trace.
findings.evidence: if(verdict==='ok'){ a.docs[key]='✓ Verified'; if(a.docNotes)delete a.docNotes[key]; toast('✓ '+key.replace('_',' ')+' approved','ok'); openApplicantDetail(appId,true);
findings.impact: A security control on identity verification is enforced in one direction only, and the permissive direction is the unaudited one.

findings.title: demoDoubleRefund() is a production-reachable money mover
findings.detail: demoDoubleRefund (L20131-L20141) issues two genuine recordRefund calls of 25.00 SAR each against Object.keys(DB.riders)[0], with reason 'Duplicate-click test' and source 'demo'. It is a plain global function with no permission check and no confirmation spec of its own, existing only to demonstrate idempotency suppression.
findings.impact: A diagnostic helper in shipped code writes real refund rows, real credit notes and real ledger postings against a live rider.

findings.title: recordRefund has no permission gate of its own
findings.detail: recordRefund (L3176-L3202) never calls requirePerm or can(). Its only protections are (a) the caller's requirePerm('manage_subscriptions') at L5550 and (b) the guardAction confirmation spec installed at L17901. Both are bypassable: window.__skipGuards is a plain global, and the module boot block sets it to true for the whole seed run (L21833), during which every guarded money action runs unconfirmed.
findings.impact: Any code path or console call that reaches recordRefund moves money out of the business with no RBAC check at the point of the write.

findings.title: Refund amount is unbounded
findings.detail: The only validation in recordRefund is if(!(amount>0))return null. There is no upper bound, no comparison against the original payment or invoice, and no per-role authority ceiling - unlike goodwill credits, which are checked against a reason-code ceiling by compCheck (L15412-L15434).
findings.impact: A refund of arbitrary size passes validation and posts to the ledger; nothing caps a mistaken or malicious amount.

findings.title: Subscription cancellation books the same refund twice
findings.detail: confirmCancelSub calls recordRefund(sub.rider, refund, ...) and creditRiderWallet(sub.rider, refund, ...) with the same refund amount inside one if(refund>0) block. The ledger consequence is contra.refunds debited net + tax.vat_output debited vat with cash.gateway credited amount (L19969-L19973), AND expense.goodwill debited amount with liability.wallet credited amount (L19985-L19988). contributionMargin then counts the same money twice, once in the refunds giveback (L15728) and once in goodwill (L15729). The modal's own row is labelled 'Net refund to wallet' (L5543), implying only the wallet leg.
findings.impact: Every subscription cancellation refund costs the business twice the intended amount, and contribution margin double-counts the giveback.

findings.title: Cash commit functions are unguarded globals
findings.detail: commitCashResolve (L12171) and commitCashRepayment (L12203) contain no requirePerm and no requirePagePerm of their own; the double gate lives only in their openers, resolveCashEntry (L12147-L12148) and recordCashRepayment (L12188-L12189). commitCashRepayment's only guard is if(owed<=0){closeModal();return;} before it zeroes the debt.
findings.impact: Calling window.commitCashRepayment('DRV-0103') writes off that driver's entire outstanding cash debt with no permission check at the point of the write.

findings.title: confirmApplyDeduction has no re-apply guard
findings.detail: confirmApplyDeduction reads prevStatus purely to build the audit diff (L7076, L7082) and then unconditionally sets d.status='applied' and subtracts the amount from p.pending. Nothing checks whether the deduction was already applied or waived. The UI hides the button after the first application, but the function is a plain window global.
findings.impact: Re-invoking the function on an already-applied deduction subtracts the penalty from the driver's balance a second time.

findings.title: executePayout reports success even when the payout was refused
findings.detail: executePayout (L8716-L8747) performs no permission check of its own. It renders a 'Submitting to bank network' spinner, then inside a 1100 ms setTimeout calls payDriver - which may refuse via requirePerm('process_payouts') at L7024 - and unconditionally renders the 'Payment sent' screen and unshifts a notifLog entry telling the driver the money will arrive within three business days. Nothing checks whether payDriver moved anything.
findings.evidence:
payDriver(driverId);
    var msg='Your payment of '+amt.toFixed(2)+' SAR has been confirmed and will arrive within 3 business days.';
findings.impact: A permission-denied payout produces a full success UI plus a false notification to the driver; the operator believes money was sent when nothing moved.

findings.title: Four of six declared wallets page permissions are never enforced
findings.detail: PAGE_PERMISSIONS.wallets declares view, process_payouts, release_escrow, apply_deductions, cash_review and cash_repayment (L10630-L10637). Grep for requirePagePerm('wallets' returns exactly two hits: cash_review at L12148 and cash_repayment at L12189. The payout, escrow and deduction actions gate on the legacy global permissions (requirePerm('process_payouts') L7024 and L7050, requirePerm('release_escrow') L7059, requirePerm('apply_deductions') L7073) instead, and wallets.view is never checked at all.
findings.impact: A role whose page-permission matrix revokes wallets.process_payouts, wallets.release_escrow or wallets.apply_deductions can still perform all three actions as long as it retains the global legacy permission; the matrix silently does nothing.

findings.title: releaseEscrow never checks the hold's status
findings.detail: releaseEscrow looks the hold up by id and releases it immediately; e.status is never read. The status==='ready' test lives only in renderEscrow, which decides whether to draw the button (L8927). Calling window.releaseEscrow('ESC-1041') releases a 4-of-5-trip hold, and the confirmation modal that precedes it still prints 'All 5 trips completed successfully' because that banner is unconditional and uses tripsRequired (L8942).
findings.impact: Money held specifically because a subscription is incomplete can be paid out to the driver, defeating the entire purpose of escrow.

findings.title: waiveDeduction is completely ungoverned
findings.detail: waiveDeduction (L8986-L8992) is seven lines long and contains no requirePerm, no requirePagePerm, no confirmation modal and no logAction. A single click on the Waive button permanently sets d.status='waived'. The permission written for exactly this action - apply_deductions, labelled 'Apply / waive deductions' (L3233) - is checked on the apply path (L7073) but not here. This is the only status-changing action on the page with none of the four controls.
findings.impact: A penalty against a driver can be written off by any user with no permission check, no confirmation and no audit record of who did it or why.

findings.title: A subscription cancellation books the same refund twice
findings.detail: commitCancelSub calls recordRefund(...) at L5562 and creditRiderWallet(...) at L5563 for the same computed refund figure. recordRefund posts contra.refunds + tax.vat_output debit against cash.gateway credit (money leaving the gateway); creditRiderWallet posts expense.goodwill debit against liability.wallet credit (a new liability owed to the rider). Both postings balance individually, so postLedger's F11 guard passes and neither is rejected.
findings.impact: For every subscription cancellation the trial balance shows cash leaving Eyvar AND an equal wallet liability created for the same money — the refund is recognised twice and goodwill expense is overstated by the full refund amount. The rider's wallet is credited even though the ledger says the money went back to their card.

findings.title: Compensation authority ceilings are bypassed by picking a different reason label
findings.detail: The entire compCheck authority path — per-case ceiling, daily ceiling, per-rider 30-day pattern check, second-approver threshold and the goodwill-ledger entry — runs only inside `if(reason.indexOf('Goodwill')>=0)`, a substring test on the free-text label of the reason dropdown. Selecting 'Manual top-up', 'Promo code redemption', 'Referral bonus' or 'Trip cancellation refund' skips all of it.
findings.impact: A Support agent whose per-case ceiling is 75 SAR and daily ceiling 600 SAR can credit an unlimited amount to any rider by choosing 'Manual top-up' instead of 'Goodwill / apology credit'. No goodwill-ledger row is written either, so the spend is invisible to the compensation-policy report.

findings.title: recordRefund moves money with no permission check and no direct audit entry
findings.detail: recordRefund unshifts a REF-#### line into DB.refunds, issues a sequential credit note reversing the VAT, and posts contra.refunds + tax.vat_output debits against a cash.gateway credit. The function body contains no requirePerm() call of any kind. It is also the only money-mover in this module that never calls logAction itself — the only audit trace is the credit_note_issued entry written inside issueCreditNote, and only when a credit note is actually produced. It is confirm-gated (guardAction('recordRefund'), L17900), and that gate is bypassable by window.__skipGuards.
findings.impact: Cash leaving the payment gateway is protected by a confirmation dialog alone. Any role — including one with no finance permission at all — can trigger a refund through commitCancelSub, and the refund itself leaves no attributable audit-log line naming who processed it.

findings.title: Rider money is gated on a messaging permission, not a finance permission
findings.detail: commitWalletAdjust — the only UI path that credits or debits a rider wallet in either direction — checks requirePerm('contact_users'), labelled 'Call / message riders & drivers'. The Support role (USR-3, USR-4) holds ['manage_tickets','view_profiles','contact_users'] and can therefore move money, while the Finance role (USR-2) lacks contact_users and cannot adjust a wallet at all. None of the 13 keys in PERMISSION_LABELS is checked for wallet movement.
findings.impact: Any operator who can message a rider can also credit or debit that rider's prepaid balance without limit (unless the reason string happens to contain 'Goodwill'), while the finance team is locked out of the control entirely. The permission model provides no meaningful separation of duties over customer funds.

findings.title: The second-approval flag is a bare global with no rider, amount or actor binding
findings.detail: When compCheck returns needsApproval, commitWalletAdjust sets window.__compApproved=true and returns without crediting. The next invocation reads the same unbound global and treats the credit as approved. The flag is keyed to nothing — not the rider, the amount, the reason code, the actor or the session — and it lives on window, so it survives navigation between pages. It is also never initialised; the first read is undefined and happens to be falsy.
findings.impact: An operator can trip the flag with a 250 SAR goodwill credit to rider A, cancel, and then have a 250 SAR credit to rider B pass as an 'approved exception' with no second person involved. The control that exists to force dual authorisation above 200 SAR provides none.

findings.title: resolveDispute records a credit in the audit log but moves no money
findings.detail: resolveDispute computes amount = perTrip (refund), perTrip*0.5 (goodwill) or 0 (reject), then sets d.status='resolved' and d.outcome, re-renders and writes the audit line 'Dispute DSP-07 resolved: refund — 17.30 SAR credited to Sara Al-Ghamdi'. It never calls recordRefund, creditRiderWallet, commitWalletAdjust, issueCreditNote or sendSystemEmail. The confirmation gate simultaneously promises '<amount> credited to <claimant>' and 'A credit note is issued against the original tax invoice.'
findings.impact: The rider never receives the money the operator was told they authorised, no credit note is issued so the VAT stays declared, and — worst — the activity log, which Finance uses as the reconciliation trail, now contains a positive record of a credit that never happened. Reconciling the audit log against the ledger will show a payment that does not exist.

findings.title: approveRateCard() publishes a new live commercial rate card with no permission gate
findings.detail: approveRateCard(version) marks the current DB.rateCard as superseded, unshifts it onto DB.rateCardHistory and promotes the chosen draft to DB.rateCard with status 'live'. It enforces a maker-checker rule (self-approval refused) and requires an attached simulation, and a danger-styled GATE_SWEEP confirmation wraps it — but it never calls requirePerm() or can(). Mechanically confirmed: the function body from L21582 to L21601 contains no permission check of any kind, unlike every mutating handler on the plans page which opens with requirePerm('manage_plans').
findings.impact: Any signed-in role that can reach the Settings pricing card can put a new fare card live for every subsequent trip. The self-approval block is the only barrier, and it is defeated by two colluding or two low-privilege accounts. The confirmation modal is a UX gate, not an authorisation gate.

findings.title: commitUserSwitch is an ungated full RBAC bypass
findings.detail: openUserSwitch() is reachable from the top-bar avatar (L578, onclick="openUserSwitch()") and the sidebar footer menu (L3085). commitUserSwitch() then reassigns the module-level CURRENT_USER_ID to whichever team user was picked. It contains no requirePerm call and no guardAction confirm - its only check is that the target is not status 'Invited'. Because can() resolves permissions purely from DB.teamUsers.find(x=>x.id===CURRENT_USER_ID), every subsequent requirePerm in the panel now evaluates against the assumed identity.
findings.evidence: function commitUserSwitch(){ ... if(nu.status==='Invited'){toast('That member has not logged in yet','err');return;} ... CURRENT_USER_ID=nu.id;
findings.impact: Any operator - including a Support user with 3 of 13 permissions - can become the Owner in two clicks and then perform every gated action in the panel, including manage_team and manage_settings. The audit entry records switch_user, but every action taken afterwards is attributed to the assumed user, not the real one.

findings.title: Impersonation is confirmation-gated but not permission-gated
findings.detail: impersonate(userId) sets CURRENT_USER_ID with no requirePerm check. The only barrier is guardAction('impersonate', ...) at L21090, which renders a confirm dialog; guardAction replaces the global and re-invokes the original on confirm, and window.__skipGuards bypasses it entirely. A confirm dialog is not authorization.
findings.evidence: function impersonate(userId){ if(!window.__realUserId)window.__realUserId=CURRENT_USER_ID; var u=DB.teamUsers.find(function(x){return x.id===userId;}); if(!u)return; CURRENT_USER_ID=userId;
findings.impact: The 'View as' button appears on every row of the team table for every operator (it is hidden only on your own row). Any operator can assume the Owner's permission set and commit Owner-only actions, with the audit log attributing them to the Owner.

findings.title: The second approver for large goodwill credits is the same operator
findings.detail: compCheck sets needsApproval when the amount exceeds DB.compPolicy.secondApprovalAboveSAR (200) or the rider's 30-day history exceeds 150 SAR / 3 credits. commitWalletAdjust satisfies that requirement with a global boolean: if(chk.needsApproval && !window.__compApproved){window.__compApproved=true; toast('press Confirm again'); return;}. Pressing Confirm a second time clears the flag and issues the credit. There is no second identity, no approval record, and the flag persists across modals until the next successful credit resets it.
findings.evidence: if(chk.needsApproval && !window.__compApproved){ window.__compApproved=true; toast('Second approval required - press Confirm again to record this as an approved exception','warn'); return; }
findings.impact: The only control on large or repeated goodwill payments is a double-click by the same person; money leaves the platform with no independent authorisation and no trace of who approved it.

findings.title: resetBranding bypasses the permission gate
findings.detail: saveBranding begins with if(!requirePerm('manage_settings'))return; resetBranding has no such check — it goes straight to replacing DB.branding. Both functions are confirm-gated, but a confirmation dialog is not a permission control: any operator, regardless of role, can wipe the panel's branding for every user.
findings.impact: A shared, platform-wide setting can be destroyed by a user who is explicitly not allowed to change it — a permission-control bypass.

findings.title: rebuildAllHistory has no permission gate
findings.detail: rebuildAllHistory calls reconstructHistory() immediately, with no requirePerm. reconstructHistory iterates every rider and generates trip and payment records into DB.trips and DB.payments (plus pushes onto DB.drivers[*].trips). By contrast saveDataWindow, which only changes an integer, gates on manage_settings. The confirmation dialog is not a permission control.
findings.impact: Any operator who can reach the Settings page can fabricate hundreds of trip and payment records across every rider account, regardless of role.

findings.title: Every CSV export is completely ungated
findings.detail: None of exportRiders, exportDrivers, exportSubscriptions, exportPayments, exportAuditLog, exportInbox, exportPushLog, exportEmailLog or exportSnapshots calls requirePerm or is wrapped by guardAction. Only captureDailySnapshot — which merely appends a summary row — checks manage_settings.
findings.impact: Anyone who can reach the Settings page can download rider phone numbers, driver details, the entire payment ledger and the audit log; the pane's footnote promises accountability through the log but no authorisation.

findings.title: rebuildAllHistory fabricates payment records with no permission check
findings.detail: rebuildAllHistory calls reconstructHistory(), which generates trip and payment rows into DB.payments to match billing lifetime totals. It is wrapped by guardAction (a confirm dialog) but never calls requirePerm, so no role check stands in front of it.
findings.impact: Any operator who reaches the Data-integrity tab can create payment records that did not exist; the rows are flagged 'reconstructed' but they are real entries in the money collection.

findings.title: The demo button issues a real refund with no permission check and no confirmation
findings.detail: demoDoubleRefund picks the first rider, calls the patched recordRefund(rid,25,'Duplicate-click test','demo','DEMO-1') twice and relies on idempotency to suppress the second. The first call is a genuine refund: it writes DB.refunds, issues a credit note (DB.creditNotes, DB.creditNoteSequence) and posts to the ledger. It has no requirePerm, no GATE_SPECS entry, no guardAction wrapper and the same btn sm styling as the button beside it.
findings.impact: SAR 25 leaves the books against a real customer record and appears on the Finance page as an ordinary operator-issued refund, from an unlabelled demo button anyone reaching Settings can press.

findings.title: Wallet idempotency keys expire after one second
findings.detail: The refund key is fully deterministic, but the wallet credit and debit keys append Math.floor(nowMs()/1000). Two identical operations more than one second apart therefore produce different keys and are both executed.
findings.impact: A double-click slower than one second on a wallet credit or debit moves money twice — precisely the failure mode the module header says the design exists to prevent.

findings.title: Audit summaries are injected into the page as raw, unescaped HTML
findings.detail: auditRowsHTML interpolates e.summary directly into a table cell at L9301 with no escaping, and neither auditDiffHTML (L3156-L3172) nor auditEntityLink (L9281-L9285) escapes anything either — diff values are string-concatenated raw, and actorName is interpolated into a title attribute at L9300. Summaries are composed at the call site from operator free text and entity names (e.g. suspendSurge's reason at L21539, rider and driver names, ticket subjects). The injection sink is mechanically confirmed; whether any real value currently carries markup was not executed, matching the doc's UNVERIFIED note.
findings.impact: Operator-supplied text can inject markup or script into the panel's own security log — the one surface that must be trustworthy — and the payload re-executes for every viewer on every render, including inside the actor-history modal and the Settings preview.

findings.title: exportAuditLog is neither permission-gated nor itself audited
findings.detail: Mechanically confirmed by reading the whole function (L7623-L7626): it contains no requirePerm, no requirePagePerm and no logAction. Its only call site is the Settings > Data Export button at L2031. By contrast doExport() writes logAction('export_data', ...) at L9215. The export also always covers the full DB.auditLog array, ignoring the page's active actor, action and text filters.
findings.impact: Any operator who can reach the Data Export tab can pull the entire audit trail to a local file, and doing so leaves no trace in the audit trail — a security control that fails silently in exactly the exfiltration case it exists to record.

findings.title: `openInvoiceModal()` writes to a money collection with no permission gate
findings.detail: Reaches DB.invoiceSequence, DB.invoices (directly or through a helper, ≤3 call hops) but neither `requirePerm()` nor `can()` appears anywhere on that path. Every other money path in the panel is gated, so this is an inconsistency in the RBAC choke-point pattern documented at L3116-L3131.
findings.impact: Any signed-in operator, regardless of role, can trigger a balance-changing write.

findings.title: Badge formulas hardcode the demo date 25 June
findings.detail: refreshNavCounts() defines 'today's trips' by string-matching the literal '25 Jun' against t.date, and 'expiring soon' by parseInt(x.ends,10)-25 <= 3. Both treat day-of-month 25 as today.
findings.impact: On any date other than 25 June the Quick Rides badge, the All Trips subtitle and the Renewal badge display counts that are simply wrong, with no indication they are frozen.

findings.title: Ten of fifteen sidebar badges are stale until their page is opened
findings.detail: refreshNavCounts() updates only sbb-dash, sbb-subs, sbb-qr, sbb-renew and sbb-requests. The other ten (predictive, fraud, inbox, corporate, readiness, coverage, compliance, safety, zones, ticket/contacts/commit/fairness) are written by their own page's render function. They are non-zero at first paint only because the 100ms one-shot init pass renders most pages once at boot.
findings.impact: A subscription cancelled from the Subscriptions page does not change the Coverage badge until Coverage is opened. Operators triage from numbers that can be arbitrarily out of date.

findings.title: closeModal() wipes every request claim on any modal close
findings.detail: closeModal() unconditionally calls reqClearLocks(), which deletes _locking, claimedBy and claimedAt from every entry in DB.rideRequests and DB.subscriptionRequests. This runs when any of the 99 modals closes, including modals with nothing to do with request claiming.
findings.impact: An operator who opens and closes an unrelated modal silently releases every claim another operator holds on ride and subscription requests, so two people can be routed onto the same work.

findings.title: The one-shot init pass is 45 unguarded sequential calls
findings.detail: A single setTimeout(fn, 100) runs 45 statements in order, eagerly rendering every page in the app including the roughly 30 that are display:none. There is no try/catch anywhere in the block.
findings.evidence: One-shot init setTimeout(...,100) at L14556-14600; startTickEngine() is call 42 of 45
findings.impact: A throw in any one of the 45 calls silently aborts everything after it, including startTickEngine() at position 42 - the simulation would simply never start, with no error surfaced to the operator.

findings.title: TOAST_MAX=1 drops every alert in a burst except the last
findings.detail: While stack.children.length >= TOAST_MAX, the oldest child's timer is stopped and the node is removed synchronously. The comment explains the synchronous removal is deliberate because an async fade would never shrink the count.
findings.evidence: var TOAST_MAX=1; /* was 3 - even after moving the stack to a safer corner, 3 stacked toasts were still tall enough to land on other buttons */
findings.impact: When several alerts fire in the same tick only the last is ever seen. 330 of 349 calls are mitigated by the notification-centre mirror, but the 19 calls passing notify=false rely on the caller pushing its own notification - a manual pairing that cannot be verified statically.

findings.title: Unescaped innerHTML interpolation across all modals, toasts and tables
findings.detail: All 99 modal sites, all 349 toast calls and every table renderer build HTML strings by concatenating DB values. toast() strips tags only when building the title= attribute, not for the visible message.
findings.impact: Any operator- or rider-entered string (names, notes, ticket subjects, refusal grounds) becomes a script-injection vector the moment this panel is fed real data.

findings.title: window.__skipGuards is a public global bypass for all 88 gates
findings.detail: The flag exists so the boot IIFE can seed data without opening 45 confirmation dialogs. It is set true for the whole seed loop and restored afterwards, but it is a plain writable property of window.
findings.evidence: window.__skipGuards=false;   /* programmatic/seed calls bypass the UI gate */
findings.impact: One line in the console, or any injected script, disables every confirmation gate in the panel for the rest of the session.

findings.title: Zero persistence, while every gate promises durability
findings.detail: Verified: zero matches for localStorage, sessionStorage, DOMContentLoaded or window.onload across all 21,857 lines. There are no cookies, no IndexedDB, no fetch/XHR and no service worker. All state lives in the in-memory DB object.
findings.impact: Every 'Recorded in the activity log under your name' and 'Applies to every operator immediately' consequence in the 88 gates describes state that a page refresh destroys. Operators are asked to confirm permanence the system cannot provide.

findings.title: 19 of 41 pages have no entry in the permission matrix
findings.detail: The panel contains 41 page shells (verified: grep -c 'class="page' returns 41). PAGE_PERMISSIONS covers 22. The uncovered 19 are p-exec-overview (L583), p-corporate (L634), p-corp-detail (L644), p-fraud (L650), p-rwallets (L1020), p-plan-edit (L1082), p-my-account (L1151), p-notifications-all (L1171), p-all-pending (L1324), p-applicant-detail (L1342), p-ticket-detail (L1380), p-profile (L1384), p-inbox (L1392), p-commitment (L1397), p-fairness (L1402), p-contacts (L1409), p-interventions (L2068), p-requests-sub-all (L2123) and p-requests-instant-all (L2144).
findings.evidence: STANDING RULE for future work: any new page or major new action built into this panel gets an entry added here in the same change - permissions are not an afterthought bolted on later. (L10556-10559)
findings.impact: Several are materially sensitive: Fraud & Risk, Rider Wallets (money), Corporate Account detail (billing), 360 Profile (PII), Applicant Detail (KYC documents) and Contact Drivers (contact data plus SLA). None appear in the granular matrix UI at #page-perm-matrix, so an administrator reading that screen cannot even see that they exist.

findings.title: 37 of 52 granular permission keys are never enforced, including all 22 view keys
findings.detail: The 20 requirePagePerm call sites cover 15 distinct page.perm pairs: compliance.edit_dates, wallets.cash_review, wallets.cash_repayment, coverage.assign_backup, coverage.promote_backup, safety.update_steps, safety.suspend, safety.close, growth.pause_promo, growth.create_promo, growth.recalc_tiers, growth.send_message, zones.steer, predictive.act and support.manage. canPage() has exactly two call sites - its own declaration and requirePagePerm - so no navigation, sidebar or go() path consults it. defaultPagePerms grants view to everyone on every page unconditionally by design (comment at L10653).
findings.evidence: grep -c 'canPage(' => 2 (the declaration at L10674 and the call inside requirePagePerm at L10681)
findings.impact: The granular layer is largely a UI that describes a policy the runtime does not apply. The 15 unenforced action keys are at least covered indirectly by the broad layer, but the 22 view keys are enforced nowhere at all - so the page-visibility model the matrix presents to an administrator is fiction.

findings.title: executePayout() reports 'Payment sent' even when the permission guard denied the payout
findings.detail: executePayout shows a 'Submitting to bank network' spinner, then inside a setTimeout calls payDriver(driverId). payDriver checks requirePerm('process_payouts') and returns early on denial. executePayout does not check the return value: it unconditionally writes a 'Your payment of N SAR has been confirmed' entry into d.notifLog and rewrites the modal to 'Payment sent'.
findings.impact: An operator without process_payouts sees a lock toast and a 'Payment sent' confirmation at the same time, and a false payment-confirmed message is written into the driver's notification history. The money did not move, so the driver is told they were paid when they were not.

findings.title: Rider wallet credits and debits are gated on a communications permission
findings.detail: commitWalletAdjust adds or removes money from a rider wallet and is guarded by requirePerm('contact_users') - described in PERMISSION_DESC as 'Call or message a rider or driver directly from their profile'. contact_users is held by Owner, Ops Manager and Support. The finance permissions (view_finance, process_payouts) are not consulted. The action is also confirm-gated as a rich gate at L17889 with danger set on debit.
findings.impact: Support operators, who deliberately hold no finance permission, can credit and debit rider wallets. The permission model says they can only call and message.

findings.title: The password change is theatre that writes a real audit entry
findings.detail: changeMaPassword validates only that a current password was typed, that the new one is at least 8 characters, and that it matches the confirmation. The current password is never compared against anything and the new password is never stored anywhere. It then clears all three inputs, toasts 'Password updated' and calls logAction('change_password','team_user',CURRENT_USER_ID,...) with empty before and after objects.
findings.evidence: The current password is never verified against anything and the new password is never stored
findings.impact: The Activity Log accumulates entries asserting credential changes that did not occur. The file's own comment at L2989-2994 acknowledges the local-state pattern, but writing an audit record makes the fiction durable and could be relied on in an investigation.

findings.title: view_profiles is granted to everyone and enforced nowhere
findings.detail: Verified by counting every quoted requirePerm call: 131 sites across 12 keys, with view_profiles at exactly zero. All 5 seeded users hold it. p-profile is also absent from PAGE_PERMISSIONS, and can() has only one functional call site (L3084, deciding whether the My Account 'Edit role permission matrix' button renders).
findings.impact: The 360 profile surface - trip history, documents, payments, phone numbers - is reachable by any operator with no check, and the permission that was designed to govern it is decorative.

findings.title: The currency and timezone settings are write-only
findings.detail: The selector offers 7 currencies (L1475-L1481) and 7 timezones (L1485-L1493). Every read of .currency is L7982 (repopulate its own select), L7989 (audit snapshot) and L7994 (write); .timezone adds only L19760 where it is concatenated into a static sentence. Nothing formats money or converts a date with either value.
findings.impact: Selecting USD still prints ' SAR' at all 92 fmtSAR call sites and selecting Europe/London converts no date — settings that appear to work, are audited as changed, and have no effect.

findings.title: Avg renewal rate renders 'NaN%'
findings.detail: renewRateAvg parses DB.riders[*].stats.renewalRate with parseInt. The field is a display string ('100%', '91%' or the em-dash '—'). parseInt('—',10) returns NaN and the guard x!=null does not filter NaN, so the running average becomes NaN, Math.round(NaN) is NaN, and NaN!=null is true — the card prints the literal text 'NaN%'. Active subscription SUB-1052 maps to rider RDR-2031 whose renewalRate is '—', so this fires with the shipped seed data.
findings.impact: An executive-facing card shows 'NaN%' instead of a renewal rate on a fresh load.

findings.title: No permission gate on company-wide revenue
findings.detail: Neither the sidebar entry nor the router branch calls can() or requirePerm(), and there is no PAGE_PERMISSIONS check for exec-overview. Any role that can see the sidebar can open the page and read total revenue, driver earnings, platform net and escrow.
findings.impact: Company-wide financials are visible to every signed-in operator regardless of role.

findings.title: Total driver earnings includes cancelled trips
findings.detail: totalDriverEarn reduces over every entry of DB.trips with no status filter, unlike totalRevenue which filters status==='Paid'. 'Platform net (est.)' is totalRevenue - totalDriverEarn and inherits the error.
findings.impact: Both the driver-cost line and the platform-net line on the Financial position card overstate cost and understate margin.

findings.title: 'Send renewal payment reminder early' sends no reminder
findings.detail: The button calls commitRetentionAction(subId,'payment-reminder'). Inside commitRetentionAction the sendSystemEmail branch is guarded by kind==='offer', so the payment-reminder path produces only an audit line, a toast and a bell notification. Nothing is sent to the rider.
findings.impact: An operator believes a renewal reminder went out when the rider was never contacted.

findings.title: Declared 'view' permission is never enforced
findings.detail: PAGE_PERMISSIONS.predictive declares both a view and an act permission, but window.go dispatches to renderPredictivePage() with no requirePagePerm('predictive','view') check. Only the act permission is enforced, inside openRetentionAction and commitRetentionAction.
findings.impact: A role explicitly denied view access still sees churn scores, at-risk drivers and revenue-at-risk.

findings.title: Account suspension has no confirmation gate
findings.detail: commitSuspendAccount writes d.suspended, removes a driver from dispatch matching (or blocks a rider from new subscriptions), logs, notifies and navigates away — on a single click of the modal's Suspend button. The function appears in neither GATE_SPECS nor GATE_SWEEP, so guardAction never wraps it, even though comparable operational actions such as precautionSuspend are gated there. The only friction is the modal itself.
findings.impact: A misclick permanently suspends an account and stops a driver's income with no confirm step.

findings.title: Pairing signal is computed over generated trip history
findings.detail: historyBoot() calls reconstructHistory(), which synthesises trips, assigns each a pseudo-randomly chosen driver via seededRand, and pushes the ids onto both the rider's and the driver's trips arrays. Those trips carry reconstructed:true and get a provenance warning wherever a trip is rendered, but the fraud page reads the counts silently. The module banner's claim that every signal comes from real trip history does not hold for this card.
findings.impact: A '3+ shared trips' collusion flag against a named driver and rider can be an artefact of the seeded RNG.

findings.title: Quick rides badge under-reports the day's total
findings.detail: #dash-qr-count is set to qrEx.length — quick rides today whose status is not 'Done' — while the card header reads 'Quick rides — today'. The completed rides are folded into a green footer row instead. KPI tile 2 uses the correct qrT.length, so the two numbers on the same screen disagree.
findings.impact: The card badge shows a smaller number than the day's actual quick-ride volume.

findings.title: The overdue KPI counts hardcoded -1 sentinels
findings.detail: Three item types - dispatch, leg-uncovered and critical incident - set dueMs to a hardcoded -1 rather than a real deadline. Because breached is dueMs<0, every such item is permanently overdue and permanently inflates both the 'Overdue right now' KPI and the sidebar badge, rendering as 'overdue 0m'.
findings.impact: The single most attention-grabbing number on the page is systematically wrong, and the badge that drives operator attention inherits the same inflation.

findings.title: WORK_ROUTING routes eleven queues to a role that does not exist
findings.detail: WORK_ROUTING maps 11 of the 12 queue keys to the role string 'Operations'. The real role vocabulary is TEAM_ROLES = ['Owner','Ops Manager','Finance','Support'] (verified at L10501) and the seeded DB.teamUsers carry Owner, Finance, Support, Support and Ops Manager. With the default role filter on, an Ops Manager matches nothing and sees an empty inbox reading 'Nothing open in the queues routed to Ops Manager.' Owner sees all 12 queues, Support sees 4, Finance sees 1.
findings.evidence: var WORK_ROUTING={ ticket:['Support','Operations','Owner'], fairness:['Operations','Owner'], ... }; var TEAM_ROLES=['Owner','Ops Manager','Finance','Support'];
findings.impact: The role the routing table was clearly written for is the one role that sees nothing - the operations manager's entire work queue is invisible by default.

findings.title: Eleven producers emit undeclared notification types
findings.detail: Ten call sites emit type 'warn' and one emits 'ok'. Neither is a key of the notifIcon map nor matched by any branch of notifPriority, so both fall through to the generic bell icon, a grey left bar and the Low tier. The correct spellings 'warning' and 'success' exist and are used by the toast bridge. Affected: manager-approval requests (L5112, L5120, L10277), driver commitment prompts (L4777, L4838, L4847), decline-streak flags (L12005), corporate policy violations (L12439), low-rating alerts (L12453), orphan credit notes (L15887) and regulator-threshold warnings (L16719).
findings.impact: Money-approval requests and compliance warnings are triaged to the bottom of the page as informational, defeating the module's entire priority-first premise.

findings.title: pingBorderStyle is emitted as literal text instead of being called
findings.detail: In renderActiveTrips the fragment for pingBorderStyle(t) sits inside the single-quoted JS string that builds the row div, so it is written into the markup as literal characters rather than evaluated. The stale-GPS red/amber left border never renders and the malformed attribute text leaks into the DOM. pingBorderStyle is therefore effectively dead code.
findings.impact: The visual escalation that marks a trip as having lost GPS signal never appears, so the ping thresholds the tick engine maintains have no effect on the row.

findings.title: Reassign and cancel update only the live board, never the trip record
findings.detail: commitLiveReassign sets t.driver on the DB.liveTrips entry and confirmCancelLiveTrip splices that entry out, but neither touches DB.trips[id]. The historical record keeps the previous driver and the 'In trip' status.
findings.evidence: var t=DB.liveTrips.find(function(x){return x.id===id;}); if(!t||!DB.drivers[drvId])return; var oldName=nm2(t.driver); t.driver=drvId;
findings.impact: After either action the Live Map history table and the Trips page report a driver and a status that contradict what actually happened, and the audit entry describes a change the trip record does not reflect.

findings.title: The canvas is never redrawn while Live mode is selected
findings.detail: The tick engine's map branch calls updateLiveMarkers() when MAP_MODE === 'live' and drawMap() otherwise. updateLiveMarkers is the dead Leaflet renderer and returns on its first line because _lmap is null, so in Live mode nothing redraws. Trip progress (t.prog) keeps advancing every tick, so the underlying data moves while the picture does not.
findings.impact: The Live tab, whose own banner says 'updates every second', shows a frozen map; only switching to History or selecting a trip forces a redraw.

findings.title: Auto-renew toggle mutates the DB with no permission gate
findings.detail: toggleAutoRenew and commitAutoRenewOff both write DB.subscriptions and emit auto_renew_toggle audit entries without any requirePerm call, unlike every other write in the module (openSettlement, doFreeze, confirmCancelSub, commitDriverChange, commitNewSub all gate on manage_subscriptions).
findings.impact: Any signed-in role, including one deliberately denied manage_subscriptions, can turn a rider's renewal preference on or off.

findings.title: Filter-bar search input is inert
findings.detail: The search box in the card header has no id, no name and no oninput/onkeyup handler, and no function reads it. renderSubscriptionsTable only reads the three hidden custom-select fields.
findings.impact: Operators type a rider or driver name into a visible search box and nothing happens, with no feedback that the control is not wired.

findings.title: No exit from the Frozen state
findings.detail: doFreeze sets sub.status='Frozen' and the modal copy promises 'Trips will not be scheduled until you unfreeze', but no unfreeze or resume function exists in the file. The only ways out are cancel and settle, both of which terminate the subscription.
findings.impact: A subscription frozen for a rider's two-week trip can only be resumed by cancelling and re-selling it, losing the package and its history.

findings.title: Two different driver-commission rates inside one module
findings.detail: The table's Paid / Driver column derives the driver's share from the flat EYVAR_COMMISSION_PCT=20 inside subEconomics, while buildSubProfile uses commissionRateForPlan, which reads DB.plans[key].eyvarPct (20 weekly, 18 biweekly, 15 monthly). For a bi-weekly or monthly package the two screens disagree about what the driver has earned.
findings.impact: For SUB-1052 (Bi-weekly Comfort, 412.00 SAR) the table implies 80% to the driver and the profile 82% - a displayed money figure that is wrong on one of the two screens.

findings.title: commitAddEmployee has no permission gate
findings.detail: commitAddEmployee mutates DB.corporateAccounts[corpId].riders and DB.riders[rid] and writes a config_updated audit entry without any requirePerm call, unlike its sibling removeEmployeeFromCorp which gates on manage_subscriptions.
findings.evidence: function commitAddEmployee(corpId){ var rid=... c.riders.push(rid); DB.riders[rid].corpAccountId=corpId;
findings.impact: Any signed-in user can attach a rider to a company account, redirecting that rider's spend onto the company's consolidated bill.

findings.title: Consolidated invoice re-bills the entire payment history
findings.detail: lineItems iterates every Paid payment of every linked employee with no date filter, while the card copy promises 'every linked employee's payments this cycle'.
findings.impact: Every monthly invoice charges the company for everything it has ever paid, so the totals compound month over month.

findings.title: Invoice sequence advances when the preview opens
findings.detail: openCorpInvoiceModal increments DB.invoiceSequence and mints the invoice number as part of building the modal, before any send. Closing the preview does not roll it back.
findings.impact: Repeatedly opening the preview permanently burns numbers and gaps a VAT invoice series, which a tax audit treats as missing invoices.

findings.title: Corporate id generator is collision-prone
findings.detail: commitNewCorp mints the id from the current account count plus one, with no collision retry. The subscription generator by contrast retries on collision (L5090).
findings.impact: With CORP-001 and CORP-002 present, removing CORP-001 and creating a new account regenerates CORP-002 and silently overwrites the existing company, its riders and its policy.

findings.title: No-shows KPI and filter are permanently empty
findings.detail: Nothing in the file writes a trip status containing 'no-show' - verified across every status assignment. The No-shows tile therefore always reads 0 / 0% rate and setTripsKindFilter('noshow') always empties the table.
findings.impact: A headline operational metric reads zero regardless of reality, and the filter behind it is unusable.

findings.title: Receipt line items need not sum to the printed total
findings.detail: When a trip has no stored fareBreakdown, openTripReceipt builds one from the independent 4.00 / 1.35 / 0.42 rate card with surge=1 and seed=1, then overwrites only fb.gross with parseFloat(t.fare).
findings.impact: A customer-facing itemised receipt shows base, distance and time figures that do not add up to what the rider actually paid.

findings.title: Entire KPI strip is hardcoded HTML
findings.detail: All four tiles - value, colour, delta and bar width - are literals in the page markup. No render function targets them; there is no #quickrides-kpis element and nothing writes into #p-quickrides .g4. Live equivalents for three of the four are computed elsewhere (liveSubtitles, refreshNavCounts, captureDailySnapshot) and never wired in.
findings.evidence:
Quick rides today
63
up 9% vs avg
findings.impact: Four fabricated operational numbers sit directly above a live table, so an operator reading Cancel rate 6.3% or Eyvar net 332 is reading nothing at all.

findings.title: The quoted fare estimate has no relationship to what is charged
findings.detail: updateNrrFareEstimate computes km, minutes and a fare from the chosen districts, but commitNewRideRequest stores none of them on the request. completeTrip later generates the distance at random and recomputes the fare from that.
findings.impact: An operator quotes a fare to a caller on the phone that the system will not honour; the actual charge is unrelated to the route the caller asked for.

findings.title: The Review button on cancelled rides does nothing
findings.detail: resolveAlert relabels the button, disables it, and after 600 ms fades the row and toasts. No DB field is written, no audit entry is made, and the row returns to full opacity on the next render.
findings.impact: An operator believes they have resolved a cancelled ride; nothing is recorded and the item reappears.

findings.title: A completed renewal writes no audit entry and no payment record
findings.detail: renderSuccess() rewrites the subscription (or creates one) and refreshes two other pages, but calls neither logAction nor any DB.payments write. Contrast capturePaymentHold() on the Requests path, which creates a DB.payments record and logs payment_captured.
findings.impact: Money is nominally charged but Finance sees no payment and the activity log has no record of who renewed what — the renewal is unreconcilable and unattributable.

findings.title: sbb-renew sidebar badge uses a broken expiry rule
findings.detail: refreshNavCounts() derives the badge from parseInt(x.ends,10)-25 <= 3. It takes the leading day-of-month out of the ends string and subtracts the literal 25, so the month is ignored ('2 Jul' scores -23 and counts as expiring), there is no lower bound so already-expired subscriptions are included, and the window is 3 days while the page itself uses 7.
findings.impact: The sidebar badge and the page total routinely disagree, so the operator is given a wrong count of work outstanding.

findings.title: The renewal page and the charge path are entirely ungated
findings.detail: renderRenewalPipeline(), renewalMenu(), openHealthBreakdown(), openRenewFlow(), processCharge() and renderSuccess() contain no requirePerm or requirePagePerm call. The only gates in the whole flow are sendRenewalApprovalRequest ('contact_users') and commitRetentionAction ('predictive.act').
findings.impact: Any operator who can reach the page can run the full charge-and-activate flow on any rider's subscription without a permission check.

findings.title: 'Upcoming (24h)' applies no 24-hour filter
findings.detail: renderReadiness() sorts DB.upcomingSubTrips by minutesUntil and counts the whole array. Seeded records UST-6 (minutesUntil 1290) and UST-8 (1340) are ~21.5 and ~22.3 hours out and are included; anything beyond 1440 minutes would be counted too, and fmtCountdown renders every such trip as the literal 'Tomorrow'.
findings.impact: The page's headline number does not mean what its label and the page subtitle say it means.

findings.title: Departed trips never leave the readiness board
findings.detail: tickEngine() only decrements minutesUntil while it is greater than 0, and the sole removal path is confirmPostponeTrip()'s splice. Nothing marks a trip as departed or completed, so a trip that reaches 0 stays at 0 forever.
findings.impact: The Critical and High sections fill permanently with departed trips, so the KPI tiles, section counts and sidebar badge all inflate without bound and the board stops being actionable.

findings.title: Replacement-driver candidates ignore availability and eligibility
findings.detail: resolveUnavailable() builds candidates by filtering only on id !== t.driver and matching vehicle type, then takes the first three in key order. It performs no busy check, no status check, no dispatchEligibility() call and no distance ranking — unlike assignBackup() and nearestAvailableDrivers().
findings.impact: A busy, suspended or ineligible driver can be offered and assigned as the replacement on a trip that is already in a critical state.

findings.title: Selected compensation is never applied
findings.detail: The compensation screen offers a free ride, 20% off the next renewal, 10 SAR wallet credit or nothing. finalizeReassign() writes no wallet credit, no promo and no credit note — it only closes the modal, re-renders, logs an audit line and toasts.
findings.evidence: toast('✅ Driver reassigned · Rider notified · Compensation: '+(labels[comp]||comp),'ok');
findings.impact: Riders are promised compensation for a disruption that no system ever grants, creating a support liability with no record beyond a log line.

findings.title: The rider notification is never sent and its text is discarded
findings.detail: The notify-rider modal prefills a #notif-msg textarea, but sendRiderChangeNotif() reads only #notif-new-driver. No sendSystemEmail, no push, no notification of any kind is dispatched; the toast nonetheless claims '✅ Rider notified · New driver assigned · ETA updated in app'.
findings.evidence: toast('✅ Rider notified · New driver assigned · ETA updated in app','ok');
findings.impact: The rider is never told their driver changed while the operator is told they were — a user-facing action that silently does nothing.

findings.title: Materialised subscription ids are generated with no collision check
findings.detail: materializeSubscription() picks 'SUB-'+(1200+rand(800)) and assigns DB.subscriptions[newSubId] directly. The renewal wizard, by contrast, loops with while(DB.subscriptions[newSubId]) until the id is unique.
findings.impact: Assigning a driver to a subscription request can silently overwrite an existing subscription record, losing that rider's plan, dates and trip quota.

findings.title: Snapshot export is ungated, unaudited and one-way
findings.detail: exportRequestsSnapshot() serialises DB.rideRequests and DB.subscriptionRequests in full, builds a Blob and triggers a browser download. It calls neither requirePerm nor logAction, and no import counterpart exists, so the stated 'safety net against refresh-loss' only works in one direction.
findings.impact: Any operator can exfiltrate the entire rider-linked request corpus with a single click and nothing records that it happened.

findings.title: Approved-driver id generation can overwrite an existing driver
findings.detail: approveDriver derives the new key as 'DRV-0'+(106+Math.floor(Math.random()*90)), giving DRV-0106 through DRV-0195 with no uniqueness check before the assignment DB.drivers[newId]={...}. DRV-0106 (Reem Al-Otaibi) already exists in the seed, so roughly one approval in ninety silently replaces a live driver record along with its trips, payments, complaints and stats.
findings.impact: Silent data loss of a live driver record, including their financial history.

findings.title: docStatus is read in two places and written in none
findings.detail: grep for docStatus across all 21,857 lines returns exactly two reads — the 'docs' branch of the roster filter and the docsExpiring computation in fleetCounts() — plus the unrelated helper docStatusMeta(). Nothing ever assigns it. The 'Documents at risk' supply KPI and the matching Register-panel tile are therefore permanently 0, the 'will auto-suspend on expiry' sub-label never appears, and clicking that tile always empties the roster. The real expiry data lives in DB.driverDocs with docDaysLeft()/docState() and is never bridged into docStatus.
findings.impact: A compliance KPI that ops relies on to spot upcoming auto-suspensions silently reports zero risk at all times, and its filter is a dead end.

findings.title: Driver incentives are never persisted
findings.detail: sendDriverIncentive builds four hardcoded offer cards and confirmDriverIncentive closes the modal and toasts. No DB.driverBonusLog entry is written, no audit entry is recorded and no permission is checked. The driver 360° profile's Earnings breakdown reads DB.driverBonusLog for its '🏆 Incentive bonuses earned' row, so that row will always read +0.00 SAR no matter how many incentives were 'sent'.
findings.impact: Financial commitments made to drivers leave no record anywhere in the panel.

findings.title: No driver record has a status field, so the pending KPI is structurally zero
findings.detail: All six seeded DB.drivers records omit .status and approveDriver() does not set it on the record it creates. Consequently the filter status!=='pending' in renderDriversTable is a no-op and fleetCounts().drivers.pending always evaluates to 0 while the amber pending card immediately above it counts 5 open applications from DB.pendingDrivers. Two 'pending' numbers on the same screen read from different collections and can never agree.
findings.impact: The supply KPI strip reports 'nothing waiting' next to a card listing five applicants blocking supply.

findings.title: reviewDriver() is a stub that appears to take disciplinary action
findings.detail: The modal offers Send warning / Temporary suspension / Reassign riders / Clear flag in a custom select, but the selected value is never read. Apply simply calls closeModal() and toasts '✅ Review action applied'. There is no permission gate, no state write and no audit entry, and the amber warning box shows the same invented text for every driver.
findings.evidence: Flagged: Late 3× consecutive, on-time rate dropped to 88%.
findings.impact: An operator can believe they suspended a driver when nothing happened, and there is no audit trail to reveal the discrepancy.

findings.title: Approval can overwrite an existing driver record
findings.detail: The new key is 'DRV-0'+(106+Math.floor(Math.random()*90)) — DRV-0106 to DRV-0195 — assigned directly with no uniqueness check. DRV-0106 already exists in the seed data, so a collision replaces a live driver together with its trips, payments, complaints and stats.
findings.impact: Silent, unrecoverable loss of a live driver record on approval.

findings.title: Nothing at all blocks approval
findings.detail: approveDriver reads none of a.docs, a.docNotes, a.docExpiry, a.bank.status or the vehicle-class verdict before creating the driver record. Every check in the funnel is advisory copy inside the confirmation modal. A mismatched vehicle class, a rejected licence and an unverified bank account can all be approved with two clicks.
findings.impact: The KYC gate is entirely procedural; the system will activate a driver in any document state.

findings.title: Rejected documents look identical to pending ones in both applicant lists
findings.detail: applicantRowHTML builds each document chip with a single test for a leading ✓, falling back to b-amber for everything else. A '✗ Rejected' verdict therefore renders as the same amber chip as '⏳ Pending'. Only the detail page's docStatusMeta distinguishes the three states.
findings.impact: The triage screen cannot distinguish 'waiting on a scan' from 'we refused this scan', which is the single most important distinction at that stage.

findings.title: Rejection promises a notification that is never sent
findings.detail: The rejection confirmation modal states 'This applicant will be notified and removed from the pending queue.' rejectDriver sets status, closes the modal, re-renders, audits and toasts — it calls neither sendSystemEmail nor pushOpsNotification. Only approval sends mail.
findings.impact: Rejected applicants are never told, and the operator is told they were.

findings.title: The 'Pending approval' KPI and the pending card can never agree
findings.detail: The supply KPI reads fleetCounts().drivers.pending, a count of DB.drivers records with status==='pending' — a field no driver record ever carries. The card immediately above reads DB.pendingDrivers filtered by its own status field. The KPI is structurally 0 and displays 'nothing waiting' above a card listing five applications.
findings.impact: The headline supply metric contradicts the queue it sits on top of.

findings.title: The approval modal counts rejected documents as merely pending
findings.detail: confirmApproveDriver computes notVerified with the same indexOf('✓')!==0 test, so an explicitly rejected document — including one rejected for suspected forgery — produces the soft amber copy 'N document(s) are still pending automated verification. You can still approve, but consider waiting for results first.' rather than a hard block or even a distinct warning.
findings.impact: The last checkpoint before activation actively downplays a refused identity document.

findings.title: The verification document set and the expiry document set do not match
findings.detail: a.docs carries license, id_card, vehicle_reg, background and insurance — the five items an operator approves or rejects. DOC_TYPES carries license, vehicle_reg, inspection, insurance and operating_card — the five items that receive expiry dates and are copied into DB.driverDocs at approval. id_card and background are verified but never get an expiry date; inspection and operating_card get an expiry date and drive auto-suspension but are never shown, previewed, approved or rejected.
findings.evidence: var DOC_TYPES=[['license','Driving license'],['vehicle_reg','Vehicle registration (Istimara)'],['inspection','Periodic inspection (Fahs)'],['insurance','Insurance'],['operating_card','Transport authority operating card']];
findings.impact: Two of the five compliance-tracked documents are never actually inspected, and two of the five inspected documents are never tracked for expiry.

findings.title: Promotion from the sign-ups queue drops fields and never dequeues
findings.detail: openNewRiderProfile copies only id, name, phone, dob, nid, address and city into the new DB.riders record, omitting gender, hasPhoto, device, appLang, lastIp, ipLocation and movementLog — all of which exist on the source record and are all rendered by buildEntityProfile, which will show em-dashes and 'No location history recorded yet.' instead. It also never removes the entry from DB.newRiders, so the person remains in the New sign-ups card indefinitely and is counted both there and in the rider total.
findings.impact: Data captured at sign-up is discarded at the moment it becomes useful, and the intake queue never drains.

findings.title: Rider KPI tiles 2 and 3 count subscriptions instead of riders
findings.detail: fleetCounts().riders.withSub filters DB.subscriptions by /active|expiring/i on the subscription status, producing a count of subscriptions. quickOnly then subtracts that subscription count from the rider count. A rider holding two active subscriptions is counted twice under 'On a subscription', and 'Quick-ride only' can go negative once subscriptions outnumber riders.
findings.impact: The rider composition strip — the first thing on the page — reports arithmetically incoherent figures.

findings.title: The New sign-ups badge is a static literal that no code updates
findings.detail: The span carries id 'new-riders-count' with the text 3 baked into the markup. A grep across the whole file returns exactly one occurrence of that id — the markup itself. renderNewRiders writes the list body but never the badge, so the count reads 3 permanently regardless of DB.newRiders.
findings.impact: A visible intake counter that can never be right except by coincidence.

findings.title: The Status column ignores subscription status and suspension
findings.detail: The cell renders 'Active' whenever rr.subs is non-empty and 'On-demand' otherwise. It never inspects the referenced subscriptions' status, so a rider whose only subscription is Cancelled or Expired still reads Active, and it never checks rr.suspended, so a suspended rider is indistinguishable from a healthy one.
findings.impact: The roster's only status signal is wrong for exactly the riders ops most needs to notice.

findings.title: reviewDriver is a stub wired to two live action surfaces
findings.detail: The modal shows the same hardcoded finding for every driver and its Apply button only closes the modal and toasts. There is no permission gate, no DB write and no audit entry, yet reviewDriver is a primary driver action on the profile action bar and the Escalate action on every complaint profile.
findings.impact: An operator who escalates a complaint or applies a driver warning gets a success toast while nothing at all is recorded.

findings.title: Rider trip history is fabricated to close the gap against the billing aggregate
findings.detail: ensureHistory runs before anything on the rider profile is measured and delegates to buildRiderHistory, which synthesises the difference between stats.totalTrips and entityDerived().trips with a seeded PRNG. By default it generates only 55 percent of the gap; the rest stays 'held in billing' until fetchFullHistory flips window.__fetchFullHistory. Routes, distances, durations, fares, hours and ratings are all invented within hardcoded ranges.
findings.impact: Trip rows an operator can click, quote and open receipts from are generated data, marked only by a small amber 'rebuilt' pill. Any operational decision taken on a rebuilt trip is taken on a fiction.

findings.title: Departure-risk countdowns are derived from trip-id digits
findings.detail: departureRisk computes minsToPickup as 20 minus the trip-id digits modulo 18, giving a deterministic 3 to 20 minutes with no relation to any schedule or ETA. The page then filters on minsToPickup <= 20, which given that formula can never exclude a row.
findings.impact: The card that drives the Call captain and Record absence decisions presents a fabricated countdown as fact, and its KPI filter is a no-op.

findings.title: Forfeiture is written to the audit log and nowhere else
findings.detail: recordAbsence logs plan_earnings_forfeited with the amount and the subscription, but debits no wallet, no escrow record and no payout row. The same holds in reverse for decideEmergency: upholding a claim logs that the amount was restored and sets ev.waived, without any balance movement. Only the emergency-cover path posts real ledger entries, via the acceptEmergency override.
findings.evidence: logAction('plan_earnings_forfeited','driver',driverId, exp.remainingSAR.toFixed(2)+' SAR of undelivered plan earnings forfeited on '+subId
findings.impact: Every figure the enforcement ladder shows as forfeited, at risk or restored is narrative, so the panel and any real payout system would disagree about what a captain is owed.

findings.title: The 21:00 confirmation cut-off is never evaluated
findings.detail: confirmDeadline is read in display strings only - the KPI sub-label, the confirmation card header, the settings form and the tier copy. There is no scheduler or timer that runs autoHandoff for unconfirmed legs at the cut-off; handing a leg to a backup is a manual button press. The entire prevention layer, described in the module header as the highest-leverage control, depends on an operator remembering.
findings.evidence: confirmDeadline:'21:00',  /* fixed evening cut-off, not a rolling 24h window */
findings.impact: A leg nobody clicked on by 21:00 is not converted into a managed withdrawal; it silently becomes an absence at pickup time with the full penalty ladder attached.

findings.title: The most destructive actions on the page are ungated
findings.detail: PAGE_PERMISSIONS has no commitment key. recordAbsence, which forfeits earnings, pulls the plan, freezes the captain and at tier 3 sets planAccess to terminated, has no requirePerm call - only a guardAction confirmation dialog. confirmPlanLeg, autoHandoff, respondBackupOffer, acceptEmergency, declineEmergency and reinstateProbationary are likewise ungated. Only decideEmergency and saveCommitPolicy check a permission.
findings.impact: Any operator who can open the page can permanently remove a captain from the plan system, with a confirm dialog as the only barrier.

findings.title: commitBackup writes the shared backup registry with no permission check
findings.detail: The coverage.assign_backup and manage_subscriptions gates live on assignBackup (L13187-L13188), the function that opens the picker modal. commitBackup itself begins by writing DB.subBackups with no requirePerm/requirePagePerm call. Any caller that reaches commitBackup directly bypasses the page permission entirely.
findings.impact: The permission control on backup assignment is enforced only at the UI entry point, not at the write; the audit entry is still written, attributing the change to an operator who may not hold the permission.

findings.title: Coverage table and coverage KPIs use two different definitions of 'covered'
findings.detail: Columns 4, 6 and 7 and the row background test the raw registration `bak = DB.subBackups[s.id]` (L13170), while the four KPIs, the card badge and the sidebar badge test `subIsCovered()` (L13150), which additionally re-runs `dispatchEligibility`. A registered-but-ineligible backup therefore renders as '✓ <name>' / 'Protected' in the row while being counted as Exposed in the KPI directly above it — precisely the discrepancy the shared subIsCovered definition was introduced to eliminate (comment L17468-L17471). The Plan-commitment twin renderCoverage() does render the third 'registered but ineligible' state; this page does not.
findings.impact: An operator can see 'Protected' on a subscription that the platform itself counts as exposed, and will skip assigning a real backup for a plan that has none in practice.

findings.title: d.docStatus is read in two places but assigned nowhere
findings.detail: grep of docStatus returns exactly four hits: L6380 (Drivers table 'docs' filter), L7093 and L10847 (docStatusMeta — an unrelated applicant document-verification verdict) and L20925 (fleetCounts). No DB.drivers literal carries a docStatus property and no `.docStatus =` assignment exists. The real expiry truth lives exclusively in DB.driverDocs and is reachable only through docDaysLeft/docState/complianceScan.
findings.impact: The Drivers page 'docs' filter always returns zero rows and fleetCounts().drivers.docsAtRisk is always 0, directly contradicting Compliance's 'Expired — suspended: 1'. Compliance is the only surface in the panel that tells the truth about document expiry.

findings.title: Sidebar badge is wrong from first paint and never refreshes in the background
findings.detail: The only assignment to sbb-compliance is inside renderCompliancePage(), whose four call sites (L8797 router, L11076 after saving dates, L13319 KPI filter, L13378 dead markDocRenewed) all require the page to have been opened. The 60-tick timer calls complianceScan() unconditionally — so the suspension and bell alert do fire in the background — but re-renders only when #p-compliance carries class 'on'.
findings.impact: Before the first visit the badge shows the hardcoded 0 while DRV-0104 is already expired and auto-suspended; a driver crossing into expiry mid-session produces a bell alert but no badge change.

findings.title: The page permission is checked on modal open but not on commit
findings.detail: openDocDateEditor checks both requirePerm('approve_drivers') (L11051) and requirePagePerm('compliance','edit_dates') (L11052). saveDriverDocDates checks only requirePerm('approve_drivers') — the page-scoped permission is never re-evaluated at write time.
findings.impact: A user whose compliance.edit_dates permission is revoked while the modal is open can still commit new expiry dates, which in turn drives auto-suspension and auto-un-suspension of drivers.

findings.title: A precautionary suspension can never be lifted
findings.detail: precautionSuspend writes a reason beginning 'Precautionary — pending …'. The only deletion site for DB.complianceSuspensions in the entire file is Compliance's auto-lift at L13312, which requires the reason to start with 'Expired'. closeIncident never touches the suspension store, and no 'lift suspension' or 'un-suspend' handler exists anywhere.
findings.impact: A driver suspended pending investigation stays off dispatch — including on their active subscriptions — for the life of the session, even after the incident is closed and the four protocol steps are complete.

findings.title: No path exists to create an incident
findings.detail: Every reference to DB.incidents in the file is a .find(), .filter() or .forEach() — L13398, L13408, L13450, L13469, L13477 in this module and L14223, L14295, L14345, L14375, L19188 downstream. There is no push, no 'log incident' button, no SOS ingestion path and no API. The three seeded records are the entire universe.
findings.impact: In a live system the safety queue could never receive anything; the module can only ever process the three demo records.

findings.title: Sidebar safety badge is wrong from first paint with no background refresh at all
findings.detail: sbb-safety is assigned only inside renderSafetyPage(), whose call sites are L8798 (router), L13396 (its own KPI filter) and L13462/L13471/L13481 (its own three action handlers). Unlike Compliance, the tick engine (L12509-L12624) contains no safety hook; even refreshInbox(), which does read DB.incidents, updates only sbb-inbox.
findings.impact: An operator who never opens the page sees 0 next to 'Safety' indefinitely while two incidents — one a critical SOS — sit open.

findings.title: No promo redemption engine exists anywhere in the file
findings.detail: A grep for discountPct across the file hits L2890-L2894, L4521-L4577, L4662, L5935, L6076-L6146, L13496-L13499, L13515, L13554 and L21500. Every hit outside the promo block L13495-L13560 belongs to the subscription-plan cadence discount (CADENCE_META, L4521), not to promo codes. A promo's discountPct never touches a fare, a subscription price or a payment.
