findings.impact: The entire promo campaigns card is a display surface over numbers no code produces or consumes; launching a campaign has no effect on what any rider pays.

findings.title: promo.spent, uses and newSubs are never incremented
findings.detail: Verified by grep: the only `.spent` references are reads — promoROI (L13504), the burn calculation (L13510), the burn bar (L13516) and contributionMargin (L15725). The only writes to a `.spent` property in the file belong to steering offers (L14180-L14181), a different object. commitNewPromo creates every campaign with spent, uses and newSubs at 0.
findings.impact: Budget burn %, the burn bar colour, ROI and the ROI colour are frozen at seed values for seeded rows and permanently 0 / 0.0× for any campaign created in-session — an operator monitoring a live campaign sees a dead dashboard.

findings.title: sendBulkMsg sends nothing
findings.detail: The handler validates permissions and non-empty text, then writes logAction('bulk_message',…), toasts and clears the textarea. There is no DB.pushOutbox (L13835) or DB.emailOutbox (L13834) write and no recipient resolution, despite sendPushNotification (L7735) and sendBroadcast (L7694) existing elsewhere and doing exactly that. The bm-ch channel value appears only inside the audit summary string.
findings.evidence:
logAction('bulk_message','segment',seg.id,'Bulk '+document.getElementById('bm-ch').value+' to "'+seg.label+'" ('+seg.count+' recipients)',{},{});
  toast('📣 Sent to '+seg.count+' recipients — "'+seg.label+'"','ok');
findings.impact: The toast reports a delivery to N recipients that never happened, and the audit log records it as a sent message — the most confidently false success message on the page.

findings.title: The advertised budget auto-pause does not exist
findings.detail: No code sets status to 'exhausted' or 'expired'; the only runtime status writes are pausePromo (L13529) and resumePromo (L13530). Both states are reachable only from seed data. Meanwhile the card sub-note (L1270), the modal info block (L13542) and the source comment (L13489-L13493) all assert the campaign pauses itself when the budget is consumed.
findings.impact: The product tells the operator in three places that runaway promo spend is impossible. Since spent never moves either, the safety mechanism is doubly absent — a real integration would inherit an unguarded budget.

findings.title: The incentive 'active' toggle is the only ungated DB write on the page
findings.detail: The per-row toggle is an inline onchange that assigns DB.incentives[i].active straight from the checkbox and raises a toast. It has no requirePerm, no requirePagePerm and no logAction — unlike addIncentiveRule and removeIncentiveRule, which are both manage_plans-gated, audited and confirm-gated.
findings.impact: Any operator can silently switch a money-committing captain incentive on or off, with no permission check and no trace in the Activity log; the 🏆 Award button appears or disappears on the next render.

findings.title: The surge zone picker treats the zones array as an object
findings.detail: openSuspendSurge builds its picker with Object.keys(DB.zones||{}).slice(0,8). DB.zones is an array (L13952), so Object.keys yields the index strings '0'…'5', and because the array is non-empty the intended ['RUH-CENTRAL','RUH-NORTH'] fallback never fires.
findings.impact: Surge suspensions are recorded against numeric index strings rather than zone names, so the suspension cannot be matched back to a district — a cross-module data-integrity bug in the Pricing module caused by this module's data shape.

findings.title: Zone demand, supply and failure counts are frozen literals
findings.detail: DB.zones is a six-row hardcoded array with no id, city, lat/lng, polygon or timestamp. No code updates demand, supply or failures30d from DB.rideRequests, DB.subscriptionRequests, driver availability or any failure log. Every KPI, ratio, failure rate, recruitment priority and 'needs +N drivers' figure on the page — and zoneCongestionMultiplier feeding estimateEtaMin — derives from these three numbers.
findings.impact: The recruitment map never changes, and ETAs computed anywhere in the panel inherit the mock congestion it produces.

findings.title: A refund never marks its source payment Refunded
findings.detail: No function anywhere in the file mutates DB.payments[x].status. recordRefund does not flip the source payment. A fully refunded payment therefore keeps satisfying the p.status==='Paid' filter in contributionMargin().gross and in riderLTV (L4033-L4039). The two seeded 'Refunded' payments are the only ones in that state, and they are seed literals.
findings.impact: Revenue and rider lifetime value are overstated indefinitely by the full amount of every refunded payment.

findings.title: contributionMargin counts driver earnings from cancelled trips
findings.detail: gross filters DB.payments on p.status==='Paid' (L15721) but driverEarn reduces over every entry in DB.trips with no status filter at all (L15722-L15723). Cancelled trips that carry a non-zero driverEarn depress net without any matching revenue line.
findings.impact: The headline gross-margin figure and the contribution margin beneath it are both understated by the driver earnings on cancelled trips.

findings.title: Escrow and payout money never reaches the double-entry books
findings.detail: ACCOUNTS declares liability.escrow (L19870) and liability.driver (L19869), but liability.escrow is never posted to and liability.driver is only ever credited by postFareCapture's driver_accrual leg (L20047), never debited on settlement. releaseEscrow (L7058), payDriver (L7023) and confirmProcessAll (L7049) mutate DB.payouts with no postLedger call.
findings.impact: The trial balance shows a permanently growing captain-payable that no settlement ever clears, and escrow never appears in the books at all.

findings.title: findInvoiceForRefund falls back to an arbitrary invoice
findings.detail: After failing to match on k===rel, p.trip===rel or p.sub===rel, findInvoiceForRefund takes the first payment for that rider with status 'Paid' (L15857-L15859). The resulting credit note is issued against an unrelated invoice - wrong amount, wrong period - and is marked unlinked:false, i.e. silently 'correct'. This is worse than the unlinked case it was written to avoid, because nothing flags it.
findings.impact: A VAT reversal can be filed against an invoice it does not relate to, with no warning chip and no ops notification, corrupting the tax record.

findings.title: KPI tiles contradict both each other and the live data
findings.detail: All seven KPI tiles are literal strings. KPI 2 says Eyvar net 9,246 / 19.2% while the totals row of the table beneath says 8,752 / 18.1%. KPI 3 says driver payouts 38,984 while the table says 39,478. KPI 5 says 501.98 held in escrow while renderEscrow computes 138.40 from DB.escrowHolds (69.20 + 69.20); the sum of all four holds is 500.98, matching nothing. KPI 7 says deductions 65.00 (all three seeded deductions) while renderDeductions sums only pending rows to 45.00.
findings.impact: An operator reading the finance page sees revenue, payout and escrow figures that no live collection supports and that contradict the table directly below them.

findings.title: recordRefund writes no audit entry of its own
findings.detail: recordRefund (L3176-L3202) contains no logAction call. The only audit trace a refund leaves is (a) the caller's own logAction, e.g. cancel_subscription at L5560, and (b) the credit_note_issued entry written inside issueCreditNote (L15883). A direct recordRefund call with no credit note issued leaves no audit trail at all. renderRefundsTable also offers no void, reverse or edit action.
findings.impact: Money leaves the business without a first-class audit record naming the actor and amount; the audit trail depends entirely on the caller.

findings.title: Refund idempotency key has no time component
findings.detail: The override builds key = idemKey('refund', riderId, r2(amount), relatedId||reason||''). Two legitimately distinct refunds of the same amount to the same rider for the same reason (e.g. two 25.00 SAR 'Rider request' refunds where relatedId is falsy) collapse to the same key, and the second is suppressed with only a warn toast and a duplicate_suppressed audit entry. Wallet credit and debit keys, by contrast, append Math.floor(nowMs()/1000) (L19980, L19994).
findings.impact: A second legitimate refund silently does not happen; the operator sees a warn toast and no refund row, and the rider is never repaid.

findings.title: Refund IDs are derived from array length, not a sequence
findings.detail: id is built as 'REF-'+String(DB.refunds.length+1).padStart(4,'0'). With the two seeds present (REF-0002, REF-0001, length 2) the first new refund is REF-0003, which is correct only while nothing is ever removed. Any deletion or reorder produces a duplicate id. Contrast DB.creditNoteSequence (L15848, incremented at L15869), a true monotonic counter.
findings.impact: Refund identifiers can collide, breaking the credit-note back-reference and any downstream reconciliation keyed on REF ids.

findings.title: The finance page permission is declared but never enforced
findings.detail: PAGE_PERMISSIONS.finance declares perms [{key:'view', label:'View financial reports'}] with legacy 'view_finance'. Grep for requirePagePerm('finance' returns nothing, and view_finance is never passed to requirePerm anywhere in the file. Neither the go() hook at L8815 nor any of the three render functions gates on it.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user reaches the full revenue, margin, refund and credit-note view regardless of their permission matrix.

findings.title: Cash debt accrues even on honest reports
findings.detail: applyCashDebtImpact is called unconditionally for every generated cash event, including classification 'match' and 'over_report'. A driver who reports every riyal correctly still accumulates 20% of every cash fare as debt and will eventually cross the -300 cap and be suspended from cash collection (L12082, L12103). The page's own explainer frames the debt as arising from an under-report or a driver who never reports (L1000), which the code does not match.
findings.impact: Honest drivers are progressively suspended from cash work, and the 'Total driver debt outstanding' KPI is a gross cash-float metric being presented as a fraud signal.

findings.title: Cash-debt auto-deduction is promised three times and never implemented
findings.detail: The debt-ledger card header says 'Auto-deducted from the next payout' (L1014), the row badge for a non-blocked driver says 'Deducted from next payout' (L12262), and the page explainer says the debt is 'deducted automatically from their next payout' (L1000). No code path connects DB.driverCashDebt to DB.payouts: neither payDriver (L7023) nor confirmProcessAll (L7049) reads driverCashDebt.
findings.impact: A driver with 250 SAR of outstanding cash debt is paid their full pending balance, and the platform never recovers the commission it is owed.

findings.title: Cash-debt repayment is all-or-nothing, self-attested and audit-blind
findings.detail: commitCashRepayment sets DB.driverCashDebt[driverId] = 0 with no amount input, no reference number, no payment method and no partial option - the modal offers only 'Confirm {owed} repayment' (L12199). The audit entry passes {} for both before and after, so auditDiffHTML renders no diff; the cleared balance survives only inside the free-text summary string.
findings.impact: An operator can clear any amount of driver debt on their own assertion, and the audit log cannot show what balance was written off.

findings.title: Deduction overflow is silently discarded
findings.detail: p.pending = Math.max(0, p.pending - d.amount). A 30 SAR no-show penalty against a driver with 10 SAR pending removes 10 SAR and forgets the other 20. There is no carry-forward field, no negative balance and no warning. Applying a deduction to a driver with no pending balance at all marks it 'applied' and moves nothing. The preview modal shows 0.00 SAR for 'Balance after deduction' (L8982) with no indication that part of the penalty evaporated.
findings.impact: Penalties are under-collected without anyone noticing, and the audit record claims the full amount was deducted.

findings.title: No driver-money movement is posted to the ledger
findings.detail: Neither releaseEscrow, payDriver, confirmProcessAll, confirmApplyDeduction, commitCashResolve nor commitCashRepayment calls postLedger (L19917). ACCOUNTS['liability.escrow'] (L19870) is declared and never posted to, and liability.driver is credited by postFareCapture's accrual leg (L20047) but never debited on settlement.
findings.impact: The trial balance shows a permanently growing captain-payable that no settlement clears, and escrow, deductions and cash debt never appear in the double-entry books at all.

findings.title: No idempotency protection on any driver-money action
findings.detail: The refund and rider-wallet paths are wrapped in withIdempotency (L19962, L19978, L19994). payDriver, confirmProcessAll, releaseEscrow, confirmApplyDeduction and commitCashRepayment are not. A double submit on Confirm - Pay is prevented only because p.pending is zeroed on the first pass (L7030), and a double release is prevented only because the splice makes the second findIndex fail (L7061-L7064) - protection by accident rather than design. confirmApplyDeduction has no such accidental protection at all.
findings.impact: Deduction and repayment actions can be replayed, and the payout and escrow paths depend on incidental state mutation rather than an explicit idempotency key.

findings.title: The escrow lifecycle is not implemented
findings.detail: No code creates an escrow hold, no code increments tripsCompleted, and no code transitions held to ready. The only mutations to DB.escrowHolds are the seed literal at L2801 and the splice inside releaseEscrow at L7064. The page's headline promise - subscription payments are held in escrow and only released once the full plan is delivered (L972) - has no runtime mechanism behind it, and the 'ready' branch of the renderer can never be entered at runtime.
findings.impact: The core protection the page advertises - money withheld until service is delivered - exists only as seed data and a manual release button.

findings.title: creditRiderWallet performs no sign check on the amount
findings.detail: creditRiderWallet(riderId,amount,reason,actorNote) applies Math.round((w.balance+amount)*100)/100 with no validation that amount is positive. commitWalletAdjust rejects amount<=0 at the UI layer, but none of the seven programmatic call sites (processReferral L3868/L3869, commitCancelSub L5563, confirmWelcomeOffer L11184, acceptEmergency L17337) validate the sign of the value they pass.
findings.impact: A negative 'credit' drives the balance below zero, entirely bypassing debitRiderWallet's insufficient-funds guard, and posts a reversed ledger entry that still balances so postLedger accepts it. The rider is also emailed that money was 'added' to their wallet.

findings.title: Every wallet credit is expensed to goodwill regardless of its actual reason
findings.detail: The expense-account chooser tests the reason string against /goodwill|apolog/i, then /compensat/i, then falls through to 'expense.goodwill'. Four of the five credit-modal reasons ('Trip cancellation refund', 'Referral bonus', 'Promo code redemption', 'Manual top-up') and all programmatic reasons except the compensation ones match nothing and land on the fallback.
findings.impact: Referral bonuses, promo redemptions, manual top-ups and cancellation refunds all inflate the expense.goodwill account. Goodwill-spend reporting and contribution margin are materially overstated, and there is no way to separate marketing spend from service recovery in the ledger.

findings.title: Every wallet debit is recognised as fare revenue
findings.detail: The debit wrapper posts a fixed pair: liability.wallet debit against revenue.fares credit, with no branch on the reason. One of the three debit-modal reasons is 'Correction — issued in error', which exists specifically to reverse a mistaken credit.
findings.impact: Correcting an operator's own mistake fabricates fare revenue. Revenue is overstated by the value of every corrective debit, and no contra account exists to reverse it.

findings.title: No rollback when the ledger rejects a wallet posting
findings.detail: The credit and debit wrappers run __origCreditWallet / __origDebitWallet first — which mutate w.balance, unshift the WTX record, write the audit entry and send the rider email — and only then call postLedger. If postLedger's balance/known-account guard fails it pushes to DB.moneyRejects, logs ledger_rejected, toasts and returns null. Nothing reverses the balance change that already happened.
findings.impact: The wallet balance and the general ledger permanently diverge with no reconciliation path. DB.moneyRejects records that the posting was refused, but the rider keeps the balance and the operator has already been told the credit succeeded.

findings.title: The refund idempotency key has no time bucket, so a second legitimate refund is suppressed forever
findings.detail: The wallet credit and debit keys end with Math.floor(nowMs()/1000), giving a one-second duplicate window. The refund key does not: idemKey('refund',riderId,r2(amount),relatedId||reason||''). Once a refund of a given amount for a given relatedId has been recorded, withIdempotency returns the cached entry for every subsequent identical call and logs duplicate_suppressed.
findings.impact: Two genuinely separate refunds of the same amount against the same subscription (for example two identical monthly cancellations) can never both be processed — the second silently returns the first refund's record and no money moves, while the operator sees a duplicate-suppressed warning rather than a failure.

findings.title: window.__skipGuards globally disables every money confirmation dialog
findings.detail: guardAction wraps each gated global and checks window.__skipGuards before rendering the confirmation. The flag exists so programmatic and seed calls can bypass the UI gate, and the boot sequence sets it for the whole seed run. Nothing scopes it to a call site or clears it on error, and it is a plain window property reachable from the console or any other code path.
findings.impact: With the wallet action already gated only on contact_users, the confirmation dialog is the last control before money moves; __skipGuards removes it globally for wallet adjustments, refunds and every other gated action at once.

findings.title: A Critical (T1) ticket can never raise a first-response SLA breach
findings.detail: slaState computes frBreached = !firstResponseAtMs && frMs>0 && elapsedFr>frMs. All five T1 reason codes (CAP_CONDUCT, TRP_GHOST_COMPLETE, SAF_RIDER_UNSAFE, SAF_ACCIDENT and the T1 tier default) set fr:0, so frMs is 0 and the condition short-circuits to false forever.
findings.impact: The most urgent tickets in the system — safety incidents and captain misconduct with an immediate-response target — never appear under the 'breaching' filter for first response, never raise the ⚠ 'No first response' badge, and never fire the first_response ops notification. Only the much later resolution breach surfaces them.

findings.title: Half the Support KPI row is static HTML that no code ever updates
findings.detail: #tk-open and #tk-prog are recomputed by renderTickets, but 'Resolved (Jun)' carries the literal 38 and 'Avg response time' the literal '14 min' with no id at all, so nothing can write to it. All four tiles are class='kpi click' and scroll to the ticket list when clicked.
findings.impact: Two of the four headline support metrics are permanently wrong and cannot be corrected without editing the markup — an operator reading the row cannot tell which two numbers are live.

findings.title: Ticket permission gating is applied inconsistently across the module
findings.detail: createTicket, createTicketFor, sendTicketReply, setTicketStatus, closeConversation, reopenTicket, commitChangeReason and commitBulkReason contain no requirePerm or requirePagePerm call. bulkStatus, bulkAssignMe and commitMassEvent all require manage_tickets. PAGE_PERMISSIONS.support defines view and manage grants that only Disputes and Lost & Found actually enforce.
findings.impact: The same operation is gated or ungated depending on the route taken: resolving one ticket from the detail page needs no permission, while resolving the same ticket through the bulk bar needs manage_tickets. Re-coding a ticket in bulk is ungated even though single re-coding is exposed on a permissioned page. The permission model gives no reliable guarantee about who can change ticket state.

findings.title: Ticket subjects and thread messages are rendered as raw HTML
findings.detail: buildTicketDetailBody injects msg.msg directly into the bubble markup and renderTickets injects t.subject into the queue row, with no escaping in either path. Both values originate from free-text inputs (nt-sub, tkd-reply).
findings.impact: A stored-XSS surface as soon as ticket content comes from customers rather than seed data — the injected script would execute in an operator session that has permission to move money and change ticket state.

findings.title: No dispute can be created
findings.detail: DB.disputes is a seeded two-element array. There is no newDispute, no openDispute, no push and no unshift against DB.disputes anywhere in the file — the only writes are the status/outcome assignments inside resolveDispute.
findings.evidence:
DB.disputes=[
  {id:'DSP-07',sub:'SUB-1075',claim:'"Driver never arrived on Tuesday" — rider requests one trip refunded',…}
findings.impact: The dispute workflow is a demo of resolution only. Real rider money claims have no entry point, and once the two seeded disputes are resolved the card is permanently inert.

findings.title: No lost-and-found record can be created
findings.detail: DB.lostFound is a seeded three-element array with no creation function. The TRP_LOST_ITEM reason code (§4.2, T3, fr 15, res 2880, upd 30, owner Ops) exists on tickets, but nothing links a ticket carrying it to an LF-## record.
findings.impact: A rider reporting a lost item can only ever raise a ticket; the item never enters the Lost & Found workflow, so the driver-confirmation and return steps are unusable and the 30-minute update promise on the ticket has no operational counterpart.

findings.title: The dispute gate's notify checkbox and internal note are collected and discarded
findings.detail: The resolveDispute gate declares two options — cfa-notify (checked by default, 'Notify the claimant of the outcome') and cfa-note ('Internal note (optional)'). runConfirm gathers both into window.__confirmValues. resolveDispute's body never reads window.__confirmValues at all.
findings.evidence: options:[{id:'notify',type:'checkbox',label:'Notify the claimant of the outcome',default:true},{id:'note',type:'text',label:'Internal note (optional)',placeholder:'Why this decision'}]
findings.impact: The claimant is never notified even though the operator explicitly confirmed they should be, and the reasoning the operator typed for the decision is silently thrown away — the audit line records only the outcome keyword.

findings.title: The 'Driver will be 10-15 min late' response is inert but claims the rider was notified
findings.detail: In logDriverCall the 'delay' branch changes no state at all — no driverStatus write, no notification push, no email, no contact row — yet the toast reads '⏳ Delay logged — rider will be notified'. The 'moving' and 'unavailable' branches both mutate driverStatus; only 'delay' is a no-op.
findings.evidence: msgs.delay = '⏳ Delay logged — rider will be notified'
findings.impact: An operator believes they have logged a delay and triggered a rider notification when nothing was recorded and no message was sent — a user-facing action that silently does nothing.

findings.title: The intervention count over-reports by one whenever both tiers are populated
findings.detail: buildInterventionItems returns an array of HTML strings, and when the critical list is non-empty it pushes the '⏱ Watch — action needed within the hour' separator div into that same array (L9524). Both renderInterventionsPage (L10343) and renderDashboard (L10442) set their badge to iv.length, counting the separator as an item.
findings.impact: A displayed operational count is wrong by one on both the page and the dashboard widget in exactly the case that matters — when there is both critical and watch work.

findings.title: Three counters over the same data disagree
findings.detail: #iv-page-count (L10343) and #dash-intervene-count (L10442) both use buildInterventionItems().length, which includes SLA tickets and applies the 60-minute window and the scCfg scenario filter. refreshNavCounts computes #sbb-dash separately at L9397-L9399 as (DB.rideRequests||[]).length plus one per upcomingSubTrip whose tripScenario key is unavailable, unassigned or late — no SLA tickets, no time window, and every ride request regardless of status or age.
findings.impact: The sidebar badge routinely disagrees with the card badge for the same concept, so an operator cannot tell how much urgent work actually exists.

findings.title: Four disjoint pricing models coexist and this page edits the one riders do not see
findings.detail: DB.plans (this page), PLANS + CADENCE_META + CADENCE_DAYS (new-sub and renewal flows, L4389/L4519/L11231), DB.quickRideTypes + surge (L13908/L13883), and DB.rateCard (Settings, L21431) are four independent rate sets. Editing a plan here changes only commissionRateForPlan() (L4463) and the dashboard cancellation-cap alert (L10366). Durations are duplicated three times (duration, CADENCE_DAYS, the {weekly:5,biweekly:10,monthly:22} leg map at L21485) and discounts twice (discountPct vs CADENCE_META).
findings.impact: The price a rider is quoted, the price an operator edits and the price the finance rate card models can all disagree with no warning anywhere. A pricing change made on this page is largely cosmetic.

findings.title: Plan status has no effect on what riders can buy
findings.detail: renderNewSubModal() builds its plan option list from the frozen PLANS constant (L4571) and never reads DB.plans or checks status. Deactivating or archiving a plan therefore does not remove it from the New Subscription form, directly contradicting the Activate modal's copy ('the plan appears in the renewal flow and new-subscription form', L5952) and the Deactivate copy ('hides this plan from new subscriptions', L5972).
findings.evidence: doActivatePlan: p.status='Active'; … logAction('activate_plan',…) — but the new-sub modal iterates Object.keys(PLANS), never DB.plans
findings.impact: An operator who deactivates a plan believes it is off sale. It is not — riders can still subscribe to a plan the business has withdrawn, at the frozen constant's price rather than the edited one.

findings.title: No JS range validation on the commission and discount percentages
findings.detail: #fp3-comm carries HTML min=0 max=100 step=0.1 and #fp3-disc carries min=0 step=0.1 with no max at all. numval() applies only parseFloat with a previous-value fallback — neither field is clamped in JS, and the browser attributes are bypassable. eyvarPct is the one plan field with a real downstream consumer: commissionRateForPlan() (L4461–L4466) derives the driver payout rate from it. A discountPct above 100 makes dc = g × (1 − d/100) negative in cr().
findings.impact: An out-of-range Eyvar percentage propagates into the driver commission rate for every subscription trip on that plan; an out-of-range discount produces negative plan totals in the preview with no warning anywhere.

findings.title: The Status dropdown in the plan editor is a no-op
findings.detail: #fp3-status-wrap renders a fully functional three-option custom select (Active / Draft / Archived) built by renderPlansFormSelects(); cselPick writes the chosen value into the hidden #fp3-status input. savePlan() never reads that input — status is absent from the before snapshot (L6126–L6127) and from every write in the setTimeout body (L6131–L6142). Verified by reading the whole of savePlan() L6117–L6149: 'fp3-status' does not appear.
findings.impact: An operator sets a plan to Active or Draft in the editor, clicks through the danger confirmation, sees a success toast — and the status is unchanged. Status can only actually be changed from the plans-table Activate/Deactivate buttons or the Archive button.

findings.title: Default currency setting has no consumer
findings.detail: DB.opsConfig.general.currency is written by saveGeneralConfig and read back by renderGeneralConfig, and by nothing else. All money rendering appends a hardcoded 'SAR' (e.g. gateway volume L7467).
findings.impact: An operator can set the platform currency to USD, see a success toast and an audit entry, and every figure in the panel still reads SAR - a settings control that misrepresents money.

findings.title: Logo upload and removal bypass RBAC and leave no audit trail
findings.detail: Every other Settings mutation opens with requirePerm('manage_settings') and closes with logAction. clearLogo() and handleLogoUpload() do neither: they write DB.opsConfig.general.logoDataUrl directly and call applySiteBranding() immediately, so the change lands before (and independently of) the gated Save button.
findings.evidence: function clearLogo(){ DB.opsConfig.general.logoDataUrl=''; var f=document.getElementById('cfg-gen-logo-file');if(f)f.value=''; applySiteBranding(); toast('Logo removed','info'); }
findings.impact: An operator without manage_settings can change or wipe the panel's browser-tab identity, and the activity log records nothing - the only settings write in the pane with neither a gate nor an audit entry.

findings.title: Audit attribution during impersonation contradicts the stated consequence
findings.detail: The impersonation confirm dialog lists as consequence #2: 'Any action you take is recorded against your name, not theirs.' But logAction builds each entry with actorId: CURRENT_USER_ID and actorName from the same lookup, and CURRENT_USER_ID is the impersonated user for the whole session. Only impersonation_started/impersonation_ended carry the real operator, and even those do so only inside the summary string via nm2(window.__realUserId) - their own actorId is already the impersonated id, because CURRENT_USER_ID is reassigned before logAction is called.
findings.evidence: CURRENT_USER_ID=userId; logAction('impersonation_started','permission',userId, nm2(window.__realUserId)+' began viewing the panel as '+u.name+' ('+u.role+')');
findings.impact: Every action taken while impersonating is logged against the impersonated employee. The audit trail actively misattributes, and the UI tells the operator the opposite.

findings.title: Invited accounts carry live permissions
findings.detail: commitInvite immediately assigns permissions via defaultPermissionsForRole(role). can() checks only that the permission key is in u.permissions - it never inspects u.status. The Invited state is purely cosmetic for RBAC, and nothing ever transitions it to Active.
findings.evidence: function can(permKey){ var u=DB.teamUsers.find(function(x){return x.id===CURRENT_USER_ID;}); return !!(u&&u.permissions&&u.permissions.indexOf(permKey)>=0); }
findings.impact: USR-4 Noura is seeded as Invited with 3 permissions and would pass every corresponding gate. An Owner invite grants all 13 permissions to an account that has never authenticated.

findings.title: No way to remove or deactivate a team user
findings.detail: The row action set is fixed at Permissions / View as / Edit. commitInvite pushes to DB.teamUsers; commitEditTeamUser mutates in place. There is no splice, no status setter, no revoke path anywhere in the pane or in any modal it opens.
findings.impact: Offboarding is impossible through the UI. The only mitigation available is stripping permissions one by one in the per-user modal, which still leaves the account in the roster and still lets it be impersonated.

findings.title: Clicking a mixed cell silently grants the permission to everyone in the role
findings.detail: A mixed cell is rendered with no checked attribute and data-mixed="1"; indeterminate is then set post-render. A checkbox that is indeterminate but unchecked resolves to checked=true on the first user click, so onchange fires toggleRolePermission(role, perm, true) - a grant. The operator's intent when clicking a partially-filled cell is ambiguous, and the UI resolves it in the permissive direction with no confirmation.
findings.evidence: h+='<td style="text-align:center" data-role="'+r+'" data-perm="'+p+'"><input type="checkbox" class="rm-cb"'+(allHave?' checked':'')+(mixed?' data-mixed="1"':'')+' ... onchange="toggleRolePermission(...,this.checked)"
findings.impact: Deliberate per-user overrides created through the per-user Permissions modal are flattened upward across every holder of the role in one click, and the toast reports a successful grant rather than warning that overrides were destroyed.

findings.title: Granular revocations do not propagate to the broad layer
findings.detail: Sync is strictly one-way. toggleRolePermission and saveUserPermissions push broad changes down into pagePerms; togglePagePermission writes only u.pagePerms[pageKey] and never touches u.permissions. Since the money-moving commits in the Wallets area are gated by requirePerm (broad), not requirePagePerm, unticking the granular equivalent has no effect. This directly contradicts the L10555-L10559 design comment claiming the two layers cannot become disconnected sources of truth.
findings.evidence: affected.forEach(function(u){ if(!u.pagePerms)u.pagePerms=defaultPagePerms(u.permissions); var list=u.pagePerms[pageKey]=u.pagePerms[pageKey]||[]; var idx=list.indexOf(permKey); if(grant&&idx<0)list.push(permKey); if(!grant&&idx>=0)list.splice(idx,1); });
findings.impact: An administrator who revokes 'Process driver payouts' in the Detailed page permissions matrix sees the checkbox clear and a confirmation toast, while the Finance role can still process payouts, release escrow and apply deductions. A revocation that appears to have taken effect has not.

findings.title: Most granular action checkboxes are decorative
findings.detail: grep finds 20 occurrences of requirePagePerm( - one declaration plus 19 call sites, covering only compliance, wallets (cash actions only), coverage, safety, growth, zones, predictive and support. The remaining 30 of the 52 keys, including every 'view' key and destructive actions such as requests.cancel, live.cancel_trip, subscriptions.settle, drivers.approve and plans.edit, are never checked by any code path.
findings.impact: The Detailed page permissions matrix presents a fine-grained authorization model in which most switches do nothing. An operator configuring least-privilege access is misled about what has actually been restricted.

findings.title: The Settings page itself is not access-controlled
findings.detail: PAGE_PERMISSIONS.settings declares a 'view' action, but requirePagePerm('settings','view') has no call site. go('settings') runs a long chain of render functions with no permission check of any kind, and every settings-panel div is present in the DOM for all operators.
findings.impact: Any operator, including a Support user with 3 of 13 permissions, can read every configuration value in the panel - payment gateway settings, operational limits, cancellation fees, the full team roster and the entire permission matrix - even though they cannot save changes.

findings.title: cityStats() is hardcoded to Riyadh
findings.detail: The Zones / Drivers / Riders columns of the cities table, the deactivation confirm modal's driver and rider counts, and the executive-overview cities table all call cityStats(name), which returns real numbers only when the name is the literal string 'Riyadh' and {zones:0,drivers:0,riders:0} for everything else. Drivers and riders do carry a `city` field that a correct implementation would filter on; cityStats ignores it.
findings.impact: Every non-Riyadh city permanently displays zero activity, so an operator cannot see whether a city has drivers or riders before turning it off — and the high-impact deactivation confirm can never fire for any city but Riyadh.

findings.title: gw.enabled and gw.isDefault have no enforcement point
findings.detail: Grep of DB.paymentGateways returns only the seed array and the five Settings functions (render, toggle, set-default, add, remove). No charge, checkout, refund, payout, invoice or ledger path reads either flag. The 'cash.gateway' ledger account is a single aggregate with no link to which gateway row is enabled or default. Panel copy ('Turning a gateway off stops new charges through it') and the disable toast ('riders can no longer pay with it') are not backed by any code.
findings.impact: The two controls the tab exists for silently do nothing; an operator who disables a gateway believes charges have stopped when they have not.

findings.title: A feePct above 100 silently voids the refund
findings.detail: The fee input has min="0" but no max, and saveCancellationPolicy applies parseFloat with no bound check. cancelSub computes refund = grossRefund − fee, which goes negative once feePct exceeds 100; confirmCancelSub then guards with if(refund>0) and skips the wallet credit entirely.
findings.impact: Money: a misconfigured percentage leaves the rider with neither a refund nor a recorded charge, and the cancellation still completes.

findings.title: The 10 SAR after-arrival fee tier is unreachable
findings.detail: confirmCancelLiveTrip maps reason 'rider_request' to qr_after_grace, 'rider_noshow' to qr_rider_noshow, and anything else to null. The live-trip cancel modal offers exactly those three reasons plus ops_decision, and none maps to qr_after_arrival. Grep for qr_after_arrival returns only its seed line.
findings.impact: A rider who cancels after the driver has arrived is charged the 5 SAR after-grace fee instead of the configured 10 SAR — the money charged is wrong, and editing the after-arrival row has no effect.

findings.title: Automatic compensation bypasses the entire authority model
findings.detail: The emergency-dispatch path calls logGoodwill(d.riderId, d.riderCompensation, 'CAP_NOSHOW', 'Policy compensation - automatic, not agent discretion') directly at L17339, without going through compCheck. Per-case ceilings, per-agent daily ceilings, the per-rider 30-day abuse signal and the second-approval threshold are all skipped, and the entry is attributed to the current agent in the ledger.
findings.evidence: logGoodwill(d.riderId, d.riderCompensation, 'CAP_NOSHOW', 'Policy compensation - automatic, not agent discretion')
findings.impact: Policy-driven credits accumulate against an agent's ledger without ever being tested against the limits that govern manual credits.

findings.title: comp:0 hard-blocks goodwill and every new code is created with it
findings.detail: compCheck rule 1 treats rc.comp===0 as an absolute block (except for OTHER_UNCODED), and 31 of the 40 seeded codes carry comp:0. addReasonCode creates every new code with comp:0, and there is no control anywhere in the UI to set or edit comp - the field is not rendered in the registry table at all.
findings.impact: Any code an operator adds through this panel silently forbids goodwill forever, and the only fix is editing the source file.

findings.title: Saving reason codes destroys tier inheritance for every code
findings.detail: renderReasonCodesTable pre-fills the First-response and Resolve inputs with tg.fr and tg.res - the RESOLVED values from rcTargets(), which substitute the tier default whenever the code stores null. saveReasonCodes then writes whatever is in the input back onto the record (rc[f]=inp.value===''?null:parseInt(...)). The first time anyone presses 'Save changes', every code that had been inheriting its tier default is saved with that number pinned as an explicit override, so later edits to the SLA tier table no longer move those codes.
findings.impact: One innocuous save silently converts all 40 codes from inherited to hard-coded SLA clocks, defeating the tier system the panel is built around.

findings.title: Reset deletes maxUploadMB and disables the upload size limit
findings.detail: DB.branding.maxUploadMB is assigned separately, later in the file, from the logo-upload block. resetBranding replaces the whole object with a 4-key literal that does not include it. Afterwards renderBrandingSettings interpolates undefined into the caption ('up to undefined MB') and handleLogoFile computes maxBytes = undefined*1024*1024 = NaN, so the guard f.size > NaN is always false.
findings.impact: One click on 'Reset to default' silently removes the 12 MB upload cap for the rest of the session and shows a broken caption.

findings.title: A negative data window is accepted and flags every account
findings.detail: The input carries min="1", but saveDataWindow only does parseInt(value,10)||13. A typed -5 parses to -5, which is truthy, so it is stored. windowStartMs() then returns nowMs() + a positive offset — a future timestamp — and windowSplit finds zero trips inside the window for every entity, making every account with a stored total an orphan. There is no upper bound either.
findings.impact: One bad entry turns the entire alert list red and would justify a mass history rebuild that is not needed.

findings.title: Reconstructed driver earnings use a hardcoded 20% commission
findings.detail: buildRiderHistory writes driverEarn:(fare*0.8).toFixed(2) on every generated trip. DB.rateCard.commission.onDemand is 22 (subscription is 20), so on-demand reconstructed earnings are systematically 2 percentage points high and ignore the rate card entirely.
findings.impact: Driver earnings figures derived from reconstructed history are wrong, and they feed the same profile surfaces the integrity tab exists to make trustworthy.

findings.title: The rebuild's fare model contradicts the live rate card
findings.detail: buildFareBreakdown hardcodes base 4.00, perKm 1.35, perMin 0.42. DB.rateCard.classes.economy is base 5.00, perKm 1.20, perMin 0.40 (comfort is 8.00 / 1.75 / 0.55). Every reconstructed receipt is therefore itemised under rates that never existed on the platform. The gate copy calls these 'the fare rules' as though they were the rate card.
findings.evidence:
function buildFareBreakdown(km,min,surge,seed){
  var base=4.00, perKm=1.35, perMin=0.42;
findings.impact: Reconstructed receipts are line-by-line auditable against a pricing model the business never used, which is worse than an unexplained total in a dispute.

findings.title: Undated trips are counted as inside the window
findings.detail: windowSplit treats a trip as inside the window when its dateMs is undefined OR is at or after the boundary. Seeded trips generally carry only a display date string and no dateMs; only reconstructed trips set it. Because the patched reconcileEntity defines orphan as (stored>0 && window.inside===0), any account holding even one undated seeded trip is reclassified from red 'no records' to amber 'window gap'.
findings.impact: The alert this tab exists to raise is suppressed for exactly the accounts most likely to have a broken import.

findings.title: Consent seeding always picks the oldest version, contradicting its own comment
findings.detail: getUserConsent() claims in the block comment above it to seed each user on 'the version that was live around when they joined', but the code reverses the versions array and unconditionally takes versions[0] — the OLDEST version. entity.joined is used only as the acceptedAt display string. Every seeded rider and driver therefore starts on v1.0 of everything while the current versions are 2.1 / 1.3 / 3.0.
findings.impact: All three document cards render a red 0% compliance badge from first paint, so the tab's headline number is meaningless and every user appears to need re-consent.

findings.title: No code path ever records a consent
findings.detail: The only write to entity.consents anywhere in the file is the lazy seed inside getUserConsent(). There is no 'record acceptance' function, no admin override and no simulated app-side acceptance, so isConsentCurrent can only ever go from true to false when a new version is published.
findings.impact: The compliance percentage is monotonically non-increasing; the re-consent workflow can never be completed inside the panel.

findings.title: 'Sent today' is a substring match, not a 24-hour window
findings.detail: The KPI filters on e.ts.indexOf(new Date().toLocaleString([],{month:'short',day:'numeric'})) >= 0 while its caption reads 'last 24 hours'. It depends on both calls producing the same locale fragment.
findings.impact: A displayed operational number is wrong for any locale whose formatting differs, and it is a calendar-day count rather than the rolling window it claims.

findings.title: 'Sent today' is a substring match, not a 24-hour window
findings.detail: The KPI filters p.ts with indexOf on the locale-formatted month/day while its caption reads 'last 24 hours'.
findings.impact: A displayed number contradicts its own label and breaks under a different browser locale.

findings.title: effectiveSurge() is dead code, so surge suspension changes no price
findings.detail: effectiveSurge is the only function that reads DB.surgeSuspensions or surge.capByCity into a multiplier, and it has zero call sites. The multiplier every live quote uses comes from currentSurgeMultiplier(), which reads DB.surgeConfig.capMultiplier (2.5) and DB.surgeSchedule instead.
findings.impact: The pane's stated safety lever — ops can suspend surge — records an audit entry and a row on screen while riders in that zone keep paying the same surge.

findings.title: Four-eyes approval is defeated by the acting-user switcher
findings.detail: approveRateCard blocks approval only when draft.proposedBy === CURRENT_USER_ID, and CURRENT_USER_ID is client state that the panel's own switch_user action changes.
findings.evidence: if(draft.proposedBy===CURRENT_USER_ID){toast('⛔ You proposed this card — a second person must approve it','warn');
findings.impact: The separation-of-duties control the guard dialog advertises can be bypassed by one person in two clicks.

findings.title: No permission check on any pricing action
findings.detail: proposeRateCard, approveRateCard and suspendSurge never call requirePerm or requirePagePerm; only guardAction confirmation dialogs stand in front of approve and suspend, and propose has neither. saveDataWindow (L20515) and setRotaSlot (L19671) in neighbouring tabs do gate on manage_settings.
findings.impact: Any operator who can open Settings can propose and publish a rate card or suspend surge, regardless of role.

findings.title: The rate card prices nothing outside its own tab
findings.detail: Greping every consumer of DB.rateCard, fareFor, planQuote, surgeCapFor and effectiveSurge shows readers only inside the pricing module (L21413-21775). Live quotes use DB.quickRideTypes with DB.surgeConfig/DB.surgeSchedule, subscription quotes fall back to DB.plans, and reconstructed history uses hardcoded literals in buildFareBreakdown.
findings.evidence: function currentSurgeMultiplier(){ var cfg=DB.surgeConfig; ... return Math.min(mult,cfg.capMultiplier||2.5); }
findings.impact: Four Economy per-km rates coexist (1.20 rate card, 1.10 quick-ride type, 1.10 plan template, 1.35 history reconstructor), so the tab's worked cost table does not describe what any rider is charged.

findings.title: The surge-suspension zone picker lists array indices, not zones
findings.detail: DB.zones is an array of {name,demand,supply,failures30d} objects, but openSuspendSurge builds its options with Object.keys(DB.zones||{}).slice(0,8), which on an array returns the index strings '0'..'5'. The fallback list ['RUH-CENTRAL','RUH-NORTH'] never fires because zones.length is 6.
findings.impact: Every suspension is recorded against a zoneId of '0'..'5', so the record identifies no real zone and the suspension list shows meaningless ids. The correct expression is DB.zones.map(z=>z.name).

findings.title: backfillFareLedger writes money collections with no permission gate
findings.detail: The button iterates every trip and calls postFareCapture, which writes DB.ledger through postLedger, DB.moneyRejects on a refused posting and DB.idempotency for every key. There is no requirePerm call, no GATE_SPECS entry and no guardAction registration for backfillFareLedger anywhere in the file.
findings.impact: A journal-writing operation on the money collections is available to anyone who can open the Settings page, with no confirmation step.

findings.title: fetchFullHistory writes payments with no permission check
findings.detail: fetchFullHistory sets window.__fetchFullHistory and calls buildRiderHistory(id), which materialises older trips and payments into the operational store for the session. It has a guardAction confirm dialog but no requirePerm.
findings.impact: Records are added to DB.payments for a customer on the say-so of anyone who can open a profile, with no role check and no cap.

findings.title: Half the money paths never post, so three accounts are structurally wrong
findings.detail: Driver payouts (L7034, L7055), escrow release (L7069), deductions (L7082), tips (L12450), credit-note issue and corporate invoicing do not post to the ledger. Only refunds, wallet credits and debits, emergency settlements and fare captures do.
findings.impact: liability.driver accrues from every driver_accrual and is never cleared, so the trial balance's captain payable is cumulative accrual rather than an outstanding obligation; liability.escrow and ar.rider are permanently zero.

findings.title: The refunds reconciliation row is permanently wrong and its fix is multiplied by zero
findings.detail: DB.refunds[].amount is gross while the refund journal entry books contra.refunds net of VAT and tax.vat_output separately. The reconciliation adds accountBalance('tax.vat_output')*0, which costs a full ledger walk and contributes nothing.
findings.impact: The pane's own honesty table shows a permanent difference of roughly the VAT rate on every refund, training operators to ignore the one number that is supposed to signal a real divergence.

findings.title: commitHandover has no permission gate
findings.detail: setRotaSlot opens with if(!requirePerm('manage_settings'))return;. commitHandover, on the same pane, calls no requirePerm at all: it unshifts a record into DB.handovers and, when the transfer checkbox is left checked (it is checked by default), rewrites ownerId, ownerName and touchedAtMs on every claim the current user holds, then refreshes the ownership surfaces across the panel. Its only gate is the guardAction confirm dialog, which is a UI confirmation, not an authorisation check.
findings.impact: Accountability for live work items can be reassigned - including to an invited, never-logged-in user - without any permission being held.

findings.title: The escalation tier never escalates
findings.detail: onCallName('secondary') maps to the 'escalation' tier but has zero call sites in the file; onCallName's only caller is the SLA breach notification at L14945, which always asks for 'primary'. There is no timeout that promotes a breach from primary to escalation and no fallback when the primary slot is empty - the notification simply carries the literal string '- NOBODY ON CALL -'. The escalation tier is populated, displayed and gap-checked, but nothing consumes it.
findings.impact: Half the rota - 21 of 42 slots that operators are asked to keep filled - has no effect on any escalation path.

findings.title: 135 of 161 action keys have no label, so the only structured filter reaches 14% of activity
findings.detail: ACTION_LABELS (L2898-L2911) defines exactly 26 keys, verified by reading the block. The doc's cross-check counts 220 literal logAction call sites using 161 distinct keys, leaving 135 unlabelled and 189 call sites (86%) unreachable. The action-type dropdown is built as Object.keys(ACTION_LABELS) at L9238 and is ACTION_LABELS' only consumer. config_updated alone has 40 call sites — more than the entire labelled set — and is absent. No label is orphaned: every one of the 26 has at least one call site.
findings.impact: Security events (change_password, toggle_2fa, log_out_session, impersonation_started/ended, session_started, toggle_page_permission), all money keys and all three GDPR erasure keys are unfilterable, and free-text search does not cover the action field.

findings.title: The 500-entry cap silently destroys history
findings.detail: L3148 sets DB.auditLog.length = 500, dropping the oldest entries with no warning, no indicator in the UI, no export prompt and no counter of what was lost. The page shows no sign that the log is capped.
findings.impact: Audit history is irrecoverably lost during exactly the busy periods that generate the most events, and settingsLastUpdated reverts to 'No changes recorded yet' when a section's entry ages out.

findings.title: The declared page permission for the activity log is never enforced
findings.detail: PAGE_PERMISSIONS['audit-log'] is declared at L10650 as {label:'Activity Log', icon:'🕵️', legacy:null, perms:[{key:'view', label:'View activity log'}]}, it is defaulted through defaultPagePerms and it is rendered as a grantable toggle in the permissions matrix. Grep for requirePagePerm('audit-log' returns zero hits, while 8+ other pages do call it (compliance, wallets, coverage, safety, growth).
findings.impact: Administrators can grant or revoke 'View activity log' in the permissions UI and nothing changes — every user can read the full log, including permission_denied and impersonation entries.

findings.title: Global search returns only the first hit and cannot search most entities by name
findings.detail: resolveId(raw) uppercases the query, then tries an exact key hit in riders, drivers, trips, subscriptions, payments and complaints in that fixed order, and falls back to a substring match on .name in riders and drivers only. Only the first match is returned and there is no disambiguation UI, no typeahead and no results list.
findings.evidence: buckets = ['riders','drivers','trips','subscriptions','payments','complaints']; fallback name search covers buckets[0] and buckets[1] only
findings.impact: Trips, subscriptions, payments and complaints are findable only by exact id. A rider key always shadows a same-named driver key with no way to reach the other record.

findings.title: No URL routing, hash or History API
findings.detail: window.go(id,el,isBack) is a show/hide switch. Navigation state lives only in the JS globals navStack and navCurrent. goBack() is an app-internal stack the browser's own Back button does not touch, so pressing browser Back leaves the app entirely.
findings.impact: Refresh always returns to dashboard. Deep links, bookmarking and browser back/forward are impossible; an operator cannot send a colleague a link to a record.

findings.title: Page `interventions` is unreachable — no `go('interventions')` call site exists
findings.detail: The page div, its `titles` entry, its `subs` entry, its router branch (`renderInterventionsPage()`) and its render function all exist, but nothing anywhere in the file calls `go('interventions')`, so a user can never navigate to it.
findings.impact: A fully built page (live trip interventions) ships as dead weight and its render path is never exercised.

findings.title: The impersonation bar covers the topbar it lives inside
findings.detail: #impersonation-bar is a child of .topbar but is position:fixed; top:0; left:0; right:0; z-index:80. #call-bar is the same pattern anchored bottom-right.
findings.impact: While impersonating, the amber banner obscures the page title, the back button and the global search box - exactly the controls an operator needs to get out of the impersonated session.

findings.title: The support page is dispatched twice on every navigation
findings.detail: Two separate if(id==='support') blocks exist in the go() dispatch chain. Both fire on the same navigation, running renderSupportTeam() plus renderTkFilterSelect(), renderTickets(), renderDisputes() and renderLostFound().
findings.impact: Five render functions run for one page visit; a future maintainer editing one block will not find the other.

findings.title: Unknown page id fails silently to a blank screen
findings.detail: go() removes .on from every .page, then adds .on to #p-<id> only if that element exists. An unknown id therefore shows nothing and sets the title to the raw id via titles[id]||id.
findings.evidence: add .on to #p-<id> if it exists (L8782-8783); #tb-title = titles[id] || id (L8785)
findings.impact: A routing typo produces a blank white screen with a lowercase slug in the title bar and no error anywhere.

findings.title: A legacy native-alert stub is still wired as a live confirm button
findings.detail: confirmModal() fires alert('Subscription confirmed and activated!') then closeModal(). It remains the confirm handler of openRenewModal (modal #17 of 99).
findings.evidence: function confirmModal(){alert('\u2705 Subscription confirmed and activated!');closeModal();}
findings.impact: The renew/upgrade flow ends in a browser alert and mutates nothing - the subscription is not actually renewed.

findings.title: A throwing gate builder silently removes its own gate
findings.detail: guardAction wraps the builder call in try/catch and sets spec=null on failure. A null spec is the documented signal for 'no gate needed', so the original function then runs unguarded.
findings.evidence: try{spec=builder(...)}catch(e){spec=null;}  // spec=null means the original runs unguarded
findings.impact: A bug anywhere in one of the 90 gate builders converts a confirmed destructive action into a one-click one, with no error surfaced.

findings.title: About 120 lines of Leaflet map code bind to an element that does not exist
findings.detail: grep for map-leaflet returns four hits, all outside the DOM: a CSS rule (L349), a comment (L11514), a getElementById (L11571) and an L.map() call (L11573). No id="map-leaflet" element exists in the markup. initLeafletMap() therefore returns at its guard, _lmap stays null forever, updateLiveMarkers() returns immediately, and TRIP_COORDS, TRIP_COLORS, carIcon(), mapBearing(), lerpPath(), _carMarkers, _routeLines and the flyToBounds selection code are unreachable. The source documents the removal itself at L11514-11520.
findings.evidence: var el = document.getElementById('map-leaflet');  // no such element exists anywhere in the markup
findings.impact: The tick engine calls updateLiveMarkers() every second to no effect, and a second OSM tile-layer URL is kept in the file but never fetched. The live map the operator actually sees is the dependency-free canvas renderer.

findings.title: Confirmation coverage is asymmetric between add and remove
findings.detail: addCustomGateway and addCustomLimit are confirm-gated in GATE_SWEEP, but removeGateway (L7507) and removeCustomLimit (L7421) are not in any registry and have no bespoke modal. Flagging an account goes through openFlagAccountModal while commitUnflagAccount (L9042) is one click. removeCity (L7890), removeRideType (L12368), removeEmployeeFromCorp (L6751) and removeAvatar (L2963) are likewise unconfirmed. All except removeAvatar do still check a broad permission and write an audit entry.
findings.impact: A misclick on a small danger button permanently deletes an operating city, a payment gateway or an operational limit with no undo, while the far less consequential add path asks for confirmation.

findings.title: Four modal-scoped intervals leak when the overlay is clicked
findings.detail: _rrTrackInterval (1000ms, L2509), _subTrackInterval (1000ms, L4791 and L5165) and _nsDispatch.interval (250ms, L4962) are cleared only by their own bespoke close handlers. closeModal() does not clear any of them.
findings.evidence: closeModal() removes .open and calls reqClearLocks() only - no interval cleanup
findings.impact: Dismissing one of these modals by clicking the scrim leaves a 250ms or 1000ms timer re-rendering into a removed DOM subtree for the rest of the session.

findings.title: Function `acceptPlanTerms()` is defined but never called
findings.detail: Defined at L17133 (6 lines). The identifier appears exactly once in the whole file — at its own definition — so no call site, onclick binding or string reference exists.
findings.impact: Unreachable logic that still has to be read and maintained; may be a feature that was wired up and then orphaned.

findings.detail: Defined at L21523 (8 lines). The identifier appears exactly once in the whole file — at its own definition — so no call site, onclick binding or string reference exists.
findings.impact: Unreachable logic that still has to be read and maintained; may be a feature that was wired up and then orphaned.

findings.detail: Defined at L19555 (13 lines). The identifier appears exactly once in the whole file — at its own definition — so no call site, onclick binding or string reference exists.
findings.impact: Unreachable logic that still has to be read and maintained; may be a feature that was wired up and then orphaned.

findings.title: guardAction monkey-patches globals, so captured references bypass the gate
findings.detail: guardAction replaces window[name] at load time and marks it __guarded. Installation is spread across five thousand lines: installActionGates() at L18089, installUniversalGates() at L18383, nine standalone calls, then installGateSweep() at L20903.
findings.evidence: Monkey-patches window[name]; marks window[name].__guarded = true; returns false if window[name] is not a function
findings.impact: Any code holding a reference to the original function captured before installation calls the ungated version. Install order is load-bearing and unenforced.

findings.title: No keyboard dismissal and no modal accessibility semantics
findings.detail: Verified: zero matches for Escape or keyCode in the whole file. The only keydown handlers are two Enter-to-search inputs (L571, L909). There is no role=dialog, no aria-modal, no focus trap and no focus restore.
findings.impact: A modal is dismissable only by mouse (overlay click, the X button or a footer button). Keyboard-only and screen-reader users are trapped, and tab order leaks into the page behind the scrim.

findings.title: Only one confirmation gate can be pending at a time
findings.detail: __confirmPending is a single module-global assigned by confirmAction(o). A second confirmAction call while one is pending overwrites it with no warning.
findings.impact: The first pending action is silently abandoned; runConfirm then executes the second action's onConfirm while the operator may believe they are confirming the first.

findings.title: The __guardToken re-entrancy window lets nested calls through ungated
findings.detail: __guardToken is set to the action name just before the original is invoked from onConfirm, so the wrapper lets it through once. A nested call to the same action inside that window also passes.
findings.evidence: __guardToken: re-entrancy token set to the action name just before the original function is invoked
findings.impact: A confirmed action that internally re-invokes itself performs the second mutation with no gate.

findings.title: The 1Hz tick engine never stops
findings.detail: startTickEngine() installs a 1000ms interval that is never cleared and has no page-visibility or idle pause. Every second it advances live trips, rolls Math.random() acceptance probabilities, mutates DB.rideRequests, fires toasts and notifications, and re-renders visible pages; modulo buckets add slaSweep (%15), refreshInbox (%20), markPresence (%30), liveSubtitles (%45) and a heavy %60 block that recomputes compliance and driver/rider tiers.
findings.evidence: TICK_ACCEL = 30 (L11952) - the demo clock advances about 30x real time
findings.impact: CPU burn and continuous DB mutation in a backgrounded tab; an operator returning after an hour finds a simulated world that moved on without them.

findings.title: The audit script that was supposed to enforce gate coverage does not exist
findings.detail: The GATE_SWEEP header comment describes extracting every onclick-reachable function, scanning its body for DB writes and comparing against the registry - finding 52 mutating actions firing on a single click, of which 7 were judged trivial and 45 were registered. It names audit_mut.js as the re-runnable deliverable that will fail the moment somebody adds an ungated action.
findings.evidence: header comment L20738-20754 names audit_mut.js as 'the deliverable'
findings.impact: The stated invariant is unenforced, and the 52/45/7 figures cannot be re-derived or confirmed current.

findings.title: Two render-blocking CDN assets serve one optional thumbnail
findings.detail: Leaflet CSS (L469) and Leaflet JS (L470) load from unpkg.com in <head> with no SRI hash, no crossorigin, no defer/async and no local fallback. Following #16, their only live consumer is the 200x110px city-picker preview map in Settings (showCityMapPreview, L7864-7875).
findings.impact: Roughly 150KB blocks first paint on every page view; a CDN outage or a CSP without unpkg.com degrades the panel. The code does guard with typeof L === 'undefined' at L7871, L11572 and L11580, so a failed load degrades rather than throws.

findings.title: 135 of 161 audit action keys are unlabelled and unfilterable
findings.detail: 220 real logAction() call sites use 161 distinct string-literal action keys (there are zero computed keys). ACTION_LABELS holds 26. Its only consumer is L9238, which builds the Activity Log 'All action types' dropdown. Audit rows themselves print e.summary verbatim, so a missing label does not break rendering - it makes the action invisible to the filter. Security-relevant unlabelled keys include impersonation_started, impersonation_ended, toggle_page_permission, change_password, toggle_2fa, log_out_session, erasure_executed, erasure_rejected, erasure_requested, account_suspended, auto_suspend, precaution_suspend, rate_card_self_approval_blocked, comp_blocked, edit_data_window, legal_version_published, history_rebuilt and config_updated (40 call sites, the highest-volume key in the file).
findings.impact: An auditor cannot filter for impersonation, permission changes, credential changes or GDPR erasure execution. Note the asymmetry: toggle_role_permission is labelled but its granular twin toggle_page_permission is not, so the two halves of the same permission screen are filterable and unfilterable respectively.

findings.title: Audit ids collide permanently once the 500-entry cap is reached
findings.detail: id is 'AUD-'+String(DB.auditLog.length+1).padStart(4,'0'), computed from the array length before the unshift. Once the array is pinned at 500 every subsequent entry receives AUD-0501. The Activity Log free-text search includes e.id in its haystack (L9330).
findings.impact: Audit ids stop being unique identifiers. Searching for a specific entry id after truncation returns an unbounded set, and any downstream system keying on the id would overwrite records.

findings.title: commitInvite creates structurally incomplete user records
findings.detail: The pushed object carries only id, name, email, role, lastLogin, status and permissions. It omits phone, photo, twoFA and pagePerms. Ids are 'USR-'+(length+1) with a collision-avoiding while loop at L10537. Starting permissions come from defaultPermissionsForRole, the intersection of every current holder of that role, which returns [] for a role with no holders.
findings.evidence: pushes {id,name,email,role,lastLogin,status,permissions} - no phone, no photo, no twoFA, no pagePerms
findings.impact: renderTeamTable reads u.twoFA as undefined and shows the red '2FA off' badge for every newly invited member regardless of reality, so the security column is misleading from the moment a user is created. avatarOrInitials and renderMaProfile do handle the missing fields correctly.

findings.title: manage_settings is a single-operator capability behind 30% of all guards
findings.detail: Verified distribution: manage_settings accounts for 39 of the 131 requirePerm call sites. Only USR-1 (Sarah Al-Rashid, Owner) holds it. The guarded surface includes cities, gateways, dispatch radius, operational limits, security policy, branding, legal version publication, the data-retention window, reason codes, SLA policy, the on-call rota, broadcast and push sending, and GDPR erasure execution and rejection.
findings.impact: If that one account is unavailable, no configuration change of any kind can be made by anyone - including the GDPR erasure execution path, which has a statutory clock. There is no second holder and no break-glass path other than the ungated avatar switch in finding #1.

findings.title: nm2() cannot resolve team-user ids, so impersonation audit summaries print raw ids
findings.detail: nm2(id) resolves DB.riders[id] || DB.drivers[id] only. Both impersonation summaries call it on a USR-* id: L21073 uses nm2(window.__realUserId) and L21084 uses nm2(CURRENT_USER_ID).
findings.evidence:
logAction('impersonation_started','permission',userId,
    nm2(window.__realUserId)+' began viewing the panel as '+u.name+' ('+u.role+')');
findings.impact: The one audit line that is supposed to name the real operator behind an impersonation prints 'USR-1 began viewing the panel as ...' instead of a human name.

findings.title: Plan-feature deletion and reordering are unconfirmed and unaudited
findings.detail: removePlanFeature(i) splices PLAN_FEATURES; pfDrop(e,i) reorders it with two splice calls. Neither calls logAction and removal has no confirmation dialog. The change is only recorded when savePlan (L6118, gated on manage_plans) subsequently logs save_plan.
findings.evidence: removePlanFeature(i) -> PLAN_FEATURES.splice(i,1) with no confirm and no logAction
findings.impact: Individual feature-bullet deletions are invisible in the audit trail; only the aggregate save is recorded, so it is impossible to tell who removed which commitment from a plan.

findings.title: Privileged read-modals open for anyone; only the commit is gated
findings.detail: viewUserPermissions (L10800), editTeamUser (L10468) and openInviteModal (L10502) have no permission check. Their commits - saveUserPermissions (L10814), commitEditTeamUser (L10485) and commitInvite (L10530) - each check manage_team.
findings.evidence: viewUserPermissions(userId) at L10800 - modal with 13 .tog checkboxes carrying data-perm, no guard
findings.impact: A Support user can open the invite modal, fill it in and click Send invite before being told they lack manage_team. The permission model is invisible until the last click, and the read-modal leaks the full permission set of any colleague to anyone.

findings.title: renderSidebarPerms is called twice but defined nowhere
findings.detail: Verified: a scan for 'function renderSidebarPerms(' across the whole file returns no match. It is called at L21075 (impersonate) and L21086 (stopImpersonating), both behind typeof guards.
findings.impact: Whatever sidebar permission refresh impersonation was meant to trigger never runs, so the sidebar keeps showing the pre-impersonation state - reinforcing the impression that nothing changed.

findings.title: Roles are derived from live data, so a role with no holders disappears
findings.detail: Roles are not first-class objects. renderRoleMatrix (L10753) and renderPagePermMatrix (L10718) build the column list by deduping DB.teamUsers.map(u=>u.role) at render time. TEAM_ROLES (L10501) declares four roles but is used only to populate the invite and edit selects. A cell is checked only when allHave is true, which requires usersWithRole.length>0 (L10761).
findings.evidence: renderRoleMatrix() and renderPagePermMatrix() derive the role list at render time from DB.teamUsers.map(u=>u.role) deduped
findings.impact: If the last holder of a role is edited to a different role, that role's column silently vanishes from both matrices and its permission set becomes unreachable through the UI. Combined with commitEditTeamUser deliberately not changing permissions on a role change, a user can end up displayed under a role whose matrix state nobody configured.

findings.title: Self-lockout attempts are blocked but not audited
findings.detail: toggleRolePermission (L10780) and saveUserPermissions (L10820) both refuse to let a user revoke their own manage_team. Both return early after a toast, with no logAction call - unlike requirePerm and requirePagePerm, which log permission_denied on every denial.
findings.evidence: L10780 and L10820 are policy blocks that toast only and write no audit entry
findings.impact: An attempted privilege self-destruction - a plausible precursor to or symptom of an account compromise - leaves no record at all, while ordinary permission denials do.

findings.title: The audit log is a 500-entry ring with silent truncation
findings.detail: logAction unshifts each entry then truncates: if(DB.auditLog.length>500)DB.auditLog.length=500. Oldest entries are dropped with no warning, no archive and no UI indication that truncation occurred. config_updated alone fires from 40 call sites.
findings.impact: A settings-heavy session can push genuine security events - a permission grant, an impersonation, an erasure execution - off the end of the log, and neither the operator nor an auditor is told anything was lost.

findings.title: The two identity-switch mechanisms do not cooperate
findings.detail: Mechanism A (commitUserSwitch, from the avatar) never sets window.__realUserId and never calls renderImpersonationBar(). Mechanism B (impersonate, from the Settings team row) does both. The bar's visibility guard at L21039 only checks __realUserId !== CURRENT_USER_ID.
findings.evidence: commitUserSwitch reassigns CURRENT_USER_ID and updates 3 DOM nodes; it never touches window.__realUserId or renderImpersonationBar()
findings.impact: An avatar switch produces no amber banner and no 'Back to my account' affordance - the operator is silently someone else with no visible indicator and no return path except a page reload. Using the avatar switch while already impersonating leaves __realUserId pointing at a third party, so the banner stays visible but names the wrong return target.

findings.title: applyLanguage uses textContent, irreversibly flattening inline markup
findings.detail: L7949 caches el.textContent as the 'English original' and L7951 assigns el.textContent. Any translated element containing child markup is flattened on the FIRST Arabic toggle and can never be restored, because the cache already captured the flattened text. Two confirmed victims: L1992 sec.planned_title whose source is 'Planned Coming soon', and L1502 gen.disclaimer which contains really does translate.
findings.impact: After one language toggle the 'Coming soon' badge disappears permanently and the disclaimer explaining the translation feature loses its emphasis — the element that explains the feature is broken by the feature.

findings.title: Arabic plan data is mandatory to enter and impossible to see
findings.detail: savePlan refuses to save without nameAr (validation at L6125, toast '⚠ Both English and Arabic names are required') and validatePlanFeatures refuses without every features[].ar (L6053). Both fields round-trip only through their own editor inputs (L6070, L6015) and into audit diffs (L6126, L6146). Neither has a single user-facing render site — no table, card, list, dropdown, receipt or export displays them; the plans table and every subscription string uses plan.name.
findings.evidence: PLAN_FEATURES module default and DB.plans seeds carry .ar strings at L2891/L2893/L2895 and L5993-L5995, read only back into their own inputs
findings.impact: Operators are compelled to produce translations that no screen in the panel — English or Arabic — will ever display.

findings.title: Nothing is number-, date- or currency-localised
findings.detail: Intl., NumberFormat, DateTimeFormat, RelativeTimeFormat and PluralRules each return zero matches. The single money formatter is fmtSAR(n){return n.toFixed(2)+' SAR';} at L4394 with 92 call sites — no separators, no symbol, no locale, always LTR-suffixed. Of 19 toLocale* call sites, 8 hard-pin 'en-GB', 10 pass [] (the viewer's browser locale) and 1 passes nothing; not one derives its locale from DB.opsConfig.general.language. toFixed appears 248 times and is locale-blind by definition; Arabic-Indic digits appear 0 times.
findings.impact: The same panel shows different date formats to different operators depending on their OS locale, never follows its own language setting, and renders 1234567.50 SAR without separators.

findings.title: The doc's 'seven orphan dictionary keys' finding is contradicted by the source
findings.detail: The doc (§4.2B, F5) asserts that stabgrp.daily_ops, .money, .people, .comms, .platform, .records and .other are dead data evidencing an abandoned refactor. In fact SETTINGS_GROUPS (L21270-L21277) carries an i18nKey per group and reorderSettingsTabs() (L21278, called from presenceBoot at L21393, itself registered in the boot sweep at L21825) creates a header element per group and sets data-i18n from that key at L21296. Six of the seven keys are therefore live and translatable, because applyLanguage re-queries document.querySelectorAll('[data-i18n]') on every call and the boot sweep runs synchronously before the setTimeout that calls applyLanguage at L14596. Only stabgrp.other (L21307) stays unused, because SETTINGS_GROUPS covers all 21 tabs so the leftovers branch never fires. The doc's related claim that 'no JS string literal emits a data-i18n attribute' is narrowly true only because these use setAttribute rather than string concatenation.
findings.impact: A future translator reading the doc would delete six dictionary keys that are actually rendering the live settings rail group headers.

findings.title: The language choice is never persisted
findings.detail: localStorage, sessionStorage, setItem, getItem, indexedDB and document.cookie all return zero matches across the whole file. The language lives only in DB.opsConfig.general.language, an object literal re-seeded to 'en' at L2570 on every load and re-applied at boot by L14596. The in-product copy acknowledges this limitation for the LOGO (gen.logo_note, L1511) but never mentions that the same applies to language.
findings.impact: Choosing Arabic flips the sidebar immediately, but any refresh, any new tab and any other person opening the file lands back in English with no warning.

findings.title: Translation coverage is 86 of 621 static elements and 1 of 41 page shells
findings.detail: Verified by grep: exactly 86 data-i18n occurrences with 86 unique keys, 39 in the sidebar and 47 in p-settings. Forty of the 41 page shells carry none. Every visible surface built by innerHTML string concatenation is structurally unreachable by the applyLanguage loop, which only ever queries the static DOM. The panel's own disclaimer at L1502 declares this scope, so it is an acknowledged limit rather than an undiscovered defect — but the running application is effectively 0% translated.
