findings.impact: An Arabic operator sees an Arabic left rail attached to a wholly English application; Arabic mode is a navigation label set, not a usable Arabic interface.

findings.title: 'New riders (48h)' applies no time filter
findings.detail: The tile value is (DB.newRiders||[]).length — the raw length of a hand-seeded three-element array. Nothing anywhere windows the array to 48 hours.
findings.impact: A KPI labelled with a time window reports an unbounded total; the number will never decay.

findings.title: Both trend charts are drawn from fabricated snapshots
findings.detail: DB.dailySnapshots is 30 pre-fabricated rows (SNAP-0001 26 Jun through SNAP-0030 25 Jul) with invented totalRevenue/quickRideRevenue/subRevenue strings, while the caption under the charts claims 'From captured Daily Snapshots'.
findings.impact: The revenue trend an executive reads is demo data presented as captured history.

findings.title: cityStats() hardcodes 'Riyadh'
findings.detail: cityStats(name) returns real zone/driver/rider counts only when the name is exactly 'Riyadh'; every other city returns {zones:0,drivers:0,riders:0}. The same string is hardcoded a second time in renderExecOverview for the fail-rate column, and zonesForCity is assigned all of DB.zones unconditionally with an inline comment saying every zone is assumed to be in the seed city.
findings.impact: Adding a fifth city, or renaming Riyadh, silently produces all-zero rows in the Cities & regions health table.

findings.title: Escrow held excludes 'ready' holds
findings.detail: escrowHeld counts only DB.escrowHolds entries with status==='held'. The shipped seed contains two 'ready' holds worth 329.60 and 32.98 SAR that never appear on the card.
findings.impact: Money genuinely held by the platform is missing from the executive escrow figure.

findings.title: Page renders empty at boot
findings.detail: The boot setTimeout block calls renderExecTrendChart() but not renderExecOverview(); the router branch is the only caller of renderExecOverview. If exec-overview were ever the initially visible page, the KPI strip, both tables and all lists would be blank.
findings.impact: A first-paint of this page without navigation shows charts but no numbers.

findings.title: 'Renewal due soon' half of the payment-risk rule is never evaluated
findings.detail: The card caption promises 'Prior declined attempt + renewal due soon', but membership is purely DB.paymentRisk key presence plus the first non-cancelled subscription for that rider. The subscription's ends date is displayed but never tested.
findings.impact: Riders are flagged as renewal-payment risks months before any renewal is due.

findings.title: DB.paymentRisk is a single hardcoded literal
findings.detail: DB.paymentRisk is declared as one object literal with one rider key and never written to anywhere in the file. It is the sole input to the Renewal-payment-risk card, the -20 payment-risk deduction in subHealthScore, and one of the three terms of KPI 1.
findings.evidence: DB.paymentRisk={'RDR-1041':'Prior renewal attempt declined once (card ···4821) before succeeding on retry'};
findings.impact: A whole card and part of a headline KPI are demo scaffolding with no production data path.

findings.title: KPI 'At-risk drivers' and the driver table describe different populations
findings.detail: The KPI counts every driver with driverRiskScore < 80; the table lists every driver with at least one reason. Signal 5b (outstanding cash debt, not blocked) appends a reason with a zero deduction, so a driver can appear in the table at score 100 without being counted by the KPI. The reverse cannot happen, so the table is a strict superset.
findings.impact: The headline count and the list below it disagree, with no explanation on screen.

findings.title: Loyalty-offer email has no deliverable rider address
findings.detail: The offer branch calls sendSystemEmail(sub.rider, ...), which resolves emailFor(toId). Seeded rider records carry no email property at all — only drivers, team users and inbound-message records do — so the outbox entry records toEmail '—'.
findings.impact: The one retention action that claims to contact the rider produces an undeliverable outbox record.

findings.title: Open-issue deduction is unbounded
findings.detail: driverRiskScore subtracts 15 per open dispute or incident with no cap, so seven open issues alone floor the score at 0 regardless of documents, suspension or cash state.
findings.impact: One noisy driver dominates the availability ranking and masks the reasons behind the score.

findings.title: parseShortDate hardcodes the year 2026
findings.detail: parseShortDate matches a day and a three-letter month and returns new Date(2026, mon, day). A subscription whose started/ends pair crosses into 2027 produces ends < started, the ends>started guard fails and the behind-expected-pace signal is silently skipped.
findings.impact: The most heavily weighted churn signal (-25) silently stops firing for year-crossing plans.

findings.title: Payment-risk rows take only the first matching subscription
findings.detail: For each flagged rider the code uses .find() over non-cancelled subscriptions, so a rider holding two active plans contributes one row and one subscription id.
findings.impact: Payment risk on a rider's second active subscription is invisible.

findings.title: Repeat-incident tally ignores status and never decays
findings.detail: The tally counts every DB.disputes and DB.incidents entry keyed on x.against regardless of status, with no time window — unlike the Plan Commitment module which has counterWindowDays and decayDays. Nothing constrains the key to be a driver id, and the seeded incident INC-013 with against:null is skipped.
findings.impact: A driver whose incidents were all resolved a year ago stays permanently flagged as a repeat-pattern risk.

findings.title: Retention actions are not idempotent and leave no trace on the record
findings.detail: commitRetentionAction never mutates the subscription. The health score, band and the 'Retention action' button are unchanged afterwards and no re-render is triggered, so the same button can be pressed repeatedly, each press writing a fresh audit line, a fresh bell notification and (for 'offer') a fresh email.
findings.impact: Duplicate outreach to the same rider with no 'already actioned' badge or cooldown.

findings.title: totalSignals is computed and never read
findings.detail: A multi-line expression tallies disputes and incidents through a nested IIFE and then runs the result through .filter(function(k){return true;}) — a literal no-op — assigning to totalSignals, which no later line references. KPI 1 uses a different expression on line 14378.
findings.impact: Wasted work on every render and a misleading variable that suggests a KPI it does not feed.

findings.title: Collision audit omits pending applicants and team users
findings.detail: identityCollisions() indexes only DB.riders and DB.drivers. DB.pendingDrivers, DB.teamUsers and DB.inboundMessages are never indexed — and DB.teamUsers holds the only duplicate email in the whole file.
findings.impact: A pending applicant reusing an existing driver's phone is not caught, which is the case the pre-migration audit most needs.

findings.title: device is a model string, not a fingerprint
findings.detail: Rider and driver device values are of the form 'iPhone 15 · iOS 17.5'. The referral rule flags a pair when a.device === b.device, so two unrelated people on the same phone model and OS version match. The seed data already contains such a pair across collections (RDR-2031 and DRV-0106).
findings.impact: False self-abuse flags against unrelated riders, each carrying a one-click suspend button.

findings.title: Identity collisions are excluded from every count
findings.detail: totalFlags sums only the three renderFraudPage signals, and the KPI row has no collision card. A cross-role collision — described in-product as the one that breaks dispatch because an event keyed on an ambiguous identity can reach the wrong client — contributes nothing to the KPIs or the sidebar badge.
findings.impact: The highest-stakes signal on the page is invisible to anyone scanning counts.

findings.title: No PAGE_PERMISSIONS entry for the fraud page
findings.detail: The PAGE_PERMISSIONS map covers subscriptions, coverage, compliance, safety, growth, zones, predictive, finance, wallets, plans, support, settings and audit-log but has no fraud key, so canPage('fraud', anything) is always false and defaultPagePerms() never generates grants for it. Nothing on the page calls requirePagePerm('fraud',…), so this is inert today, but the Settings permission matrix offers no row for the page and the only enforcement is the broad approve_drivers check inside commitSuspendAccount.
findings.impact: The page cannot be granted or revoked per role; suspension is gated only by a permission borrowed from driver approval.

findings.title: Pairing rule has no baseline or normalisation
findings.detail: The caption promises pairs riding together 'far more than random chance would suggest', but the rule is an absolute count of >= 3 shared trips with no comparison against either party's total volume. A driver with three lifetime trips all with one rider is treated identically to one with 300 trips of which 3 were with that rider. It is also asymmetric: it iterates drivers and counts riders, so a rider's own total is never consulted.
findings.impact: New drivers are systematically over-flagged and high-volume drivers under-flagged.

findings.title: Referral self-abuse offers no action against the referrer
findings.detail: DB.referralLog records both a referrerBonus and a refereeBonus, but the flagged row renders a Suspend button only for the referee. The referrer is a link only, and there is no control to claw back either bonus or void the referral.
findings.impact: The party who profits most from self-referral abuse cannot be acted on from the detection surface.

findings.title: Suspending navigates away and never re-renders the page
findings.detail: commitSuspendAccount calls openProfile(entityId,true) and refreshes the Drivers or Riders table but never calls renderFraudPage(), so the flag list the operator was working through is both left behind and left stale.
findings.impact: Clearing a list of flagged accounts requires re-entering the page after every single action.

findings.title: The 'Shared device / IP' card never reads device
findings.detail: The card title, its caption and all four detected-reason strings say device/IP, but the grouping key is r.lastIp alone. r.device is never read in this block — only the referral rule reads it.
findings.impact: A shared device on two different networks is not detected, despite the card claiming to cover it.

findings.title: 'Today' is hardcoded in three independent places
findings.detail: renderDashboard filters trips with (t.date||'').indexOf('25 Jun')===0, the renewal pipeline declares var today=25 separately, and the refunds chip filters r.date==='25 Jun'. None reads REQ_NOW_REF or the wall clock. The page header additionally hardcodes 'Thursday 25 Jun 2026 — Good morning, Sarah', with the operator name not read from meUser()/CURRENT_USER_ID.
findings.impact: The whole page is pinned to one demo day and greets every operator as Sarah.

findings.title: Cancellation cap alert uses the weekly cap for every rider
findings.detail: The alert compares each rider's cancelled trips today against DB.plans.weekly.cap (=1) regardless of which plan the rider is actually on; the bi-weekly cap of 2 and the monthly cap are ignored.
findings.impact: Riders on longer plans are flagged as cap-breached when they are within their allowance.

findings.title: No permission gate on the default landing page
findings.detail: requirePerm is never invoked from renderDashboard or from any of the page's inline handlers. Gating happens only downstream — commitNewSub checks manage_subscriptions and commitRequestAssign checks live_ops — so any signed-in operator sees today's revenue chip, alert queue, intervention feed and renewal pipeline.
findings.impact: Operational and financial summary data is visible to every role by default.

findings.title: priorityCall is passed a display name where an entity id belongs
findings.detail: The renewal-risk alert calls priorityCall(nm2(sb.rider)) — a name — and leaves the third parameter (entityId) undefined, so logPriorityCall records entityId||name and the audit entry is keyed by a display name rather than an id. This is the exact defect the file's own audit note describes for the Renewal page; it survives here.
findings.impact: Priority-call audit entries cannot be reliably joined back to the rider record.

findings.title: refreshOwnershipSurfaces guards on an undefined function
findings.detail: The dashboard/interventions branch of refreshOwnershipSurfaces tests typeof renderInterventions==='function'. A file-wide grep finds that identifier at exactly one line — this one; only renderInterventionsPage exists. The typeof guard swallows the miss silently.
findings.impact: Claiming, releasing or taking over a work item never refreshes the dashboard's intervention feed.

findings.title: Two conflicting health colour band sets
findings.detail: openHealthBreakdown colours a renewal health score green at >=70 and amber at >=40; healthBand (used by the Predictive page) uses >=80 Healthy and >=50 At risk. A score of 45 is red in the modal but 'At risk' amber elsewhere; 75 is green in the modal but 'At risk' elsewhere.
findings.impact: The same subscription reads as two different severities depending on which surface an operator opens.

findings.title: Two divergent intervention counts
findings.detail: #dash-intervene-count is buildInterventionItems().length — SLA tickets plus ride requests plus upcoming sub-trips filtered by a 60-minute cut-off. The sidebar badge #sbb-dash is computed by refreshNavCounts as DB.rideRequests.length plus every unassigned/unavailable/late upcoming trip with no time filter. The two numbers will normally disagree.
findings.impact: The sidebar and the card on the page it links to show different urgency counts.

findings.title: Item actions are executed via new Function() string eval
findings.detail: inboxOpen evaluates the item's action string through new Function(). Every action string is assembled internally from DB record ids with no escaping applied, so a record id containing a quote produces a syntax error that is swallowed by the catch and silently degrades to a generic go().
findings.impact: A string-eval path over unescaped record ids is a latent injection surface, and its failure mode is a silent wrong navigation rather than an error.

findings.title: KPI tiles ignore both the tab and the role filter
findings.detail: All four KPI tiles are computed from the unfiltered inboxItems() set, so they always describe the whole system rather than the list the operator is looking at.
findings.impact: The headline numbers and the list below them can describe different populations, so an operator cannot reconcile the tile with what they see.

findings.title: No inbox action is permission-gated
findings.detail: requirePerm() never appears anywhere in the ownership or inbox blocks (L18828-L19321). Claim, release, take over and close-the-whole-case all mutate DB.ownership and DB.cases without any permission check.
findings.evidence: function claimItem(type,id,silent){ var me=meUser(), k=ckey(type,id), cur=whoHolds(type,id);
findings.impact: Any signed-in user can seize or release work another operator is holding, and can close an entire correlated case, with no permission control.

findings.title: Opening an item silently claims it
findings.detail: inboxOpen calls claimItem(type,id,true) when the item is unheld. The silent flag suppresses only the toast - the claim and its claim_taken audit entry are still written. The source comment at L19299-L19300 states this is deliberate, but there is no view-only affordance anywhere in the module.
findings.impact: An operator glancing at a queue removes work from the unassigned pool without realising it, and colleagues see it as taken.

findings.title: Ownership and cases are seeded empty while the default tab is Mine
findings.detail: DB.ownership and DB.cases are initialised as empty objects and _inboxTab defaults to 'mine', so a fresh load always opens on the 'You are not holding anything' empty state even when the queues contain work.
findings.impact: The module's first impression is an empty screen, hiding the work it exists to surface.

findings.title: Rendering the inbox mutates ownership state and writes audit rows
findings.detail: whoHolds() auto-releases any claim untouched for longer than DB.ownershipConfig.staleMin (30 minutes) and writes a claim_expired audit entry as a side effect of being read. renderInbox calls it up to three times per item per render and the tick engine re-renders on a 20-tick cadence.
findings.impact: A pure read path writes to DB and the audit log, so the audit trail records expiries at whatever moment a render happened to touch the record rather than when they occurred.

findings.title: Sidebar badge uses logical OR instead of addition
findings.detail: updateInboxBadge computes n = breachedCount, falling back to unclaimedCount only when the first is zero. As soon as a single item is breached the unclaimed count stops being reported entirely, so the number silently changes meaning while the only visual cue is the a/n class swap.
findings.impact: The sidebar count means two different things depending on state, so operators cannot learn to trust it.

findings.title: Tab counts are computed from the unfiltered item set
findings.detail: The three tab labels take their counts from all = inboxItems() (L19242-L19245) while the rows rendered underneath come from inboxFiltered(), which additionally applies the role filter. A tab can therefore read 'Everything . 9' and render zero rows.
findings.impact: The operator is told there is work waiting that the list refuses to show, with no explanation of the discrepancy.

findings.title: The my-work chip navigates to the wrong page
findings.detail: #my-work-chip reads '<n> mine', is maintained by updateMyWorkChip() in the inbox module and is titled 'Items you are holding right now', but its onclick is go('support',null).
findings.evidence: 0 mine
findings.impact: The one global affordance for 'show me what I am holding' takes the operator to a queue that is only one of the twelve sources.

findings.title: Two independent work builders over overlapping data
findings.detail: inboxItems() and the dashboard's buildInterventionItems() read overlapping sources but share no code. Instant ride requests never enter the inbox, and lost-and-found, PDPL erasure and coverage items never enter the dashboard intervention feed.
findings.impact: The two 'what needs attention now' surfaces disagree, so neither can be treated as complete.

findings.title: Alert and complaint types have no click destination
findings.detail: handleNotifClick routes only ticket, approval, renewal and payout. The type 'alert' is the most common runtime type (16 producers) and depends entirely on its action closure; the seed records N1 (alert) and N6 (complaint) carry no action, so clicking them marks read and nothing else happens.
findings.evidence: else if(n.type==='ticket')go('support',null); else if(n.type==='approval')go('drivers',null); else if(n.type==='renewal')go('renewal',null); else if(n.type==='payout')go('wallets',null);
findings.impact: Clicking the highest-priority category of notification can be a dead end with no feedback that nothing happened.

findings.title: DB.notifications grows without bound
findings.detail: There is no size cap and no eviction, in contrast to DB.contacts which is trimmed to 2000 at L14933. tickEngine runs every second and every toast in the panel mirrors into the array, while the full page renders every record into a single innerHTML assignment.
findings.impact: A long-running session degrades the page render and the bell count without limit.

findings.title: Live Map filter chips clear the notification page's chip highlight
findings.detail: setNotifFilter correctly scopes its chip reset to '#p-notifications-all .map-fchip', but the Live Map's setMapFilter uses an unscoped document.querySelectorAll('.map-fchip') and calls classList.toggle('on', c.getAttribute('data-filt')===val). The notification chips carry no data-filt attribute, so getAttribute returns null, the comparison is false and their on class is removed.
findings.impact: After using the map filters, the notifications page (and the Requests page) shows no selected chip while _notifPageFilter still holds the old value, so the visible state contradicts the applied filter.

findings.title: markAllRead mutates DB with no permission gate
findings.detail: markAllRead writes to every record in DB.notifications on a single click and is absent from the gateAll registry, whose header comment claims every function reachable from an onclick was extracted and its body scanned for writes to DB.
findings.impact: A DB-mutating action escaped the permission sweep the file claims is exhaustive, so the registry cannot be trusted as complete.

findings.title: No audit trail for reading or clearing notifications
findings.detail: There is no logAction call anywhere in the notification module (L2171-L2327). Neither markAllRead nor handleNotifClick records who dismissed what or when.
findings.impact: A critical safety or suspension alert can be cleared by anyone with no trace, so there is no way to establish whether it was seen.

findings.title: Notification title and description are injected as raw HTML
findings.detail: notifRowHtml interpolates n.title and n.desc into an innerHTML string with no escaping. Toast-derived entries carry the toast's msg verbatim, which is itself rendered as HTML by the toast helper.
findings.impact: Inert while all data is local mock data, but a real XSS surface the moment any notification string derives from user input.

findings.title: The bell badge is priority-blind
findings.detail: updateBellBadge counts every unread record equally, so the priority triage the whole module is built around never reaches the one number an operator actually watches.
findings.impact: A stack of low-priority toast confirmations is visually indistinguishable from a stack of critical SOS alerts.

findings.title: The full page never live-updates
findings.detail: pushOpsNotification refreshes the dropdown only when it is already open and never calls renderAllNotificationsPage, even though markAllRead and handleNotifClick both include the classList.contains('on') re-render guard. tickEngine produces notifications every second.
findings.impact: An operator watching the notifications page sees a stale list and must click a filter chip or leave and re-enter to discover new critical alerts.

findings.title: #live-last-update is permanently empty
findings.detail: The only writer of #live-last-update is updateLiveMarkers(), which is dead. Grep finds the element referenced at exactly two places: its markup at L775 and the dead writer at L11582.
findings.impact: The freshness indicator next to 'Live tracking' never shows a time, so the operator has no signal that the view is stale.

findings.title: cancelRequest deletes a ride request with no confirmation
findings.detail: cancelRequest is permission-gated and audited but splices the record straight out of DB.rideRequests on a single click, with no confirm dialog - unlike the live-trip cancel path, which requires a second modal.
findings.evidence: if(!requirePerm('live_ops'))return; var idx=DB.rideRequests.findIndex(function(x){return x.id===id;}); if(idx<0)return; var r=DB.rideRequests[idx]; DB.rideRequests.splice(idx,1);
findings.impact: A misclick on a dense sidebar row destroys a pending rider request irrecoverably, with only a toast as feedback.

findings.title: logDriverCall changes state without writing an audit entry
findings.detail: Logging an urgent driver call sets t.driverStatus to 'moving' or 'unavailable' (with unavailReason 'Declined trip after call') and can auto-open resolveUnavailable, but writes no logAction entry - unlike logPriorityCall, commitAddStop, assignNearestDriver and every other state-changing action on this page.
findings.impact: Marking a captain unavailable - the trigger for a replacement dispatch - leaves no audit record of who did it or why.

findings.title: setMapFilter's chip reset is not scoped to this page
findings.detail: setMapFilter iterates document.querySelectorAll('.map-fchip') across the whole document and toggles the on class by comparing data-filt to the clicked value. The class is shared by the Notifications page chips (L1177-L1182) and the Requests page chips (L2092-L2097), neither of which has a data-filt attribute, so their on class is stripped. Both of those modules scope their own resets correctly.
findings.impact: Using the map filters silently desynchronises the visible chip selection on two other pages from the filter state they are actually applying.

findings.title: The entire Leaflet/OSM layer is unreachable
findings.detail: L11526-L11635 implements a full Leaflet map: TRIP_COORDS, TRIP_COLORS, carIcon, initLeafletMap, updateLiveMarkers, showHistoryRoute and renderLiveMap. renderLiveMap has no callers and initLeafletMap is called only from renderLiveMap. updateLiveMarkers (called from tickEngine) and showHistoryRoute (called from selectTrip) both return immediately because _lmap is null. The element they bind to, #map-leaflet, exists only as an orphan CSS rule at L349.
findings.impact: Roughly 110 lines of map code, seven sets of real Riyadh coordinates and two CDN assets are carried for a feature that cannot execute.

findings.title: The stats bar shows the history-selected trip while in Live mode
findings.detail: setMapMode('live') calls updateMapStats(), which reads DB.trips[activeTrip]. activeTrip defaults to TRP-7741 and is only ever changed by history-side interactions, so the Live view shows a specific historical trip's driver, distance, duration and on-time verdict beneath a 'Live tracking' banner.
findings.impact: Static historical figures are presented in a context that implies they are live.

findings.title: Toasts claim the rider was notified when nothing was sent
findings.detail: commitLiveReassign toasts 'rider notified' and sendRiderChangeNotif toasts 'Rider notified' with no sendSystemEmail or pushOpsNotification call in either path. By contrast commitAddStop does call sendSystemEmail.
findings.impact: Operators are told a customer communication went out when none did, so nobody follows up.

findings.title: Trips created during the session have no map presence
findings.detail: commitRequestAssign and driverAcceptOffer push new live trips with mapTrip null and a random id of the form TRP-91xx, which is absent from MAP_ROUTES. focusLiveTrip therefore always warns and drawMap draws no dot for them.
findings.impact: Every trip created after load is invisible on the map and untrackable, so the map only ever reflects the three seeded trips.

findings.title: 'At risk' status filter can never match
findings.detail: The status filter offers an 'At risk' option but no code path anywhere assigns status='At risk'. At risk exists only as a computed Health value derived from hasOpenComplaint, which is not stored and not filterable.
findings.impact: Selecting the filter always shows the empty state, implying there are no at-risk subscriptions when the Health column may show several.

findings.title: 'Auto-reassigns after 2:00' is display text only
findings.detail: The dispatch UI renders a note promising automatic reassignment after two minutes, but sendSubDispatchRequest has no auto-reassign timeout - the poll only resolves accept or decline at respondInSec.
findings.impact: Ops trust a safety net that does not exist and may leave a stalled request unattended.

findings.title: cancelSubDispatch aborts a dispatch silently
findings.detail: Cancelling an in-flight subscription dispatch clears the interval, nulls _nsDispatch and closes the modal. There is no toast, no audit entry and no record that a driver was sent a request and then abandoned.
findings.impact: A driver who was pinged and then dropped leaves no trace, so repeated abandoned requests against one driver are invisible to ops.

findings.title: changeDriver defaults to a hardcoded subscription id
findings.detail: changeDriver(subId) begins by defaulting subId to 'SUB-1041' - a leftover from the removed hardcoded p-sub-detail page.
findings.impact: Any future call site that omits the argument silently opens the change-driver flow against an unrelated real subscription.

findings.title: Duplicated needsApproval branch in finalizeNewSub
findings.detail: finalizeNewSub contains two identical if(needsApproval){...return;} blocks back to back; the first always returns, so the second is unreachable.
findings.impact: Dead code that will diverge on the next edit to the approval-hold path, since a maintainer may change only one copy.

findings.title: Export ignores the active filters
findings.detail: exportRows('subscriptions') always maps Object.keys(DB.subscriptions) in full; the plan, vehicle and status filters that shaped the on-screen table are not consulted.
findings.impact: A user looking at three filtered rows and clicking Export CSV silently receives every subscription in the system.

findings.title: Granular subscription permission keys are declared but unenforced
findings.detail: The permission registry declares subscriptions.{view, change_driver, settle} with legacy:'manage_subscriptions', but every call site in this module checks only the legacy string. Whether can() internally maps the granular keys was not resolvable from the call sites read.
findings.impact: A role intended to view subscriptions but not settle them gets both, or neither, depending on the legacy key alone.

findings.title: Modal openers are ungated; only commits check permission
findings.detail: freezePlan, cancelSub, changeDriver and renderNewSubModal all open freely; the requirePerm('manage_subscriptions') gate lives on doFreeze, confirmCancelSub, commitDriverChange and commitNewSub. openSettlement is the sole exception, gated at open.
findings.impact: A permissionless user can fill in an entire destructive modal before being blocked, and learns the full shape of the flow.

findings.title: Profile trip log sorts lexicographically, not chronologically
findings.detail: buildSubProfile sorts the trip log with localeCompare over date labels of the form '25 Jun 07:00'. String order puts '5 Jul' before '25 Jun' and orders months alphabetically.
findings.impact: The trip history on a subscription profile is presented as newest-first but is not, which misleads anyone reconstructing what happened in a dispute.

findings.title: Seeded subscriptions lack the scheduling schema
findings.detail: None of the 7 seeded subscriptions carry days, departTime, direction, route, perTripFare or startOutcome - fields only written by finalizeNewSub. evaluateSubStart returns immediately, directionArrows falls through to one-way and the corporate geo check reads an undefined sub.route.
findings.impact: Every scheduling, direction and geo-policy feature is silently inert for the entire seeded dataset, so those paths are never exercised on first open.

findings.title: Settlement audit before-state is falsified
findings.detail: The logAction call hardcodes {status:'Active'} as the before payload no matter what the real prior status was, so settling an Expiring, Frozen or Pending Approval package records a transition that never happened.
findings.impact: The audit trail cannot be trusted to reconstruct a subscription's lifecycle, which is exactly what an early-termination dispute would need.

findings.title: sub.postponements has no writer
findings.detail: buildSubProfile renders a full Postponed-trips banner keyed on d.postponements, but no function in the file ever assigns that field. The doc marks this UNVERIFIED as to whether an external or removed flow populated it.
findings.impact: A whole rendering path is unreachable, so postponement history is invisible even if it were recorded elsewhere.

findings.title: A zero cap or zero radius is stored as no restriction
findings.detail: saveCorpUsagePolicy coerces the numeric policy fields with parseFloat(...) || null, so a deliberate 0 collapses to null - which every consumer reads as 'no limit'. The inputs advertise min=0.
findings.impact: An operator who sets a 0 SAR cap to freeze a company's spend actually removes the cap entirely.

findings.title: corp-detail has no router render hook
findings.detail: window.go handles corporate only; there is no if(id==='corp-detail') branch. The detail page renders solely because openCorpDetail calls renderCorpDetail immediately after navigating.
findings.impact: Any other route to corp-detail - back navigation, a deep link, a future call site - leaves the previous company's DOM on screen under a stale header.

findings.title: Covered radius is measured as the crow flies
findings.detail: geoDistanceKm is plain Euclidean over the map's percentage coordinates scaled by GEO_SCALE_KM, with no ROAD_CIRCUITY_FACTOR, while computeRouteKm applies a 1.35 multiplier for the same geography when pricing.
findings.impact: A destination the pricing engine considers 13.5 road-km away is judged 10 km by the policy check, so real out-of-radius trips pass.

findings.title: Employee removal has no confirmation
findings.detail: The red Remove button on each employee row calls removeEmployeeFromCorp directly, with no confirm modal, although the file uses confirm() for comparable destructive actions elsewhere.
findings.impact: A misclick unlinks an employee, removing their spend from the company's bill with no undo.

findings.title: Geo-radius rule never fires on seeded data
findings.detail: The radius check requires both pol.officeDistrict and pol.geoRestrictKm and then reads sub.route, a field written only by finalizeNewSub. All 7 seeded subscriptions lack it.
findings.impact: The seeded CORP-001 policy declares a 12 km radius from Olaya / KAFD that can never produce a violation, so the feature reads as working when it is inert.

findings.title: Invoice and add-employee modals open ungated
findings.detail: openCorpInvoiceModal and openAddEmployeeModal both open with no requirePerm; the invoice opener additionally carries the DB.invoiceSequence side effect.
findings.impact: An unauthorised user can read a company's full billing position and permanently advance the VAT invoice counter.

findings.title: Invoice send gates on a different permission from every other corporate write
findings.detail: commitSendCorpInvoice requires view_finance while commitNewCorp, saveCorpBillingContact, saveCorpUsagePolicy, setCorpStatus and removeEmployeeFromCorp all require manage_subscriptions.
findings.impact: A corporate-ops role that can rewrite a company's billing contact may be unable to send its invoice, and a finance role the reverse.

findings.title: Manager approval has no approver portal
findings.detail: The UI states it plainly: the approver receives an email and replies or calls in, with no login of their own, and ops records the outcome manually on the subscription profile.
findings.evidence: The approver gets an email and replies or calls in - they don't have their own login to click approve/reject directly.
findings.impact: Every approval decision depends on an ops person transcribing an out-of-band reply, so the audit trail records the transcription rather than the approver's own act.

findings.title: Monthly cap is checked against a lifetime average
findings.detail: The cap check compares pol.monthlyCapSAR against riderLTV(r)/riderTenureMonths(r), which is the average across the rider's whole tenure rather than the current calendar month's spend.
findings.impact: A long-tenured heavy spender passes a cap this month's real spend would breach, and a new employee's first big month is flagged forever.

findings.title: System email is sent with an address where an entity id is expected
findings.detail: sendSystemEmail(toId,...) resolves toName via nm2(toId) and toEmail via emailFor(toId)||'-'. commitSendCorpInvoice passes a raw email string, and finalizeNewSub does the same with corpPol.approverEmail, so emailFor returns null.
findings.impact: Corporate invoice and approval emails are logged in DB.emailOutbox with a broken recipient field, so the email log cannot prove who was contacted.

findings.title: Vehicle-tier check uses an arbitrary subscription
findings.detail: riderVehicleTier maps the rider's subs array and takes the first truthy entry, so a rider holding both an Economy and a Comfort package is judged on whichever happens to be first.
findings.impact: Tier violations are reported or missed non-deterministically for multi-package employees.

findings.title: Work-hours policy is stored but never evaluated
findings.detail: corpPolicyViolations implements only the cap, tier and geo checks. workHoursOnly has a checkbox but no consumer, and workHoursStart/workHoursEnd have neither a UI control nor a reader anywhere in the file.
findings.impact: A company told its coverage is restricted to work hours gets no such restriction and no violation reporting.

findings.title: List has no search, filter, sort or pagination
findings.detail: renderCorporateList maps every key of DB.corporateAccounts unbounded into #corp-tbody with no controls of any kind.
findings.impact: Acceptable at one seeded account, unusable at a real B2B book of business.

findings.title: No close, suspend or archive path for an account
findings.detail: setCorpStatus accepts any status string but the only call site in the file passes 'Active'. No function removes an entry from DB.corporateAccounts and there is no Suspend or Close control anywhere.
findings.impact: A company that stops trading stays Active forever, keeps counting toward Employees covered and Total corporate spend, and keeps generating invoice-due alerts.

findings.title: 'View route' does not carry the trip
findings.detail: The trip profile's View route button calls go('live',null), opening the Live Map at its default state. openRouteReplay exists and does target a specific trip, but is not wired to this button.
findings.impact: Investigating a specific route requires manually finding the trip again on the map.

findings.title: dateMs sort key exists only on reconstructed trips
findings.detail: tripsTable sorts descending on dateMs||0, but dateMs is written only by buildRiderHistory. Seeded and live trips have no dateMs and all tie at 0, falling back to whatever order they arrived in.
findings.impact: A rider or driver trip history that claims to be newest-first mixes reconstructed trips above every real one regardless of date.

findings.title: Eyvar commission computed two different ways
findings.detail: The table subtracts the extra-stop fee from the platform cut; the receipt does not, computing fare minus driverEarn only.
findings.impact: For any multi-stop trip the ledger and the receipt state different platform revenue for the same ride.

findings.title: Fairness-case audit behaviour unconfirmed
findings.detail: openRatingDispute and openReportRider delegate to fcNew; the doc records that the function body was not read, so whether a rating dispute or rider report writes an audit entry is unverified.
findings.impact: If fcNew does not audit, a captain's rating dispute leaves no trace outside the fairness store.

findings.title: Filter state is global and survives navigation
findings.detail: window.__tripsLowOnly and window.__tripsKindFilter persist across page changes, while the low-rating button's active styling is applied only inside toggleLowRatingFilter.
findings.impact: Returning to All Trips can show a filtered subset with an un-highlighted button, so the operator believes they are seeing every trip.

findings.title: Flagging a trip does not refresh the All Trips table
findings.detail: flagTrip and unflagTrip re-render the Quick Rides table but never call renderTripsTable, so the red row tint and flag glyph on this page go stale.
findings.impact: An operator who flags a subscription leg from its profile returns to a ledger that still shows it unflagged.

findings.title: Money and distance fields are strings coerced ad hoc
findings.detail: km, min, fare and driverEarn are all stored as strings and parsed at each use site. The cancelled seed record TRP-9003 carries the em-dash placeholder for km, min and driverEarn, which parseFloat turns into NaN.
findings.impact: The ||0 guard saves this page, but the Quick Rides page prints the raw placeholder, and any new consumer that forgets the guard will render NaN into a money column.

findings.title: Ticket creation from a trip is ungated and unaudited
findings.detail: createTicketFor unshifts a full ticket into DB.tickets, stamps an SLA and fires an auto-reply, with neither requirePerm nor logAction - unlike every other write reachable from the trip profile.
findings.impact: Tickets appear in the support queue with no record of who created them or whether they were allowed to.

findings.title: Trip ledger is readable with no permission check
findings.detail: PAGE_PERMS declares trips with legacy live_ops and a view perm, but renderTripsTable never calls can() or requirePerm and go('trips') is not wrapped either.
findings.impact: Every trip, rider name, driver name, fare and rating is visible to any signed-in role regardless of the declared permission.

findings.title: Two Status-badge mappings disagree on 'Late'
findings.detail: The page uses an inline ternary with only red/green/blue branches, so 'Late +8' falls through to blue. The shared statusBadge tests /late|expir|pend/i and renders it amber.
findings.impact: A late trip looks like a normal in-progress trip on the page that exists to surface problems.

findings.title: 'Today' is claimed but no date filter is applied
findings.detail: The card title reads 'All quick rides - today' and the page prose says '63 today', but renderQuickRidesTable filters only on kind and reverses. The Dashboard's quick-ride card does apply a 25 Jun date filter; this page does not.
findings.impact: Every quick ride ever recorded is listed under a heading promising today, so counts read off the table are wrong.

findings.title: completeTrip does not re-render this table
findings.detail: completeTrip re-renders Live Ops, the Dashboard and the Subscriptions table but never calls renderQuickRidesTable, so a ride finishing while the page is open does not appear.
findings.impact: An operator watching the quick-rides ledger sees a stale list and must navigate away and back to refresh it.

findings.title: Export drops three visible columns and over-selects rows
findings.detail: exportRows('quickrides') emits no Tip, Driver earns or Pay column although all three are shown in the table, and filters on kind !== 'Subscription' rather than kind === 'Quick ride'.
findings.impact: The CSV does not match the screen, and any future trip kind would silently be exported as a quick ride.

findings.title: Flagged quick rides are invisible on this page
findings.detail: The Trip ID cell omits the flag glyph that All Trips appends, and the row tint is keyed on cancellation only, not on t.flagged - even though flagTrip explicitly re-renders this table.
findings.impact: A quick ride flagged for a corporate-policy violation shows here as an ordinary completed ride.

findings.title: No page-level permission guard
findings.detail: PAGE_PERMS.quickrides is declared with legacy live_ops and a view perm, but renderQuickRidesTable never calls can() or requirePerm and go('quickrides') is unwrapped.
findings.impact: Every quick ride, rider name, driver name, fare and payment method is readable by any signed-in role.

findings.title: Ride-request commit has no permission check
findings.detail: requirePerm('live_ops') gates openNewRideRequestModal only; commitNewRideRequest performs the DB write and the audit entry with no gate of its own and is directly callable.
findings.impact: The permission model depends on the UI path being the only way in, which is not an enforceable boundary in a single-file app.

findings.title: Ride-request ids can collide
findings.detail: The id is 500 plus the array length plus a random 0-399, with no uniqueness check, on an array that has no index.
findings.impact: Two requests can share an id, and every lookup by id - including the tracking modal - then resolves to whichever comes first.

findings.title: The 1 s tracking interval may outlive the modal
findings.detail: Only closeRideRequestTracking clears _rrTrackInterval. Any other path that closes the modal - an overlay click, a closeModal() from elsewhere - would leave a 1 s timer rewriting #modal-content. The closeModal body was not read, so whether it clears intervals is unconfirmed.
findings.impact: A leaked timer would overwrite whatever modal is open next, once per second, for the rest of the session.

findings.title: The Large vehicle type cannot be requested
findings.detail: The vehicle-type select offers only Economy and Comfort, although DB.quickRideTypes defines Large with its own base fare and per-km rate and the pricing page can edit it.
findings.impact: A caller needing a Large vehicle cannot be served from the ops panel despite the rate card existing.

findings.title: Tracking cannot be reopened once closed
findings.detail: openRideRequestTracking has exactly one caller, at the end of commitNewRideRequest. Nothing on the Requests page or anywhere else can reopen tracking for an existing request.
findings.impact: An operator who closes the modal loses the live view of a request that is still being dispatched, with the Requests page as the only fallback.

findings.title: Tracking modal resolves the accepted trip by rider
findings.detail: Once driverAcceptOffer splices the request out of DB.rideRequests, the modal finds the resulting trip by matching DB.liveTrips on rider rather than on the request id it was opened with.
findings.impact: A rider with a second concurrent live trip makes the tracker show the wrong trip and its Open trip button navigate to the wrong record.

findings.title: A renewal that creates a new subscription generates no upcoming trips
findings.detail: The else-branch of renderSuccess() writes a fresh DB.subscriptions record directly without calling generateUpcomingTripsForSubscription(), unlike materializeSubscription() on the Requests path.
findings.impact: The new subscription never appears on Trip Readiness, so its first legs are unmonitored before departure.

findings.title: autoRenew is never seeded, so the manual-renewal KPI is always zero at boot
findings.detail: The only writes to sub.autoRenew are inside toggleAutoRenew() — true at L5450 and false at L5477. No seeded subscription carries the field, and every check is a strict === false, so at boot the 'Manual renewal required' tile reads 0 and the manual filter yields an empty page.
findings.impact: One of the page's three headline metrics and one of its three filters are inert until an operator manually turns auto-renew off somewhere else.

findings.title: cancelledThisMonth is computed and never used
findings.detail: renderRenewalPipeline() computes cancelledThisMonth on every render but no code path reads it. The name is also inaccurate — the filter has no month restriction, it counts every subscription whose status matches /cancel/i.
findings.impact: Wasted work on every render and a misleading variable name that invites future misuse as a monthly churn metric.

findings.title: Discount labels on wizard options are cosmetic
findings.detail: renewOptionsFor() tags the bi-weekly option 'Save 5%' with a '5% discount applied' sub-line and the monthly option 'Save 10%', but each option's price is read straight from PLANS[cadence][vehicleKey] with no adjustment.
findings.impact: The operator quotes a discount to the rider that the charged amount does not reflect.

findings.title: KPI tiles are computed after the filter is applied
findings.detail: The _renewalFilter predicate runs at L3334-L3339, before the KPI counts at L3340-L3342. With a filter active, all three tiles and the page subtitle describe only the filtered subset, so 'Expiring this week' stops showing the week total.
findings.impact: The headline metric silently changes meaning when a filter is on, and the 'Expiring this week' tile can never highlight as active because its on-state test excludes 'all'.

findings.title: openRenewFlow falls back to a hardcoded demo rider
findings.detail: openRenewFlow(rider) resolves flowRider as resolveFlowRider(rider || 'RDR-1041'), and the module-level flowRider is also initialised to 'RDR-1041'. A falsy argument therefore silently targets the demo rider instead of failing.
findings.impact: A mis-wired call site would charge and renew the wrong rider's subscription with no warning.

findings.title: Retention-action confirmation copy overstates what the action does
findings.detail: GATE_SWEEP.commitRetentionAction warns 'May issue credit or change the subscription terms' and 'Recorded against the rider and in the activity log', but commitRetentionAction() only closes the modal, logs, toasts and pushes a notification — no subscription field is written and no credit is issued.
findings.impact: Operators are asked to confirm consequences that do not occur, which erodes the meaning of every other confirmation dialog.

findings.title: The 'Try another card' form is entirely inert
findings.detail: tryAnotherCard() renders Card number, Expiry, CVV and Name on card inputs, none of which has an id and none of which is read anywhere. Its 'Save & charge' button calls processCharge(), which re-uses the same hardcoded Visa ···· 4821.
findings.impact: An operator can type a different card and the system will charge the original one, with no indication that the input was ignored.

findings.title: The payment gateway is a random draw, and its comment disagrees with the code
findings.detail: processCharge() waits 1800 ms and then sets success = Math.random() > 0.25, i.e. ~75% success. The comment immediately above claims ~80%.
findings.impact: No real charge is attempted, and one in four renewal attempts fails for no reason, which will confuse anyone demoing or testing the flow.

findings.title: The renewal pipeline is not re-rendered after a successful renewal
findings.detail: renderSuccess() calls renderSubscriptionsTable() and renderReadiness() but never renderRenewalPipeline(), so the board the operator launched the wizard from still shows the subscription as expiring.
findings.impact: The operator may renew the same subscription twice because the row does not disappear from the pipeline.

findings.title: VAT is never computed in the renew wizard
findings.detail: Step 2 renders a 'VAT (15%)' row whose value is the literal string 'included', and Total to charge is identical to Subtotal. Real VAT arithmetic exists elsewhere in the file, in getOrCreateInvoice().
findings.impact: The charge summary shown to the operator is not a real tax breakdown and cannot be reconciled against an invoice.

findings.title: Compensation label map has a typo on the default option
findings.detail: The label map keys the discount as '-20off' while the radio's data-comp attribute is '20off'. Because '20off' is the default selected option, labels[comp] is undefined for the most common case and the code falls back to the raw value via labels[comp]||comp.
findings.evidence: var labels={free:'Free next ride','-20off':'20% off next renewal',credit:'10 SAR credit',none:'No compensation'};
findings.impact: The toast and the audit entry read 'Compensation: 20off' instead of '20% off next renewal', so the log is unreadable for the most frequent case.

findings.title: finalizeReassign is ungated although its predecessor is gated
findings.detail: confirmReassign() calls requirePerm('manage_subscriptions') but finalizeReassign(), which writes the audit entry for the reassignment, has no gate. It is defined on window so it is globally reachable.
findings.impact: The audit record for a gated action can be produced by an ungated call, weakening the guarantee that the gate provides.

findings.title: logNdvContact records nothing
findings.detail: The nearby-drivers modal's '📞 Call' button leads to quickContactDriver() then logNdvContact(), which writes no state and no audit entry — it only toasts and returns to the candidate list. Its three outcome options are cosmetic.
findings.impact: Calls made to drivers from the dispatch picker leave no trace, so contact history is incomplete.

findings.title: readinessStatus and tripScenario disagree despite a comment asserting they cannot
findings.detail: The header comment above tripScenario() states it 'mirrors readinessStatus()'s exact priority order (same fields, same thresholds) so the two can never disagree'. In fact readinessStatus classifies the unconfirmed case as level 'high' with colour red while tripScenario returns colour amber for the equivalent case, and readinessStatus has no 'unassigned' branch at all.
findings.impact: The same trip is coloured red on the readiness table and amber in the nearby-drivers banner and dashboard interventions feed; a trip with a missing driver id falls through readinessStatus to 'On track'.

findings.title: Support tickets are created from readiness with no gate and no audit
findings.detail: createReadinessTicket() unshifts a new record onto DB.tickets with priority High and a fixed assignee. It calls neither requirePerm nor logAction, unlike most other ops writes in the file.
findings.impact: Any operator can inject urgent tickets into the support queue with nothing in the activity log tying the ticket to who raised it.

findings.title: The driver 'delay' response writes nothing while the toast promises notification
findings.detail: logDriverCall() handles 'moving' and 'unavailable' with field writes but has no branch for 'delay'; the toast map nonetheless says '⏳ Delay logged — rider will be notified'.
findings.impact: A known 10-15 minute driver delay is invisible to the board and to the rider, despite the operator being told it was logged and communicated.

findings.title: The readiness sidebar badge double-counts overlapping conditions
findings.detail: The badge is the arithmetic sum of the unconfirmed, not-moving and unavailable KPI sets, which are not disjoint. A trip that is unavailable and also unconfirmed within 60 minutes is counted in two of them.
findings.impact: The badge can exceed the number of trips actually needing attention, overstating the queue.

findings.title: Two of the four rider-call outcomes are discarded
findings.detail: logCallOutcome() reads the select and writes state only for 'confirmed'. 'no_answer', 'cancelled' and 'delay' produce a toast and nothing else — no field write, no audit entry, no ticket.
findings.impact: A rider who explicitly asked to cancel their trip leaves no record anywhere, so the trip stays on the board and the cancellation is lost.

findings.title: Every materialised subscription is stamped with a fixed weekday set
findings.detail: materializeSubscription() always writes days: ['Sun','Mon','Tue','Wed','Thu']; the inline comment concedes 'this pipeline doesn't collect explicit day choices yet, unlike the New Subscription builder'.
findings.evidence: days:['Sun','Mon','Tue','Wed','Thu'] /* standard work week — this pipeline doesn't collect explicit day choices yet
findings.impact: The days field drives generateUpcomingTripsForSubscription, so readiness legs are created for days the rider may not have asked for and omitted for days they did.

findings.title: Live-trip and payment ids are random with no collision check
findings.detail: commitRequestAssign and driverAcceptOffer both mint 'TRP-'+(9100+rand(900)); capturePaymentHold mints 'PAY-'+(6000+rand(3900)). Neither checks whether the id already exists.
findings.impact: A collision silently overwrites an existing live trip or an existing payment record, the latter being a financial record.

findings.title: Page size is a single shared variable across two independent lists
findings.detail: REQ_ALL_PAGE_SIZE is one module-level variable reassigned by onReqAllPageSizeChange for either page. Each custom select is built only once, guarded by a check for the existing element, so a select can keep displaying a value that is no longer in force.
findings.impact: Changing rows-per-page on one full list silently changes the other, and the two selectors can display contradictory values.

findings.title: Reopening an expired request destroys the original request time
findings.detail: reopenSubReq() sets status back to pending, deletes expiredAt and overwrites requestedAt with fmtReqNowLabel(). Since reqAgeMinutes derives entirely from requestedAt, this restarts the 2-hour search window and erases when the rider actually asked.
findings.impact: The record of the rider's original request time is lost, so true time-to-match and SLA history cannot be reconstructed.

findings.title: Requests can be claimed without any permission check
findings.detail: assignManually() and openSubReqAssign() write claimedBy and claimedAt before any gate; requirePerm is only reached at commit time in commitRequestAssign ('live_ops') and commitSubReqAssign ('manage_subscriptions').
findings.impact: An operator with no assignment permission can lock every request in the queue, blocking colleagues who do have the permission, and the claim is never audited.

findings.title: The 'declined' status is unhandled by both the badge and the chips
findings.detail: rejectSubReqCorp() sets r.status='declined'. reqStatusBadge has no branch for it and falls through to the generic grey span, and reqStatusMatch only maps pending|searching|offered, assigned and expired|no_drivers, so 'declined' matches none of the three status chips.
findings.impact: A request a corporate manager declined is invisible under every status filter and shows a raw lowercase status string, so declined sign-ups fall out of the operator's view.

findings.title: The requests sidebar badge uses inconsistent semantics for its two halves
findings.detail: The badge counts instant requests with status !== 'assigned' — which includes expired and no_drivers rows — but subscription requests only when status === 'pending'. The same expression is duplicated in renderRequestsPage and refreshNavCounts.
findings.impact: Terminal expired instant requests inflate the outstanding-work badge indefinitely, while the equivalent subscription rows do not.

findings.title: The rider's stated preference is never shown to the operator
findings.detail: Seeded subscription requests carry notes such as 'First subscription — wants female driver if available' and 'Wants the same driver daily if possible'. buildSubReqRow() renders nine cells and none of them is r.notes; generated rows set it to an empty string.
findings.impact: The operator matching a driver cannot see the constraint the rider asked for, so assignments will violate stated preferences.

findings.title: The status filter does not carry over to the full-list pages
findings.detail: renderRequestsSubAll and renderRequestsInstantAll build their rows straight from the sorted arrays and apply only the search box; neither reads _reqFilter.
findings.impact: An operator who filters to 'Pending' and then clicks the card title to see everything lands on an unfiltered list, losing their filter with no indication.

findings.title: Two seeded requests point at a non-existent subscription
findings.detail: SREQ-002 and SREQ-005 both carry assignedSub:'SUB-1052b'. No such key exists in DB.subscriptions, and buildSubReqRow renders a 'View sub' button whenever status is assigned and assignedSub is set.
findings.impact: Clicking 'View sub' on either row opens a broken profile for an id that does not resolve.

findings.title: Approval attributes the decision to a hardcoded operator
findings.detail: approveDriver writes a.decidedBy='Sarah Al-Rashid' and a.decidedAt='Just now' regardless of who is signed in, while the logAction call on the very next line resolves CURRENT_USER_ID. The applicant record and the audit trail can therefore name two different people for the same decision, and decidedAt carries no timestamp at all.
findings.impact: KYC decisions cannot be reliably attributed, which is exactly what an onboarding audit trail exists to do.

findings.title: Capacity is a static seed string, never derived
findings.detail: The Capacity column reads d.capacity, a free-text seed value ('Full', '1 open', '2 open', '3 open') that no code recomputes. driverActiveSubCount() exists and is used on the profile card, and capacityOpen(d.capacity) parses the string during dispatch, but neither writes it back. A newly approved driver has no capacity field at all and renders '—'.
findings.impact: Dispatch capacity decisions are made against a value that drifts away from real subscription assignments.

findings.title: driver_max_active_subs is displayed as a limit but not enforced
findings.detail: The limit is seeded enabled:true, enforced:false, enforcedBy:null, yet the roster's Active subs column renders stats.activeSubs in a used/limit form that implies enforcement. DRV-0103 displays 6/6, above the configured maximum of 5.
findings.impact: The roster implies a cap that no code applies, and displays a driver already exceeding it.

findings.title: DRV-0106 has no document record and is invisible to compliance
findings.detail: DB.driverDocs carries entries for DRV-0101 through DRV-0105 only. DRV-0106 has no document row at all, so complianceScan() never evaluates it, it can never be auto-suspended for an expired document, and it never appears in the compliance queue.
findings.impact: One sixth of the seeded fleet operates outside document-expiry enforcement.

findings.title: finalizeReassign compensation label lookup uses the wrong key
findings.detail: The compensation option cards carry data-comp values free / 20off / credit / none, with 20off pre-selected. The label map inside finalizeReassign keys that entry as '-20off'. The default selection therefore falls through labels[comp]||comp and both the audit summary and the toast print the raw string '20off' instead of '20% off next renewal'.
findings.evidence: var labels={free:'Free next ride','-20off':'20% off next renewal',credit:'10 SAR credit',none:'No compensation'};
findings.impact: The most commonly chosen compensation is recorded in the audit log as an opaque token, weakening the record of what a rider was promised.

findings.title: finalizeReassign has no permission gate
findings.detail: commitLiveReassign, which swaps the driver on an in-progress trip, calls requirePerm('live_ops') first. finalizeReassign, which swaps the driver on an upcoming subscription trip and grants rider compensation, calls no permission check at all before mutating state and writing the audit entry.
findings.impact: Any operator who can reach the Trip Readiness screen can reassign drivers and issue rider compensation regardless of role.

findings.title: No path exists to create a driver or an application from the panel
findings.detail: The page's primary header button is an inline toast stub. Drivers can only enter DB.drivers through approveDriver(), and DB.pendingDrivers has no creation UI at all, so the applicant queue can only shrink.
findings.evidence: <button class="btn p sm" onclick="toast('Driver onboarding form would open here','info')">+ Onboard driver</button>
findings.impact: The fleet-growth workflow is unreachable from the ops panel; the most prominent button on the page does nothing.

findings.title: Tier filter cannot be cleared once set
findings.detail: filterDriversByTier assigns _driverTierFilter=tier without the click-to-toggle logic that setDriverFilter uses, and none of the four tiles maps to the 'all' sentinel. The variable is module-scope and survives navigation, so go('drivers') does not reset it either. Once a tier is picked the roster stays filtered for the rest of the session.
findings.impact: Operators lose access to the full roster with no visible way to recover it short of reloading the panel.

findings.title: Two incompatible definitions of a low rating, and no low-rating filter on the roster
findings.detail: The Limited tier tile and its filter hardcode d.rating>0 && d.rating<3.5, while lowRatingThreshold() reads DB.opsConfig.notifications.lowRatingThreshold (default 2.5) and isLowRating() applies it. The only 'low rating' toggle in the file, toggleLowRatingFilter(), belongs to the All Trips table and filters trips by driverRatingGiven, not the drivers roster.
findings.impact: A driver flagged 'Limited' on this page may not be considered low-rated by the notification engine, and vice versa.

findings.title: Two rating limits with the same value, only one of them wired up
findings.detail: DB.opsLimits contains driver_min_rating_for_dispatch (3.5★, enabled:true, enforced:true, with an enforcedBy reference) and driver_min_rating (3.5★, enabled:true, enforced:false, enforcedBy:null). Only the first is consulted by driverAutoRestricted(). Editing the second in Settings changes nothing at runtime.
findings.impact: Ops can adjust a visible safety threshold and believe it took effect when it is inert.

findings.title: All-Pending search resets on navigation while the input keeps its text
findings.detail: The go() dispatch calls renderAllPending('') unconditionally for the all-pending page, including when arriving via Back. The #pending-search input retains whatever was typed, so the visible query and the rendered list disagree until the next keystroke.
findings.impact: Operators lose their filter silently and see a box that claims a filter is still applied.

findings.title: Approval pushes a spurious history frame
findings.detail: After approving, approveDriver re-opens the applicant detail page with openApplicantDetail(id) and no isBack flag, so pushHistory() runs and the current page is stacked on itself. Pressing Back afterwards returns to the same applicant detail page rather than the list. setDocStatus does this correctly by passing true.
findings.impact: Navigation history is corrupted at exactly the point the operator wants to return to the queue.

findings.title: Blank expiry dates are written as empty strings and silently defaulted
findings.detail: saveDocExpiry collects each of the five date inputs; empty ones are pushed onto missing[] for the warning toast but are still written into a.docExpiry as ''. docExpiryViewHTML treats '' as falsy and shows 'Not set', so it round-trips visually, but approveDriver's enteredExpiry[key]||defaultExpiry also treats '' as falsy and substitutes today+1 year without further warning at that point.
findings.impact: A document with no known expiry silently receives a full year of compliance runway.

findings.title: decidedBy is hardcoded on both approve and reject
findings.detail: Both approveDriver and rejectDriver stamp decidedBy='Sarah Al-Rashid' and decidedAt='Just now' irrespective of the signed-in operator, while the accompanying logAction resolves CURRENT_USER_ID. The decision badge in the list therefore names a person who may not have made the decision.
findings.impact: The visible attribution on the applicant record contradicts the audit log for the same event.

findings.title: Document approve/reject buttons stay live after approval
findings.detail: The submitted-documents card is guarded only by 'a && a.docs' with no isApproved check, unlike the expiry card which is explicitly suppressed for decided applicants. The ✓/✕ buttons therefore remain functional on an already-approved application, mutating a.docs with no downstream effect on the created driver.
findings.impact: Operators can appear to change verification outcomes after activation, with no effect and no warning.

findings.title: No status filter, sort or pagination on All-Pending
findings.detail: renderAllPending lists all of DB.pendingDrivers in array order with only a name/id/plate substring search. Decided and open applications interleave, and a.applied is relative free text ('24 Jun · 2 days ago') that cannot be sorted or aged.
findings.impact: The queue cannot be worked oldest-first or filtered to open items, which is the normal way to run a KYC backlog.

findings.title: No way to create an application
findings.detail: The only affordance that suggests creating one is the Drivers page's '+ Onboard driver' button, which is an inline toast stub. DB.pendingDrivers is seeded once and can only shrink as applications are decided.
findings.evidence: onclick="toast('Driver onboarding form would open here','info')"
findings.impact: The funnel cannot be exercised end to end, and the demo queue drains permanently.

findings.title: Reconsider leaves the applicant record internally inconsistent
findings.detail: reconsiderApplicant sets a.status='pending' and audits the reopen, then immediately chains into confirmApproveDriver. It never clears a.reason, a.decidedBy or a.decidedAt and never re-renders the lists. If the operator cancels the approval modal the record sits as 'pending' while still carrying the old rejection reason and decidedAt:'Just now'; decisionBadge shows '⏳ Pending review' over stale decision data.
findings.impact: The funnel's own state becomes untrustworthy after a cancelled reconsideration.

findings.title: The confirmation modals are not permission-gated
findings.detail: confirmApproveDriver and confirmRejectDriver open freely; only the terminal approveDriver/rejectDriver calls requirePerm('approve_drivers'). An operator without the permission reads a full decision screen, presses the confirm button, and only then receives the denial toast.
findings.impact: Permission boundaries are discovered late, and the UI implies capabilities the role does not have.

findings.title: The expiry-date audit entry records no before or after values
findings.detail: logAction('save_doc_expiry','applicant',appId, summary, {}, {}) passes empty objects for both the before and after payloads. The actual dates appear only inside the free-text summary and cannot be diffed or queried.
findings.impact: Changes to compliance-critical dates cannot be reconstructed from the audit trail.

findings.title: The plate number is lost on approval
findings.detail: a.plate is captured at application time, displayed on the applicant Vehicle card and searchable in the All-Pending list, but approveDriver does not copy it into the driver record. An approved driver's Vehicle card therefore shows 'Plate number: —', and the plate can no longer be used to find them.
findings.impact: The single most useful field for identifying a vehicle on the road is discarded at activation.

findings.title: LTV and the reconciliation view read payments through different paths
findings.detail: riderLTV walks only the ids listed in d.payments[]. entityDerived() instead scans all of DB.payments looking for entries whose entity is the rider. A payment recorded against a rider but never appended to their payments array is therefore counted by the profile's 'in panel records' provenance line and excluded from LTV, the watchlist ranking and the corporate spend rollups that reuse riderLTV.
findings.impact: Two numbers derived from the same ledger on the same screen can disagree, with no indication which is authoritative.

findings.title: LTV's amount parser does not strip thousands separators
findings.detail: riderLTV sums parseFloat(p.amount) over Paid payments. Amounts are formatted strings like '86.50 SAR'; parseFloat('1,040.00 SAR') returns 1. The reconciliation path's numOf() strips non-digits first and would return 1040, so the two would disagree. No seeded payment currently contains a comma, making this latent rather than live.
findings.impact: A single four-figure payment would silently reduce a rider's lifetime value to about one riyal, changing their churn-watchlist position.

findings.title: No flagged or suspended badge in the riders table
findings.detail: commitFlagAccount and commitSuspendAccount both call renderRidersTable() after mutating the record, and the flag modal's own copy promises the flag will be 'visible to the whole team on their profile and in the Riders table'. The table renders neither state. The equivalent drivers table renders both a red 🚫 Suspended chip and an amber Under review chip.
findings.impact: A moderation action the UI claims is visible on this page is not, so flagged riders are handled as normal.

findings.title: Promoted new riders always show a one-month tenure
findings.detail: DB.newRiders records carry joined strings like '25 Jun · today'. openNewRiderProfile copies that string verbatim into the created DB.riders record. riderTenureMonths splits on space, finds '25' at index 0, fails the month-name lookup and returns the floor value 1. Every promoted rider therefore reports Tenure 1 mo forever, and their avg monthly spend equals their entire lifetime value.
findings.impact: Two of the three figures on the Customer value card are wrong for every rider who came through the sign-ups queue.

findings.title: Renewal rate is a display-only seed string
findings.detail: stats.renewalRate holds strings such as '100%', '91%', '—' that are read by the roster column and the profile KPI tile but are never computed anywhere in the file. There is no derivation from DB.subscriptions and no writer.
findings.impact: A whole column of the roster shows fixture data that will never update as subscriptions renew or lapse.

findings.title: Retention offers send on one click with no gate and no confirmation
findings.detail: sendRetentionOfferToRider immediately calls sendSystemEmail with a promo email, audits and toasts. It has no requirePerm call and no confirmation modal. The welcome offer on the very same page requires contact_users and goes through a modal, so the two customer-contact paths are gated inconsistently.
findings.evidence: function sendRetentionOfferToRider(riderId){ var rr=DB.riders[riderId]; if(!rr)return; sendSystemEmail(riderId,'A little something before you go 🎁'
findings.impact: Any operator can send marketing mail to a customer with a single misclick and no undo.

findings.title: riderHealth and riderChurnRisk disagree about a zero rating
findings.detail: riderHealth guards with rr.rating && rr.rating < 4, so a rating of 0 is falsy and the rider is reported Healthy. riderChurnRisk uses (d.rating || 5) < 4, which for a stored 0 evaluates 0 < 4 and adds a point with the reason 'Rating below 4★'. The same seeded rider (RDR-2090) is therefore green in the Health column and penalised in the Churn risk column.
findings.impact: Two adjacent columns of the same row give opposite readings on the same field.

findings.title: The churn model's 'activeSubs' variable holds all subscriptions
findings.detail: activeSubs is built by mapping every id in d.subs through DB.subscriptions and filtering only for existence, not for status. Rule 1 then adds a point only when activeSubs.length === 0, so a rider whose single subscription is Cancelled escapes the 'no subscription' penalty while still collecting the +2 cancelled-subscription penalty. The naming actively invites the wrong reading.
findings.impact: The churn score understates risk for the specific population — lapsed subscribers — the watchlist exists to catch.

findings.title: The Vehicle column invents 'Economy' for riders with no subscription
findings.detail: vehType is derived from the first subscription's plan string; when there is no subscription the ternary falls through to the literal 'Economy' and renders the same b-eco badge a real Economy subscriber gets. Nothing marks it as a default.
findings.impact: A fabricated vehicle tier is presented indistinguishably from a recorded one, on every quick-ride-only rider.

findings.title: Two functions write contradictory page subtitles
findings.detail: renderRidersTable rewrites #p-riders .ph-l p as '{n} total · {n} with active subscription · {n} quick-ride only · {n} new (24h)', counting riders whose subs[] array is non-empty regardless of subscription status. liveSubtitles rewrites the same element as '{n} registered · {n} with an active subscription · {n} quick-ride only', using the fleetCounts subscription-based count. Whichever ran last wins: at boot liveSubtitles runs after renderRidersTable, but any flag, suspend or erasure action re-renders the table and swaps the text back.
findings.impact: The same headline metric changes value and wording depending on which action the operator last performed.

findings.title: Driver KPI tiles lack the provenance chips riders get
findings.detail: The rider variant of the stat row attaches provenanceChip('stored') and a derived sub-line to Total trips and Total paid. The driver variant reads d.stats raw with no chip and no sub-line, although entityDerived works identically for drivers and reconcileEntity explicitly supports DB.drivers.
findings.evidence: isDrv variant reads stat.totalTrips / stat.monthEarn / stat.onTime / stat.activeSubs with no provenanceChip call
findings.impact: A driver with an orphaned record shows the red reconcile banner but no per-tile context explaining which figure is the billing aggregate and which is derived.

findings.title: Four DB buckets are unreachable from global search
findings.detail: resolveId only checks riders, drivers, trips, subscriptions, payments and complaints. DB.newRiders, DB.pendingDrivers, DB.tickets and DB.corporateAccounts are not buckets, so typing RDR-3001, APP-2201, TKT-505 or a company id returns 'No record found' even though applicants, tickets and corporate accounts all have dedicated detail pages reached by other routes.
findings.impact: The global search box, advertised as universal, silently fails for four entity families including new-rider records that only become searchable after openNewRiderProfile promotes them.

findings.title: History reconstruction never runs for drivers
findings.detail: buildRiderHistory returns null immediately when the id is not in DB.riders, so a driver whose stats.totalTrips exceeds the trips linked to them stays permanently divergent with no fill-in and no way to close the gap from the UI.
findings.impact: Driver reconciliation surfaces the divergence but offers no remedy, unlike the rider path which both fills in and offers a Fetch full history button.

findings.title: Missing consents default to the oldest document version
findings.detail: getUserConsent lazily creates a consent record using versions.slice().reverse()[0].version, described in the source comment as the oldest, safest assumption. Every seed user therefore starts non-compliant on any legal document that has more than one version, and the Device and access card immediately paints them amber as outdated.
findings.evidence: versions.slice().reverse()[0].version  /* default to the oldest, safest assumption */
findings.impact: Consent compliance percentages and the per-profile ToS and Privacy badges are driven by an assumption rather than by a recorded acceptance, which is the wrong basis for a regulatory answer.

findings.title: Name resolution is first-match-wins over an unordered object walk
findings.detail: resolveId falls back to a name substring search across DB.riders and DB.drivers only, iterating with for..in and returning the first hit. Searching a shared family name such as Al-Harbi silently resolves to whichever record the engine enumerates first.
