There is no disambiguation UI, no match count, no fuzzy matching, no partial-id matching and no phone-number search.
findings.impact: An operator searching by name can open and act on the wrong customer record without any signal that other matches existed.

findings.title: Payment profiles are read-only dead ends
findings.detail: buildPayProfile emits one two-card grid and nothing else - no refund control, no invoice link, no audit trail - even though getOrCreateInvoice exists in the same file and the trip profile links to openInvoiceModal for the very same payment.
findings.evidence: buildPayProfile emits only the Payment kvCard and the Linked kvCard
findings.impact: Any payment-level action forces the operator back out to the trip or the Finance page, and there is no in-place record of what was done to a payment.

findings.title: Post-mutation refreshes push spurious history entries
findings.detail: openProfile pushes the current navCurrent onto navStack unless isBack is true. Four refresh call sites omit the flag: commitWalletAdjust, commitEditTip, fetchFullHistory and openNewRiderProfile. Every in-place refresh therefore adds a stack entry pointing at the profile you are already on.
findings.impact: Pressing Back after adjusting a wallet or editing a tip returns the operator to the same profile, and repeated edits can silently fill the 40-entry navStack cap.

findings.title: Subscription route is looked up by rider, not by subscription
findings.detail: buildSubProfile resolves the Route row with DB.upcomingSubTrips.find(t => t.rider === d.rider) rather than matching the subscription id, falling back to a dash.
findings.impact: A rider holding two subscriptions sees the same route printed on both subscription profiles, which is the wrong route on at least one of them.

findings.title: The 360 profile cannot be localised at all
findings.detail: The p-profile markup carries no data-i18n attributes, not even on the Back button, and all five body builders concatenate hardcoded English into HTML strings injected via innerHTML. The data-i18n sweep that translates static markup has nothing to attach to.
findings.impact: The app's most-visited drill-down screen is English-only, and localising it means rewriting all five builders rather than adding attributes.

findings.title: Ticket creation from a profile writes no audit entry
findings.detail: createTicketFor unshifts a new ticket into DB.tickets, stamps the SLA and runs the auto-reply, but never calls logAction. Every other state-changing handler reachable from the profile (flag, unflag, suspend, reinstate, wallet adjust, tip edit, complaint resolve) does.
findings.impact: Tickets opened on a customer's behalf leave no trace in the activity log, so who opened them and when cannot be reconstructed.

findings.title: Tickets opened from a driver profile are stamped as rider tickets
findings.detail: createTicketFor hardcodes the thread role as 'rider' and the agent as Sarah Al-Rashid. The driver action bar passes a driver id as entityId, so a driver-originated ticket carries a rider role on its first thread message.
findings.impact: Ticket routing, SLA reporting and any role-based reply template downstream see a driver contact as a rider contact.

findings.title: An overturned rating cannot always be removed from the average
findings.detail: The recomputation runs only when drv.ratingCount is greater than 1, using ((rating*n)-given)/(n-1) clamped to 1..5. When the count is missing or 1 the code sets averageAdjusted false and leaves the stored average untouched, voiding only the individual score. The in-code rationale states that a seeded average with no denominator cannot be un-averaged.
findings.impact: A captain can win a rating dispute and still carry the unfair score in their displayed average, with only a small meta note explaining why.

findings.title: Cases are never de-duplicated
findings.detail: commitRatingDispute can be run repeatedly on the same tripId with no guard. Suspension appeals are de-duplicated only in the UI - the row hides the File appeal button when an Open appeal already exists, but commitDriverAppeal itself has no check and is reachable from the Plan-commitment row menu.
findings.impact: The open-case queue, the SLA clock set and the contact-volume counters can all be inflated by duplicate filings on the same underlying event.

findings.title: Fairness case filing is completely ungated
findings.detail: PAGE_PERMISSIONS has no fairness key, so requirePagePerm is never called for this page. Only decideFairness checks a permission, and it uses the global approve_drivers key. commitRatingDispute, commitReportRider and commitDriverAppeal all write to DB.fairnessCases, DB.contacts and DB.auditLog with no permission check at all.
findings.evidence: if(!requirePerm('approve_drivers'))return;   // the only permission check in the module
findings.impact: Anyone who can reach the page can open coded cases that count toward contact volume and CPT reporting, and can file appeals against a suspension on a captain's behalf.

findings.title: Fleet average earnings per hour is an unweighted mean of rates
findings.detail: renderCaptainEconomics computes avg as the sum of each captain's perHour divided by the row count, rather than total earnings divided by total engaged hours. A captain with a single five-minute trip carries the same weight as one with four hundred trips, and the under-earner threshold of 0.7 times that average is derived from it.
findings.impact: The displayed fleet benchmark and every red under-earner flag derived from it can be materially wrong, and nothing in the on-screen caveat mentions the weighting.

findings.title: No rationale is ever captured for a fairness decision
findings.detail: fcNew initialises c.rationale to null and nothing in decideFairness or the rendered rows ever writes or displays it, despite the module header comment and the gate copy resting the whole design on the captain being served a reason.
findings.impact: An overturned or upheld case records who decided and when but never why, which is precisely the record an appeal process needs to hold up.

findings.title: Overturning a rider report has no corrective path
findings.detail: decideFairness has corrective branches for Rating dispute and Suspension appeal only. A Rider report is simply marked Overturned; the gate copy says the report is dismissed and no action is taken against the rider, which happens to be true only because nothing acted on the report in the first place.
findings.evidence: corrective branches are guarded by c.kind==='Rating dispute' and by DB.drivers[c.driverId].suspended
findings.impact: A rider report that was already feeding the rider no-show counter on the rider profile keeps feeding it after being overturned, because riderNoShowCount filters on reasonCode and not on case status.

findings.title: The sidebar case counter goes stale after a decision
findings.detail: #sbb-fairness is computed only inside updateContactsBadge. renderFairnessPage never touches it, unlike the coverage, compliance and safety pages which set their own badges inline. seedFairness even calls updateContactsBadge explicitly to work around a boot-order race.
findings.impact: Deciding the last open case from this page leaves the sidebar showing a non-zero queue until some other code path calls updateContactsBadge.

findings.title: Upholding a case does nothing beyond setting a string
findings.detail: The uphold path sets status, decision, decidedBy and decidedAtMs, logs fairness_decision and re-renders. No strike is recorded, nothing is written to the driver record, and no notification is sent - although the gate consequence copy states that the captain is notified of the outcome.
findings.impact: The consequence promised to the operator in the confirmation dialog does not happen, so a captain is never actually told the original decision stands.

findings.title: A rejected emergency claim captures no grounds
findings.detail: decideEmergency writes only status, decidedBy and decidedAtMs on rejection, while its own toast says the grounds must be served to the captain and the gate copy calls a rejection with no reason the way appeal processes lose their legitimacy.
findings.evidence: toast(uphold ? 'Upheld - forfeiture reversed and the strike removed' : 'Rejected - grounds must be served to the captain', ...)
findings.impact: The appeal route's stated legitimacy condition is unenforceable because the reason is never recorded anywhere.

findings.title: acceptEmergency is later wrapped with idempotency and ledger posting
findings.detail: A second assignment near the end of the file wraps acceptEmergency in withIdempotency and, when the dispatch reaches Accepted, posts a double-entry pair for the replacement cover and a second pair for the recovery from the absent captain. The doc's money-mechanics section documents only the original function.
findings.impact: The module's real settlement behaviour is richer than documented, and the blanket claim that money is only ever logged does not hold for the emergency-cover path.

findings.title: Captain responses to a dispatch are operator-simulated
findings.detail: The only way a dispatch is accepted or declined is by an operator pressing buttons labelled Simulate accept and Simulate decline on the dispatch row. There is no captain-facing channel, so the entire money settlement including the rider credit is triggered by an ops click.
findings.impact: The dispatch flow's timings, acceptance rates and net-cost figures are all products of manual simulation rather than real captain behaviour.

findings.title: Policy-save validation multiplies the limit by zero
findings.detail: The statutory ceiling check reads tiers[1].freezeDays >= regulatorCancelLimit*0 && tiers[1].freezeDays > 30. The left comparison is always true, so the guard reduces to a bare freezeDays > 30 test with no reference to the regulator limit it claims to enforce.
findings.impact: Raising the regulator limit or lowering it has no effect on the warning, so an internal freeze can be configured past the statutory ceiling without the warning firing correctly.

findings.title: Probation is recorded but has no behaviour
findings.detail: reinstateProbationary deletes planAccess and writes planProbation and planProbationUntilMs with a hardcoded 30-day window, logging that one absence during probation removes access again. Neither field is read anywhere, and recordAbsence has no probation branch.
findings.impact: A reinstated captain who reoffends during probation is treated exactly like any first-tier offender, contradicting the audit line written at reinstatement.

findings.title: Terms acceptance is implemented but unreachable
findings.detail: acceptPlanTerms unshifts a record into DB.termsAcceptances and logs plan_terms_accepted, but no UI calls it and DB.termsAcceptances is never rendered - while the saveCommitPolicy gate tells the operator that captains must re-accept if the terms version changes.
findings.impact: There is no way to see or record which captains accepted which version of PLAN-TERMS, so the retroactivity promise in the gate cannot be honoured.

findings.title: The 45-second dispatch acceptance window is display-only
findings.detail: dispatchWindowSec appears in the offer log line and in the Settings form, but nothing expires an unanswered dispatch offer or advances offerIndex on a timeout. The only real expiry in the module is the 20-minute offerWindowMin applied to standing backup offers by offerState.
findings.impact: A dispatch offered to an unresponsive captain stays Offered indefinitely while the rider waits, with the UI implying an automatic escalation that never happens.

findings.title: The captain-preview card is hardwired to the first fixture driver
findings.detail: The card that shows what the captain sees before deciding calls exposureLineHTML(Object.keys(DB.drivers)[0]), so it always renders the first driver in the seed object regardless of context.
findings.impact: The exposure amounts, tier label and strike count on that card belong to an arbitrary captain and mean nothing for anyone else.

findings.title: The driver share is a hardcoded 80 percent in two money formulas
findings.detail: absenceExposure and commitmentReserve both compute the captain's share as paid*0.8. EYVAR_COMMISSION_PCT exists in the same file and subEconomics uses it, but neither function references either.
findings.impact: Changing the platform commission leaves every forfeiture, exposure and reserve figure on this page computed at the old rate, and the two numbers would silently disagree with the Finance surfaces.

findings.title: The regulator window ignores the configured counter window
findings.detail: regulatorCount hardcodes nowMs() - 30*86400000 instead of reading counterWindowDays, which is exposed as an editable setting and used by absenceCount.
findings.impact: Changing the absence counter window in Settings silently desynchronises the internal counter from the statutory one that is meant to track it.

findings.title: The seven-day appeal window is never enforced
findings.detail: appealWindowDays is stated in the recordAbsence gate copy as the window in which a captain may file an emergency claim, but openEmergencyClaim performs no age check on the absence event, and the absence row keeps offering the File emergency claim button as long as the event is not waived and has no claim.
findings.evidence: function openEmergencyClaim(absId){  // no comparison of ev.tsMs against appealWindowDays
findings.impact: The policy boundary the operator is told about in the confirmation gate does not exist in code, in either direction.

findings.title: The sidebar leg counter goes stale after confirming a leg
findings.detail: #sbb-commit is computed only inside updateContactsBadge, guarded on DB.commitPolicy because pendingConfirmations is hoisted and callable before this module's data exists. renderCommitmentPage never updates it.
findings.impact: Working through the confirmation queue on the page leaves the sidebar count unchanged until some unrelated code path refreshes it.

findings.title: The two absence counters disagree about decayed strikes
findings.detail: absenceCount excludes events with waived or decayed set. regulatorCount excludes only waived, so a strike that decayed out of the internal counter still counts toward the GAT statutory counter shown in the same table row.
findings.evidence: e.driverId===driverId && e.tsMs>=since && !e.waived  // regulatorCount omits the !e.decayed test
findings.impact: A captain can show zero live strikes and a non-zero regulator count in adjacent columns with no explanation, and the source does not state whether this is intentional.

findings.title: Tier demotion is promised but never applied
findings.detail: The second tier carries demoteTier true, which is read only by exposureLineHTML for the deterrence string and by renderCommitSettings for the read-only ladder text. No code path ever changes d.lvl.
findings.impact: The captain-facing deterrence line and the settings page both state a consequence that the system does not deliver.

findings.title: #sbb-coverage is stale until the page is visited and never changes CSS class
findings.detail: The badge is assigned only inside renderCoveragePage(); refreshNavCounts() (L9392-L9409) and the tick loop never touch it, so it shows the static markup value until the operator navigates to Coverage. It also only ever has its textContent set — the literal class="sb-badge a" from L516 stands permanently, so it renders in its active style even at 0.
findings.impact: The sidebar under-reports exposed subscriptions for the whole session unless the page is opened, and shows an alert-styled badge when there is nothing to alert about.

findings.title: Detected slot overlaps have no remedy in the UI
findings.detail: When a driver holds two or more subscriptions in one half-hour bucket the cell renders a red '⚠ N overlap' badge whose title lists the subscription ids, but no reassign, split or resolve control is offered anywhere on the page.
findings.impact: The page identifies the exact failure mode it exists to prevent and then leaves the operator with no in-product way to act on it.

findings.title: No cap on how many subscriptions one captain can back
findings.detail: The candidate modal displays each candidate's existing load as `Object.keys(DB.subBackups).filter(k=>DB.subBackups[k]===c.id).length` ('Backup for N other subscription(s)'), but nothing in assignBackup or commitBackup rejects or warns above any threshold.
findings.impact: One captain can be registered as the backup for every active plan, which is indistinguishable from having no backup coverage the moment that captain is unavailable.

findings.title: promoteBackup never increments driverChanges
findings.detail: promoteBackup permanently reassigns the rider's captain (`s.driver=bak`) but does not touch the driverChanges counter, unlike the two other places a captain changes — recordAbsence (L16704) and acceptEmergency (L17343).
findings.impact: A permanent captain change made from Coverage never registers against the same-captain promise metric, so that metric under-reports continuity breaks.

findings.title: slotOf() strips AM/PM without converting to 24-hour time
findings.detail: The scheduled time is normalised with `String(ust.scheduledTime).replace(/ ?[AP]M/i,'')`, which removes the meridiem marker but leaves the number untouched, so '7:30 PM' becomes '7:30' and buckets into the 07:30 morning slot.
findings.impact: Any evening subscription leg is counted as morning-peak occupancy, which can manufacture a phantom double-booking or hide a real one.

findings.title: Slots outside 06:00-08:30 silently collapse into the 07:00 column
findings.detail: After bucketing, `return slots.indexOf(slot)>=0?slot:'07:00';` sends any out-of-range time to the 07:00 column rather than dropping it or widening the grid. The same '07:00' literal is also the fallback when a rider has no upcoming trip at all.
findings.impact: The 07:00 column is inflated by both unknown and out-of-window trips, so overlap warnings there are unreliable in both directions.

findings.title: Two different definitions of 'the active book'
findings.detail: activeSubsList() (this page) uses a blacklist — anything whose status does not match /cancel/i — while backupCoverage() (L17482, used by the Plan-commitment coverage card) uses a whitelist /active|expiring/i. With the shipped seven-row fixture both yield the same five rows, so the divergence is latent.
findings.impact: Any new subscription status (paused, on-hold, trial) would be counted by one surface and not the other, reproducing the two-pages-two-numbers problem the shared subIsCovered was introduced to fix.

findings.title: A blank date field cannot clear an existing value
findings.detail: saveDriverDocDates writes each field only when it is non-empty (`if(v)docs[dt[0]]=v;`), so clearing an input and saving silently retains the old date. There is no other UI that removes a date.
findings.impact: There is no way to mark a document as 'not on file' once a date exists, so a mistakenly-entered expiry can only be replaced, never withdrawn.

findings.title: A missing expiry date renders as a healthy green 'NaNd' badge
findings.detail: complianceScan guards with `if(!exp) return;` (L13301) but renderCompliancePage does not — it calls docState(docDaysLeft(exp)) directly. For a missing key, new Date('undefinedT00:00:00') is Invalid Date, every comparison against NaN is false, and docState falls through to its green branch.
findings.impact: A partial record — creatable via saveDriverDocDates, which skips blank fields — reads as compliant in green, and because complianceScan also ignores missing dates a driver with no dates at all is silently 'compliant' and never auto-suspended.

findings.title: Automatic un-suspension is completely silent
findings.detail: The suspend branch writes a suspension record, a logAction('auto_suspend',…) entry and a persistent bell notification. The lift branch deletes the record and does nothing else — no audit entry, no notification, no toast.
findings.evidence: delete DB.complianceSuspensions[d]; /* docs renewed — lift the automatic hold */
findings.impact: A driver returning to dispatch leaves no trace in the Activity log, so the record of who was off the road and for how long is one-sided and unauditable.

findings.title: compliance.view is declared but never enforced
findings.detail: PAGE_PERMISSIONS.compliance declares {key:'view',label:'View compliance'} and defaultPagePerms grants it to every role, but no canPage('compliance','view') call exists anywhere — neither go() (L8779-L8827) nor renderCompliancePage checks it.
findings.impact: The permissions matrix in Settings shows a control that does nothing; a role with view removed still sees the whole fleet's document status.

findings.title: driverRiskScore uses an undocumented 14-day document band
findings.detail: Compliance's only banding formula is docState with 0/7/30 thresholds. driverRiskScore (Predictive) subtracts 40 for an expired document and otherwise 20 when `worst <= 14` — a fourth threshold that appears in no Compliance rule and in no UI label.
findings.impact: A driver can be marked at-risk in Predictive on a threshold that no Compliance surface explains or exposes, making the score unreconcilable with the page it derives from.

findings.title: markDocRenewed() has no call site
findings.detail: grep of markDocRenewed returns exactly one hit — its own definition at L13370. It picks the single document with the fewest days left and pushes its expiry one year out from the demo clock. The source itself documents the superseding at L10989-L10991 ('auto-guessed a year out (Compliance's old "mark renewed")') and L11048-L11049 ('replacing the old "guess a year out" shortcut').
findings.impact: Roughly twelve lines of permission-gated, audit-writing renewal logic are unreachable; a reader auditing renewal paths must know to ignore it.

findings.title: The auto-suspend reason string is never upgraded for an already-suspended driver
findings.detail: The guard `if(expired.length && !DB.complianceSuspensions[d])` skips the write whenever any suspension already exists, including Safety's 'Precautionary — pending INC-xxx investigation' (L13468). Because that string does not begin with 'Expired', the un-suspend branch will not clear it either — but neither is the expiry ever recorded.
findings.impact: A driver who is precautionarily suspended and then has a document expire shows only the incident reason; if the incident suspension is later cleared by hand the expired document is not re-detected on the same scan pass that cleared it.

findings.title: 'Closed this month' has no month filter
findings.detail: The tile counts `DB.incidents.filter(i=>i.status==='closed').length` — every closed incident ever. The data model has no closed-at or closable date field and `opened` is free text ('Yesterday 18:40', '22 Jun'), so the label cannot be made true without a schema change.
findings.impact: A metric presented as a monthly throughput figure is a lifetime total and will only ever grow.

findings.title: A permission denial leaves the protocol checkbox visually ticked
findings.detail: toggleIncStep's gate returns before renderSafetyPage(), so the checkbox keeps the state the browser already applied while DB.incidents is unchanged.
findings.impact: After a denial toast the UI shows a safety protocol step as completed when it is not, until some other action forces a re-render.

findings.title: filterSafety('all') is unreachable from the UI
findings.detail: _safetyFilter defaults to 'all' and the predicate has an 'all' fall-through (`return true;`), but a grep of the file finds no call to filterSafety with 'all' — tiles 1-3 set open/critical/closed and tile 4 navigates to Compliance. The filter is module-scope and survives navigating away and back.
findings.impact: Once any tile is clicked, the only way back to the unfiltered incident queue is a full page reload.

findings.title: Inconsistent permission gating across the module's three write actions
findings.detail: precautionSuspend requires both requirePerm('approve_drivers') and requirePagePerm('safety','suspend'); closeIncident requires only requirePagePerm('safety','close') with no broad-permission check; toggleIncStep requires only requirePagePerm('safety','update_steps').
findings.impact: Finalising a safety record — an irreversible action with no reopen path — is the least-gated of the three writes.

findings.title: KPI 2 counts open-critical but its filter is status-agnostic
findings.detail: The tile value is `open.filter(i=>i.severity==='critical').length` (computed over the open subset) while the filter it triggers is `i.severity==='critical'` with no status test.
findings.impact: As soon as any critical incident is closed, clicking a tile reading '1' lists more than one card. Invisible in the seed data because no closed incident is critical.

findings.title: No reopen action despite the confirm text promising one
findings.detail: The close confirmation reads 'This finalizes the record — reopen it manually if new information comes in later', but no reopen handler exists and closed incidents render with zero action buttons and disabled checkboxes.
findings.evidence: if(!confirm('Close incident '+incId+'? This finalizes the record — reopen it manually if new information comes in later.'))return;
findings.impact: The dialog promises a capability the product does not have; new information about a closed safety incident has nowhere to go.

findings.title: precautionSuspend force-completes step 'act' without an incident_step audit entry
findings.detail: The handler overwrites inc.steps.act with {done:true,by:currentUserName(),at:'Just now'} — including over any prior by/at — but writes only logAction('precaution_suspend',…). No matching logAction('incident_step',…) is emitted.
findings.impact: The Activity log shows the incident's step count changing with no step event, and any earlier attribution on step 3 is silently replaced.

findings.title: safety.view is declared but never enforced
findings.detail: PAGE_PERMISSIONS.safety declares {key:'view',label:'View incidents'} and defaultPagePerms grants it to every role, but no canPage('safety','view') call exists — neither go() nor renderSafetyPage checks it.
findings.impact: The permissions matrix offers a control over SOS and harassment-report visibility that has no effect.

findings.title: The incident queue never sorts by severity
findings.detail: The only sort key is open-before-closed; severity is not consulted. A 'high' open incident can therefore render above a critical SOS.
findings.impact: In a longer queue the life-safety item is not guaranteed to be at the top of the page; the current seed order masks the defect.

findings.title: Two of three seeded incidents reference trips that do not exist
findings.detail: TRP-8977 (INC-013) and TRP-8720 (INC-011) appear only in DB.incidents and DB.lostFound; neither is a key in DB.trips. Only TRP-9012 (INC-014) resolves. INC-011 is closed so its action row never renders, which means one of the two reachable 'Open trip' buttons is broken.
findings.impact: Clicking 'Open trip' on the open accident incident produces toast('No record for TRP-8977','err') instead of the trip record an investigator needs.

findings.title: Un-ticking a step destroys its attribution irrecoverably
findings.detail: The un-tick branch replaces the step object wholesale with {done:false}, discarding by and at. Re-ticking writes the current user and the literal 'Just now', so the record of who originally performed the step is lost — defeating the accountability trail the module's own comment claims at L13444-L13446.
findings.impact: The incident's audit trail can be laundered by any operator with update_steps: untick then retick reassigns authorship of a completed safety step.

findings.title: A wallet-crediting action is gated only on contact_users
findings.detail: commitProcessReferral checks requirePerm('contact_users') and nothing else, then credits two rider wallets via creditRiderWallet at the configured bonus amounts. No finance-shaped permission (process_payouts, manage_settings) is required, and no confirm gate is installed on the commit.
findings.impact: A support-tier role with only messaging permission can move money into rider wallets, and that spend lands directly in the Finance contribution margin.

findings.title: CSAT / NPS card is a static picture describing automation that does not exist
findings.detail: renderCsat writes a fully hardcoded HTML string: CSAT 4.6/5 (n=212), NPS +42 (n=131), plus prose stating CSAT fires on ticket close, NPS on package completion, and detractors (≤6) auto-open a follow-up ticket. No survey trigger exists in setTicketStatus (L2368) or closeConversation (L2398), no NPS trigger exists on package completion, and no auto-ticket code exists.
findings.impact: Two headline satisfaction metrics are presented as measured results with sample sizes; nothing in the panel measures them.

findings.title: getReferralCode(riderId) is never called
findings.detail: grep of getReferralCode returns exactly one hit — its own definition. It would lazily generate and store rider.referralCode from the first word of the rider's name plus the last four digits of the rider id.
findings.impact: No rider ever has a referral code generated or displayed, so the 'referee who used the code' flow is entirely operator-driven with no code to give out.

findings.title: Incentive rules are never evaluated and the tier commission benefit is never applied
findings.detail: Incentive `rule` strings are plain prose, honestly disclosed as manually awarded in the source comment at L13891-L13894 and in the UI footer at L13684. Separately, seed rule INV-3 promises Gold-tier captains 'Commission 20% → 17%', but driverCommissionRate() (L4467) and commissionRateForPlan() (L4461) read only DB.opsConfig.pricing.driverCommissionPct and ignore d.lvl entirely — even though recalcDriverTiers does write d.lvl.
findings.impact: The tier system computes and logs promotions that carry no economic consequence, and the incentive that names the benefit will never deliver it.

findings.title: MSG_SEGMENTS recipient counts are hardcoded and stale by construction
findings.detail: The five segments carry fixed counts (8, 8, 5, 3, 142) baked into a module-level const, never recomputed from DB. Real audience-count helpers exist in Settings — broadcastAudienceCount (L7673) and pushAudienceIds (L7711) — but are not used here. The '142 active subscribers' figure contradicts the live subscription book.
findings.impact: The operator picks an audience by a number that is wrong, and the audit entry records that wrong number as the recipient count.

findings.title: pausePromo is confirm-gated but resumePromo is not
findings.detail: GATE_SWEEP.pausePromo (L20877-L20879) wraps Pause with a danger confirmation listing consequences. resumePromo, which shares the growth.pause_promo permission and puts a campaign back into spend, has no gate entry at all.
findings.impact: Stopping spend requires a confirmation; restarting it does not — the gate is on the safer of the two directions.

findings.title: perUserLimit, target and expires are inert fields
findings.detail: All three are captured at creation and rendered in the table (target as `p.target+' · '+p.perUserLimit+'/user'`, L13523) but no code validates a redemption against the per-user limit, matches a rider against the target, or compares expires to any clock. The 'Specific zone' target option has no accompanying zone selector and is not wired to DB.zones.
findings.impact: A campaign can be configured with eligibility rules and an expiry that the platform will never enforce, so the table communicates constraints that do not exist.

findings.title: Referral bonus amounts have no upper bound and coerce junk to zero
findings.detail: saveReferralConfig reads both bonus fields with parseFloat(...)||0. The markup carries min=0 step=1 but no max, and the ||0 fallback silently turns any non-numeric entry into 0 rather than rejecting it. The action is confirm-gated but the gate does not validate.
findings.impact: A mistyped bonus can be saved at any magnitude and paid on every subsequent referral, or silently zeroed so the programme pays nothing while appearing enabled.

findings.title: Referral qualification is manual and the referrer bonus is uncapped
findings.detail: processReferral's five guards check only that the programme is enabled, both ids are present and different, the referee is not already in the log, and both rider records exist. There is no trip, spend or tenure threshold. Guard 4 caps a referee at one referral for life but places no cap on how many referees one referrer may bring.
findings.impact: One rider can be credited an unbounded number of referrer bonuses, and abuse detection is entirely post-hoc in the Fraud module (shared IP/device check at L5610-L5613), after the money has already been credited.

findings.title: Retention cohorts are a hardcoded matrix with hardcoded narrative
findings.detail: renderCohorts builds its table from a local array of five cohorts (Feb-Jun 2026) with fixed retention percentages, and the footer paragraph quotes those figures in prose. The function never reads DB.subscriptions.
findings.impact: The only retention analysis in the panel is a picture; it will show the same five cohorts regardless of the subscription book's actual state.

findings.title: #sbb-zones is stale until the page is first opened
findings.detail: The badge is written only inside renderZonesPage(), which runs on go('zones') (L8800) or a steering tick while the page is visible (L14186-L14188). refreshNavCounts() (L9392-L9409) updates five other badges via put(...) but not this one, and renderZonesPage is absent from the boot block (L14556-L14600).
findings.impact: The sidebar shows the hardcoded 0 instead of 2 supply-starved zones until the operator navigates to Zones; the same staleness class as sbb-coverage, sbb-compliance, sbb-safety and sbb-predictive.

findings.title: Momentum's 'today' cut-off is a hardcoded date that does not follow the clock
findings.detail: zoneSubMomentum splits requests into today and prior by `parseInt(r.requestedAt.split(' ')[0],10) >= 25`, a literal matching the demo clock's date (25 Jun 2026, REQ_NOW_REF L9555). REQ_NOW_REF is advanced by the tick engine (L9680) but the 25 is not.
findings.impact: As the simulated clock rolls past the 25th the today/prior split stops meaning anything, and the /2 prior-window divisor is likewise pinned to the seed data's ~2-day span.

findings.title: Steering offers are broadcast platform-wide, not to the target zone
findings.detail: steerableDrivers() filters DB.drivers on status!=='pending', absence from DB.complianceSuspensions and !driverLiveState(d).busy. Nothing filters by proximity to zoneName, and the offer record stores the resulting count as sentTo.
findings.impact: Every eligible driver anywhere receives every zone's offer, so the modal's 'The offer goes to N available drivers' is a platform-wide count and the incentive is not actually targeted at repositioning to that district.

findings.title: Steering-offer acceptance is a coin flip, not a driver
findings.detail: tickSteerOffers gives each active offer a 25% chance per tick of one acceptance, incrementing accepted and adding amount to spent, bounded by the cap. The comment at L14172-L14174 is explicit that offers wind down with the demo clock.
findings.impact: The 'N accepted so far' figure, the spend total and the audit entry written when the offer closes all describe simulated activity; unlike promos, the auto-close discipline is at least genuinely implemented.

findings.title: The free action is gated harder than the money-spending one
findings.detail: queueRecruitment requires the broad manage_settings permission (not a zones.* page perm) and is wrapped by GATE_SWEEP.queueRecruitment (L20875-L20876) with a confirmation modal. openSteerOffer/commitSteerOffer require live_ops plus zones.steer and have no confirm gate at all, despite committing a SAR budget.
findings.impact: A role granted live_ops can spend money on a steering offer without confirmation but cannot add a zone to a free recruitment list.

findings.title: The one-offer-per-zone rule is enforced only in the opener
findings.detail: openSteerOffer checks `DB.steerOffers.some(o=>o.zone===zoneName && o.status==='active')` before rendering the modal. commitSteerOffer re-checks only requirePagePerm('zones','steer') and then pushes unconditionally.
findings.impact: Two rapid commits from a stale modal stack two live offers on the same zone, defeating the stated 'one active offer per zone to avoid stacking spend' design rule and doubling the budget exposure.

findings.title: The recruitment queue has no view and no lifecycle
findings.detail: queueRecruitment pushes {zone, queuedAt: fmtReqNowLabel(), status:'Queued'} onto DB.recruitmentQueue. The array has no list view anywhere in the file; it surfaces only as the per-row '📣 Recruitment queued' badge. status is written once and never changed, queuedAt is stored and never rendered, and there is no dequeue, complete or cancel action.
findings.evidence: DB.recruitmentQueue=[]; /* zones actually queued for a driver acquisition campaign */
findings.impact: Queuing is a one-way write: the recruitment team's actual work list is invisible in the panel and a zone can never be un-queued.

findings.title: The supply>0 guard excludes the worst case from 'supply-starved'
findings.detail: The starved predicate `z.supply>0 && z.demand/z.supply>=3` is used in four places — the KPI tile 2 count and sidebar badge (L14133/L14140), the table filter (L14144), the momentum signal (L14065) and Predictive Signals' structural list (L14358). The divide-by-zero guard means a zone with zero available drivers is not counted as starved. Latent: no seed zone has supply===0.
findings.impact: A district with demand and no drivers at all — the maximum-severity case — would be filtered out of every starved view, the sidebar badge and the predictive shortage list.

findings.title: Zones cannot be created, edited or deleted
findings.detail: DB.zones is a hardcoded array with no CRUD UI anywhere in the file — no add/edit/delete modal on this page and none in Settings, despite Settings carrying a 'Cities & zones' tab label (stab.cities, L7918) whose zone half is unimplemented. Adding a district requires editing the HTML source.
findings.impact: The supply/demand map cannot follow the business into a new district without a code change.

findings.title: backfillCreditNotes issues notes with no ledger posting
findings.detail: The ledger postings for a refund live in the recordRefund override (L19962-L19976), not in issueCreditNote. backfillCreditNotes (L15945-L15951) calls issueCreditNote directly for existing refunds that lack a note, so every backfilled note exists with no corresponding contra.refunds / tax.vat_output posting.
findings.impact: Credit notes exist in the tax record with no matching journal entry, so the ledger understates reversed VAT.

findings.title: Contribution card and credit notes are not rendered at boot
findings.detail: The boot sequence calls renderRefundsTable() at L14585 but neither renderContributionCard() nor renderCreditNotes() appears in the boot list (L14565-L14600). Both containers stay empty until the user navigates to the finance page and the go() hook at L8815 fires.
findings.impact: Two of the four cards on the money page are blank on first paint, including the only live financial model on the screen.

findings.title: Credit-note 'unlinked' is a terminal dead end
findings.detail: unlinked is written once, at creation, as !inv (L15879). No code path ever sets it back to false. The modal tells the operator 'This credit note stands alone until finance links it' (L15906) and the ops notification says finance must link it manually (L15888), but no linking UI or function exists anywhere in the file.
findings.impact: A credit note that cannot be filed accumulates permanently, with the product instructing an action that is impossible to perform.

findings.title: DB.payments has no runtime writer
findings.detail: The only writes to DB.payments are the ten seed literals at L2695-L2704 and the per-entity id arrays that reference them. No function creates a payment, and no function mutates a payment's status, so the Paid / Refunded / Pending states are seed-only with no transitions.
findings.impact: The payment collection cannot reflect any real activity; every invoice, LTV and gross-revenue figure derived from it is frozen at seed values.

findings.title: Every refund and credit note carries a frozen demo date
findings.detail: recordRefund writes date:'25 Jun' as a literal with the comment 'frozen demo clock'. issueCreditNote sets issuedAt to entry.date || fmtReqNowLabel(), so it always inherits '25 Jun'. Every credit note issued in a session therefore carries the same date on a document whose purpose is tax-period attribution.
findings.evidence: date:'25 Jun', /* frozen demo clock - matches every other date in the panel */
findings.impact: Credit notes cannot be attributed to the correct tax period, and the refunds ledger has no usable chronology.

findings.title: ledgerReconcile's refund row can never balance
findings.detail: The refunds row compares ops (r2 of the VAT-inclusive DB.refunds total) against accountBalance('contra.refunds') + accountBalance('tax.vat_output')*0. The VAT term is multiplied by zero, so a VAT-inclusive figure is compared against a VAT-exclusive contra balance and row.diff is permanently non-zero by roughly the VAT component.
findings.impact: The reconciliation screen always shows a refund discrepancy, training operators to ignore a control that is supposed to surface real breaks.

findings.title: Money amounts are stored as strings and parsed with parseFloat
findings.detail: DB.payments[*].amount is a string such as '86.50 SAR'. Every consumer parses it with parseFloat (contributionMargin L15721, getOrCreateInvoice L4400, riderLTV L4035). parseFloat('640 SAR') gives 640, but a comma-grouped string such as '1,640.00 SAR' - which does appear in DB.riders[*].stats.totalPaid at L2620 - parses to 1 with no error thrown.
findings.impact: A single locale-formatted amount anywhere in the data silently becomes 1 SAR in every derived total.

findings.title: Refund rows are immutable
findings.detail: renderRefundsTable emits seven display cells per row and no action column - no void, no reverse, no re-issue, no edit. Combined with the single terminal 'Processed' status, a refund created in error cannot be corrected from the UI at all.
findings.impact: An erroneous refund is permanent from the operator's point of view; correction requires direct data manipulation.

findings.title: confirmProcessAll audits the wrong driver count
findings.detail: The preview computes ids = Object.keys(DB.payouts).filter(pending>0) (L7038); the commit recomputes ids = Object.keys(DB.payouts) with no filter (L7051). The money moved is correct because the if(p.pending>0) guard sits inside the loop, but the audit entry reports driversProcessed: ids.length and the summary says '{ids.length} payouts processed', i.e. every driver with a payout record. With the seed this coincides (3 = 3); the moment one driver has a zero balance the audit trail overstates the batch.
findings.impact: The audit record of a bulk money movement misstates how many drivers were actually paid.

findings.title: deductionNote holds a single overwritten slot
findings.detail: p.deductionNote = {amount:d.amount, type:d.type} is an assignment, not a push. Two deductions in one cycle leave only the second visible on the payout row (L8757) and in the payment confirmation modal (L7200).
findings.impact: The operator approving a payment sees an understated summary of what was deducted from it.

findings.title: Escrow progress bar has no zero-guard
findings.detail: The bar width is Math.round(e.tripsCompleted / e.tripsRequired * 100). A hold with tripsRequired 0 yields Infinity or NaN and emits style='width:NaN%'. Every other percentage in the file uses a truthiness guard, e.g. gross ? net/gross*100 : 0 at L15738.
findings.impact: A malformed hold renders a broken progress bar rather than a safe zero.

findings.title: Escrow release destroys the hold rather than archiving it
findings.detail: releaseEscrow calls DB.escrowHolds.splice(idx,1) rather than transitioning the hold to a 'released' state. The record - amount, sub, rider, trips delivered - is gone. Only the free-text logAction summary survives.
findings.impact: Escrow history is unrecoverable after release, so a disputed release cannot be reconstructed from the data.

findings.title: Escrow seed amounts embed a take rate the plan config contradicts
findings.detail: Every seeded hold equals the subscription's paid amount times 0.80: 86.50x0.8=69.20 (SUB-1041), 412.00x0.8=329.60 (SUB-1052), 41.22x0.8=32.976 rounded to 32.98 (SUB-1060), 86.50x0.8=69.20 (SUB-1075). That implies a flat 20% Eyvar commission, but DB.plans.biweekly.eyvarPct is 18 (L2892) and DB.plans.monthly.eyvarPct is 15 (L2894), and SUB-1052 is Bi-weekly Comfort while SUB-1060 is Monthly Comfort. Since no code computes escrow at all, the discrepancy can never be reconciled at runtime.
findings.impact: Either the escrow seed or the plan take-rate configuration is wrong, and the product gives no way to tell which.

findings.title: No partial amounts anywhere on the page
findings.detail: The page contains zero input, select or textarea elements (verified across L968-L1017), and none of the six modals contains an input either: Confirm payment uses p.pending, Process all uses the sum, Release escrow uses e.amount, Apply deduction uses d.amount, the cash modals are display-only, and Record repayment uses the full negated debt. Partial payouts, partial escrow releases, partial deductions and partial repayments are all impossible.
findings.impact: Any real-world part settlement has to be faked or skipped entirely.

findings.title: No reversal path for applied deductions, waived deductions or escalated cash entries
findings.detail: d.status='applied' (L7077) and d.status='waived' (L8989) are both terminal - no function sets a deduction back to pending. commitCashResolve's 'escalated' outcome is likewise terminal, and the modal states the escalation 'cannot be undone from here' (L12162).
findings.impact: Every mistake on this page is permanent from the UI, with no correction workflow.

findings.title: renderCashReconciliation is missing from the boot list
findings.detail: The boot sequence calls renderPayoutsTable (L14578), renderEscrow (L14579) and renderDeductions (L14580) but never renderCashReconciliation. The four cash KPIs (L1004-L1007), the tolerance label (L1010), the cash queue (L1011) and the debt ledger (L1015) stay at their placeholder dash until the page is first opened.
findings.impact: Half the page is blank on first paint, including the driver-debt figures that gate cash collection.

findings.title: The earnings statement is unrelated to the payout it claims to itemise
findings.detail: openEarningsStatement iterates d.trips - the driver's entire trip array (L7217) - while the modal above it settles p.pending, a separate number from DB.payouts. Nothing links a trip to a payout cycle, there is no totals row, and the two figures can never be reconciled. The link that opens it is labelled 'View detailed trip-by-trip earnings statement' (L7206), implying it itemises the payout.
findings.impact: The one screen offered as evidence for a payment amount does not explain that amount, and an operator could reasonably believe it does.

findings.title: The escrow release banner asserts completion unconditionally
findings.detail: The green banner reads 'All {e.tripsRequired} trips completed successfully. This amount will move to {driver}'s available payout balance immediately.' It is rendered unconditionally and uses tripsRequired rather than tripsCompleted, so invoking the modal on a 4-of-5 held hold still claims all 5 trips completed.
findings.impact: The confirmation screen actively misinforms the operator about the very condition the release is supposed to depend on.

findings.title: All wallet, ledger and idempotency state is in-memory only
findings.detail: DB.ledger, DB.idempotency and DB.moneyRejects are initialised as plain in-page objects, and no localStorage, fetch or XMLHttpRequest appears anywhere in the wallet path. A block comment above the ACCOUNTS chart states the accounting layer 'is a model, not an accounting system'.
findings.impact: Every balance, ledger line, duplicate-suppression key and rejected posting is lost on page reload, including the goodwill ceilings that depend on DB.goodwillLedger. This is expected for a demo but means no figure on the page survives a refresh.

findings.title: Audit entries for wallet moves never record the prior balance
findings.detail: Both creditRiderWallet and debitRiderWallet call logAction with before={} and after={balance:w.balance}. auditDiffHTML treats an empty-but-truthy before as a normal change and prints only differing fields, so the balance the wallet held before the movement is never captured.
findings.impact: A wallet balance cannot be reconstructed or reconciled from the activity log alone; an investigator can see what the balance became but never what it was, which defeats the purpose of a before/after audit trail on a money account.

findings.title: Choosing the goodwill reason never refreshes the authority preview
findings.detail: The amount input and the reason-code select both pass compPreview(riderId) as their change handler, but the reason select is built with an empty onChangeExpr. compPreview itself returns immediately unless the currently selected reason already contains 'Goodwill'.
findings.impact: The panel showing the operator's per-case and daily authority, and the rider's 30-day goodwill history, appears only if they pick 'Goodwill / apology credit' first and then go back and edit the amount or reason code. In the natural order of filling the form it is permanently blank.

findings.title: Committing a wallet adjustment navigates away from the wallets list
findings.detail: After a successful credit or debit, commitWalletAdjust calls closeModal(), then openProfile(riderId) unconditionally, then renderRiderWalletsList(). openProfile fires regardless of which page the operator started from.
findings.impact: An operator crediting from the wallets list is thrown onto a rider profile after every single adjustment, and the following renderRiderWalletsList runs against a now-hidden page. Batch work is impossible and a second failed adjustment can go unnoticed.

findings.title: Compensation policy's Operations tier is unreachable dead configuration
findings.detail: DB.compPolicy.roles is keyed Owner / Operations / Support / Finance / default, but the seeded DB.teamUsers roles are Owner / Finance / Support / Support / 'Ops Manager'. compLimitsFor falls back to roles['default'] for any unmatched role name.
findings.impact: Yousef Al-Balawi (USR-5, 'Ops Manager') is silently limited to 50 SAR per case and 300 SAR daily instead of the intended 200/2000, and the Operations row of the compensation-policy table describes limits no user can ever receive.

findings.title: No page-level permission gate on the rider-wallets page
findings.detail: The router branch for rwallets calls renderRiderWalletsList() directly with no requirePagePerm call, unlike the driver-wallets cash actions which call requirePagePerm('wallets','cash_review') and requirePagePerm('wallets','cash_repayment').
findings.impact: Every logged-in operator, regardless of role, sees every rider's balance, their transaction history and the platform's total wallet liability figure.

findings.title: Reading a wallet creates one
findings.detail: getRiderWallet writes {balance:0,transactions:[]} into DB.riders[id] on a plain read. The 360 profile injects walletCardHTML for every non-driver, which calls getRiderWallet unconditionally. The wallets table's row filter is DB.riders[id].wallet, so a materialised empty wallet is enough to add the rider to the list.
findings.impact: The wallets list grows by browsing: an operator who opens ten rider profiles adds ten zero-balance rows, and the 'Riders with a balance … out of N total' KPI denominator becomes meaningless relative to the visible list.

findings.title: The rider is emailed before the ledger posting is validated
findings.detail: sendSystemEmail runs at the end of __origCreditWallet, which completes before the wrapper calls postLedger. If postLedger's guard rejects the posting, the email has already been queued into DB.emailOutbox.
findings.evidence: if(actorNote!==false)sendSystemEmail(riderId,'Your Eyvar wallet was topped up 💳','Hi '+r.name+',\n\n'+amount.toFixed(2)+' SAR was added to your Eyvar wallet.
findings.impact: The rider is told their balance rose even when the accounting side of the transaction was refused, producing a customer-facing promise the ledger does not back.

findings.title: The wallet duplicate-suppression window is one wall-clock second
findings.detail: Both wallet idempotency keys embed Math.floor(nowMs()/1000). Two identical credits about 1.1 seconds apart produce different keys and both execute in full.
findings.impact: The protection catches only double-clicks landing inside the same second; a slow double-submit or a retried request a moment later double-credits the rider.

findings.title: 'Critical' priority renders in the neutral grey badge
findings.detail: rcPriority maps T1 to 'Critical' and createTicket writes that value verbatim. Both badge maps (queue row and detail header) handle only High → b-red and Medium → b-amber, so Critical falls through to b-grey, the same class as Low. Re-coding coerces Critical to High, so the value survives only on freshly created T1 tickets.
findings.evidence: rcPriority(code): T1→'Critical', T2→'High', T3→'Medium', T4→'Low' (L14745-L14748); badge map handles High→b-red, Medium→b-amber, else b-grey
findings.impact: In the queue, a Critical safety ticket is visually indistinguishable from a Low renewal query. The create and re-code paths also disagree about whether Critical exists as a stored value.

findings.title: 'Waiting on customer' has no setter, so the SLA pause branch is unreachable
findings.detail: The status is offered as a filter option in renderTkFilterSelect and is the sole trigger for slaMarkStatus's pause bookkeeping (pausedSinceMs / pausedMs), but no button, modal or bulk action ever assigns it to t.status.
findings.evidence: tiers.T2 = {…, pauseOnCustomer:true}  /* the pause path keys on status==='Waiting on customer', which nothing sets */
findings.impact: The SLA resolution clock can never be paused through the UI, so tickets legitimately blocked on a customer reply keep accruing elapsed time and eventually breach. The pauseOnCustomer flag on three of the four tiers is dead configuration.

findings.title: Bulk 'Assign to me' writes a field nothing displays
findings.detail: bulkAssignMe sets t.assignee to the current user's name and logs ticket_assigned per ticket. The queue row and the detail Ticket-info kvCard both render t.agent, a separate field that bulk-assign never touches and that createTicket hardcodes to 'Sarah Al-Rashid'.
findings.impact: The operator sees a success toast and an audit entry, but the ticket continues to show the original agent everywhere in the UI — a user-facing action that visibly does nothing.

findings.title: createTicketFor never re-renders the ticket queue
findings.detail: createTicket ends with closeModal();renderTickets(); createTicketFor omits the renderTickets() call. It is the commit function for openSupportTicket, openLowRatingTicket and openDesyncTicket.
findings.evidence: closeModal();renderTickets();  /* present in createTicket L2436, absent from createTicketFor */
findings.impact: A ticket raised from a trip profile, a low-rating card or a desync card does not appear in the queue until something else triggers a re-render, so the agent cannot confirm it was created.

findings.title: Every reason picker shares one hard-coded hidden field id
findings.detail: reasonSelectHTML(cselId,selected,onChangeExpr) always emits the hidden field with id 'nt-reason' regardless of the wrapper id passed, and gvRC() reads document.getElementById('nt-reason'). The five distinct wrappers (csel-nt-reason, csel-nt-reason2, csel-chg-reason, csel-bulk-reason, csel-lr-reason, csel-ds-reason) all collide on that one id.
findings.evidence: 'Search 38 reason codes…',onChangeExpr||null,null);   /* inside reasonSelectHTML, which always emits fieldId 'nt-reason' */
findings.impact: The design works only because exactly one modal is ever open at a time. Any future surface that renders two reason pickers simultaneously would silently read the wrong one and stamp the wrong reason code, SLA targets and script onto the ticket.

findings.title: Every ticket and every agent reply is attributed to a hardcoded name
findings.detail: createTicket, createTicketFor and sendTicketReply all write 'Sarah Al-Rashid' as the agent / thread author instead of resolving the current user from CURRENT_USER_ID or DB.teamUsers.
findings.impact: The conversation thread and the Assigned-agent field are wrong for every user except USR-1, so a customer-facing transcript credits work to the wrong person and the ticket cannot be attributed to whoever actually handled it.

findings.title: Reopening a paused ticket leaves it paused forever
findings.detail: slaMarkReopen increments reopenCount, clears resolvedAtMs and empties slaBreaches, but does not clear pausedSinceMs. slaState then adds (now - pausedSinceMs) to the paused total on every evaluation.
findings.evidence: slaMarkReopen(t): reopenCount++, resolvedAtMs=null, slaBreaches=[]  /* pausedSinceMs untouched */
findings.impact: A reopened ticket that had been paused accumulates unbounded paused time, so its resolution clock effectively stops and it can never breach or appear as at-risk.

findings.title: Ticket creation, replies and resolution write no audit entry
findings.detail: createTicket, createTicketFor, sendTicketReply and setTicketStatus never call logAction. Only closeConversation (ticket_closed), reopenTicket (ticket_reopened), commitChangeReason (ticket_reason_changed), the bulk operations, commitMassEvent, slaSweep breaches and toggleScriptStep produce audit entries.
findings.impact: The most common support actions leave no trace in the activity log. Who resolved a ticket, who replied to a customer and who opened a ticket cannot be established after the fact — only who closed or reopened it.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — no persistence layer for tickets
findings.detail: Every ticket write targets in-memory DB.* structures. The source doc reports that no fetch, XMLHttpRequest, localStorage or backend call was found for tickets; 'DB path' throughout means the in-page object graph. This was carried through from the doc and not exhaustively re-confirmed here.
findings.impact: Every ticket, thread message, SLA clock, ownership claim and script-progress record is lost on reload.

findings.title: Dispute claim and evidence text are injected as raw HTML
findings.detail: renderDisputes concatenates d.claim and each evidence pair directly into the card markup with no escaping.
findings.evidence: {id:'DSP-06',sub:'SUB-1052b',claim:'"Charged for Comfort, driver arrived in Economy vehicle"',…}
findings.impact: Currently inert because both disputes are hand-authored seed data, but the field is the natural landing place for a rider-submitted claim, which would make it a stored-XSS surface in an operator session.

findings.title: Lost & Found advances immediately with no confirmation and no reversal
findings.detail: advanceLF checks the page permission, moves l.status one step along LF_FLOW, re-renders, audits and toasts. There is no confirmAction gate, no undo, no backwards transition and no terminal 'not found / unrecoverable' state.
findings.impact: A single mis-click marks a customer's item as returned when it has not been, and there is no way to correct the record. An item that is genuinely lost forever stays stuck in 'searching' with no closing state.

findings.title: The arrival-evidence lookup key works only because traces are hand-seeded under subscription ids
findings.detail: renderDisputes and openArrivalEvidence both key on d.trip||d.sub. Neither seeded dispute defines a trip field, so the subscription id is always used — and seedArrivalTraces deliberately seeds traces under 'SUB-1075' and 'SUB-1052b' to match.
findings.impact: The telemetry verdict — the centrepiece of the 'evidence-first' model, and the line that appears inside the confirmation gate — silently renders nothing for any dispute whose trace was not hand-seeded, including any real dispute that carries a trip id.

findings.title: The dispute outcome is written but never rendered
findings.detail: resolveDispute sets d.outcome to 'refund', 'reject' or 'goodwill'. renderDisputes shows only a status badge — blue 'Open' when status==='open', green 'Resolved' otherwise — and drops the entire right-hand column once resolved. No renderer reads d.outcome.
findings.impact: After resolution the card cannot tell an operator whether the claim was upheld, rejected or settled at 50 %; that decision is recoverable only by searching the activity log.

findings.title: Two cards on the same page enforce different permissions
findings.detail: resolveDispute requires requirePerm('manage_subscriptions') AND requirePagePerm('support','manage'); advanceLF requires only requirePagePerm('support','manage'). manage_subscriptions is a Subscriptions permission borrowed for a Support action.
findings.impact: A support agent granted support.manage can advance a lost item but is blocked from resolving a dispute unless they also hold a subscriptions permission — the grant labelled 'Resolve tickets & disputes' does not in fact allow resolving disputes.

findings.title: A priority call produces no contact row, so it is invisible to CPT
findings.detail: logPriorityCall (L9161-L9165) writes only a logAction('priority_call', ...) entry and toasts. It never calls logContact, so nothing lands in DB.contacts. priorityCall itself (L9149) is a purely cosmetic modal — a pulsing 'Calling — HH:MM' pill whose time is captured once at open and never updated — with 13 call sites across the panel.
findings.impact: Every '📞 Call' button in the panel is invisible to contacts-per-1,000-trips, the channel mix and average handling time — the page's core metric systematically under-counts outbound contact.

findings.title: A T1 (Critical) code can never register a first-response breach
findings.detail: slaState computes frBreached as !obj.firstResponseAtMs && frMs > 0 && elapsedFr > frMs. DB.slaPolicy.tiers.T1 sets firstResponseMin:0 (L14652), and CAP_CONDUCT, TRP_GHOST_COMPLETE, SAF_RIDER_UNSAFE and SAF_ACCIDENT all carry an explicit fr:0. With frMs === 0 the guard short-circuits and the flag can never be set.
findings.impact: The strictest SLA tier — covering safety incidents and captain misconduct — has the weakest first-response enforcement: no breach fires, no notification is pushed, no sla_breach audit entry is written.

findings.title: All eight reason pickers emit the same hidden field id
findings.detail: reasonSelectHTML(cselId, selected, onChangeExpr) hard-codes fieldId='nt-reason' on its customSelectHTML call (L14761), and customSelectHTML emits the hidden value input as id=fieldId (L5352). gvRC() (L14750) then reads getElementById('nt-reason'). Eight pickers — new-ticket (L2423, L2546), change-reason (L14894), low-rating (L15314), bulk (L16188), log-contact (L16223), desync (L16448) and wrap-up (L20286) — all emit the same id. The source comment at L14749 acknowledges the pattern ('Reads the reason picker in whichever ticket modal is open'). Nothing in this build mounts two at once, since #modal-content holds one modal, so the collision is latent rather than live.
findings.evidence: the id is a constant rather than derived from cselId, so two mounted pickers would give getElementById two candidates
findings.impact: Any future change that renders two reason pickers simultaneously would make every wrap-up and contact silently take its code from the wrong control, with no error.

findings.title: Declaring a mass event leaves the CPT table and SLA list stale
findings.detail: commitMassEvent closes the modal and calls renderTickets() and renderContactsExtra() at L16134, but never renderContactsPage(). Since the commit pauses the SLA clocks on every grouped non-master ticket, the breaching/at-risk figures and the exposure list it just changed are not refreshed until the next 15-second slaSweep.
findings.impact: For up to 15 seconds the operator sees the pre-grouping breach counts immediately after the action that was supposed to fix them.

findings.title: Dismissing the screen-pop orphans the pending ring record
findings.detail: The screen-pop's close control calls closeModal() directly (L20231) and the Open 360° footer button calls closeModal(); openProfile(hit.id) (L20234). Neither clears _pendingRing; only answerCall (L20245) and abandonCall (L20255) do. The stale ring record therefore survives and is consumed by the next answerCall, whose waitSec is computed from the OLD ring timestamp.
findings.impact: A falsely inflated speed-to-answer is recorded on an unrelated later call, distorting both ASA and the service-level percentage.

findings.title: handledMin is patched by array position, not by contact id
findings.detail: Both commitWrapUp (L20313) and commitLogContact (L16238) write to DB.contacts[0] on the assumption that their own logContact call just unshifted there. logContact returns nothing usable for this and the two statements are not atomic with respect to any other logContact call (the SLA sweep, auto-replies, ticket stamping and eight other modules all call it).
findings.impact: Any interleaved logContact attaches the measured handling time to the wrong contact, corrupting the Avg handling figure on the channel strip.

findings.title: logDriverCall mutates trip state with no permission check and no audit entry
findings.detail: window.logDriverCall (L8559-L8571) writes t.driverStatus and t.unavailReason on the matched DB.upcomingSubTrips record, closes the modal, re-renders readiness and can chain into resolveUnavailable. It contains no requirePerm call and no logAction call — verified by reading the whole function body.
findings.impact: A trip-level state change that can trigger a reassignment cascade leaves no record of who made it and is available to any operator regardless of role.

findings.title: Most priorityCall call sites pass a name where an entity id is expected
findings.detail: priorityCall(name, context, entityId) has 13 call sites; only three (L11780, L11781, L3376) pass an entityId. The remaining ten pass only a display name. logPriorityCall then audits against entityId||name (L9163), so the audit entry's entityId is a person's name string. The source itself documents this bug class at L20547-L20551, noting the renewal call site 'would log against nothing' and that 'it never surfaced because no seeded subscription scores below 40 — a latent bug hiding behind demo data'.
findings.impact: Audit rows for calls are keyed by name rather than id, so resolveId's entity link is non-deterministic and auditForEntity can never surface those calls on the right profile.

findings.title: The at-risk filter does not exclude update-breached tickets
findings.detail: Both renderContactsPage (L15017) and updateContactsBadge (L14966) define atRisk as slaState(t) && !s.frBreached && !s.resBreached && s.resPct >= DB.slaPolicy.atRiskPct. updBreached is not in the exclusion set, so a ticket whose update clock has already breached but whose resolution clock is past 75% qualifies for both the breaching filter and the atRisk filter.
findings.impact: Such a ticket appears twice in the concatenated SLA-exposure list and is double-counted in the 'N more at risk' KPI sub-label.

findings.title: Two different definitions of 'open ticket' coexist on the same page
findings.detail: renderContactsPage filters open tickets as t.status!=='Resolved' && t.status!=='Closed' (L15015), while updateContactsBadge — which drives the sidebar badge for the same page — filters as !t.resolvedAtMs (L14962). The two diverge whenever a ticket's status text is changed without slaMarkStatus running to set resolvedAtMs, or vice versa.
findings.impact: The sidebar badge and the on-page KPI can disagree about how many tickets are breaching, with no way for an operator to tell which is right.

findings.title: Wrap-up writes a contact channel value that has no label
findings.detail: screenPop is called with channel 'inbound' (from onIncomingCall, L20194) or 'whatsapp' (L20198). answerCall stores that raw value as sess.channel (L20246), and commitWrapUp passes it straight into logContact at L20310. A wrapped phone call therefore lands in DB.contacts with channel:'inbound', a value absent from the chLabel map at L16250 and from the log-contact picker's option list. Only 'whatsapp' happens to match a real channel key.
findings.impact: The channel-mix strip renders a bare unlabelled 'inbound' counter alongside the labelled channels, and phone calls wrapped through the console are never counted as phone_in.

findings.title: No permission gate anywhere on the page or its three actions
findings.detail: The router branch at L8788 checks nothing. assignManually (L11871) checks nothing — its only guards are the soft _locking flag and the claimedBy ownership check, neither of which is audited. showNearbyDriversMap (L8354) checks nothing. openTicketDetail (L8879) was not read. The first requirePerm on this path is requirePerm('live_ops') inside commitRequestAssign at L11884, two clicks away. Neither buildInterventionItems, renderInterventionsPage, assignManually nor showNearbyDriversMap appears in installActionGates (L17853+) or GATE_SWEEP (L20769+).
findings.impact: Any operator who reaches the page can take ownership claims on ride requests and open the driver picker for any trip without a permission check or an audit entry.

findings.title: refreshOwnershipSurfaces calls a function that does not exist
findings.detail: L19054 reads: if((pg==='dashboard'||pg==='interventions')&&typeof renderInterventions==='function')renderInterventions(); Grep for renderInterventions (word-bounded, excluding renderInterventionsPage) returns exactly one hit — that line — and no definition anywhere. The typeof guard turns it into a permanent silent no-op.
findings.impact: Ownership and claim changes never refresh either the dashboard intervention widget or this page, so a claimed item keeps looking unclaimed until an unrelated render happens.

findings.title: The 31-60 minute watch band is unreachable for a not-moving driver
findings.detail: tripScenario is evaluated top-down. Branch 3 ('late') requires minutesUntil <= 30 && driverStatus === 'not_started'. Branch 5 ('watch') claims minutesUntil <= 90 && driverStatus === 'not_started' and is NOT a key in the builder's scCfg map (L9491-L9495), so it is silently dropped at L9500. A not-started driver 45 minutes out therefore produces key 'watch' and never appears, even though the builder's own doc-comment at L9427 promises 'driver issues with 30-60 min window: time to act before it becomes red'.
findings.impact: Only 'unavailable' trips can ever occupy the watch tier; a driver who has not left with 45 minutes to pickup is invisible to the list meant to catch exactly that.

findings.title: The builder's documented request sort is not implemented
findings.detail: The triage doc-comment at L9436 states 'Items within each tier are sorted by urgency (minutesUntil asc, waiting-timer desc for requests)'. In the code, no_drivers requests are pushed with sort:0 (L9480) and every other request with sort:999 (L9486); r.waiting is a 'M:SS' string that is never parsed anywhere in the builder.
findings.impact: A rider who has been waiting four minutes sorts identically to one waiting ten seconds, so the list does not order by the thing the comment says it orders by.

findings.title: The card's copy contradicts what it renders
findings.detail: The surviving card is titled 'Live trip interventions' and annotated 'kept here because these are trip-level actions, not queue items' (L2075), while the deprecation prose above it says the queue work moved to the work inbox. But renderInterventionsPage calls buildInterventionItems() unmodified (L10341), and branch 0 of that builder (L9452-L9474) emits SLA-ticket rows — the archetypal queue item. Nothing narrows the builder for this page.
findings.evidence: kept here because these are trip-level actions, not queue items
findings.impact: The page still duplicates the dashboard widget exactly as its own deprecation copy complains, and the toolbar subtitle 'Live requests + red-readiness upcoming trips' (L2169) omits the SLA rows entirely.

findings.title: The clicked row is not refreshed after taking a claim
findings.detail: assignManually sets r.claimedBy and r.claimedAt then calls renderRequestsPage() and renderRideRequests() (L11877) before opening the driver picker. renderInterventionsPage is not among them, so the ownership lock it just took is invisible on this page until the next renderDashboard pass — up to 60 seconds away.
findings.impact: Two operators can both see an unclaimed row and both click Assign now, which is exactly what the soft lock exists to prevent.

findings.title: The interventions page is unreachable from the UI
findings.detail: Mechanically confirmed: grep for go('interventions' and go("interventions" across all 21,857 lines returns zero hits, and there is no <div class="sb-item"> for it in the sidebar (L480-L547). The router branch at L8788 exists and works, and titles/subs entries at L2168-L2169 are populated, but nothing calls the router with that id. The only realistic route is a developer console call to window.go, after which goBack() makes it a legitimate history entry. There is no hash router and no deep-link parser in the file. Meanwhile the page's DOM is kept perpetually current: renderInterventionsPage() is called at boot (L14591) and unconditionally by every renderDashboard() pass (L10447), which itself fires on the 60-tick timer (L12614), on trip completion (L12471), on driver offer acceptance (L12486) and on manual assignment (L11900).
findings.impact: Work is spent every minute rebuilding a list nobody can open, and the SLA/request/trip rows it holds are only reachable through the dashboard widget and the work inbox.

findings.title: Watch-tier sort keys are on incompatible scales
findings.detail: Within the watch bucket, at-risk SLA tickets carry sort:500 (L9473), searching requests carry sort:999 (L9487) and subscription trips carry raw minutesUntil, which the builder's own cut-off caps at 60 (L9516). The three are sorted together ascending.
findings.impact: Every watch-tier sub-trip always outranks every watch-tier ticket and request regardless of real urgency, and breached SLA rows tie with no_drivers requests at sort:0 so ties resolve by push order rather than by urgency.

findings.title: activate_plan audit entry hardcodes the prior status as Draft
findings.detail: doActivatePlan() logs before={status:'Draft'} regardless of the plan's real prior status, so activating an Archived plan records a false transition. doDeactivatePlan() hardcodes {status:'Active'} too, but that one is guaranteed correct because the Deactivate button only renders when the plan is Active. doArchivePlan() records the real prior status.
findings.impact: The activity log cannot be trusted to reconstruct a plan's lifecycle; an Archived → Active revival is indistinguishable from a routine Draft → Active publish.

findings.title: addSurgeWindow() does not validate that endHour is greater than startHour
findings.detail: The add handler checks only that the four inputs are non-blank and non-NaN. currentSurgeMultiplier() matches with hour >= s.startHour && hour < s.endHour, so an overnight window entered as 20 → 4 can never match any hour and the multiplier silently never fires. The HTML min/max (start 0–23, end 1–24) do not catch the inversion.
findings.impact: A surge window configured for late-night demand is accepted, listed in the table as enabled, and does nothing. There is no feedback that it will never trigger.

findings.title: Archived is behaviourally identical to Draft — archived plans stay in the list with a one-click Activate button
findings.detail: doArchivePlan() only sets p.status='Archived'; the object is never removed from DB.plans. renderPlansTable() computes isActive = p.status==='Active', so an archived plan renders with the primary Activate button, which flips it straight back to Active. The only difference from Draft is the badge text — both render as b-grey.
findings.evidence: var isActive=p.status==='Active'; … +(isActive?'<button class="btn sm danger" onclick="confirmDeactivatePlan(…)">Deactivate</button>':'<button class="btn sm p" onclick="confirmActivatePlan(…)">Activate</button>')
findings.impact: Archiving conveys no protection. A plan deliberately retired can be revived by anyone with manage_plans in one click, and the plans list grows without bound.

findings.title: can() reads a flat per-user permission array, not the granular role matrix
findings.detail: can(permKey) resolves DB.teamUsers[CURRENT_USER_ID].permissions.indexOf(permKey) >= 0. The permission-matrix module for plans (L10638–L10641) declares legacy:'manage_plans' with granular view/edit keys, but every call site in this module checks the legacy string only. No reconciliation of the granular keys back into u.permissions was found.
findings.evidence: requirePerm('manage_plans') is the sole gate on every mutating handler here; the granular plans.view / plans.edit keys are never tested
findings.impact: The permission matrix UI can imply finer control than the runtime actually applies — a user granted plans.view could still hold the legacy manage_plans string, or vice versa. Marked unverified: the reconciliation path, if any, lives outside this module.

findings.title: newPlan() creates a plan with no audit entry
findings.detail: newPlan() finds the first free new<n> key, inserts a full plan object into DB.plans and routes to the editor. It calls requirePerm('manage_plans') but never logAction(), and it has no GATE_SWEEP entry. It is the only DB write in the module that leaves no audit trace.
findings.impact: Plan creation is invisible in the activity log. A half-finished Draft plan can appear in DB.plans with no record of who added it or when.

findings.title: plan.sortOrder is stored, edited, saved and audited but nothing sorts by it
findings.detail: sortOrder is seeded per plan (1/2/3), defaulted by newPlan() to Object.keys(DB.plans).length+1, editable via #fp3-sort, written by savePlan() and included in the audit diff — yet renderPlansTable() iterates raw Object.keys(DB.plans) and no other code path reads the field.
findings.impact: An operator can carefully order the plan list and see no change. The rider-facing ordering the field implies does not exist.

findings.title: planFloorCheck() — 'the check that blocks a publish' — is never invoked
