findings.detail: planFloorCheck(cls,km,min,cadence,roundTrip,proposedPrice) returns {ok: price >= floor, shortfall}. The comment immediately above describes it as the check that blocks a publish. Grep across the file finds only its definition; planLegPrice()'s only call site is inside planQuote(). No plan-save or rate-card path calls either.
findings.impact: No margin floor or break-even check is ever enforced against a plan price. A plan can be saved and activated below the modelled break-even with nothing objecting.

findings.title: removeRideType() deletes on a single click with no confirmation gate
findings.detail: Every other destructive action in this module has a GATE_SWEEP entry (saveRideTypes, saveSurgeConfig, saveSurgeSchedule, addRideType, addSurgeWindow, removeSurgeWindow — L20792–L20826). removeRideType has none and no bespoke modal, so the Remove button deletes immediately. It is gated on manage_plans and audited, and the button only renders for t.custom rows, so the three seeded types cannot be removed this way.
findings.impact: A misclick permanently removes a bookable ride type. Existing trips referencing that type fall through to quickRideFare()'s first-entry fallback, silently repricing them.

findings.title: saveSurgeSchedule() logs empty before/after objects
findings.detail: saveSurgeSchedule() reads every [data-surge-field] input back into the matching window, then logs 'Surge schedule updated' with {} for both before and after. saveRideTypes() does it correctly — it deep-clones the array first (L12376) and passes a real diff (L12385).
findings.impact: The audit log records that surge multipliers changed but not which window, from what, to what — the highest-blast-radius pricing control in the module has no reconstructable history.

findings.title: Surge windows have no zone dimension and ignore the rate card's per-city cap and suspensions
findings.detail: DB.surgeSchedule windows are time × weekday only. A separate per-city cap (DB.rateCard.surge.capByCity = {RUH:2.0, JED:2.0}, L21459) and a per-zone suspension mechanism (DB.surgeSuspensions L21464, suspendSurge() L21534, effectiveSurge() L21523) exist on the rate card but are never consulted by currentSurgeMultiplier(), which applies only DB.surgeConfig.capMultiplier (2.5).
findings.evidence: return Math.min(mult, (DB.surgeConfig.capMultiplier||2.5));  /* no capByCity, no suspension lookup */
findings.impact: A zone suspended for safety or regulatory reasons still surges through the quick-ride path, and the 2.0× city cap is silently exceeded up to 2.5×.

findings.title: The Active toggle on a ride type is inert
findings.detail: Each ride-type row exposes an Active toggle bound to data-type-field="active", committed by saveRideTypes() and displayed by renderRideTypesTable(). quickRideFare() does not filter on t.active — it looks the type up by name and prices it normally — and no other consumer of the flag exists.
findings.evidence: function quickRideFare(typeName,km,min){ … (no t.active check anywhere in the lookup or the fallback chain)
findings.impact: Deactivating a ride type does not stop it pricing or being bookable. The control implies a kill switch the app does not have.

findings.title: The ride-type Example column omits surge while the charged fare applies it
findings.detail: renderRideTypesTable() computes example = (t.baseFare + 10*t.perKm + 20*t.perMin).toFixed(2) with no surge term, while quickRideFare() multiplies the same base by currentSurgeMultiplier(). The example cell is also static until the next re-render — editing the inputs does not update it.
findings.impact: During a 1.5× evening-rush window the table shows 20.50 SAR for an Economy 10 km / 20 min trip while the rider is actually charged 30.75 SAR. Operators price against the wrong number.

findings.title: cselPick() fires on every status option but its result is thrown away
findings.detail: renderPlansFormSelects() builds the status select via customSelectHTML() and passes no onChangeExpr, so each option's onclick only updates the hidden #fp3-status input and the visible label. Nothing else reacts, and savePlan() never reads the input. Separately, the select's option list is built once per DOM lifetime — the if(!document.getElementById('csel-fp3-status')) branch means later opens only call cselSetValue().
findings.impact: Reinforces the no-op Status dropdown: the control is fully interactive and completely disconnected from any state change. cselSetValue() also silently does nothing when no matching option exists, so an unexpected status value would leave a stale label.

findings.title: ecoActive and comfortActive are dead data with misleading toast copy
findings.detail: toggleVehicleActive() writes p.ecoActive / p.comfortActive and logs the change, and loadPlanEditForm() reads them back into the checkboxes — but no renderer, pricing function or rider-facing path reads either field. The toast asserts a rider-visible effect that no code path implements.
findings.evidence: toast(checked?'✅ '+vehicleType+' enabled — riders will see it on this plan':'🚫 '+vehicleType+' disabled — hidden from this plan until re-enabled',checked?'ok':'warn');
findings.impact: An operator disables Comfort on a plan, gets an explicit confirmation that riders can no longer see it, and nothing changes anywhere.

findings.title: Feature-point add, remove and reorder are ungated, unconfirmed and unaudited
findings.detail: addPlanFeature() (L6030), removePlanFeature() (L6037) and pfDragStart/pfDrop (L6041–L6049) all mutate the PLAN_FEATURES buffer with no requirePerm(), no confirmation modal and no logAction(). The refusal only arrives at Save, where requirePerm('manage_plans') runs. Because the buffer is discarded on the next load, the destructive effect is not persisted — but there is no feedback until the save attempt.
findings.evidence: function removePlanFeature(i){  /* no requirePerm, no confirm, no logAction */
findings.impact: A user without manage_plans can delete every rider-facing feature point and only discover the refusal after clicking Save. When the user does have the permission, the feature-list changes reach DB via savePlan() with no per-operation audit trail.

findings.title: Feature-point HTML escaping covers double quotes only
findings.detail: renderPlanFeatures() builds each row by string concatenation and escapes feature text with String(f.en||'').replace(/"/g,'"') before interpolating it into a value="…" attribute. <, > and & are not escaped. The amber character-hint blocks interpolate f.en.length, which is a number and therefore safe.
findings.impact: Feature text is operator-entered and rider-facing. Escaping only one of the four HTML-significant characters is a latent injection path if this rendering pattern is reused where the attribute quoting is looser.

findings.title: No unsaved-changes guard, and Cancel is only a partial cancel
findings.detail: Both exits (← Plans, L1083, and the footer Cancel, L1127) call go('plans',null) directly with no dirty check. Typed core-data values are discarded, and PLAN_FEATURES edits are discarded on the next open because loadPlanEditForm() rebuilds the buffer from p.features — but toggleVehicleActive() has already written ecoActive/comfortActive to DB and those persist.
findings.impact: Cancel means different things to different fields on the same form. An operator who cancels out of an edit session still leaves the vehicle-active flags changed.

findings.title: numval() silently reverts a cleared numeric field, so the required rate markers are unenforced
findings.detail: numval(id, fallback) returns the fallback when parseFloat yields NaN, and every call site passes the plan's current stored value. Clearing #fp3-emin and saving therefore restores the old rate with no error and no zero. The SAR/min * and SAR/km * column headers imply required fields but nothing validates them.
findings.impact: An operator who deliberately clears a rate to zero it out gets the old rate back and a success toast. Silent no-op on a money field.

findings.title: The live preview and the saved value disagree for an empty field
findings.detail: gv(id) used by upd() is parseFloat(...)||0, so a blank input previews as 0. numval(id, fallback) used by savePlan() keeps the previously stored number for the same blank input. The two readers of the same DOM elements apply opposite fallback rules.
findings.impact: Clearing the discount field shows a full-price preview strip, then saves the old discount. What the operator sees before confirming is not what is written.

findings.title: The save audit diff omits status, ecoActive, comfortActive and features
findings.detail: savePlan() snapshots 12 fields into before and mirrors the same 12 into after. Of the plan's 17 keys, key is immutable, but status, ecoActive, comfortActive and features are excluded from the diff even though features is written in the same block and the audit summary quotes its length.
findings.evidence: logAction('save_plan','plan',p.key,'Saved '+p.name+' plan — core data, '+p.features.length+' feature points, vehicle pricing',before,{name:p.name,…})
findings.impact: The audit entry claims a feature-point count changed but cannot show which bullet was added, edited, reordered or deleted — the rider-facing copy on a plan card has no reconstructable change history.

findings.title: Three of this page's audit action keys are missing from ACTION_LABELS
findings.detail: ACTION_LABELS (L2899–L2913) registers activate_plan and deactivate_plan but not save_plan (L6146), archive_plan (L6172) or toggle_vehicle_active (L6114). Confirmed by reading the whole map: the only plan-related entries are activate_plan and deactivate_plan on L2911.
findings.evidence:
activate_plan:'Activate plan',deactivate_plan:'Deactivate plan',
  permission_denied:'Permission denied (blocked)',switch_user:'Switched acting user',export_data:'Exported data'
findings.impact: The activity log shows raw snake_case keys for the three most common plan-editor actions, so the audit trail is harder to scan and filter exactly where plan pricing changes are recorded.

findings.title: toggleVehicleActive() leaves the checkbox out of sync with DB on permission failure
findings.detail: The vehicle Active checkboxes are plain onchange handlers, so the box has already flipped visually by the time requirePerm('manage_plans') refuses. Nothing reverts this.checked. The same early return happens when currentPlanKey is null (L6112) — again after the box has flipped.
findings.impact: The form shows a vehicle as disabled that DB still has enabled (or the reverse) until the page is re-entered, so an operator can believe an action succeeded when it was refused.

findings.title: reorderSettingsTabs targets a class that does not exist
findings.detail: L21279 looks for '.settings-nav'; the markup class is '.settings-nav-col' (L1419). A grep for 'settings-nav' returns L21279 as the only hit outside 'settings-nav-col'. The function survives on its fallback, document.querySelector('[data-tab]').parentElement, which resolves correctly only because the first [data-tab] element in the document happens to be the General button at L1421. Inserting any earlier element with a data-tab attribute silently retargets the whole reorder.
findings.impact: A fragile selector that appears to work; a future DOM addition would move or destroy the settings nav grouping with no error.

findings.title: The 6-group reorder is boot-only and unguarded
findings.detail: reorderSettingsTabs() is called exactly once, from presenceBoot() at L21393, after markPresence, a DB.teamUsers filter, mountUxBlocks() and liveSubtitles(). If any of those throws first, the nav stays in its 3-group markup order and no error surfaces. Nothing re-runs the reorder and switchSettingsTab does not verify group state.
findings.impact: A boot failure earlier in presenceBoot silently degrades the Settings nav to the build-order grouping the reorder exists to fix.

findings.title: The eager 35-call router branch has no error isolation
findings.detail: L8819 is a single unguarded statement sequence of 33 data-refresh calls plus switchSettingsTab('general') and fitSettingsNavHeight(). An exception at call n prevents calls n+1 onward, including the two shell operations, so the page would render with no visible panel at all. The branch also runs in full on every return to Settings: 19 tbody rebuilds, the whole audit log filtered and paginated, renderPricing/renderIntegrity/renderWindowSettings/renderLedger, and 11 linear scans of DB.auditLog in renderSettingsMeta - with no memoisation, dirty flag, or per-tab lazy render.
findings.impact: One failing tab renderer takes out all 21 panes and leaves the Settings page blank.

findings.title: The Settings shell has no permission gate
findings.detail: No requirePerm call exists in switchSettingsTab (L7314-7331), in the L8819 router branch, or on any of the 21 nav buttons (L1421-1443). requirePerm('manage_settings') is enforced only per save action inside each tab. Read access to the Ledger, Permissions, Security and Legal panes is therefore open to any signed-in operator.
findings.impact: Sensitive configuration - the role permission matrix, ledger postings, session controls - is readable by every operator regardless of role; only writing is controlled.

findings.title: Two entry points land on the wrong tab
findings.detail: The router branch ends with switchSettingsTab('general') unconditionally, so the top-bar on-call chip (L568, title 'Who is on call right now') and the Work Inbox PDPL erasure item (L19204, QUEUE_ROUTE.erasure='settings') both open Settings on General - 16th in the reordered rail, in a different group from what the operator asked for. go() accepts no tab argument, although the mechanism to deep-link exists and is used once at L1811.
findings.impact: The escalation chip and the erasure queue item both require the operator to hunt for the right tab manually.

findings.title: Empty-string saves are silently discarded
findings.detail: All seven fields are written with the pattern val(id)||g.field. Clearing 'Company / site name' and pressing Save keeps the previous name, shows the success toast and writes an audit entry whose before/after are identical for that key.
findings.impact: No General field can ever be blanked, and the operator gets a success confirmation for a change that did not happen.

findings.title: No persistence layer - saved settings die on reload
findings.detail: The pane's own note (L1511) states the file has no backend. Confirmed mechanically: the whole 21857-line file contains zero occurrences of localStorage, sessionStorage or indexedDB, so DB.opsConfig is in-memory only.
findings.evidence: Since this file has no backend server, re-opening the file fresh (or sharing it with someone else) resets to the default logo
findings.impact: Every General setting, and every other Settings tab's config, resets to the seed on reload. Any claim of durable configuration is false.

findings.title: Support email and phone are write-only fields
findings.detail: Both are seeded, editable, saved and audited, but no other code path reads DB.opsConfig.general.supportEmail or .supportPhone - they appear on no receipt, notification or footer.
findings.impact: Changing the published support contact has no effect on anything users see.

findings.title: Timezone setting has no consumer
findings.detail: DB.opsConfig.general.timezone is never read outside renderGeneralConfig/saveGeneralConfig. Audit timestamps use new Date().toLocaleTimeString([]) - the browser's zone - and applyCityToggle formats dates with a hardcoded 'en-GB' locale.
findings.impact: Operators in a different zone see local times while believing the panel is pinned to Asia/Riyadh; audit timestamps are not comparable across operators.

findings.title: Inviting as Owner grants all 13 permissions with no additional confirmation
findings.detail: defaultPermissionsForRole returns the intersection of permissions held by every current holder of the role. USR-1 is the only Owner and holds all 13, so an Owner invite produces a full-permission account - including manage_team and manage_settings - from a three-field modal with a single Send invite click and no guardAction gate.
findings.impact: Privilege escalation in one step for anyone holding manage_team: invite a new Owner (any email address), then use 'View as' on it. No confirmation names the permission count being granted.

findings.title: lastLogin and status never change after creation
findings.detail: lastLogin is a free-text string set once, either by the seed or by commitInvite's literal 'Not yet'. Neither impersonate, stopImpersonating nor commitUserSwitch touches it, and nothing sets status from 'Invited' to 'Active'.
findings.impact: The two columns operators would use to spot a stale or unused account are permanently frozen, so the roster cannot support any access review.

findings.title: TEAM_ROLES and the matrix role columns are two different lists
findings.detail: The invite and edit selects are built from the hardcoded TEAM_ROLES array. Both permission matrices derive their columns from DB.teamUsers.map(u=>u.role) deduped (L10714, L10753). They agree today only because all four seed roles are held. Separately, DB.compPolicy.roles keys on 'Operations', which is not in TEAM_ROLES.
findings.impact: If the last holder of a role were re-roled, that role's matrix column disappears while the invite select still offers it - and a new user invited into it would receive an empty permissions array (defaultPermissionsForRole returns [] for a role with no holders).

findings.title: The invite email is never sent
findings.detail: The invite modal hint states 'They will receive an email invite.' commitInvite validates, pushes the record, closes the modal, re-renders, logs and toasts - it makes no sendSystemEmail call, a function used elsewhere in the file (e.g. L12455).
findings.evidence: They will receive an email invite. Role determines what they can see and do - check the permission matrix below once added.
findings.impact: An invited operator is never notified; the account sits in the roster with live permissions and no one outside the panel knows it exists.

findings.title: The last Owner can be demoted, and there is no recovery
findings.detail: commitEditTeamUser writes u.role with no check on how many Owners remain. The self-protection guards only cover revoking your OWN manage_team (toggleRolePermission L10781, saveUserPermissions L10809) - nothing stops one manage_team holder from demoting or de-permissioning another, including the last Owner. Combined with the absence of any delete/restore path, the panel has no way back.
findings.impact: manage_settings is held only by the Owner role in the seed. Stripping it from the last Owner permanently locks every one of the eleven Settings save functions out of the panel for that session.

findings.title: twoFA is display-only with no setter and no default on new users
findings.detail: u.twoFA is read at L10454-L10456 to render a compliance chip when DB.opsConfig.security.require2FA is on. No code path writes it. commitInvite's record literal omits the field entirely, so every invited user is twoFA: undefined - falsy, therefore rendered as non-compliant.
findings.evidence: var twoFABadge=require2FA?(u.twoFA?' 2FA on':' warning 2FA off'):'';
findings.impact: The Security tab can flag a 2FA requirement the panel gives operators no way to satisfy; with the seed, turning the policy on immediately marks USR-2, USR-3 and USR-4 as non-compliant permanently.

findings.title: Audit entry ids collide and the log silently truncates at 500
findings.detail: logAction builds id as 'AUD-'+String(DB.auditLog.length+1).padStart(4,'0'), then unshifts the entry at index 0 and hard-truncates with DB.auditLog.length=500. Ids therefore describe position at write time rather than sequence, and once the log reaches 500 entries every subsequent entry receives the identical id AUD-0501 while the oldest entries are dropped with no archive and no warning.
findings.impact: The audit trail that requirePerm and requirePagePerm rely on to record permission_denied events is neither uniquely keyed nor durable. In a busy session, denial and privilege-change events scroll off permanently, and duplicate ids make any downstream export or reconciliation unreliable.

findings.title: No role entity - matrix columns are derived from the current roster
findings.detail: Both matrices compute their columns as DB.teamUsers.map(u=>u.role) deduped in first-appearance order. There is no create/rename/delete-role path, and a role loses its column the moment no team user holds it, taking its configured permission baseline with it (defaultPermissionsForRole then returns [] for that role).
findings.impact: Role configuration is not durable state - it is an emergent property of who is currently employed. Re-roling the last Finance user erases the Finance column and the role's baseline in one edit.

findings.title: No self-lockout guard on the granular matrix
findings.detail: toggleRolePermission blocks revoking your own broad manage_team (L10781) and saveUserPermissions blocks it for yourself (L10809). togglePagePermission has no equivalent check - it validates only requirePerm('manage_team') and that the role has holders.
findings.impact: Inconsistent protection across three code paths that write the same authorization state. The practical blast radius is limited only because settings.manage_team is itself never enforced (finding #7).

findings.title: Permission changes commit instantly with no confirmation and no undo
findings.detail: Neither toggleRolePermission nor togglePagePermission is registered with guardAction, unlike far less consequential settings saves (saveGeneralConfig L20771, saveCommitPolicy L18068, saveCompPolicy L18077). One onchange event rewrites permissions for every holder of the role and, for the broad matrix, regenerates their pagePerms for every page gated by that key.
findings.evidence: GATE_SWEEP={ /* settings that change how the platform behaves */ saveGeneralConfig:{t:'Save platform settings',d:true, ... }  -- no entry exists for toggleRolePermission or togglePagePermission
findings.impact: A single mis-click on a role cell can revoke a whole feature area from every operator holding that role, with recovery possible only by manually re-ticking and no record of the prior granular customisation, which the revoke path overwrites with ['view'].

findings.title: Permission state is never reflected in the UI - only at commit
findings.detail: The RBAC design comment at L3117-L3121 states the rule deliberately: one choke point per action on the COMMIT function, never on buttons. No code hides, disables or greys a control based on can()/canPage(). Combined with the unguarded Settings page (finding #3), a Support user sees every Settings tab and every save button.
findings.evidence: One choke point per action, placed on the COMMIT function (the line that actually mutates DB), never on buttons - so every UI path ... hits the same wall.
findings.impact: Operators discover their access boundary only by attempting actions, and each attempt writes a permission_denied audit entry, so ordinary UI exploration pollutes the security event log.

findings.title: renderSidebarPerms is called but never defined
findings.detail: The doc flagged this UNVERIFIED; confirmed by grep. The identifier appears exactly twice in the file, both times as if(typeof renderSidebarPerms==='function')renderSidebarPerms(); inside impersonate() and stopImpersonating(). There is no function declaration and no window assignment.
findings.impact: The sidebar is never filtered by permission. Impersonating a low-permission user changes only which commits succeed, not what the navigation offers, so 'you now see only their permissions' in the impersonation toast is inaccurate.

findings.title: Silent no-op leaves the checkbox in a state that was never written
findings.detail: Both toggles do if(!affected.length) return; before any write and before any re-render. The DOM checkbox the user just clicked stays in its new position, and no toast, no audit entry and no re-render corrects it.
findings.impact: Unreachable with the seed roster because every rendered column has at least one holder by construction, but any future path that renders a role column with no users would display a permission state that does not exist.

findings.title: The settings.manage_team granular key is never enforced
findings.detail: Every team and permission mutation in the panel gates on the broad key: commitInvite L10529, commitEditTeamUser L10486, togglePagePermission L10688, toggleRolePermission L10779, saveUserPermissions L10802 all call requirePerm('manage_team'). No call site checks canPage('settings','manage_team').
findings.impact: Unticking 'Manage team & this permission matrix' in the Detailed page permissions matrix produces a success toast and an audit entry while changing nothing about who can edit the team.

findings.title: notifyOnDispute is a stored setting with no consumer
findings.detail: 'Notify on every new dispute filed' writes DB.opsConfig.notifications.notifyOnDispute. Grep returns only the seed (L2571), renderNotificationConfig (L8006) and saveNotificationConfig (L8011-L8012). There is no dispute-filing flow to hook into, as the badge states.
findings.evidence: Notify on every new dispute filed Tracked - this file has no live dispute-filing flow to hook into
findings.impact: Dispute notification is configurable but never delivered; the setting is decoration.

findings.title: One 'email' flag also gates the in-app alert
findings.detail: The single live rule is guarded by `lowRatingCfg.emailAlerts !== false`. Inside that branch sit BOTH pushOpsNotification (in-app bell entry) and sendSystemEmail (driver email). Unchecking a box labelled 'Email alerts for high-priority events' therefore also removes the in-app ops notification. Note also that the gate is `!== false`, so an undefined flag counts as enabled.
findings.impact: An ops team that turns off email to reduce noise silently loses the only in-app low-rating alert as well, with no indication in the field label.

findings.title: Only one event type is actually wired
findings.detail: The labels promise 'high-priority events' and 'critical incidents (SOS, safety)', but the only trigger anywhere in the file that reads this config is the trip-completion low-rating branch at L12451-L12455. No SOS, safety, dispute, payment or escalation event reads DB.opsConfig.notifications.
findings.impact: The pane reads as a general alerting console but configures exactly one rule; operators may believe SOS alerting is enabled when nothing is wired.

findings.title: smsAlerts is a stored setting with no consumer
findings.detail: The 'SMS alerts for critical incidents (SOS, safety)' checkbox writes DB.opsConfig.notifications.smsAlerts and produces an audit entry, but a whole-file grep for smsAlerts returns only the seed (L2571), renderNotificationConfig (L8006) and saveNotificationConfig (L8011-L8012). No SMS gateway or reader exists. The UI badge admits this.
findings.evidence: SMS alerts for critical incidents (SOS, safety) Tracked - no SMS gateway wired up yet
findings.impact: An operator can toggle a security-critical alert channel on and see it audited as changed, while no SOS or safety incident will ever raise an SMS.

findings.title: Doc says twoFA has no setter; toggleMa2FA does set it
findings.detail: The doc (Gaps item 2) asserts u.twoFA has no setter anywhere in the file. In fact toggleMa2FA(val) at L3047 sets u.twoFA for the CURRENT_USER_ID record and audits it via logAction('toggle_2fa','team_user',...). It is reachable from the My Account modal's Security section (#ma-security-body, L1161, rendered by renderMaSecurity L3004) - not from Settings > Security or Settings > Team & Roles. It is not requirePerm-gated, but only ever mutates the acting user's own record.
findings.impact: An operator can clear their own red 2FA chip, but there is still no way to enrol another team member, so the compliance debt shown by require2FA is unclearable for everyone else.

findings.title: Invited users are created without a twoFA field
findings.detail: commitInvite() pushes {id,name,email,role,lastLogin,status,permissions} with no twoFA key (L10538). Falsy twoFA renders the red 'warning 2FA off' chip, so every newly invited member is permanently non-compliant from the ops panel's point of view, and toggleMa2FA can only fix the currently signed-in user.
findings.impact: With the policy on, the Team table accumulates unresolvable red compliance flags as the team grows.

findings.title: require2FA is a compliance chip, not an access control
findings.detail: require2FA is read in exactly one place outside the settings pane: renderTeamTable() L10454-L10456, where it decides whether to append a green '2FA on' or a red 'warning 2FA off' badge after each user's name. No commit function, no requirePerm/can() path and no navigation gate consults u.twoFA. A user badged '2FA off' retains every permission in PERMISSION_LABELS.
findings.impact: A security policy that is displayed as enforced ('Require two-factor authentication for all team members') but blocks nothing; it is a to-do list, not a control.

findings.title: sessionTimeoutMin is stored but enforced nowhere
findings.detail: A whole-file grep for sessionTimeoutMin returns exactly four hits: the seed (L2572), renderSecurityConfig (L8021) and saveSecurityConfig (L8026, L8027). There is no idle timer, no setTimeout, no activity listener and no logout path. The pane discloses this in a grey note at L1984.
findings.evidence: Saved and ready, but not enforced here - this file has no real login session to time out. A production backend would read this value to end idle sessions.
findings.impact: An 'auto-logout after inactivity' control that an operator can set, save and see audited, with zero effect on session lifetime.

findings.title: The Security settings tab has no session list
findings.detail: DB.loginSessions (L2994, five SESS- records across USR-1..USR-4) is not referenced anywhere in #stab-security (L1976-L1994), which contains only two inputs, one save button and a meta footer. Its consumers are renderMaSecurity() (L3007) and logOutSession() (L3056), both belonging to the My Account modal's Security section rendered into #ma-security-body (L1161).
findings.impact: Any assumption that this tab lets ops review or terminate operator sessions is wrong; force-logout exists only for one's own account, behind a native confirm() and with no permission check.

findings.title: 'Save search phases' commits nothing
findings.detail: saveSearchPhases() (L8115-L8120) contains only requirePerm, logAction, renderSettingsMeta and toast. Phase adds and removes already mutate DB.searchPhases the moment their own buttons are pressed, so the Save button is a no-op that nevertheless produces an audit entry claiming a configuration change.
findings.evidence: function saveSearchPhases(){ if(!requirePerm('manage_settings'))return; logAction('config_updated','settings','phases','Search phases confirmed - '+DB.searchPhases.length+' phase(s) active',{},DB.searchPhases); renderSettingsMeta(); toast(...); }
findings.impact: Operators may believe phase edits are staged until Save; they are live immediately. The audit log gains entries that record no change.

findings.title: Active-subscription count ignores 'Expiring' subscriptions
findings.detail: driverActiveSubCount filters DB.subscriptions on s.status==='Active' exactly, so any other lifecycle status - notably 'Expiring' - does not count. With allowMultiSubPerDriver closed, driverCanTakeAnotherSub then returns true for such a driver because the count is 0.
findings.impact: The 'new drivers only' policy leaks: a driver whose subscriptions are all Expiring is treated as unassigned and can be handed another one.

findings.title: Auto-expand discards the radius cap entirely
findings.detail: When no candidate is within maxKm and autoExpandRadius is not false, nearestAvailableDrivers replaces the filtered list with the complete unfiltered list rather than widening by a step, then flags out.expandedBeyondRadius. The only signal to the operator is the amber banner at L8374; automated dispatch through nextOfferCandidate/tickEngine consumes the expanded pool with no extra check.
findings.impact: A request in a thin-supply area can be offered to a driver far outside any configured radius, producing long ETAs that no setting on this pane bounds.

findings.title: Both radius Save buttons are the same function
findings.detail: L1568 ('Save Quick Ride radius') and L1598 ('Save Subscription radius') both call saveOpsRadiusConfig(), which reads #cfg-quick-radius, #cfg-sub-radius and #cfg-auto-expand and writes all three. The card layout implies two independent saves.
findings.impact: An operator experimenting with the subscription radius and pressing the Quick Ride save button commits both values, changing live subscription matching unintentionally. The audit summary at least names both.

findings.title: Coverage-blocked message points to the wrong settings tab
findings.detail: This resolves the doc's UNVERIFIED item 12 - an explanatory message IS rendered when planOptions is empty (L4609). However it directs the operator to 'Settings > Pricing > Plan visibility'; the plan-visibility radios live in the Matching & Dispatch pane (#stab-dispatch L1603-L1618), and the Pricing tab (#stab-pricing L1717) has no such control.
findings.evidence: ⚠ No driver currently covers this rider's area within the subscription radius, and Settings → Pricing → Plan visibility is set to hide plans without coverage. Adjust the rule there, or wait for coverage.
findings.impact: An operator following the instruction lands on a tab that does not contain the setting, and cannot unblock the subscription sale.

findings.title: Last-updated footers are attached to the wrong cards
findings.detail: #meta-ops-radius (L1578) closes the Quick Rides card and #meta-phases (L1600) closes the Subscriptions card, but renderSettingsMeta maps them to the 'ops-radius' and 'phases' audit entities respectively (L7341). Since saveSearchPhases/addSearchPhase/removeSearchPhase log to entity 'phases' and saveOpsRadiusConfig logs to 'ops-radius', adding a search phase updates the timestamp shown under the Subscriptions card, and changing either radius updates the one under the Quick Rides card.
findings.impact: The provenance line under each card credits the wrong change, misleading anyone auditing who last touched dispatch settings.

findings.title: No duplicate or upper-bound validation on new phases
findings.detail: addSearchPhase rejects only NaN, sec<0 and mult<1. Two phases with the same afterSec are accepted, and currentRadiusMultiplier's last-match-wins loop then silently picks whichever sorts last. There is no ceiling on either field, so ×1000 or afterSec 99999 are storable.
findings.evidence: if(isNaN(sec)||sec<0||isNaN(mult)||mult<1){toast('⚠ Enter a valid second (≥0) and multiplier (≥1)','warn');return;}
findings.impact: A mistyped multiplier can silently make the effective search radius unbounded for live quick rides, with no confirmation of the resulting km.

findings.title: Phase deletion is unreconstructable from the audit log
findings.detail: removeSearchPhase filters the array then logs a fixed string with empty before and after objects, discarding the id, afterSec and multiplier of what was deleted. The action IS confirm-gated (GATE_SWEEP.removeSearchPhase, L20821, d:true).
findings.impact: A dispatch regression caused by a deleted phase cannot be traced or reversed from the Activity tab.

findings.title: Plan-visibility coverage test is stricter than dispatch itself
findings.detail: isPlanVisibleForRider requires nearby.length>0 AND !nearby.expandedBeyondRadius, so a driver reachable only through the auto-expand fallback does not count as coverage - even though a real quick-ride offer would be sent to that same driver. It also calls nearestAvailableDrivers without elapsedSec, so no phase widening applies either.
findings.impact: With the hide rule on, riders in thin-supply areas can be offered zero plans while the platform would happily match them a quick ride - and the radio's explanatory sub-copy never mentions the interaction with auto-expand.

findings.title: renderDispatchSettings belongs to a different pane and reads unseeded keys
findings.detail: Despite the name, renderDispatchSettings() (L17408) writes into #dispatch-tbody, markup that sits inside #stab-reasons (Reason Codes & SLA, L1771-L1824) under an 'Emergency dispatch' heading. Its six keys (emergencyMultiplierPct, dispatchWindowSec, dispatchMaxCandidates, riderCompPctPer10Min, riderCompCapPct, riderCompMinSAR) are absent from the DB.commitPolicy seed (L16541-L16561), so the inputs render value="undefined" until saved once through saveCommitPolicy.
findings.impact: Anyone searching for dispatch parameters by function name lands on the wrong tab, and six emergency-dispatch fields present as undefined on first load.

findings.title: Search phases have no edit path
findings.detail: renderSearchPhasesTable emits plain text cells (''+p.afterSec+'s×'+p.multiplier+'') and a Remove button. The row carries data-phase-id but nothing ever reads that attribute back, unlike the limits and cancellation tables which support in-row editing.
findings.impact: Tuning the ladder requires delete-then-recreate, which loses the original values from the audit trail (see finding #4) and briefly changes live dispatch behaviour between the two operations.

findings.title: Activating a city is ungated
findings.detail: toggleCityActive / applyCityToggle are not registered in GATE_SWEEP. Turning a city ON — which unblocks rider matching platform-wide for that city — applies immediately on a single click. Only turning OFF a city that already has drivers or riders opens the bespoke confirm modal, and cityStats means that can only ever happen for Riyadh.
findings.impact: The one setting on this tab with real downstream effect can be flipped on without any confirmation step.

findings.title: City coordinates are written and never read
findings.detail: addCity() pushes lat and lng captured from the KNOWN_CITIES picker, and the panel copy justifies the whole autocomplete mechanism on coordinate accuracy. Grep of DB.cities shows property access only at the push and in the audit summary string; nothing in the matching or distance code reads them. nearestAvailableDrivers works from mapPos {x,y} percentages, not lat/lng. The four seeded cities have no lat/lng at all, so the record shape is also inconsistent.
findings.impact: The stated purpose of the city picker is unrealised; coordinates give a false impression that geo-aware matching exists.

findings.title: removeCity has no confirmation
findings.detail: removeCity() checks manage_settings and then filters the record out of DB.cities on a single click. There is no confirm modal and no GATE_SWEEP entry, while addCity — the less destructive action — is confirm-gated.
findings.impact: An irreversible destructive action is one misclick away, and there is no edit path to recreate the record with its original launched date.

findings.title: matchPrefix collisions reassign transactions silently
findings.detail: gatewayStats matches with p.method.indexOf(gw.matchPrefix)===0 — a case-sensitive prefix match at position 0 on a human-readable label. Since custom gateways get matchPrefix = name, a gateway named 'Visa Checkout' or 'Mada Plus' shares a prefix boundary with the built-in rows and changes what each row reports.
findings.impact: The tab's only live numbers can be silently reassigned by naming a new gateway carelessly.

findings.title: No duplicate-name check when adding a gateway
findings.detail: addCustomGateway validates only that a name was typed. addCity, by contrast, rejects duplicates case-insensitively. Because matchPrefix is set to the same string as the name, two gateways called 'Mada' would each match every Mada payment.
findings.impact: Transaction counts and volume can be silently double-counted, overstating processed money on the tab.

findings.title: Panel and confirm copy describe routing behaviour that is not implemented
findings.detail: The pane description claims turning a gateway off stops new charges; GATE_SWEEP.setDefaultGateway claims all new charges route through the selected gateway and that settlement reconciliation must be checked on both for the changeover day; GATE_SWEEP.addCustomGateway claims money will route through it once made default. None of this occurs — see finding #1.
findings.impact: Operators are told the platform behaves in a way it does not, in exactly the dialogs meant to make them stop and think.

findings.title: removeGateway can delete the current default
findings.detail: toggleGatewayEnabled refuses to disable the default gateway, and setDefaultGateway refuses to promote a disabled one — but removeGateway has no isDefault guard and no confirmation, so the default row can simply be deleted, leaving the array with zero defaults and no way to notice.
findings.impact: The single-default invariant the other two handlers work to preserve can be broken in one click.

findings.title: removeGateway's audit entry identifies nothing
findings.detail: The logAction call passes the fixed summary 'Removed payment gateway' with empty before and after objects, so the audit trail records that a gateway was removed but not which one.
findings.impact: A deletion cannot be reconstructed or attributed from the audit log.

findings.title: Automatic subscription matching bypasses the trip trust gate
findings.detail: driverTrustedForSubs (driver_min_trips_for_subs) is consulted only by the manual subscription driver picker's disabled-reason chain. nearestAvailableDrivers filters on driverAutoRestricted and, for kind==='sub', driverCanTakeAnotherSub — but never on driverTrustedForSubs.
findings.evidence: nearestAvailableDrivers filters d.suspended and driverAutoRestricted(id); driverTrustedForSubs is called only at L4496/L5688
findings.impact: A brand-new driver below the minimum completed-trip threshold can still be matched to a subscription automatically, which is exactly what the limit exists to prevent.

findings.title: Custom limits are inert by construction
findings.detail: addCustomLimit hardcodes enforced:false and enforcedBy:null, and there is no UI control or code path anywhere that sets enforced:true on a limit. Every limit created through the '+ Add a custom limit' card is permanently decorative, contradicting the addCustomLimit confirm text 'Applies to dispatch from the moment it is saved.'
findings.evidence: addCustomLimit:{t:'Add an operational limit',c:['Applies to dispatch from the moment it is saved.'],btn:'Add limit'},
findings.impact: The tab's headline extensibility claim — new limits without code changes — is only half true: rows can be added but never wired.

findings.title: driver_max_active_subs is superseded and never read
findings.detail: Seeded value:5, enabled:true, enforced:false. Multi-subscription policy is actually decided by driverCanTakeAnotherSub() using DB.opsConfig.allowMultiSubPerDriver plus a per-driver multiSubException — a binary 'one or unlimited' rule that never consults the numeric cap. Driver cards display hardcoded activeSubs strings such as '4/5' and '6/6' whose denominators do not come from this limit either.
findings.impact: The displayed capacity denominators and the configured cap are unrelated to the rule actually enforced.

findings.title: driver_min_rating duplicates driver_min_rating_for_dispatch
findings.detail: Two driver rows carry value 3.5 and unit ★. Only driver_min_rating_for_dispatch is read (driverAutoRestricted L4505 -> nearestAvailableDrivers and the subscription picker); driver_min_rating appears solely on its seed line.
findings.impact: An operator who edits the wrong of two identically-valued rows believes they have changed dispatch eligibility and have not.

findings.title: Limit label and unit are injected as raw HTML
findings.detail: limitRowHtml concatenates l.label and l.unit directly into the row markup with no escaping, and addCustomLimit performs no sanitisation on either field. The same unescaped-concatenation pattern is used by addCustomGateway and addCity elsewhere in the file.
findings.impact: Stored-XSS shaped defect in a single-file demo; a limit named with an onerror payload would execute on every settings render.

findings.title: rider_max_active_requests is never enforced
findings.detail: The row is seeded value:1, enabled:true, enforced:false, enforcedBy:null. Grep for the id returns only the seed line — no code prevents a rider from having several open ride requests. The UI badges it '● Tracked', which is honest, but the setting is configurable and inert.
findings.impact: An operator can tighten or loosen the cap with no effect on the platform.

findings.title: rider_max_cancellations_day is never enforced
findings.detail: Seeded value:3 per day, enabled:true, enforced:false. Grep returns only the seed line; no cancellation path counts per-rider daily cancellations or flags a rider on that basis.
findings.impact: Serial-cancelling riders are never flagged despite a configured cap.

findings.title: Zero is unrepresentable and invalid input becomes zero
findings.detail: The per-row value input has no min and no max attribute, and saveOpsLimits writes l.value = parseFloat(vInput.value)||0. The enforcement functions then defend against a falsy value with hardcoded fallbacks (||3 for declines, ||3.5 for rating, ||10 for trips), so a stored 0 is silently reinterpreted as the default. A limit of zero cannot be expressed, and a typo becomes a value the engine ignores.
findings.impact: The Settings UI and the dispatch engine can disagree about the configured limit with no warning to the operator.

findings.title: An uncollectable quick-ride fee is never recovered
findings.detail: When debitRiderWallet returns falsy, confirmCancelLiveTrip logs a wallet_debit entry and shows a toast saying the fee was 'added to next trip charge'. No deferred-charge mechanism exists anywhere in the file — the amount is simply never collected.
findings.evidence: 'Cancellation fee of '+fee.toFixed(2)+' SAR for '+id+' — insufficient wallet balance, added to next trip charge'
findings.impact: Revenue leakage that the audit log records as if it had been deferred rather than lost.

findings.title: The grace period is configurable but never applied
findings.detail: qr_grace_period carries graceMin:2 and is the only rule that renders the 'Grace period (minutes)' sub-field. Grep for graceMin returns exactly four lines: the row builder, the two save-loop lines, and the seed. confirmCancelLiveTrip performs no time-since-acceptance check and never looks up qr_grace_period at all.
findings.evidence: {id:'qr_grace_period',appliesTo:'quick_ride',scenario:'Rider cancels within the grace period after a driver accepts',feeAmount:0,graceMin:2,enabled:true,...}
findings.impact: The free window after driver acceptance is displayed as policy but never honoured — a rider cancelling one second after acceptance is charged the same as one cancelling ten minutes later.

findings.title: Compensation role keys do not match the team roles
findings.detail: DB.compPolicy.roles defines 'Operations' with 200/2000 SAR, but no DB.teamUsers entry carries that role. The real role string is 'Ops Manager' (USR-5), which is not a key, so compLimitsFor falls through to 'default' (50/300). An operations manager therefore has a lower ceiling than Support (75/600), and the 'Operations' row in the settings table governs nobody.
findings.impact: The compensation authority table shown to administrators does not describe the limits actually applied to their staff.

findings.title: Five save buttons on one pane silently discard each other's edits
findings.detail: The pane has five independent Save buttons, each of which re-renders its own table from DB after writing. Editing the SLA tier inputs and then pressing the reason-code 'Save changes' writes only the reason codes and then re-renders; the tier edits are lost on the next renderSlaPolicyForm(). There is no unsaved-changes indicator anywhere on the pane.
findings.evidence:
Reason code registry

-
findings.impact: Silent loss of configuration edits on the widest settings pane in the file.

findings.title: Policy saves are audited without a before/after diff
findings.detail: saveSlaPolicy, saveCompPolicy and saveCommitPolicy call logAction with only an action key, entity id and summary string - no before or after payload. saveReasonCodes passes {codes:before.length} and {codes:DB.reasonCodes.length}, i.e. only the row count, even though it deep-clones the full registry into 'before' first. Comparable handlers elsewhere (saveOpsLimits, saveCancellationPolicy) snapshot both sides.
findings.impact: A change to every SLA clock on the platform is recorded as one summary line; the audit log cannot answer 'what was it before?'.

findings.title: Reason code labels and owners are injected as raw HTML
findings.detail: renderReasonCodesTable concatenates r.labelEn into a <strong> and r.owner into an input value attribute with no escaping. owner is free text typed by an operator and persisted, and labelEn comes from the add-code composer, so both are operator-controlled strings rendered back as markup.
findings.impact: Stored markup injection through a settings pane that every operator can reach.

findings.title: reasonCode.target is invisible and inert
findings.detail: Every reason code carries target: 'rider' | 'driver' | 'corp' (28/10/2 across the 40 seeds), but the field is not rendered in the registry table and no code reads it. The rider wallet-credit modal therefore offers driver- and corporate-targeted codes exactly like rider codes.
findings.impact: Contacts can be coded against a scenario aimed at the wrong party, and the data that would prevent it is present but unused.

findings.title: Root-cause owner is write-only
findings.detail: The owner column is rendered as an editable text input and saved to DB.reasonCodes[i].owner, but no code reads it outside the registry renderer. The seed comment calls it 'the field that turns a metric into somebody's backlog'; there is no owner filter, owner report, owner routing or owner escalation anywhere in the file.
findings.impact: Operators spend effort assigning owners that nothing acts on.

findings.title: SLA tier hours:'business' is displayed but never honoured
findings.detail: The Hours column renders '24/7' or 'Business hours' from DB.slaPolicy.tiers[K].hours as static, non-editable text. slaState() computes pure wall-clock deltas with no business-hours calendar, so the T4 'business' setting has no effect: a low-priority contact opened at 02:00 accrues breach time overnight, which is exactly what the design comment at L14645 says it wants to avoid.
findings.impact: Low-priority tickets manufacture overnight SLA breaches that the configuration claims to prevent. UNVERIFIED whether a server-side SLA engine is intended to honour it - within this file it is not honoured at all.

findings.title: The statutory freeze check contains a dead sub-expression
findings.detail: The guard reads tiers[1].freezeDays >= regulatorCancelLimit*0 && tiers[1].freezeDays > 30. The first clause is x >= 0 and is always true, so regulatorCancelLimit plays no part; the effective test is the unrelated constant 30. It also only raises a warn toast and does not block the save.
findings.impact: The check that claims to keep the internal freeze below the statutory ceiling never actually compares the two values.

findings.title: A logo cannot be cleared
findings.detail: applyBranding only assigns img.src when DB.branding.logoUrl is truthy, so emptying the URL field and saving persists the empty string but leaves the sidebar showing the previously applied image until a reload.
findings.impact: Removing a logo appears to fail; the operator has no in-session way to revert to the bundled mark.

findings.title: Branding values are interpolated into markup unescaped
findings.detail: renderBrandingSettings concatenates b.logoUrl into an input value attribute and an img src, and b.wordmark into another value attribute, with no escaping. A wordmark containing a quote and angle bracket breaks out of the attribute.
findings.evidence: renderBrandingSettings() builds the pane by string concatenation of b.logoUrl and b.wordmark into value= and src= attributes
findings.impact: Stored-XSS shaped defect in a single-file demo panel; noted rather than exploitable in the intended deployment.

findings.title: Reset does not re-apply branding
findings.detail: resetBranding calls renderBrandingSettings() but never applyBranding(), so the sidebar keeps whatever logo and wordmark were last applied while the form shows the defaults. The toast admits it: 'Branding reset — reload to restore the bundled logo'.
findings.evidence:
renderBrandingSettings();
  toast('Branding reset — reload to restore the bundled logo','info');
findings.impact: The panel's visible state and its stored state disagree until the page is reloaded.

findings.title: Two competing logo stores that never synchronise
findings.detail: DB.branding.logoUrl is set by this tab and applied by applyBranding() to the sidebar mark. DB.opsConfig.general.logoDataUrl is set by the General tab's handleLogoUpload() (with a 200 KB limit) and applied by applySiteBranding() to the favicon and #logo-preview. Neither writes to the other.
findings.evidence: applyBranding() touches only .sb-logo-img and .sb-logo-text; applySiteBranding() reads DB.opsConfig.general
findings.impact: Changing the logo in one place leaves the other stale, so the sidebar and the browser tab can show different brands, with two different size limits.

findings.title: numOf strips the minus sign
findings.detail: numOf parses with String(v).replace(/[^\d.]/g,''), which removes any leading '-'. A stored total of -120 is therefore read as 120, compared as a positive figure, and never flagged as an impossible value.
findings.impact: Negative stored aggregates — a clear data fault — pass the integrity scan silently, and may even compare as matching.

findings.title: Only two aggregate checks exist
findings.detail: reconcileEntity compares only stats.totalTrips against derived trips and stats.totalPaid against the sum of Paid payments. entityDerived also returns payments and subs counts, which nothing compares. There is no check for subscriptions, ratings, wallet balances or driver earnings.
findings.impact: Whole classes of stored-vs-derived drift are invisible to a tab whose stated purpose is to surface every such disagreement.

findings.title: reconcileEntity is monkey-patched at load
findings.detail: The original function is defined at L18515 and reassigned at L20437, keeping the original as __origReconcileEntity (which is otherwise unreferenced except inside the wrapper). Only the patched version applies the window-aware orphan/expectedGap definitions. Any call site that captured the function into a local variable before the patch line would get the unpatched behaviour.
findings.impact: No such stale capture was found, but the pattern makes the classification rules silently order-dependent on script position.

findings.title: The two cards count different populations
findings.detail: renderWindowSettings computes its 'expected' and 'alert' counters over Object.keys(DB.riders) only. integrityScan, which feeds the scan card, iterates riders and then drivers. The same page therefore shows two different 'empty inside the window' totals whenever a driver is an orphan.
findings.evidence:
var accounts=Object.keys(DB.riders);
  var orphans=accounts.filter(function(id){var r=reconcileEntity(id);return r&&r.orphan;});
findings.impact: The alert number an operator acts on depends on which card they read.

findings.title: commitPublishVersion never closes its modal
findings.detail: The handler logs, re-renders and toasts but omits closeModal(), unlike sibling commit handlers such as commitSuspendSurge and replyToInbound. The modal stays open over the freshly re-rendered pane with both fields still populated.
findings.impact: Pressing Publish again appends a duplicate version row and re-points currentVersion at the same string.

findings.title: Driver ToS and Privacy consents are stored and displayed but never counted
findings.detail: renderLegalConsent builds the tos and privacy pools from DB.riders only, while getUserConsent seeds tos and privacy for drivers as well and the driver 360 profile renders both rows.
findings.impact: Driver ToS/Privacy compliance is invisible in the compliance figures and drivers never receive those re-consent reminders.

findings.title: Legal content is interpolated into innerHTML without escaping
findings.detail: doc.label, v.version, v.summary and the operator-typed version and summary strings are concatenated straight into the pane's innerHTML.
findings.impact: Operator-supplied text is executed as markup in the settings pane; a stored payload would persist for the session.

findings.title: No version format, ordering or uniqueness validation
findings.detail: The only check is that both fields are non-empty. Any string is accepted as a version, no comparison is made against the existing currentVersion, and isConsentCurrent uses strict string equality, so '2.1' and '2.10' are different versions.
findings.evidence: if(!version||!summary){toast('⚠ Enter both a version number and a summary','warn');return;}
findings.impact: Publishing 'abc' or a lower version such as '1.0' over '2.1' silently becomes the current version, and a repeated version creates a duplicate history row.

findings.title: Publishing a legal version has no confirmation gate
findings.detail: commitPublishVersion checks requirePerm('manage_settings') but appears in neither GATE_SPECS nor any guardAction() call, so no confirm dialog is shown. The lesser action on the same card — sending reminders — is gated (GATE_SPECS.sendReconsentReminder, L20857). The button's 'danger' class is cosmetic.
findings.impact: A single mis-click publishes a site-wide legal version and instantly invalidates every user's stored consent, with no chance to review.

findings.title: Broadcast and push audience lists have diverged
findings.detail: broadcastAudienceIds implements 9 segments keyed 'all' for all riders; pushAudienceIds implements 11 keyed 'all_riders' and adds economy_drivers and comfort_drivers. The two are ~90% identical code kept in step by hand.
findings.impact: A segment added to one channel silently does not exist in the other, and the same conceptual audience has two different keys.

findings.title: Inbound and outbound mail content is rendered without escaping
findings.detail: m.name, m.subject, m.message, e.subject, e.body and the operator's broadcast subject and body are all interpolated raw into innerHTML in the tables and both modals.
findings.impact: Content submitted by a member of the public through the website contact form is rendered as markup inside the admin panel.

findings.title: MAIL- ids are derived from array length
findings.detail: sendSystemEmail composes 'MAIL-'+String(DB.emailOutbox.length+1).padStart(4,'0') rather than using a monotonic counter, and replyToInbound repeats the same expression independently.
findings.impact: Removing any record would make the next send reuse an existing id.

findings.title: No preview, test-send, scheduling, opt-out handling or length cap
findings.detail: The composer sends immediately to the whole segment. There is no draft preview, no send-to-self, no schedule, no unsubscribe or suppression list, and no maxlength on the body (the push composer caps at 120 characters).
findings.impact: The confirmation gate warns the message cannot be recalled while offering no way to check it first.

findings.title: Profile button breaks for records with a null toId
findings.detail: previewEmail renders openProfile('<e.toId>') unconditionally. Inbox replies store toId:null and several corporate-approval emails pass a raw email address as toId, so the button becomes openProfile('null').
findings.impact: Clicking through from those sent emails fails with a 'No record for null' toast.

findings.title: Replying to an inbound message writes no audit entry
findings.detail: replyToInbound sets status, writes the outbox record, closes the modal and toasts, but never calls logAction — the only outbound path in this pane with no audit trail.
findings.impact: There is no record of who replied to a member of the public or when.

findings.title: replyToInbound bypasses the sendSystemEmail choke point
findings.detail: The module comment states sendSystemEmail() is the single choke point every real trigger calls, yet replyToInbound constructs and unshifts a MAIL- record inline with toId:null and the raw inbound address instead of emailFor().
findings.impact: The outbox is no longer produced by a single function, so any future change to send behaviour silently misses replies.

findings.title: Duplicated audience logic between push and email
findings.detail: pushAudienceIds() and broadcastAudienceIds() are near-identical hand-maintained implementations that already differ in segment count and in the key used for all riders.
findings.impact: Any audience change must be made twice, and the two channels already target different populations.

findings.title: No frequency cap, quiet hours, opt-out registry, templates or scheduling
findings.detail: The pane is a composer and a log. There is no delivery status, device token, opt-in registry, quiet-hours rule, frequency cap, deep link, rich payload, localisation or scheduling — while the gate warns that push fatigue costs opt-ins permanently.
findings.impact: Nothing in the panel prevents the exact harm its own confirmation dialog warns about.

findings.title: No per-recipient record is kept for a push
findings.detail: pushAudienceIds() is computed, counted and discarded; a single PUSH- record stores only a recipients integer. The Email outbox, by contrast, writes one row per person.
findings.impact: It is impossible to answer whether a specific rider or driver received a given push.

findings.title: Option text and stored audience labels disagree
findings.detail: The picker offers 'Riders with no active subscription' and 'Flagged drivers (declines/complaints)' while PUSH_AUDIENCE_LABEL stores 'No active subscription' and 'Flagged drivers'. The record keeps the label, so the log shows wording the operator never selected.
findings.impact: The sent log and the By-audience chips describe segments in different words from the composer.

findings.title: Push content is rendered without escaping
findings.detail: p.title, p.body and p.audience are concatenated straight into the table's innerHTML.
findings.impact: Operator-typed payload text is executed as markup in the settings pane.

findings.title: The audience is persisted as a label, not a key
findings.detail: sendPushNotification stores PUSH_AUDIENCE_LABEL[seg]||seg on the record instead of seg itself.
findings.impact: A past send cannot be resolved back to a segment programmatically, so there is no resend, no cohort re-derivation and no analytics by segment.

findings.title: The character counter ignores the title field
findings.detail: #push-title fires updatePushCharCount() on input, but the function reads only #push-body, so the 40-character title cap has no counter and no feedback.
findings.impact: An operator typing a long title is silently truncated at 40 characters with nothing on screen indicating the limit.

findings.title: The recipient count is computed twice and never confirmed
findings.detail: updatePushAudienceCount computes the count for the caption and sendPushNotification recomputes it at send time; the confirmation gate has no summary line and shows no count at all, although the sibling email gate advises checking the count before confirming.
findings.impact: The operator confirms an irreversible fan-out without seeing how many devices it reaches, and the figure can drift between caption and send.

findings.title: A better export path exists but is unreachable from this tab
findings.detail: exportData(btn,page) and doExport(page) offer CSV or JSON, a native save-location picker via window.showSaveFilePicker with a fallback, and row-count logging. This tab's eight buttons bypass all of it, and exportRows only knows the keys 'subscriptions', 'quickrides' and a default 'trips'.
findings.impact: Two parallel export systems with different encoders, filename conventions and audit detail, only one of which is reachable here.

findings.title: Cancelled status is matched two different ways inside one function
findings.detail: captureDailySnapshot counts active subscriptions with !/cancel/i.test(status) but counts cancelled quick rides with status === 'Cancelled'.
findings.impact: A status such as 'Cancelled by rider' counts as cancelled for one metric and not for the other, so the two snapshot figures disagree.

findings.title: Export audit entries record no row count
findings.detail: downloadCSV logs only 'Exported <filename>'. The alternative doExport path logs 'Exported N <name> rows as CSV (filename)'.
findings.impact: The audit trail cannot answer how much data left the system in any given export.

findings.title: Four exports silently drop fields
findings.detail: The audit CSV omits before/after, the email CSV omits body, the inbox CSV omits message, and the snapshot CSV omits quickRideRevenue and subRevenue. Nothing in the UI says so.
findings.impact: An operator who exports 'everything' for an investigation or a data request receives an incomplete extract without being told.

findings.title: The snapshot confirmation dialog states a rule the code does not implement
findings.detail: GATE_SPECS.captureDailySnapshot tells the operator that capturing twice in one day overwrites the earlier snapshot. captureDailySnapshot only unshifts; there is no de-duplication by date and no overwrite anywhere in the file.
findings.evidence: 'Capturing twice in one day overwrites the earlier snapshot.'
findings.impact: Operators are told an incorrect safety property and will silently accumulate multiple same-day snapshots that skew the trend chart.

findings.title: Two incompatible CSV encoders coexist
findings.detail: toCSV quotes a field only when it contains a comma, quote or newline; buildCSV quotes every field unconditionally. Both are live — this tab uses toCSV, exportIntegrity and the doExport modal use buildCSV.
findings.impact: Exports from different parts of the panel produce differently-quoted CSV for the same data.

findings.title: Comfort subscription trips are simulated as economy
findings.detail: simulateRateCard picks the class with /comfort/i.test(t.kind||''), but a subscription trip's kind is the literal 'Subscription', so every plan trip falls through to economy rates regardless of the vehicle actually used.
findings.impact: The rider-impact percentage an approver relies on understates the effect on comfort subscribers.

findings.title: Draft version ids can collide
findings.detail: proposeRateCard names drafts 'RC-DRAFT-'+(DB.rateCardHistory.length+1). approveRateCard unshifts the superseded live card into the same array, so the length-derived counter can produce a name already in use, and approveRateCard resolves drafts with .find() on version.
findings.impact: Approving one draft can publish a different draft that happens to share the generated name.

findings.title: Entering 0 in a rate field silently keeps the old value
findings.detail: All four numeric fields use parseFloat(val(id))||current, and 0 is falsy, so a deliberate zero, a blank field or a non-numeric entry all revert to the existing value with no message.
findings.impact: An operator proposing a zero base fare gets a draft that silently contains the old value, and the simulation they approve is not the change they entered.

findings.title: planFloorCheck() is dead code, so the margin floor blocks nothing
findings.detail: The comment above planFloorCheck calls it 'the check that blocks a publish. A warning gets clicked through; a block does not.' The function has zero call sites, and the Floors and guardrails bullet claiming a plan below the floor cannot go live is prose only.
findings.impact: A below-floor plan price is displayed in red and can still be proposed and approved.

findings.title: The approval dialog claims an effect the build does not have
findings.detail: The guard's first consequence reads 'Every new trip prices under this card from the moment it goes live.' No trip, quote or invoice in the panel is priced from DB.rateCard.
findings.evidence: 'Every new trip prices under this card from the moment it goes live.'
findings.impact: The operator approves a change believing it takes effect on live pricing when it changes only this tab's display.

findings.title: The versions list is capped at six with no overflow indicator
findings.detail: renderPricing renders DB.rateCardHistory.slice(0,6) and shows nothing when more exist; the per-draft Approve button is the only way to approve.
findings.impact: The seventh and later drafts are invisible and therefore unapprovable through the UI.

findings.title: A refused fare capture is recorded as done and can never be retried
findings.detail: postFareCapture wraps both postLedger calls in withIdempotency and returns true unconditionally. If independent rounding of net and VAT makes them differ from gross, postLedger rejects the entry and returns null, but the idempotency key has already been written by the wrapper.
findings.impact: The trip is silently missing from the books forever, a later backfill will not retry it, and the backfill's reported success count includes it.

findings.title: Journal entries cannot be traced to what they record
findings.detail: Each entry stores ref, tsMs and a meta payload identifying the trip, rider, refund, credit note, dispatch or driver, but the renderer prints only id, type, total and the Dr/Cr lines. moneyRejects likewise keeps ref, tsMs and postings and prints only type and why.
findings.impact: An operator looking at a posting cannot see which trip or customer it belongs to, and a refused posting cannot be diagnosed from the pane.

findings.title: Rendering the ledger walks the whole journal seventeen times
findings.detail: accountBalance iterates every entry and every posting; trialBalance calls it once per account (12), ledgerReconcile three times and demoDoubleRefund twice.
findings.impact: Render cost grows with the square of activity, and renderLedger runs on every go('settings') as well as after both buttons.

findings.title: The backfill button is a no-op after boot and floods the log
findings.detail: ledgerBoot runs the identical loop at page load, so every non-cancelled trip already has a fare-capture idempotency key. Pressing the button therefore posts nothing and drives withIdempotency's duplicate branch once per trip, each emitting a duplicate_suppressed audit entry and a warn toast.
findings.evidence: toast('⛔ Already done — this exact '+operation+' was completed '+fmtAge(nowMs()-seen.tsMs)+' ago. Nothing was charged again.','warn');
findings.impact: On a seeded panel the button appears to do nothing while filling the audit log with hundreds of duplicate_suppressed rows and queueing a toast per trip.

findings.title: The out-of-balance indicator can never fire
findings.detail: postLedger refuses any posting whose debits and credits differ, so the sum over the entries it accepted is always balanced and trialBalance().balanced is structurally true.
findings.impact: The most prominent safety signal on the pane is decorative; a real imbalance would surface only as refused postings, which are shown separately and only when non-empty.

findings.title: An invited, never-logged-in user is assignable to on-call
findings.detail: The 42 slot selects and the handover recipient select are both built from every DB.teamUsers entry with no status filter. USR-4 Noura Al-Fahad has status 'Invited' and lastLogin 'Not yet' and is offered exactly like an active operator, with no warning in the option label or on save.
findings.impact: A shift can read as covered while the named person has never logged in, which is precisely the failure the rota exists to prevent.

findings.title: Nothing actually pages the on-call person
findings.detail: The entire escalation chain ends at pushOpsNotification, an in-panel notification list. There is no SMS, push or paging transport anywhere in the file, so the rota names a person that no automated channel ever reaches. UNVERIFIED whether paging is intended to exist elsewhere - no integration is present in the artifact.
findings.impact: An operator who is asleep is named correctly and still never contacted.

findings.title: One-off cover overrides are read but never written
findings.detail: DB.onCallSchedule.overrides is declared with the shape comment {day, block, tier, userId, note, tsMs} and is consulted by onCallNow (last matching override wins, via .pop()). Nothing anywhere writes to it - no UI control, no function, no seed. The override branch and the ' (cover)' suffix appended by onCallName are therefore unreachable, and rotaGaps ignores overrides entirely, so an override that covered a hole would still be reported as a gap.
findings.evidence: overrides:[]                          /* one-off cover: {day, block, tier, userId, note, tsMs} */
findings.impact: The documented mechanism for one-off shift cover does not exist; a swap can only be recorded by overwriting the standing assignment.

findings.title: renderOnCall and the whole simple roster are orphaned
findings.detail: renderOnCall() looks up document.getElementById('oncall-body') and returns immediately when it is missing. A full-file grep for 'oncall-body' returns exactly one hit - the lookup itself at L15790. No markup declares it and no JS creates it. Consequently the two dropdowns (#oncall-primary, #oncall-secondary) and the Save roster button never render, saveOnCall() (L15799) is unreachable, onCallNameSimple() (L15785, only called from saveOnCall) is unreachable, and DB.onCall (L15776) is fully dead - written only by saveOnCall, read only by onCallNameSimple. The renderer is still invoked on every Settings open from L8819.
findings.impact: Wasted work on every Settings navigation, and a whole configuration surface plus its data object that a reader would reasonably believe is live.

findings.title: Rota changes are audited without a diff
findings.detail: setRotaSlot calls logAction('rota_updated','settings',slotKey,summary) with no before/after payload, so auditDiffHTML renders nothing for these rows. The log records who now holds a slot but not who was displaced. rota_updated is also absent from ACTION_LABELS, as is shift_handover.
findings.impact: After an incident it is impossible to reconstruct from the log who was scheduled before a slot was changed.

findings.title: The grid onChange expression reads an always-undefined this.value
findings.detail: Each cell's handler is setRotaSlot('day','block','tier', this.value || document.getElementById('rota-day-block-tier').value). cselPick executes the expression as (new Function(onChangeExpr))(), so this is the global object and this.value is undefined; the || fallback, reading the hidden input cselPick has just written, is doing all the work. Any error inside the expression is swallowed by a bare catch(e){}.
findings.impact: The mechanism works only by accident of the fallback, and failures are silent.

findings.title: The rota runs on the real clock while the panel runs on a frozen demo clock
findings.detail: currentBlock(d) and currentDayKey(d) default to new Date(), the browser's real wall clock, whereas the rest of the panel is pinned to REQ_NOW_REF (25 Jun 2026 09:14, L9555). 'On call now', 'today', the blue current-shift highlight in the grid and the day/block stamped on every handover record are therefore computed from a different moment than every other surface.
findings.impact: The escalation lookup and the grid highlight can name a different day and shift than the data the operator is looking at.

findings.title: Every audited action re-renders the whole audit UI
findings.detail: logAction ends with if(typeof renderAuditLog==='function')renderAuditLog();, unconditionally. renderAuditLog rebuilds the full Activity-log page body and its three custom selects as well as this preview, whether or not either surface is on screen. There are hundreds of logAction call sites across the panel.
findings.impact: Constant hidden DOM work on every audited action anywhere in the app. UNVERIFIED by execution - static analysis only.

findings.title: Switching settings tabs renders nothing, so panes go stale
findings.detail: switchSettingsTab toggles CSS classes only; every settings renderer fires once, up front, in the go('settings') branch. A tab opened long after navigation therefore shows data as old as the last navigation to Settings. The Activity preview is the sole exception, because logAction keeps it fresh independently.
findings.impact: Operators can act on stale configuration or stale tables without any indication.

findings.title: The Activity pane description misdescribes what it shows
findings.detail: The pane reads 'Every configuration change made in Settings, newest first.' The preview branch of renderAuditLog takes DB.auditLog.slice(0,4) with no predicate whatsoever - there is no entityType==='settings' filter anywhere in the path - so it shows the four newest entries of any kind: driver approvals, payouts, refunds, claim take-overs and everything else.
findings.impact: An operator reading the pane will conclude that no settings changes have occurred when in fact settings entries have simply been pushed out by unrelated activity.

findings.title: The declared audit-log view permission is never enforced
findings.detail: PAGE_PERMISSIONS['audit-log'] declares perms:[{key:'view',label:'View activity log'}] at L10650, but requirePagePerm('audit-log','view') is never called anywhere in the file. The 'View full activity log' button navigates straight there, and the preview itself is ungated.
findings.impact: Every operator can read the complete activity log of every colleague, including permission changes and money actions, despite a permission existing for exactly that.

findings.title: Audit ids are derived from array length and collide at the cap
findings.detail: logAction sets id:'AUD-'+String(DB.auditLog.length+1).padStart(4,'0') at L3136, then truncates the array to 500 at L3148. Once the cap is reached length stays pinned at 500, so every subsequent entry receives the same id AUD-0501. The pad width of 4 also overflows past 9999 in principle.
findings.impact: Audit ids stop being unique in exactly the high-volume situation where they matter, and searching AUD-0501 matches an unbounded number of rows.

findings.title: entry.action is never displayed
findings.detail: auditRowsHTML (L9296-L9305) renders four cells: e.ts, e.actorName, e.summary + auditDiffHTML(...), and auditEntityLink(e). The raw action key appears in no column, no tooltip and no title attribute, and ACTION_LABELS is never applied to a row.
findings.impact: A reader cannot see what kind of action a row was except by parsing the free-text summary prose, which is composed differently at every call site.

findings.title: Object and array payloads render as [object Object], and one caller marks everything changed
