findings.detail: auditDiffHTML compares with strict !== and string-concatenates values, with no serialisation and no deep compare. Callers that pass whole arrays or objects — saveCancellationPolicy (L7383), saveOpsLimits (L7441), commitSurgeSchedule (L12385), commitSearchPhases (L8117) — therefore produce [object Object] output. saveCancellationPolicy additionally passes a deep clone as before and the same live array as after, so every index compares as a different object reference.
findings.impact: The diff for several settings changes is unreadable, and the cancellation-policy diff falsely reports every field as modified on every save.

findings.title: The CSV export drops the diff and the actor id
findings.detail: exportAuditLog maps only 7 of the 10 audit fields — id, ts, actorName, action, entityType, entityId and summary (L7624). actorId, before and after are omitted, and the export ignores the page's active filters entirely.
findings.impact: The before/after diff — the strongest evidence in the log and the only record of what a value actually changed from — cannot leave the browser, and the stable actorId is replaced by a display name that a later rename would make ambiguous.

findings.title: The diff renderer cannot show deletions
findings.detail: auditDiffHTML iterates Object.keys(after) only (L3164). A key present in before and absent from after is never visited, so its removal produces no output at all; when no other key differs, RULE 4 returns an empty string and the row shows no diff.
findings.impact: Revoking a field — clearing a permission, removing an assignment — can be audited as if nothing changed.

findings.title: The entity link resolver falls back to a name substring search
findings.detail: resolveId (L3266-L3275) first tries a direct key hit in DB.riders, DB.drivers, DB.trips, DB.subscriptions, DB.payments and DB.complaints, then falls back to a substring search across rider then driver NAMES. auditEntityLink (L9281) uses it to decide whether column 4 is a clickable rowLink or grey monospace text.
findings.impact: Short or word-like entityIds resolve to whichever rider or driver name happens to contain them, so the audit row links to the wrong person; entityIds outside the six buckets (settings, USR-3, ticket ids, promo codes, idempotency keys) are non-navigable grey text.

findings.title: Timestamps carry no date and mix two incompatible formats
findings.detail: logAction writes ts via toLocaleTimeString([],{hour:'2-digit',minute:'2-digit',second:'2-digit'}) at L3137 — time only, and in the viewer's browser locale. The 8 seeded rows (L2863-L2872) use a different, dated format such as '25 Jun, 08:14 AM'. Both flow into the same Time column and into the CSV export as 'time'.
findings.impact: The Time column mixes formats, and once the log runs past a day boundary a runtime entry cannot be dated at all — including in the exported CSV.

findings.title: A no-op self-assignment of the router
findings.detail: L3115 contains the statement window.go=window.go; immediately after the empty openUserSwitchGuardless stub.
findings.impact: Harmless, but it is a leftover that suggests an abandoned wrapper.

findings.title: Badge severity class is maintained for only five badges
findings.detail: Only sbb-contacts, sb-ticket-badge, sbb-commit, sbb-fairness and sbb-inbox have their 'a' (alert/red) or 'n' (neutral/grey) class recomputed. All others keep the class baked into their markup, so sbb-subs and sbb-qr are permanently grey and every other badge is permanently red even at zero.
findings.impact: Colour stops carrying meaning: a red badge no longer implies something needs attention.

findings.title: Doc line references drift 1-3 lines from source
findings.detail: Verified offsets: openProfile is at L8827 (doc says 8829), openApplicantDetail L8865 (doc 8868), openTicketDetail L8879 (doc 8882), markAllRead L2258 (doc 2259), NOTIF_PANEL_PREVIEW L2228 (doc 2227), and inside refreshNavCounts qr is L9394, activeSubs L9395, expSoon L9396 (doc says 9393/9394/9395). The corrected values are used in this fragment.
findings.impact: Anyone navigating by the doc's line numbers lands a couple of lines early; all cited functions do exist.

findings.title: findSbEl() resolves nav elements by substring-matching a raw onclick attribute
findings.detail: findSbEl(id) scans every .sb-item and returns the one whose onclick attribute string contains "'"+id+"'". It returns the last match rather than the first.
findings.evidence: scans all .sb-item and returns the one whose onclick attribute contains "'"+id+"'"
findings.impact: Any future page id that also appears as a quoted token inside another item's onclick will highlight the wrong nav row.

findings.title: refreshNavCounts() destroys the seeded subtitle map in place
findings.detail: The function reassigns six keys on the shared subs object (subscriptions, quickrides, trips, drivers, riders, renewal) rather than computing a display string locally.
findings.impact: The literal values in the subs map at L2169 are permanently overwritten after the first navigation, so they are not the fallback a reader of that line would assume.

findings.title: Six routable ids have no subtitle entry
findings.detail: exec-overview, corporate, corp-detail, rwallets, fraud and ticket-detail appear in the titles map but not in subs, so go() sets #tb-sub to an empty string.
findings.impact: Those six pages render with an empty subtitle and a dangling separator slash.

findings.title: The .sb-logo-text class has no element
findings.detail: Two CSS rules style .sb-logo-text (L36-37, plus a mobile override at L432) but grep for class="sb-logo-text" returns zero matches in the markup. The logo is an inline base64 PNG only.
findings.impact: Dead CSS, plus a mobile rule (.sb .sb-logo-text{opacity:1!important}) that can never apply.

findings.title: The page-title fallback is the raw id
findings.detail: go() sets #tb-title to titles[id] || id, so an unregistered id surfaces to the user as a lowercase slug.
findings.impact: Internal identifiers leak into the UI on any routing mistake.

findings.title: The sidebar footer advertises a dropdown that does not exist
findings.detail: #sb-ft-role reads 'Owner - settings' followed by a down-caret. Clicking anywhere on the footer calls go('my-account', null); there is no menu. Clicking the top-bar avatar likewise goes straight to the openUserSwitch modal with no intermediate dropdown.
findings.impact: Affordance mismatch - users look for a menu that never opens.

findings.title: The sidebar pin feature is styled but unwired
findings.detail: The .sb.pin selector appears in eight CSS rules (L30, L31, L35, L37, L40, L47, L49, L54) but grep finds zero JavaScript that adds, removes or toggles the class, and no element carries it. There is no pin button in the sidebar markup.
findings.impact: Dead CSS. The intended trigger cannot be recovered from the file.

findings.title: Three badges render an empty string on zero while the rest render 0
findings.detail: sbb-fraud (L5645), sbb-corporate (L6496) and sb-readiness-badge (L13014) are written as value||'' so a zero produces an empty badge; the other twelve write a literal 0.
findings.impact: Cosmetic inconsistency: an operator cannot tell an empty badge (zero) from a badge that has never been computed.

findings.title: __gateCount is assigned by one installer and incremented by the others
findings.detail: installActionGates() assigns window.__gateCount = n at L18085; installUniversalGates() (L18381) and installGateSweep() (L20900) add to it. The arithmetic is correct only because installActionGates runs first.
findings.evidence: installActionGates() ASSIGNS window.__gateCount = n while the other two installers ADD to it
findings.impact: Any reordering of the three installers silently resets the count, and the final value also depends on how many guardAction calls returned true at runtime - so the number cannot be trusted as a coverage metric.

findings.title: A whole-body MutationObserver exists only to auto-size selects
findings.detail: new MutationObserver(...).observe(document.body, {childList:true, subtree:true}) calls scheduleAutoSizeSelects(), which debounces to a single 60ms setTimeout.
findings.impact: Every table render, every toast and every modal write re-triggers the observer. Debounced, but it is a permanent whole-document listener for a cosmetic concern.

findings.title: Function `fmtEtaMin()` is defined but never called
findings.detail: Defined at L7282 (1 line). The identifier appears exactly once in the whole file — at its own definition — so no call site, onclick binding or string reference exists.
findings.impact: Minor dead helper.

findings.title: Function `openUserSwitchGuardless()` is defined but never called
findings.detail: Defined at L3114 (1 line). The identifier appears exactly once in the whole file — at its own definition — so no call site, onclick binding or string reference exists.
findings.impact: Minor dead helper.

findings.title: Function `permIcon()` is defined but never called
findings.detail: Defined at L10544 (1 line). The identifier appears exactly once in the whole file — at its own definition — so no call site, onclick binding or string reference exists.
findings.impact: Minor dead helper.

findings.title: Function `rcCompCap()` is defined but never called
findings.detail: Defined at L14742 (1 line). The identifier appears exactly once in the whole file — at its own definition — so no call site, onclick binding or string reference exists.
findings.impact: Minor dead helper.

findings.title: Function `renderLiveMap()` is defined but never called
findings.detail: Defined at L11632 (4 lines). The identifier appears exactly once in the whole file — at its own definition — so no call site, onclick binding or string reference exists.
findings.impact: Minor dead helper.

findings.title: The boot IIFE must be last in the file, and nothing enforces it
findings.detail: The header comment states three invariants in capitals: seeds run after all data exists, each of the 16 steps is isolated with a needs[] list of DB keys, and this block must remain the last thing in the script - because function declarations hoist but var initialisers do not.
findings.evidence: header comment L21780-21806 states the block must remain the last thing in the script
findings.impact: A module appended after the IIFE would have its var initialisers unassigned when the seeds run, producing a partial boot whose only symptom is an err toast counting failed modules.

findings.title: The design-token system is bypassed in about forty places
findings.detail: 26 custom properties are declared on :root (L11-21), but roughly 40 stylesheet colours are literal hex, including two different blues for live affordances (--blue #185FA5 versus rgba(26,115,232,...) at L341/347). --sb-bg and --bg are both #EEF0F3. The .h-green/.h-amber/.h-red and .days-ok/.days-warn/.days-crit rules restate token hex values literally instead of using var(). DB.branding.accent duplicates --blue in JS at L18388. Four classes (.map-stat, .ms-item, .ms-lbl, .ms-val) are each defined twice with conflicting layout rules and the second block wins; .sm is overloaded for both .btn and .csel.
findings.evidence: --sb-bg and --bg are both #EEF0F3 - two names, one value
findings.impact: A theme change (including any future dark mode) will miss roughly forty colours, and the duplicate class definitions make layout changes unpredictable.

findings.title: The panel cannot run under any reasonable Content Security Policy
findings.detail: It requires unsafe-inline for hundreds of onclick attributes, unsafe-eval for new Function(onChangeExpr) at L5411, unpkg.com in script-src and style-src, and *.tile.openstreetmap.org in img-src.
findings.impact: Deploying this behind a standard CSP is not possible without a rewrite of the event-binding approach.

findings.title: Three registry entries are declared and then discarded
findings.detail: GATE_SPECS.openLowRatingTicket is explicitly null with the comment that the modal is the deliberate step. GATE_SWEEP.assignBackup (L20883) and GATE_SWEEP.autoHandoff (L20884) are deleted at L20886-20887.
findings.impact: 90 registered names install only 88 gates, so any count derived from the registry literals is wrong by two.

findings.title: auditDiffHTML never shows a removed field
findings.detail: The both-present branch iterates Object.keys(after) only. A key present in before and absent from after produces no diff line at all. The !after branch returns an empty string, and !before renders every after key as a creation.
findings.evidence: for each key of after: if before lacks the key, key: value; else if values differ, key: old -> new. Keys present in before but absent from after are never shown.
findings.impact: Deletions are invisible in the diff column. L10833 (edit_user_permissions) passes only counts, so a wholesale permission wipe renders as 'permissions: 13 permissions -> 0 permissions' and nothing about which permissions were removed.

findings.title: openUserSwitchGuardless() is an empty stub with no callers
findings.detail: Verified: the entire declaration is 'function openUserSwitchGuardless(){}' at L3114, and grep finds no other reference to the name anywhere in the file.
findings.impact: Dead code whose name implies a deliberate guard bypass that was either never wired up or removed without deleting the symbol. Given that the guarded path (commitUserSwitch) is itself ungated, the name is doubly misleading.

findings.title: PERMISSION_DESC.manage_team is assigned twice
findings.detail: The object literal at L3255 sets one description; a bare statement at L10520 overwrites it at module-evaluation time with 'Add or edit team members, change roles, and grant or revoke any permission - including this one.' Only the second string ever renders.
findings.evidence: PERMISSION_DESC.manage_team is mutated at module-evaluation time by a bare statement at L10520
findings.impact: A reader of the PERMISSION_DESC literal sees text that is never displayed anywhere.

findings.title: Seeded and runtime audit timestamps use incompatible formats
findings.detail: The 8 seeded rows carry full date-and-time strings such as '25 Jun, 08:14 AM' (L2863). logAction produces time-only via new Date().toLocaleTimeString([], {hour:'2-digit',minute:'2-digit',second:'2-digit'}) at L3137, with an empty locale array so the format follows the browser.
findings.impact: A log spanning both is unsortable by timestamp and ambiguous after midnight, and the format is not stable across browsers or locales.

findings.title: Team-user audit rows are never clickable
findings.detail: auditEntityLink uses resolveId to decide whether an entityId is linkable. resolveId searches riders, drivers, trips, subscriptions, payments and complaints - not teamUsers. Every entityType 'team_user' row therefore renders its USR-* id as inert monospace text. Separately, the seeded process_all_payouts row has entityId '' and auditEntityLink returns an empty string for falsy ids, so that cell is blank rather than showing a placeholder.
findings.evidence: resolveId buckets = ['riders','drivers','trips','subscriptions','payments','complaints'] - teamUsers is not among them
findings.impact: Permission and team-management entries, which are exactly the rows an auditor most wants to pivot from, are the only rows with no navigation affordance.

findings.title: The 2FA toggle mutates state without re-rendering its own label
findings.detail: toggleMa2FA(val) writes u.twoFA, logs toggle_2fa with before {twoFA:!val} and after {twoFA:val}, and toasts - but never calls renderMaSecurity(). The Enabled/Disabled text is written at L3022 during the previous render.
findings.evidence: Writes u.twoFA=val, toasts, but renderMaSecurity() is not called so the Enabled/Disabled label at L3022 stays stale
findings.impact: The toggle and its own label disagree for the rest of the page visit, so an operator cannot tell from the screen whether two-factor authentication is on.

findings.title: The permission model is unauthenticated in-memory data described to users as enforced
findings.detail: CURRENT_USER_ID is a hardcoded module-scope var with no login, token or persistence. u.permissions is a plain array on a plain object with no integrity check, and can() is a client-side indexOf. The My Account copy at L3082 states permissions are 'enforced everywhere in this panel... any blocked action shows a lock message and is logged in the Activity log as a denial', and the card header at L1165 repeats 'Enforced everywhere in this panel, not just shown here'.
findings.impact: Expected for a demo, but the copy overstates it in two directions: anyone with a console can grant themselves anything, and findings #9, #10 and #11 show the 'enforced everywhere' claim is also untrue in-panel.

findings.title: The two denial paths write incompatible entityId formats under one entityType
findings.detail: requirePerm logs entityType 'permission' with the bare key (e.g. manage_team) and summary 'Blocked - tried "<label>" without permission'. requirePagePerm logs the same entityType with a dot-joined pair (e.g. growth.create_promo) and summary 'Blocked: <currentUserName()> lacks "<Page> - <action label>"'. requirePerm passes no before/after so the diff renders empty; requirePagePerm passes {} and {} which also renders empty.
findings.evidence: requirePerm entityId = bare perm key; requirePagePerm entityId = pageKey+'.'+permKey
findings.impact: Any consumer grouping denials by entityId sees two incompatible key spaces under one entityType. permission_denied is at least one of the few security keys that IS in ACTION_LABELS, so denials are filterable.

findings.title: <html> receives lang but never dir
findings.detail: L7943 sets document.documentElement lang and the inline comment states dir is kept off <html> on purpose; the rationale comment at L370-L381 explains that mirroring layout without translated text would look broken. The visual reasoning is sound, but the accessibility consequence is unaddressed: assistive technology is told the document is Arabic while the base direction stays LTR and 40 of 41 page shells contain English content.
findings.evidence: document.documentElement.setAttribute('lang',isAr?'ar':'en'); /* lang for accessibility/SEO only — dir stays off <html> on purpose */
findings.impact: Screen-reader users in Arabic mode get English page content announced under an ar language tag with LTR base direction.

findings.title: Arabic reason-code labels render unconditionally, including in English mode
findings.detail: L14759 concatenates labelEn + '  —  ' + labelAr into every reason-code dropdown option, and L15078 gives labelAr its own always-visible table column with an inline direction:rtl — the only such inline style outside the sidebar and settings shell. Neither is gated on the current language. The source comment calls this deliberate ('the floor is in Riyadh and the guide is in English').
findings.impact: An English-only operator sees Arabic text in a dropdown they cannot read, while the Arabic-mode operator sees it on an otherwise entirely English screen.

findings.title: Arabic widens the sidebar by 32px with no main-area adjustment
findings.detail: L31 takes the expanded rail from 236px to 268px under body.lang-ar, and L435 does the same for the mobile drawer via .sb[dir="rtl"]. .main has no width rule keyed on body.lang-ar and relies on flex to absorb the difference. The two hooks (body.lang-ar for desktop, .sb[dir="rtl"] for mobile) are also two mechanisms for one concept; both are set by applyLanguage today, so they stay in sync only by convention.
findings.impact: On a narrow desktop viewport the Arabic rail eats 32px more of the content area, and no page's table layout accounts for it.

findings.title: Five settings-tab labels are used in markup but missing from the Arabic dictionary
findings.detail: stab.branding (L1431), stab.integrity (L1432), stab.rota (L1433), stab.ledger (L1434) and stab.pricing (L1435) all appear as data-i18n keys in the settings tab rail but have no entry in LANG_STRINGS.ar. Verified by grep: each returns 1 markup hit and 0 dictionary hits. Because applyLanguage falls back to el.dataset.i18nOriginal whenever dict[key] is undefined, a missing key is indistinguishable from a deliberately untranslated element — no console warning, no visual marker.
findings.impact: In Arabic mode five tab labels sit mid-rail among translated neighbours still reading Branding, Data integrity, On-call rota, Ledger and Pricing, and the failure mode is silent drift every time a new tab is added.

findings.title: No attribute is translatable
findings.detail: The file has zero occurrences of data-i18n-placeholder, -title, -alt, -html, -value or -aria. Every tooltip, placeholder and accessible name is permanently English, including the global search placeholder at L571 and the icon-button titles at L481, L545, L554, L557, L567 and L568.
findings.evidence: placeholder="Search any ID: RDR / DRV / TRP / SUB…"
findings.impact: In Arabic mode <html lang="ar"> tells assistive technology to read English title and placeholder text with Arabic phonology.

findings.title: No language toggle in the chrome, and the only path is permission-gated
findings.detail: There is no topbar switcher, no flag icon, no EN|AR control and no keyboard shortcut; greps for lang-toggle and langToggle return zero. The <select id="cfg-gen-lang"> at L1496 has no onchange or oninput, so changing it does nothing by itself — the commit is the Save general settings button at L1512, and saveGeneralConfig is gated by requirePerm('manage_settings') at L7987. In the seeded data only USR-1 holds that permission.
findings.impact: Four of five seeded operators cannot change the interface language at all, and the refusal surfaces only after they fill in the form and press Save.

findings.title: Reason codes created in the UI have permanently blank Arabic labels
findings.detail: L15121 writes new reason codes as {...labelEn:label.trim(), labelAr:'', active:true} and the add-reason-code form offers no Arabic input at all. The L15078 column then renders '—' for them and L14759 omits the Arabic half. The 47 seeded codes are bilingual; every code added thereafter is not, with no in-product path to fix it.
findings.impact: The bilingual reason-code taxonomy degrades silently as operators extend it.

findings.title: The three static stabgrp group headers in markup are removed from the DOM at boot
findings.detail: reorderSettingsTabs() removes every .settings-tab-group-lbl from the settings nav at L21288 (and again at L21311) before appending its own regrouped fragment. The three static headers stabgrp.workspace (L1420), stabgrp.operations (L1424) and stabgrp.system (L1436) are therefore gone by the time any user sees the rail, making them — not the runtime keys — the genuinely dead markup keys. The comment above L21288 states the removal is deliberate.
findings.impact: Three dictionary entries and three markup attributes are maintained for headers that never render, while the six headers that do render are documented as dead.

findings.title: 'Predictive growth signal' does no prediction
findings.detail: The card is a templated sentence with a single binary branch on activeSubs.length - cancelledSubs.length; there is no model, projection or extrapolation. The source comment acknowledges it is 'a simple, honestly-scoped trend read rather than a fabricated ML forecast'.
findings.impact: The card title promises forecasting the implementation does not provide.

findings.title: Charts never reflow on resize
findings.detail: renderTrendChart reads el.clientWidth once and bakes it into the SVG width/viewBox. renderExecTrendChart is not registered on the window resize handler (only autoSizeAllSelects is).
findings.impact: Resizing the window leaves both charts at their original width until the page is re-entered.

findings.title: Cities table has no empty state
findings.detail: citiesTb.innerHTML is set to the joined map of DB.cities; an empty array yields a bare empty tbody with no message, unlike the expansion list which has an explicit empty state.
findings.impact: An empty cities dataset renders as a headed table with no rows and no explanation.

findings.title: Doc header page-line range is wrong
findings.detail: The doc header states 'HTML lines: 583-633'. In source the page div opens at 583 and its closing is at 631 (line 632 is blank, 633 is the Corporate Accounts comment). The doc's own line-number index gives 631 correctly.
findings.impact: Downstream tooling keyed on the header range would over-read by two lines.

findings.title: Global trend tooltip node leaks across pages
findings.detail: ensureTrendTooltip() appends #trend-tooltip to document.body and nothing ever removes it; initTrendTooltips() re-attaches listeners to freshly created bars on every render.
findings.impact: A stray tooltip node persists site-wide after leaving the page.

findings.title: No i18n coverage inside the page
findings.detail: There are zero data-i18n attributes between lines 583 and 631; every string — headings, card titles, table headers, KPI labels, empty states and the predictive paragraph — is hardcoded English built by JS string concatenation. Only the sidebar label carries nav.exec-overview.
findings.impact: The page stays fully English when the panel switches to Arabic.

findings.title: No null guards in renderExecOverview
findings.detail: renderExecOverview dereferences document.getElementById(...).innerHTML for exec-kpis, exec-finance, exec-sub-growth, exec-cities-tbody, exec-expansion-list, exec-engagement and exec-predictive with no null check, while renderTrendChart guards with if(!el)return.
findings.impact: Any markup change that removes or renames a container throws and aborts the whole render.

findings.title: No toolbar subtitle for exec-overview
findings.detail: titles has an 'exec-overview' key but the subs map does not, so go() sets #tb-sub to '' via subs[id]||'' for this page while every neighbouring page shows a subtitle.
findings.impact: Cosmetic inconsistency in the toolbar.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — runtime KPI values
findings.detail: Every figure on this page depends on the live mutable DB at render time and on other modules writing to DB.payments, DB.trips, DB.subscriptions, DB.drivers, DB.riders, DB.escrowHolds and DB.newRiders. The doc marks these as static-read-only conclusions; the file was never executed. Also unverified: whether DB.newRiders is pruned to a real 48-hour window elsewhere, and whether another module mutating DB.cities (a filter call observed at 7892) reaches this table.
findings.impact: Concrete rendered numbers cannot be asserted without running the page.

findings.title: Doc header page-line range is off by one
findings.detail: The doc states 'HTML lines: L1189-L1217'. In source line 1189 is the PAGE: PREDICTIVE SIGNALS comment and the page div opens at 1190; the closing is at 1217.
findings.impact: Off-by-one in any tooling keyed on the header range.

findings.title: Scores are recomputed redundantly on every render
findings.detail: subHealthScore executes three full passes inside renderPredictivePage plus once per row in renderPredSubs; driverRiskScore runs once per driver in the KPI pass and again per driver in the table pass. No memoisation. The page also re-renders on every 60th demo tick while visible.
findings.impact: Duplicated O(n) work on every render; correctness unaffected.

findings.title: Sidebar badge omits three of the five signal types and is stale until first visit
findings.detail: #sbb-predictive is set to redSubs + atRiskDrivers only, deliberately excluding payment-risk, incident and zone signals, so it never matches KPI 1. It is written only by renderPredictivePage and is not touched by refreshNavCounts, so it reads the static markup value 0 until the page has been visited.
findings.impact: The sidebar under-reports open signals and shows 0 on a fresh session.

findings.title: Subscription-health table has no empty state
findings.detail: The thead is always emitted; when no subscription survives the non-cancelled filter the headers render over an empty body. Every other list on the page has an explicit empty state.
findings.impact: An empty table looks like a rendering failure rather than a clean slate.

findings.title: Two KPI progress bars are hardcoded
findings.detail: KPI 1's bar is width:55% and KPI 4's is width:40%, both literal, while KPIs 2 and 3 use min(100, value*20)%.
findings.impact: Two of four KPI bars convey no information but look like they do.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — runtime KPI values and table row counts
findings.detail: The four KPIs and tables 8.1-8.4 depend on DB.disputes/DB.incidents mutated by other modules, on DB.complianceSuspensions populated by complianceScan() against the advancing demo clock, and on DB.driverCashDebt/DB.cashLedger which start empty and are filled by Math.random()-gated trip generation. Whether any subscription ever reaches the Healthy band (and therefore whether the Retention action button is ever hidden) is likewise unverified, as is the .kpi.click CSS affordance.
findings.impact: Only the structural zone list is deterministic from seed data; the rest cannot be asserted statically.

findings.title: Zone rows have no deep link
findings.detail: Both the zone name and the 'Open zone' button call go('zones',null) with no zone selection, so the operator lands on the whole Zones page and must find the row again.
findings.impact: Extra navigation for every flagged zone.

findings.title: Doc header page-line range is off by one
findings.detail: The doc states 'HTML lines: L649-L673'. In source line 649 is the PAGE: FRAUD & RISK comment; the page div opens at 650 and closes at 673.
findings.impact: Off-by-one in any tooling keyed on the header range.

findings.title: GPS anomaly card is a declared non-implementation
findings.detail: The fifth card has no id, no render function and no data source — a single paragraph of prose naming three rules a real deployment would run. Both the card caption and the module banner label it as simulated and explain that flagging these would be fabricating a signal rather than detecting one.
findings.impact: Deliberate and clearly labelled; noted so nobody mistakes the card for a working detector.

findings.title: Identity collisions are not rendered at boot
findings.detail: The boot setTimeout block calls renderFraudPage() only; renderIdentityCollisions() runs solely from the router branch, so #identity-collisions holds empty markup until the page is first visited.
findings.impact: Harmless in practice because the div is only visible on this page, but the two renderers have inconsistent lifecycles.

findings.title: No outbound go() links from the page body
findings.detail: The only navigation available is openProfile. There is no path from a flag to Safety, Support or the Audit log where a fraud case would normally be worked, unlike Predictive Signals which links out to Compliance, Safety and Zones.
findings.impact: Investigating a flag means leaving via the sidebar and rebuilding context.

findings.title: No reinstate control on the fraud page
findings.detail: reinstateAccount() is wired only into the 360 profile page. Once suspended from here, the entity shows a Suspended badge on the fraud list and can be reversed only from elsewhere.
findings.impact: A mistaken suspension cannot be undone from the surface that caused it.

findings.title: No toolbar subtitle for the fraud page
findings.detail: titles has a fraud key but the subs map does not, so #tb-sub renders as an empty string via subs[id]||'' while every neighbouring page has a subtitle.
findings.impact: Cosmetic inconsistency in the toolbar.

findings.title: Pairing count re-implemented inline instead of reusing priorTripsWithRider
findings.detail: priorTripsWithRider(driverId,riderId) computes exactly the pairing statistic this page needs, but renderFraudPage re-implements the tally inline. Correcting the doc: it flagged this helper and the neighbouring hasOpenComplaint/openComplaintFor as possibly dead and left it UNVERIFIED — a file-wide grep shows all three are live, called from the subscriptions table (3530), a detail view (4288), the driver-eligibility list (5690, 5694) and 5761.
findings.impact: Duplicate logic that can drift from the shared helper; no functional defect today.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — runtime value of the pairing KPI
findings.detail: KPI 3 and the pairing card depend on reconstructHistory()'s seeded RNG over the whole rider book and cannot be asserted without executing the page. The other four cards are deterministic from seed data and their concrete outcomes are documented (one shared-IP group on 160.156.4.90; referral and identity-collision cards both render their empty states). CSS class rules were also not read.
findings.impact: The headline pairing count cannot be predicted statically.

findings.title: 'All alerts' navigates to All Trips
findings.detail: The Alert queue card's button reads 'All alerts' but calls go('trips',null), landing the operator on the All Trips page rather than any alerts view.
findings.impact: Label and destination mismatch.

findings.title: Alert list has no cap and no sort
findings.detail: alerts[] is built by appending four query results in source order and rendered whole. A large DB.deductions set or many Expiring subscriptions would produce an unbounded, unordered list.
findings.impact: The alert card degrades into an unreadable wall as data grows.

findings.title: Doc header page-line range is wrong
findings.detail: The doc states 'HTML lines: L676-L712'. In source the page div opens at 676 and its closing is at 710 (711 blank, 712 the Subscriptions page comment).
findings.impact: Downstream tooling keyed on the header range would over-read by two lines.

findings.title: KPI tile 4 is inert
findings.detail: dashKpi is called for 'Open alerts' with a null click argument, so the tile has no onclick and no cursor:pointer, unlike its four neighbours. There is no kpiScrollTo('dash-alerts') binding either, even though kpiScrollTo exists and is used on eight other pages.
findings.impact: The one KPI that names a queue on the same page cannot be clicked through to it.

findings.title: Quick-rides table has no true empty state
findings.detail: The green 'N completed ride(s) today' footer row is appended unconditionally, and there is no empty-state row for qrEx. When there are no exception rides the table shows only the footer.
findings.impact: A day with no exceptions looks like a partially rendered table.

findings.title: Refunds chip always reads 0.00 SAR at load
findings.detail: The chip sums DB.refunds where date==='25 Jun', but the seeded refunds are dated 19 Jun and 18 Jun only, so it reads 'Refunds today: 0.00 SAR' on a fresh load unless recordRefund adds a 25-Jun row during the session.
findings.impact: A header chip that looks live is always zero on first paint.

findings.title: Renewal days-left can render negative
findings.detail: dl is parseInt(x.ends,10) - 25, so a subscription whose ends day-of-month is below 25 yields a negative value and the group header reads e.g. 'Expiring in -6 days'. Seeded non-cancelled subscriptions all end 26-30 Jun, so it does not surface on a fresh load.
findings.impact: Nonsense group headers once data crosses a month boundary.

findings.title: Toolbar subtitle is a frozen date literal
findings.detail: subs.dashboard is the literal 'Thursday 25 Jun 2026 · 09:14 AM'. refreshNavCounts rewrites only the subscriptions, quickrides, trips, drivers, riders and renewal subtitles, so the dashboard's never updates.
findings.evidence: var subs={dashboard:'Thursday 25 Jun 2026 · 09:14 AM',subscriptions:'142 active subscriptions',
findings.impact: The toolbar shows a fixed date and time regardless of session state.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — New-subscription modal internals
findings.detail: The doc flags that renderNewSubModal's declaration line was located by grep rather than a direct read, and that PLANS, CADENCE_META, RIYADH_DISTRICTS, WEEKDAYS, isPlanVisibleForRider, eligibleDrivers and computeDynamicSubPrice — which populate that modal — belong to the Subscriptions/Pricing module and were not read. DB.subBackups, DB.paymentRisk and DB.complianceSuspensions seed contents referenced by subHealthScore are likewise unverified in this pass.
findings.impact: The modal's option sets and pricing preview cannot be asserted from this module's pass.

findings.title: completeItem has no effect on the inbox
findings.detail: completeItem() and closeCase() mark claims with state 'done', but renderInbox never filters on that state. An item leaves the list only when its domain predicate stops matching (for example a ticket gaining resolvedAtMs).
findings.impact: There is no way to mark inbox work finished from the inbox; the done state is written and then ignored.

findings.title: DB.ownershipConfig.warnTakeover is never read
findings.detail: The flag is declared alongside staleMin but no code path reads it; the takeover confirmation is unconditional.
findings.impact: A configuration switch that appears to control takeover warnings does nothing.

findings.title: Documentation line numbers drift from source by one to three lines
findings.detail: Verified against the source: the #p-inbox page div closes at L1395 (the doc cites L1396, which is blank); confirmTakeover is defined at L18940 (doc L18942); closeCase at L18983 (doc L18984); openCaseView at L19005 (doc L19006); workChip at L19030 (doc L19033). The doc's UNVERIFIED item about TEAM_ROLES is now resolved: it is declared at exactly L10501.
findings.impact: Line citations in the doc are close but not exact; anyone jumping to them lands a few lines early.

findings.title: Everything-tab empty state names the role even when routing is off
findings.detail: The 'all' tab empty message reads 'Nothing open in the queues routed to <role>.' regardless of _inboxRoleFilter, so with routing switched off it blames a filter that is not applied.
findings.evidence: Nothing open in the queues routed to
findings.impact: The empty state misdirects the operator toward a filter that is already disabled.

findings.title: Header comment says thirteen queues, the table defines twelve
findings.detail: The A2 module header comment opens with 'Thirteen queues' while QUEUE_LABEL defines twelve keys; the KPI sub-line renders Object.keys(QUEUE_LABEL).length, so the screen says 12.
findings.evidence: Thirteen queues, each with its own list, its own badge and its own page.
findings.impact: Documentation-in-code disagrees with the shipped behaviour, so a reader cannot tell whether a queue was dropped or never added.

findings.title: Leg and coverage items key ownership on the same subscription id
findings.detail: Ownership keys are ckey(type,id) = type + ':' + id. Both the leg items and the coverage item use a subscription id, so leg:SUB-1041 and coverage:SUB-1041 are two independent claims for what may be one underlying problem, with no case link between them by default.
findings.impact: Two operators can each claim half of the same problem and believe they own it exclusively.

findings.title: Module is entirely untranslated
findings.detail: No data-i18n attribute exists inside #p-inbox, and none of the strings produced by renderInbox, inboxItems, ownerChip, caseChip or dueChip pass through LANG_STRINGS. Only the sidebar label nav.inbox is translated.
findings.impact: Switching the panel to Arabic leaves every tab, KPI, queue label, item title and empty state in English.

findings.title: No search, no secondary filters, no pagination
findings.detail: The only controls are three tabs and one role checkbox. There is no search box, severity filter, queue-type filter, date range or pagination, and the single sort key (dueMs ascending, nulls mapped to 9e12) is not user-controllable.
findings.evidence: Breached first - a broken promise is not a queue position. Undated work sorts last, not first.
findings.impact: At any realistic queue volume an operator cannot narrow the list to a specific queue or entity.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED - confirmAction, legAck weight and coverage eligibility
findings.detail: Carried through from the doc as UNVERIFIED. confirmTakeover passes {title, summary, consequences, confirmLabel, onConfirm} to confirmAction() whose markup was not read; where legAck().weight is assigned was not traced, though the assumed-leg item branches on weight === 'weak'; and dispatchEligibility()/nearestEligibleDrivers(), which decide the coverage item's uncovered flag, were not read.
findings.impact: Three behaviours that gate what the inbox shows or confirms are asserted rather than demonstrated.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED - queue seed contents were not read
findings.detail: The doc marks this UNVERIFIED and it was not resolved in this pass. seedFairness, commitBoot, dispatchBoot, coverageBoot and gapsBoot2 populate DB.fairnessCases, DB.absenceEvents, DB.emergencyClaims, DB.emergencyDispatches, DB.erasureRequests and DB.backupRegistry, which determine how many rows the inbox actually shows on load. The boot registry was read but the individual seed bodies were not.
findings.impact: The real on-load row count for eight of the twelve queues is unknown.

findings.title: workChip() is unused by the inbox
findings.detail: workChip combines the case chip and owner chip into one helper, but renderInbox composes caseChip() and ownerChip() separately.
findings.impact: Duplicate chip-composition logic that can drift from the version actually rendered.

findings.title: Chip counts are blank until the page is first opened
findings.detail: The boot block calls updateBellBadge() but never renderAllNotificationsPage(), and the count spans ship empty in the markup, so the #nf-cnt-* spans stay blank until the first visit.
findings.impact: The chips read as bare labels with a stray empty space on first render.

findings.title: Documented page-div extent is two lines too long
findings.detail: Verified against the source: #p-notifications-all closes at L1187. L1188 is blank and L1189 is the section comment introducing #p-predictive. The doc cites L1171-L1189 throughout.
findings.impact: Cosmetic; the corrected bound is [1171,1187].

findings.title: emailAlerts gates an in-panel notification, not email
findings.detail: The low-rating producer checks DB.opsConfig.notifications.emailAlerts !== false before calling pushOpsNotification, so a setting named for email controls whether an in-panel notification appears.
findings.impact: Turning off email alerts silently suppresses an in-panel alert an operator would still expect to see.

findings.title: markAllRead lacks the null guard handleNotifClick has
findings.detail: markAllRead calls document.getElementById('p-notifications-all').classList directly, while handleNotifClick checks the element exists first. Harmless because the element is static markup, but the asymmetry is a latent trap if the page is ever built dynamically.
findings.impact: None today; a maintenance hazard if the page markup becomes conditional.

findings.title: No deduplication of repeated notifications
findings.detail: Repeated identical toasts create separate records. Only the SLA sweep guards itself, via t.slaBreaches.indexOf(kind)>=0.
findings.impact: A recurring condition floods the list and the badge with duplicates of the same fact.

findings.title: No persistence, no per-user read state, no translation
findings.detail: The file uses no localStorage, sessionStorage or IndexedDB, so read flags and every N-AUTO record are lost on reload and the badge returns to 3. CURRENT_USER_ID is never consulted by any notification function, so read state is global rather than per user. No data-i18n attribute exists in the bell, the panel or the page.
findings.impact: Switching acting user does not change what the bell shows, and nothing an operator reads or clears survives a refresh.

findings.title: NOTIF_PRIORITY_LABEL is declared and never used
findings.detail: Grep across the whole file returns exactly one occurrence - the declaration itself. The page uses the longer literals at L2318 and the chips use their own hardcoded labels at L1179-L1182, so the same four labels exist in three places.
findings.impact: Three independent copies of the priority labels can drift apart.

findings.title: Runtime timestamps never age
findings.detail: pushOpsNotification hardcodes time:'Just now' and nothing ever recomputes it. Seed records use free text such as '07:55' and '2 days ago', pinned to the fictional demo clock.
findings.impact: Every runtime notification claims to be brand new forever, so recency cannot be judged from the list.

findings.title: The notifications page has no sidebar entry and highlights nothing
findings.detail: go('notifications-all') appears at exactly one place in the file - inside openAllNotifications - so the page is reachable only through the bell dropdown. Because openAllNotifications passes a null element, the router's if(el) guard leaves whatever sidebar item was previously highlighted still highlighted.
findings.impact: The page is hard to find and, once open, the sidebar tells the operator they are somewhere else.

findings.title: Three notification types have no runtime producer
findings.detail: The types renewal, approval and complaint have full icon, priority and click-routing support but are emitted only by seed records N3, N4 and N6. No pushOpsNotification call uses them.
findings.impact: Routing paths that can never be exercised at runtime give a false impression of coverage.

findings.title: Two alert-preference settings are never read
findings.detail: DB.opsConfig.notifications.smsAlerts and .notifyOnDispute are written by the Settings tab and restored on load, but no logic anywhere reads them.
findings.impact: Two settings toggles present themselves as controls that change nothing.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED - five producer action closures and the gateAll exemption list
findings.detail: Carried through from the doc. The click action argument for the producers at L15887, L16719, L16723, L17293 and L17306 spans multiple source lines and was not read; type and title are grep-verified. Also unverified: whether markAllRead's absence from gateAll is an intentional exemption - the registry header mentions seven trivial ungated actions listed with reasons, but that list was not read.
findings.impact: Where five alerts actually take the operator when clicked is unknown.

findings.title: Conflicting .map-stat CSS declarations
findings.detail: The .map-stat and .ms-item rules are declared twice; the later block at L365-L368 wins under cascade order and the earlier block at L217-L220 has no effect.
findings.impact: Dead style rules that mislead anyone tuning the stats bar.

findings.title: Dispatch and map geometry are simulations, not models
findings.detail: MAP_ROUTES holds canvas pixel polylines rather than coordinates; simulateAsyncCommit injects a 550 ms delay and an 8% random failure on assign; driver acceptance is 0.30 + (rating-3)*0.08; a 2% per-tick roll fabricates chat messages from CHAT_TEMPLATES; and trip progress runs at TICK_ACCEL = 30x real time.
findings.impact: Nothing on this page reflects a real dispatch or routing system; the numbers are demo theatre.

findings.title: Router populates the trips table and then blanks it 50 ms later
findings.detail: The live router branch calls renderMapFilterSelects() and renderMapTripsTable(), then schedules setMapMode(MAP_MODE||'live') on a 50 ms timeout, which replaces the tbody with the 'Switch to History to browse trips.' placeholder.
findings.impact: The table flashes real rows for 50 ms on every entry before being wiped - wasted work and a visible flicker.

findings.title: Status filter chips do not affect the canvas
findings.detail: setMapFilter only re-renders the table. The canvas keeps drawing the previously selected route, so filtering to Cancelled still shows a route on the map.
findings.impact: The map and the table disagree about what the operator has filtered to.

findings.title: The live-mode bar hardcodes the active trip count
findings.detail: The banner text '3 active trips . updates every second' is a literal in the markup and is never recomputed from DB.liveTrips, even though #active-trips-count a few hundred lines below is.
findings.evidence: · 3 active trips · updates every second
findings.impact: The count stays at 3 after trips complete or are created, contradicting the sidebar count on the same screen.

findings.title: The page is entirely untranslated
findings.detail: Grep over L768-L845 finds zero data-i18n attributes. The only i18n key associated with the module is the sidebar label nav.live; the toolbar title and subtitle come from plain JS maps with no Arabic counterpart.
findings.impact: Switching the panel to Arabic leaves the whole map and dispatch board in English.

findings.title: The Send message modal is unreachable
findings.detail: openSendChatModal and commitSendChatMsg are defined but no control on p-live opens them. The Chat button calls openTripChatView, which zeroes the unread counter and opens the trip profile instead.
findings.impact: Operators cannot send a message from the live board despite the modal being fully built.

findings.title: Two external CDN dependencies load for a dead feature
findings.detail: leaflet.css and leaflet.js are loaded from unpkg.com on every page view. The only live consumer of Leaflet anywhere in the file is the Settings city preview, which guards itself with a typeof check. The source comment justifying the canvas renderer explicitly cites having no CDN and no network dependency.
findings.impact: An offline or blocked-CDN environment pays two failed network requests on load for code that never runs.

findings.title: Two near-duplicate trip table renderers that have drifted
findings.detail: renderMapTripsTable (L12660) and renderMapTripsTableFiltered (L11522-L11524) build the same nine-column table but differ: the filtered variant's vehicle fallback is 'Eco' while the unfiltered one uses 'Economy', and its replay button label is the bare play glyph rather than 'Replay'.
findings.impact: The same row renders with different text depending on which code path filled the table.

findings.title: Two of the three date options can never return data
findings.detail: All eight seeded DB.trips records carry date '25 Jun ...', while the date select offers Today, Yesterday (24 Jun) and 23 Jun. Selecting either non-today option yields the 'No trips recorded' empty state and 'No replayable trips' in the trip select.
findings.evidence: yesterday -> '24 Jun', day2 -> '23 Jun', else '25 Jun'
findings.impact: Two thirds of the history date picker is decorative with the shipped seed data.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED - wallet debit semantics, trip profile rendering and radius config
findings.detail: Carried through from the doc. debitRiderWallet() is treated as returning a boolean success flag at L11839 but its body was not read; openProfile()'s behaviour for TRP-* ids (whether it renders the DB.commLogs chat thread) is asserted only by a source comment; and whether DB.opsConfig.quickRideRadiusKm, subRadiusKm and autoExpandRadius are ever assigned anywhere was not established - only their fallbacks of 6 km, 8 km and not-false were confirmed.
findings.impact: The fee path on live-trip cancellation and the candidate radius used by every assign flow are asserted rather than demonstrated.

findings.title: 'Days left' column shows an end date
findings.detail: The column header reads 'Days left' but the cell emits the literal string 'Ends ' concatenated with sub.ends. No day count is computed for this column anywhere.
findings.impact: An operator scanning for urgency has to do date arithmetic in their head against a frozen 25 Jun today.

findings.title: Documented line numbers drift from the source
findings.detail: The doc states the page block is L713-L767; it is L713-L757. The doc places the filter read-back at L3535-L3537 and the row template at L3543-L3558; the source has them at L3511-L3513 and L3540-L3556. The 'Ends' cell is L3547, not L3551.
findings.impact: Anyone navigating by the doc's line index lands in the wrong part of the function.

findings.title: Freeze reason is captured and discarded
findings.detail: The freeze modal renders a Reason (optional) text input, but doFreeze reads only #frz-dur and the audit payload records {status, duration}. Nothing ever reads #frz-reason.
findings.impact: The stated reason for every freeze is lost, so the audit entry cannot answer why a package was paused.

findings.title: Page ships hardcoded KPI and subtitle demo numbers
findings.detail: The four KPI tiles (142/68/48/26 with deltas and bar widths), the page subtitle and the sidebar badge are literals in the markup, overwritten only once renderSubscriptionsTable runs.
findings.evidence:
Active
142
up 12 vs last week
findings.impact: A render failure or a first paint before boot shows fabricated operational numbers.

findings.title: subEconomics().driverFull is never consumed
findings.detail: driverFull is computed and included in the returned object but no call site reads it.
findings.impact: Dead field carried through every economics computation.

findings.title: Broken employee references vanish silently
findings.detail: renderCorpDetail returns an empty string for any rid missing from DB.riders, while the Account summary still counts c.riders.length.
findings.impact: A broken foreign key shrinks the visible employee table with no warning while the headcount above it disagrees.

findings.title: corpAccountId appears write-only
findings.detail: DB.riders[rid].corpAccountId is set on link and deleted on unlink, but every reverse lookup scans the accounts' riders arrays via findCorpForRider instead. No read site for corpAccountId was found.
findings.impact: A redundant denormalised field that can drift from the authoritative riders array with nothing to detect it.

findings.title: Invoice year comes from the real system clock
findings.detail: The invoice number embeds new Date().getFullYear() while every date printed beside it derives from EYVAR_TODAY = 25 Jun 2026.
findings.impact: The invoice number's year contradicts the invoice's own dates, which on a VAT document is a real defect.

findings.title: No email-format validation anywhere in the module
findings.detail: corp-contact-email, corp-bill-email and corp-pol-approver-email are all type=text with only a truthiness or ||null check.
findings.impact: A typo in the billing or approver address sends invoices and approval requests nowhere, with the outbox recording the malformed string.

findings.title: Pending approvals counter reaches only the first item
findings.detail: The Account summary Pending approvals row hardcodes pendingApprovalSubIds[0] as its click target.
findings.impact: When three packages are waiting on the same company's approver, only one is reachable from the counter that reports all three.

findings.title: Usage-policy audit diff is incomplete and aliased
findings.detail: The before snapshot captures 6 of the 10 policy keys - approverName, approverEmail, workHoursStart and workHoursEnd are omitted - and the after payload passes the same live pol object that was just mutated.
findings.impact: Changing an approver leaves no diff in the audit log, and the before/after pair can alias to the same object.

findings.title: 'Trial' status is styled but never assigned
findings.detail: The list's statusCls ternary has a Trial branch rendering b-blue, but nothing in the file ever sets status='Trial'.
findings.impact: Dead styling branch implying a trial lifecycle the product does not have.

findings.title: Asymmetric page metadata for corporate pages
findings.detail:
The titles map has entries for both corporate and corp-detail, but the subs page-subtitle map has neither, so the corporate header sub-line is a static

in HTML instead.
findings.impact: The corporate list subtitle can never reflect live counts the way every other page's does.

findings.title: expectedEmployees has no downstream behaviour
findings.detail: expectedEmployees is rendered in the Employees cell and the Company info card and nowhere else; nothing warns when linked headcount exceeds or falls short of it.
findings.impact: A target headcount is captured at signup and never acted on.

findings.title: Same status renders in two different colours
findings.detail: The list uses a bespoke statusCls ternary where Active is green; the detail Company info card uses the shared statusBadge, where Active matches /trip|active/i and renders blue.
findings.impact: The same account is green in the list and blue on its own detail page, undermining any colour convention the operator learns.

findings.title: Seed is one account with zero employees
findings.detail: DB.corporateAccounts seeds exactly CORP-001 Al-Dossari Logistics with riders:[] and status Pending, so corpTotalSpend, the employee count and every compliance figure render as zero at boot.
findings.impact: None of the spend, policy or invoice logic is exercised by the demo data, so regressions in those paths are invisible on first open.

findings.title: arrivalConfig.riderGraceMin is never read
findings.detail: DB.arrivalConfig declares riderGraceMin:10 alongside arrivalRadiusM, meetRadiusM and minDwellMin, but no code reads it.
findings.impact: A configured grace period silently has no effect on any arrival verdict.

findings.title: DESYNC_THRESHOLD_MS is declared and never used
findings.detail: The constant carries a comment explaining that a client this far behind is stuck rather than slow, but detectDesync flags any un-acked entry regardless of lag.
findings.evidence: var DESYNC_THRESHOLD_MS=20000; /* a client this far behind server state is stuck, not slow */
findings.impact: The desync KPI counts momentary lag as a stuck client, so the tile over-reports.

findings.title: Documented line numbers for two handlers are off by six
findings.detail: The doc places forceResync at L16430 and openDesyncTicket at L16443; the source defines them at L16424 and L16437. openLowRatingTicket is at L15302, not L15303.
findings.impact: Navigating by the doc's index lands mid-function.

findings.title: No export control on the page
findings.detail: exportRows carries a full 'trips' branch with its own header row, but the All Trips page ships no Export button - only Quick Rides and Subscriptions do.
findings.impact: The one page that shows every trip is the one page you cannot export from.

findings.title: Role-to-permission matrix not resolvable from call sites
findings.detail: requirePerm delegates to can(); the role table behind process_payouts, contact_users and live_ops was not read, so which roles can edit a tip, send a receipt or force a resync is unconfirmed.
findings.impact: The effective blast radius of the trip-level write actions cannot be stated from this module alone.

findings.title: Six KPI tiles injected into a four-column grid
findings.detail: The container carries the .g4 four-column grid class but renderTripsTable injects six tiles, so the strip wraps to 4 + 2.
findings.impact: The two most operationally interesting tiles - Low ratings and State desync - land on an orphaned second row.

findings.title: Top-bar subtitle is a fabricated volume figure
findings.detail: subs.trips is the literal '1,882 trips in June' and is never recomputed, against a dataset of seven seeded trips.
findings.impact: The page chrome asserts a trip volume two orders of magnitude away from what the table shows.

findings.title: Two Type-badge palettes for the same field
findings.detail: The All Trips row template renders b-com for Subscription and b-eco for Quick ride; the shared tripsTable helper renders b-blue and b-purple for the same values.
findings.impact: The same trip is one colour in the ledger and another on the rider profile, so colour carries no learnable meaning.

findings.title: Choosing a rider does not refresh the estimate
findings.detail: The rider custom select is built with no onChange expression, unlike pickup, destination and vehicle type which all call updateNrrFareEstimate.
findings.impact: Minor today because the fare does not depend on the rider, but it breaks the pattern the other three fields establish.

findings.title: directionArrows round-trip branch is unreachable here
findings.detail: The only call site in this module passes the literal 'one-way', and DB.trips records carry no direction field at all.
findings.impact: Every route renders as a one-way arrow regardless of the real trip shape.

findings.title: Documented location of resolveAlert is wrong
findings.detail: The doc places resolveAlert at L10576-L10589; the source defines it at L9166-L9174, and L10576 is a line inside the PAGE_PERMS subscriptions registry.
findings.impact: Anyone tracing the Review button by the doc's index lands in the permission registry instead.

findings.title: Money cells print raw strings
findings.detail: The Fare and Driver earns cells emit t.fare||'0.00' and t.driverEarn||'-' with no toFixed, unlike All Trips which formats both to two decimals.
findings.impact: Column alignment and decimal places depend on whatever string the writer happened to store.

findings.title: nm2() is bypassed for rider and driver names
findings.detail: Rows read rider.name and drv.name off a fallback object rather than calling the shared nm2 helper used by All Trips.
findings.impact: An unknown id renders as the raw id inside a star chip, a different failure presentation from every other trip list.

findings.title: Same pickup and destination is accepted
findings.detail: computeRouteKm returns null when pickup === dest, which resets the preview to its placeholder rather than showing an error, and commitNewRideRequest checks only that both fields are non-empty.
findings.impact: A zero-length request enters real dispatch and occupies a driver offer slot.

findings.title: Seeded requests use districts that do not exist on the map
findings.detail: REQ-501/502/503 reference King Saud University, Kingdom Tower, Airport T5, KAFD, Al Sahafa District and Al Wurud District, none of which are keys of RIYADH_DISTRICTS.
findings.impact: Any code path computing a route or distance from a seeded request returns null, so the seed exercises none of the geography.

findings.title: The 'standard' driver tier gets two different colours
findings.detail: The local lvlCls maps anything not gold/silver/new to b-silver, while the shared lvlBadge helper maps standard to b-grey.
findings.impact: A standard-tier captain reads as silver-tier on this page only.

findings.title: Tracking map discards its own distance and ETA and can render empty
findings.detail: subDispatchMapHTML computes km via geoDistanceKm and eta via estimateEtaMin and the subscription dispatch UI displays both; the ride-request tracker renders the map and ignores them. While the request is still searching there is no driver, so a blank 160 px grid is drawn with no placeholder.
findings.impact: The most useful two numbers during dispatch - how far away and how long - are computed and thrown away.

findings.title: pickPlan() depends on the implicit global event
findings.detail: pickPlan(id) reads the browser's implicit window.event to move the .selected class and check the radio, rather than taking the event as a parameter.
findings.impact: Plan selection breaks under strict mode, in engines without window.event, and whenever pickPlan is invoked programmatically.

findings.title: priorityCall's contract was not traced
findings.detail: The 'Priority call' button on at-risk rows calls priorityCall(riderName,'renewal',sub.rider). The function is defined at L9149 but its three-argument contract, writes, permission behaviour and audit were not read — it belongs to the contact/telephony module. The doc marks this UNVERIFIED.
findings.impact: The most escalatory action on the page has unknown side effects, permission behaviour and auditability.

findings.title: The 'Keep same driver?' toggle is decorative
findings.detail: The checkbox rendered next to 'Keep same driver? <name> (★<rating>) has a slot available.' has no id and is never read by renderStep2, processCharge or renderSuccess.
findings.impact: The operator believes they are making a driver-retention choice that has no effect; the availability claim is also asserted without any check.

findings.title: The renewal module is not translatable
findings.detail: Only the sidebar label carries data-i18n (nav.renewal, with an Arabic entry at L7907). Every string produced by renderRenewalPipeline, renewalListHTML, openHealthBreakdown, renewalMenu and the renew wizard is an English literal built in JS.
findings.impact: The Arabic build shows an English renewal pipeline apart from its sidebar entry.

findings.title: The same health score is banded differently on two pages
findings.detail: The renewal page bands inline at >=70 'Likely renews' / >=40 'Uncertain' / else 'At risk', while healthBand() used by Predictive Signals bands at >=80 'Healthy' / >=50 'At risk' / else 'Predicted churn'. The renewal page never calls healthBand().
findings.impact: A subscription can read 'Likely renews' on one page and 'At risk' on another, undermining trust in the score.

findings.title: Readiness ticket ids collide after any deletion
findings.detail: createReadinessTicket() derives the id from the current array length rather than a sequence.
findings.impact: Deleting a ticket makes the next created ticket reuse an existing id, silently colliding in DB.tickets.

findings.title: Several dependencies of this page were not traced
findings.detail: showEntityLocation() (L8226), nextScheduledDayLabel() (L4721), dispatchEligibility() (L17209), driverLiveState() (L7283), nearestAvailableDrivers() (L8167) and geoDistanceKm() (L7256) drive the location canvas, the postpone target date and both candidate builders, but their bodies belong to other modules and the doc marks them UNVERIFIED.
findings.impact: The permission behaviour and correctness of the postpone target-date computation and the backup-candidate eligibility filter are unconfirmed.

findings.title: The 'high' level is red on the row but amber in its section band
findings.detail: readinessStatus returns colour 'red' for the high level, rendering a h-red pill, while the High section header is emitted with the amber palette.
findings.impact: Cosmetic mismatch that makes the urgency ordering of the sections harder to read at a glance.

findings.title: The readiness module is not translatable
findings.detail: Only nav.readiness carries data-i18n (Arabic at L7907). The page heading, four KPI labels and sub-labels, both sort buttons, the sort title, every table header, badge, section band, the empty state and all seven modals are English literals in markup or JS.
findings.impact: The Arabic build shows an English readiness page apart from its sidebar entry.

findings.title: The upcoming-trips 'NAV SAFETY NET' fallback seed can never run
findings.detail: DB.upcomingSubTrips is assigned unconditionally with eight scripted scenarios, and a second statement then does DB.upcomingSubTrips = DB.upcomingSubTrips || [four records]. The || can never take the right branch.
findings.impact: Four unreachable demo records and a comment describing a safety net the code does not provide.

findings.title: Ticket routing, assignee and SLA are hardcoded
findings.detail: The routing banner promises auto-assignment to 'the Support team (Lina Al-Otaibi)', an urgent flag and a first response 'under 10 min'; the created record hardcodes agent 'Lina Al-Otaibi', priority 'High' and a fixed auto-thread message.
findings.impact: Every readiness ticket claims an SLA and an owner that no routing logic actually enforces.

findings.title: tripScenario's unassigned branch never fires
findings.detail: The first branch of tripScenario() handles a trip with no driver or a driver missing from DB.drivers. The comment above it acknowledges 'it never fires today because every seeded trip already has a driver'.
findings.impact: The unassigned-trip path is untested, and readinessStatus has no counterpart at all, so a genuinely unassigned trip would be misclassified as On track.

findings.title: Assignment and driver acceptance are simulated
findings.detail: simulateAsyncCommit() waits 550 ms and fails 8% of the time on every assign; driver acceptance is a per-second draw of 0.30 + (rating-3)*0.08 over a 12-second offer window, which exceeds 99% cumulative for any rated driver.
findings.impact: Assignment behaviour observed in the panel does not reflect any real backend, and the artificial failure rate is indistinguishable from a genuine bug during testing.

findings.title: Assignment provenance fields are written but never displayed
findings.detail: commitSubReqAssign writes r.assignedBy and r.assignedAt, and the search-window engine writes r.expiredAt, but buildSubReqRow renders none of the three.
findings.impact: The operator cannot see who assigned a request or when it expired without reading the activity log.

findings.title: Doc line numbers drift from source in three places
findings.detail: Verified against the source: the chip-count writes are at L10083-L10085 and the card badges at L10086-L10087 (the doc lists L10081-L10085); #p-requests-sub-all closes at L2141 (the doc header says L2142); #p-requests-instant-all closes at L2162 (the doc header says L2165). Inside renderRequestsSubAll and renderRequestsInstantAll the doc's line numbers run about five lines low — the search predicate is L10150-L10155, the subtitle L10157, the empty state L10159 and the pagination slice L10162.
findings.impact: Line citations in this doc's sections 7, 11.3 and 11.4 cannot be used directly for navigation without re-verification.

findings.title: Materialised subscriptions use a different date format for started
findings.detail: materializeSubscription() writes started: fmtReqNowLabel(), a 'DD Mon HH:MM' label, whereas every other subscription's started is a bare 'DD Mon' date. parseShortDate() tolerates it because it only regexes the day and month.
findings.impact: Any consumer that formats or compares started as a plain date will render or sort these records differently from the rest.

findings.title: r._alerted is set and never read
findings.detail: The tick engine sets r._alerted on requests that started life already breached, but no code reads the flag.
findings.evidence: else if(!r._alerted)r._alerted=true; /* covers requests that started life already breached */
findings.impact: A dead field whose comment implies a suppression behaviour that does not exist.

findings.title: SLA thresholds are inline literals rather than configurable limits
findings.detail: The 180-second breach and the 90-second 'Approaching SLA' warning are hardcoded comparisons inside tickEngine and reqSlaBadge, even though the same tick loop reads driver_max_consecutive_declines through getLimit().
findings.impact: The most operationally significant timings on the page cannot be tuned per city or per policy without a code change.

findings.title: The 'All' chip count ignores the active filter
findings.detail: rfilt-all-cnt is always written as the sum of the two unfiltered array lengths, while the two card badges below it are written from the filtered lists.
findings.impact: As soon as a status filter is applied the chip stops describing what the page is showing, contradicting the card badges directly beneath it.

findings.title: The dispatch candidate source was not traced
findings.detail: nearestAvailableDrivers(riderId, limit, kind, elapsedSec) decides which drivers are offered and how the search radius expands with elapsed time, and showNearbyDriversMap() was read only in outline for its request-context branches. Both belong to the dispatch module and the doc marks them UNVERIFIED.
findings.impact: Whether the offer engine respects configured ops radius phases and driver eligibility is unconfirmed from this module alone.

findings.title: The instant search placeholder understates what it matches
findings.detail: The instant full-list search filters on rider name, request id, rider id, pickup and dest, one field more than the subscription search, but its placeholder reads 'Search rider, ID, pickup…'.
findings.impact: Operators do not discover that they can search by destination.

findings.title: The live engine never produces an 'assigned' instant request
findings.detail: Both driverAcceptOffer() and commitRequestAssign() splice the record out of DB.rideRequests and push into DB.liveTrips instead of setting status='assigned'. The only assigned rows in the UI were fabricated by seedMoreRequests().
findings.impact: The '✅ Assigned' chip only ever matches demo rows, so the status filter is misleading about what the system actually produces.

findings.title: The pager disappears on an empty search result
findings.detail: Both full-list renderers write the empty-state markup and return before reaching reqRenderPager(), so the pager container keeps whatever it last rendered or nothing at all.
findings.impact: The paging controls vanish instead of showing 'Page 1 of 1', which reads as a broken page rather than an empty result.

findings.title: The requests module is not translatable
findings.detail: Only nav.requests carries data-i18n (Arabic at L7907). All three page headings, six filter chips, the value-sort chip, both search placeholders, both card titles, the export button, every table header, status/SLA/hold badge, toast and empty state are English literals.
findings.impact: The Arabic build shows an English requests queue apart from its sidebar entry.

findings.title: Three of the six filter chips have no count span
findings.detail: The All, Subscription and Instant chips carry span ids that receive counts, but the Pending, Assigned and Expired chips have no count span in the markup and no code writes to them.
findings.impact: The chip row is visually inconsistent and gives no sense of how much work sits behind each status.

findings.title: Doc 08a line numbers drift by 1-4 lines in several places
findings.detail: Verified against source: div#p-drivers spans L887–L904 (doc says L887–L906); the All drivers card is L897–L903 with thead at L900 and tbody at L901 (doc says L899–L905 / L903); the roster row cells are name L6390, capacity L6394, status L6397 (doc says 6390/6395/6398); toggleFleetCounts is L20982 (doc says 20985); setDriverFilter is L21222 (doc says 21219); supplyKpiHTML L21188 (doc says 21186); liveSubtitles L21236 (doc says 21232); openFlagAccountModal L9006, commitFlagAccount L9026, commitUnflagAccount L9042, priorityCall L9149, confirmDriverIncentive L11208; fleetCounts sub-keys are pending L20929, suspended L20930, terminated L20931, frozen L20932, docsAtRisk L20934. Doc 08a's UNVERIFIED item 17 is also resolved: mountUxBlocks does create div#rider-kpis inside #rider-kpis-anchor, so riderKpiHTML has a real target.
findings.impact: Anyone navigating the source from the doc's line index lands a few lines off; all cited constructs do exist.

findings.title: filterDriversByTier's chip parameter is unused
findings.detail: Every tier tile passes `this` as the second argument, but the function body never references chip; the active-tile highlight is recomputed from _driverTierFilter on re-render instead.
findings.impact: Cosmetic; a misleading signature.

findings.title: Missing capacity renders green, reading as 'has room'
findings.detail: The capacity cell colours red only on the exact string 'Full' and green for everything else, including the '—' fallback used when the field is absent. Every driver created by approveDriver has no capacity field and therefore shows a green dash.
findings.impact: An unknown capacity is presented with the same visual affirmation as a confirmed opening.

findings.title: The All-drivers table has no sort, search or pagination
findings.detail: Rows are emitted in Object.keys insertion order with no column-header sort handler, no search input inside #p-drivers, and no page-size control. The only text search on any fleet page is the Riders page's global search box.
findings.impact: The roster becomes unusable as the fleet grows beyond a screenful.

findings.title: The driver notification-log card never appears on seed data
findings.detail: All six seeded drivers have notifLog:[] and the card is guarded by d.notifLog.length, so it is invisible until a runtime event appends to it. Contrary to the doc's UNVERIFIED note, four runtime writers do exist (subscription reminder, subscription assignment, reassignment, and a generic driver notifier); sendSystemEmail is not one of them — it writes only DB.emailOutbox.
findings.impact: Demo and review sessions never see the delivery-log card, so it goes untested.

findings.title: Three parallel level-badge implementations
findings.detail: lvlBadge() maps lvl to class+label and is used only by openProfile; lvlBadgeSm() is a second map used by the payouts table; renderDriversTable builds its own lvlCls ternary inline. All three encode the same four tiers separately and can drift.
findings.impact: A tier added or renamed in one place will render inconsistently across screens.

findings.title: Tier filtering does not refresh the supply KPI highlight
findings.detail: setDriverFilter calls both renderDriversTable() and renderSupplyKpis(), so the active tile outline stays in sync. filterDriversByTier calls only renderDriversTable(), so the supply-tile highlight can remain from a previous state while the table content has changed.
findings.impact: The KPI strip can visually claim a filter that no longer describes the table.

findings.title: viewDriver(name) has no callers
findings.detail: The one-line function toasts 'Opening profile — '+name and is never referenced from markup or code anywhere in the file; the roster uses openProfile(id) instead.
findings.impact: Dead surface area that suggests a navigation path that does not exist.

findings.title: Applicants carry no consent record and the detail page shows none
findings.detail: buildApplicantDetailBody's Device & access card renders Device, App language and Last known IP but no Terms of Service or Privacy Policy rows, unlike the driver 360° which calls isConsentCurrent(). Whether an applicant has any consent record before approval could not be confirmed; getUserConsent creates them lazily on first read.
findings.impact: Consent state at the point of KYC decision is invisible to the reviewer.

findings.title: Doc 08b page line ranges are two lines high
findings.detail: Verified against source: div#p-all-pending spans L1324–L1339 (doc says L1324–L1341), with #pending-search at L1334 and #all-pending-list at L1337. div#p-applicant-detail spans L1342–L1348 (doc says L1342–L1350), with #appd-name/#appd-meta at L1344, the ← Back button at L1345 and #appd-body at L1347. Separately, doc 08b's UNVERIFIED items 24, 25, 26 and 27 all resolve in source: stopEv is defined at L18857, emailFor at L3572 (so sendSystemEmail does resolve a DRV id to the generated address), customSelectHTML at L5336, and REQ_NOW_REF at L9555 as new Date(2026,5,25,9,14,0) — note it is advanced by the simulation tick at L9680, so document day counts drift during a session.
findings.impact: The doc's line index lands a couple of lines off; four of its open questions are answerable from source.

findings.title: Rejection reasons are hardcoded rather than configurable
