findings.detail: Both the document-rejection reason list (five options) and the application-rejection reason list (five options) are string literals built into the modal HTML, not sourced from the panel's configurable Reason codes settings tab.
findings.impact: Reason taxonomy cannot be adjusted without a code change, and reporting on reasons drifts from the configured set.

findings.title: The search predicate dereferences a.plate unguarded
findings.detail: The filter chain reads a.plate.toLowerCase() with no existence check, unlike the surrounding guards elsewhere in the file. An application record without a plate throws inside the map and blanks the whole list.
findings.impact: One malformed record can break the entire applications page.

findings.title: The vehicle-class mismatch and unknown branches are unreachable on seed data
findings.detail: All five applicants (Elantra, Tucson, Accent, Sonata, Yaris) and all six seeded drivers use models present in VEHICLE_CLASS_MAP with classes matching their declared type, so verifyVehicleClass always returns 'match'. The red mismatch badge and the amber unknown badge — and the corresponding approval-modal warning boxes — never render without hand-editing data.
findings.impact: The feature the source comment describes as closing an audit gap is never exercised in demo or review.

findings.title: Triage footer visibility uses the total application count
findings.detail: renderPendingDrivers slices open applications to three for the list but shows the 'View all pending applications →' footer when DB.pendingDrivers.length > 3, which counts decided applications too. With four decided and one open application the footer appears beneath a single row.
findings.impact: Cosmetic inconsistency between the list and its overflow affordance.

findings.title: Cards on the Riders page cannot be collapsed
findings.detail: initCardToggles() is invoked only from openProfile, so the collapse chevrons that appear on profile cards are absent here. All three cards — New sign-ups, Retention watchlist and All riders — stay expanded.
findings.impact: Minor ergonomics; the page is long and cannot be condensed.

findings.title: driverGenderPref is consumed by dispatch but never surfaced
findings.detail: Only RDR-1041 carries driverGenderPref:'female'. It is read by the matching logic in two places but appears nowhere on the Riders page and nowhere in buildEntityProfile, so ops cannot see, verify or change a rider's driver-gender preference.
findings.impact: A matching constraint that materially affects dispatch is invisible to the people running dispatch.

findings.title: Findings are static-analysis only; runtime and CSS were not observed
findings.detail: The doc states explicitly that the panel was never loaded in a browser for this pass, so behaviour depending on boot order beyond what is written at L14556–L14600 and L21390–L21410 is inferred from source order, and no CSS rule affecting .health, .b-com or .ra was audited. Which roles actually hold contact_users was also not resolved.
findings.impact: A small residual risk that observed behaviour differs from the static reading.

findings.title: getReferralCode is defined and never called
findings.detail: The function lazily generates and stores r.referralCode (first four alpha characters of the first name uppercased plus the last four digits of the id, falling back to the prefix RIDR). A grep for the call site returns only the definition, so referralCode is never produced or displayed; processReferral works from explicitly picked rider ids instead.
findings.impact: A referral feature that appears implemented is entirely unreachable.

findings.title: No sorting, table search, pagination or export, and the KPI tiles are inert
findings.detail: The only filter is the risk select; there is no column sort handler, no search over the table body (the header box runs the global entity search instead), no pagination and no export. riderKpiHTML emits plain div.kpi elements with no onclick, unlike supplyKpiHTML on the Drivers page whose tiles are div.kpi.click and drive setDriverFilter.
findings.impact: The rider roster cannot be worked at scale, and the KPI strip that looks interactive is not.

findings.title: Rider dob and nid are stored and never rendered
findings.detail: Both fields exist on DB.newRiders records and are copied into DB.riders on promotion, but the rider Personal-information card renders only Gender, Registered address and City. The driver-side equivalents are shown on the applicant detail page; there is no rider equivalent.
findings.impact: Identity data is retained without ever being used, which is both a dead field and a data-minimisation question.

findings.title: rider.referredBy is written but never read
findings.detail: processReferral sets referredBy on the referred rider, but no render function, table, profile card or export reads the field.
findings.impact: Referral attribution is stored and then invisible.

findings.title: Toolbar subtitle claims 284 registered riders against a 10-rider dataset
findings.detail: subs['riders'] is seeded as the literal '284 registered riders'. Unlike the Drivers entry, which refreshNavCounts overwrites with a live count, nothing recomputes this value for the Riders page, so the toolbar keeps stating 284.
findings.impact: A prominently placed number that is off by a factor of twenty-eight and never corrects itself.

findings.title: Unknown rider level renders as a red pill
findings.detail: The inline class map falls through to b-red for any lvl outside gold/silver/new. lvlBadge(), used on the profile, maps the same unknown value to b-grey with the label Standard. A rider with lvl 'standard' therefore gets an alarming red pill in the roster and a neutral grey one on their profile.
findings.impact: A neutral state is presented as an alert in one view and as normal in another.

findings.title: A large set of helper bodies was never read
findings.detail: The doc explicitly marks 38 helpers as cited from call sites only, including arrivalEvidenceHTML, rideStateTimelineHTML, tripRatingsCardHTML, openTripReceipt, openInvoiceModal, sendTripReceipt, flagTrip, unflagTrip, freezePlan, changeDriver, cancelSub, toggleAutoRenew, logPriorityCall, compCheck, logGoodwill, auditForEntity and commissionRateForPlan. The role matrix behind can(permKey) and the DB.legalDocuments seed were also not read.
findings.impact: Several trip and subscription actions documented on this page have unverified runtime effects, so the module's action inventory should not be treated as complete.

findings.title: Card collapse controls exist only on rider and driver profiles
findings.detail: initCardToggles is called only inside the rider and driver branch of openProfile, so trip, subscription, payment and complaint profiles never get the collapse affordance, and this is the only page in the app that calls it at all.
findings.impact: The same shell behaves differently depending on which entity was resolved, with no explanation to the operator.

findings.title: Complaint lists get no reconciliation escalation
findings.detail: tripsTable and payTable both take a ctxId and escalate their empty state when reconcileEntity reports an orphan row. cmpTable takes only the id array, so a complaints list can never carry the same warning.
findings.impact: Inconsistent treatment of the three linked-record tables; a complaints gap looks identical to a genuinely clean record.

findings.title: Degenerate ternary in riderNoShowCount
findings.detail: The filter contains c.tsMs!==undefined ? c.openedAtMs>=since : c.openedAtMs>=since - both branches are identical, so the tsMs test has no effect. The precedence also makes the whole preceding conjunction the ternary condition, which happens to still evaluate to a boolean.
findings.impact: An intended distinction between two timestamp fields was lost; whichever field was meant to be honoured in one branch is never consulted.

findings.title: Doc line numbers drift from source in several places
findings.detail: Verified against source: reviewDriver is at L8995-L9003 not L8987-L8995 and viewDriver is at L8994 not L8985; openWalletAdjustModal is at L3962 and commitWalletAdjust at L3977 (doc says 3961 and 3978); openEditTipModal is at L4192 and commitEditTip at L4204 (doc says 4199 and 4207); resolveComplaint is at L4377; onDriverExceptionToggle L9115, commitDriverException L9130, onDriverTrustToggle L9139. The DB seed ranges are also off: riders start L2593, drivers L2631, trips L2670, subscriptions L2685, payments L2694, complaints L2706.
findings.evidence: function reviewDriver(name){  // at line 8995 in eyvar_ops_panel_v40_fixed.html
findings.impact: Anyone navigating the source from the doc's line index lands a few lines off, and in the reviewDriver case on the wrong function.

findings.title: Priority call from a profile loses its context and entity id
findings.detail: priorityCall accepts name, context and entityId, but the profile action bar calls it with only d.name, so the modal renders the default context 'manual' with no id, and logPriorityCall receives two undefined arguments.
findings.impact: Calls logged from a 360 profile cannot be attributed to the record they were made from.

findings.title: Subscription trip log sorts dates as strings
findings.detail: The sub-profile trip log sorts with DB.trips[b].date.localeCompare(DB.trips[a].date) over labels formatted as '25 Jun 07:00'. Day-first ordering happens to look right within a month and is wrong the moment the range crosses a month boundary.
findings.impact: A subscription spanning a month rollover lists its legs out of order.

findings.title: Subscription trip-log badge reads '5/5 complete'
findings.detail: The card header interpolates d.trips, which is the subscription's progress string rather than a count, into a badge suffixed with the word complete.
findings.impact: Cosmetic, but the label reads as a rendering bug on every subscription profile.

findings.title: The lazily created driverAgreement consent is never rendered
findings.detail: getUserConsent(d, true) creates a driverAgreement consent record for drivers, but the Device and access card lists only tos and privacy. The driver-agreement compliance figure is visible only in the Settings legal view.
findings.evidence: getUserConsent(d,isDrv).tos.version and .privacy are the only two consents rendered on the card
findings.impact: A driver's agreement status is invisible on the record an operator actually opens.

findings.title: Topbar title bypasses the titles map
findings.detail: openProfile assigns the literal string to #tb-title and d.id to #tb-sub, overriding titles.profile and subs.profile which already hold the same and a different value respectively.
findings.impact: The topbar title is untranslatable and does not follow the convention every other page uses, and subs.profile is effectively dead.

findings.title: Trip history newest-first sort has nothing to sort on for seed data
findings.detail: tripsTable sorts by (dateMs||0) descending, but no seeded trip carries a dateMs. Every seed trip ties at zero and keeps array order, so the newest-first promise only holds for trips generated by buildRiderHistory.
findings.impact: The ordering an operator relies on when scanning a trip history is not actually guaranteed for real seeded records.

findings.title: Wallet credit and debit are later wrapped with ledger posting
findings.detail: The doc describes commitWalletAdjust as calling creditRiderWallet and debitRiderWallet directly. Both functions are reassigned later in the file with an idempotency key and double-entry ledger postings, so the real commit path from the profile does more than the doc records.
findings.impact: The documented side effects of a wallet adjustment made from a profile are incomplete, which matters when reconciling ledger entries against audit lines.

findings.title: disputedRating is stored and never shown
findings.detail: commitRatingDispute copies t.driverRatingGiven onto c.disputedRating, but no renderer reads it; the row shows only the kind, id, detail and meta line.
findings.impact: The decider cannot see which star value is being contested without opening the trip.

findings.title: Driver fixture size is misstated in the doc
findings.detail: The doc records the demo fleet as five captains DRV-0101 to DRV-0105. The source seeds six, DRV-0101 to DRV-0106, in the drivers block beginning at L2631. captainEconomics iterates all of them.
findings.evidence: 'DRV-0106' is present in the drivers seed block
findings.impact: Any count derived from the doc's fleet size is off by one.

findings.title: Ownership and case-chip behaviour unverified
findings.detail: Each row renders workChip('fairness', c.id), which is caseChip plus ownerChip, and the decision gate calls ownershipWarning('fairness', caseId). All three live in the case and ownership modules, outside this module group, and their return shapes and click handlers were not read.
findings.impact: The row's ownership affordances and the warning shown in the decision gate are documented from call sites only.

findings.title: The human-readable case date is never rendered
findings.detail: fcNew stores date from fmtReqNowLabel alongside openedAtMs, but every row renders the age from fmtAge instead, so c.date is written and never read on this page.
findings.impact: Minor - the absolute filing timestamp is unavailable in the UI.

findings.title: The page has no filtering of any kind
findings.detail: All four KPI tiles are plain class kpi with no click class and no onclick, and renderFairnessPage declares no filter state, no search box and no sort control - unlike coverage, compliance, safety and commitment, which each have one.
findings.impact: An operator facing a long queue cannot narrow it by kind, captain, SLA state or age.

findings.title: The page is English-only despite bilingual reason codes
findings.detail: The only data-i18n attribute anywhere near the page is nav.fairness on the sidebar item. Reason codes carry labelEn and labelAr in the registry, but rcLabel returns labelEn only, so the Arabic label never appears. Every heading, KPI label, column header, button, toast and empty state is a hardcoded English literal in JS.
findings.impact: Arabic-language operators see an untranslated page even though half the underlying data is already translated.

findings.title: Three modals share one input id
findings.detail: The rating-dispute, rider-report and driver-appeal modals all render a textarea with id fc-detail. It works because only one modal is open at a time, but it is a fragile pattern that breaks the moment any of them is rendered concurrently or read after a partial close.
findings.impact: Any future change that keeps two of these modals in the DOM would silently read the wrong textarea.

findings.title: Tips are folded into earnings but not into the caveat
findings.detail: captainEconomics sums (parseFloat(t.driverEarn)||0)+(t.tip||0) into earn, while the explanatory band next to the table only discusses engaged time versus true online hours and never mentions tips.
findings.impact: A reader comparing the column against a payout report will find a discrepancy the on-screen explanation does not account for.

findings.title: Two statistics helpers defined here are unused here
findings.detail: sameCaptainStats computes the share of subscriptions with no driver change and onTimeStats the share of non-cancelled trips that are not late. Both sit inside this module's block and neither renderFairnessPage nor renderCaptainEconomics calls them.
findings.impact: Either two intended fairness metrics were dropped from the page, or the definitions belong in another module. Whether another page consumes them was not checked.

findings.title: appealId is initialised and never written
findings.detail: The absence event carries both appealId and emergencyId; only emergencyId is ever set, by commitEmergencyClaim.
findings.impact: A second appeal channel appears to have been planned and never wired.

findings.title: Boot-order fragility is acknowledged in the source
findings.detail: renderCommitmentPage guards coverageStats and DB.backupRegistry, guards renderEmergencyDispatch and renderCoverage after setting innerHTML, and pendingConfirmations guards DB.planConfirmations because the function is hoisted and callable before this module's data is assigned. The bootModules block itself carries a warning that it must remain the last thing in the script.
findings.impact: The page renders correctly only because of defensive typeof checks; reordering the single-file script would break it silently.

findings.title: Cross-module helpers documented from call sites only
findings.detail: newCase, linkToCase and caseFor (case module), creditRiderWallet and logGoodwill posting behaviour (rider wallet and goodwill modules) and ownershipWarning (ownership module) were not read. Their effects as recorded here are inferred from the call sites in recordAbsence, emergencyDispatch and acceptEmergency.
findings.impact: The downstream consequences of recording an absence and of accepting an emergency dispatch are not fully verified.

findings.title: Distance and ETA are synthetic map-grid geometry
findings.detail: gridDistanceKm takes the euclidean distance between two map-grid positions, scales it by 0.42, rounds to one decimal and returns 99 when either position is missing. ETA is Math.max(2, Math.round(km*2.4)), and the standing-backup queue entry is stubbed at 0 km and 6 minutes.
findings.impact: The nearest-captain ordering and every distance and ETA shown in the dispatch queue are demo geometry, not routing data.

findings.title: forfeitRemaining is declared on every tier and never read
findings.detail: All three ladder tiers carry forfeitRemaining true, but recordAbsence forfeits unconditionally without consulting the flag, so a tier configured not to forfeit would forfeit anyway.
findings.impact: A configuration knob that appears to exist has no effect, which is a trap for anyone editing the ladder.

findings.title: reserveForfeited is stored and never displayed
findings.detail: Every absence event records reserveForfeited from the exposure calculation, but the absence rows show only the combined forfeited figure, the freeze days and the termination flag.
findings.impact: An operator cannot see how much of a forfeiture came from the reserve versus from undelivered legs.

findings.title: reserveState is never called
findings.detail: reserveState returns the reserve amount plus whether it has been released based on delivered legs, but no renderer or handler calls it. The reserve itself ships disabled at 0 percent.
findings.evidence: function reserveState(subId){ ... return {amount, released: done>=total, done, total};
findings.impact: The release side of the commitment reserve has no surface even if the reserve is switched on.

findings.title: The absence ladder is not editable
findings.detail: renderCommitSettings renders the three tiers as read-only descriptive text into #commit-tiers, while every scalar policy value beside it is an editable numeric input saved by saveCommitPolicy.
findings.evidence: the tiers block is emitted as formatted text, with no data-cf inputs
findings.impact: Freeze lengths, forfeiture flags and the termination point can only be changed in code.

findings.title: The awaiting filter chip shows a raw key
findings.detail: commitFilterChip maps unconfirmed, risk, absences, coverage and claims to readable labels but omits awaiting, so the chip renders the internal key.
findings.evidence: label map contains unconfirmed / risk / absences / coverage / claims only
findings.impact: Cosmetic leak of an internal identifier into the UI.

findings.title: The risk KPI filter does nothing
findings.detail: KPI 3 sets _commitFilter to risk and scrolls to the risk card, but the card renders the full risk array unconditionally - there is no riskShown variable anywhere in renderCommitmentPage.
findings.evidence: the risk card maps over risk directly, with no filter branch
findings.impact: The tile advertises a filter it does not apply, and the filter chip then claims the list is filtered when it is not.

findings.title: Three doc line citations are off by one
findings.detail: Verified against source: the minsToPickup expression is at L16612 not L16613, the paid*0.8 driver share in absenceExposure is at L16653 not L16652, and the under-earner colour test in the economics table is at L16306 not L16307. All other line numbers checked in this module matched exactly.
findings.impact: Trivial navigation drift only.

findings.title: Three policy values are editable but unused here
findings.detail: riderWaitMin, riderNoShowPayPct and payoutDays are rendered as editable settings rows and saved into DB.commitPolicy, but no function in this module reads them. Whether another module consumes them was not checked.
findings.evidence: riderWaitMin:10, riderNoShowPayPct:50, payoutDays:3 appear only in the settings form within this module
findings.impact: Operators can change values that may have no effect anywhere, with helper text implying they do.

findings.title: _coverageFilter has no toggle-off, chip or Clear control
findings.detail: filterCoverage(f) simply assigns and re-renders; unlike filterCommit it does not clear on re-click, and no filter chip is rendered (contrast commitFilterChip() at L16840). The only route back to 'all' is KPI tile 1.
findings.impact: An operator can be looking at a filtered subset with no on-screen indication that a filter is applied.

findings.title: 'Exposed value' and the commitment module measure 'at risk' on different bases
findings.detail: subEconomics().remaining is a rider-side figure (gross paid minus consumed, L3612), whereas the commitment module's exposure figure uses paid*0.8, the driver share (L16652). The KPI sub-label 'SAR deferred, unprotected' is accurate for this page, but the two surfaces are not comparable.
findings.impact: Two pages quote a currency figure for the same risk concept that differ by the commission rate, inviting a reconciliation that will never balance.

findings.title: #coverage-sub is given an id but never written to
findings.detail: The page sub-line paragraph carries id="coverage-sub" but no code assigns to it, and liveSubtitles() (L21236-L21255) does not cover this page.
findings.evidence: Backup captains per subscription + driver time-slot capacity
findings.impact: A hook for a live subtitle exists but is inert; the sub-line is permanently static English.

findings.title: Candidate modal has no empty state and no Cancel button
findings.detail: If the eligibility filter leaves zero candidates the modal renders its explanatory paragraph and nothing else, with only the ✕ to dismiss it — no message tells the operator that no eligible backup exists.
findings.impact: An operator can conclude the feature is broken rather than that the fleet has nobody eligible for that subscription.

findings.title: coverageBoot() is an intentional no-op
findings.detail: The module registers a boot step {name:'backup coverage', fn:coverageBoot, needs:['backupRegistry']} at L21818, but coverageBoot() has an empty body with the comment 'nothing to seed — coverage is computed live from eligibility'. The registry is actually seeded by the literal at L13140 plus dispatchBoot() (L17427-L17442).
findings.impact: None functionally; it is a documented placeholder, noted so the boot-step list is not misread as doing work.

findings.title: Doc's HTML line references for #p-coverage drift by 1-2 lines
findings.detail: The doc gives the page range as L1220-L1235 and cites #coverage-kpis at L1225, #coverage-exposed-count at L1227, #coverage-list at L1228 and #capacity-grid at L1233. Verified against source: the page div spans L1220-L1233, #coverage-kpis is L1224, #coverage-exposed-count L1226, #coverage-list L1227 and #capacity-grid L1231. The JS line references in the same doc check out exactly.
findings.impact: Anyone navigating the source from this doc's HTML index lands one or two lines off; the corrected numbers are used throughout this fragment.

findings.title: KPI 3 and KPI 4 apply the identical filter
findings.detail: Both 'Exposed (no backup)' (L13156) and 'Exposed value' (L13157) call filterCoverage('exposed') with the same title attribute, so the two tiles are behaviourally indistinguishable.
findings.evidence: onclick="filterCoverage('exposed')" title="Show only subscriptions with no backup"
findings.impact: A click target that promises a different view of the data does nothing different.

findings.title: The capacity grid ignores the page filter
findings.detail: renderCapacityGrid() always calls activeSubsList() directly (L13241) rather than the filtered set, so selecting 'Exposed' above leaves the grid below unchanged and unexplained.
findings.impact: The two halves of the page can disagree about which subscriptions are in scope, with no visual cue that the lower card is unfiltered.

findings.title: Two KPI progress bars carry fixed widths
findings.detail: KPI 1 ('Active subscriptions') renders its bar at a fixed width:70% and KPI 4 ('Exposed value') at width:40%, neither derived from the value shown above it. KPI 2 and KPI 3 are correctly data-driven percentages.
findings.impact: Two of four tiles carry a visual that reads as a proportion but conveys no information.

findings.title: KPI bar widths are cosmetic
findings.detail: Tile 1's bar is a fixed width:100%; tiles 2-4 use Math.min(100, n*20), an arbitrary scale on which five drivers fills the bar.
findings.impact: The bars imply a proportion of the fleet that they do not represent.

findings.title: KPI tiles 2-4 do not sum to tile 1 and healthy drivers have no tile
findings.detail: A driver's band is the minimum rank across all five documents, so bands are mutually exclusive per driver. Drivers whose worst document is more than 30 days out (worst===3) appear only in tile 1 and can be reached only via the 'all' filter.
findings.impact: The tiles read as a breakdown but are not one; an operator checking the arithmetic will find a shortfall with no on-screen explanation.

findings.title: No search, pagination, export or sticky header on a whole-fleet page
findings.detail: The document table's only concession to scale is max-height:420px with overflow-y:auto on #compliance-list; the header row is not sticky and there is no search box, no sort control and no export.
findings.impact: At real fleet size the page becomes an unnavigable scroll with no way to find a specific driver or hand the list to anyone else.

findings.title: The Regulatory integrations card is entirely inert
findings.detail: Three hardcoded rows (Wasl, ZATCA e-invoicing Phase 2, Absher/Yakeen) each render the same fixed `⚠ Not connected`. There is no state, no data source, no toggle and no code path that could ever change the badge. The card is followed by a disclaimer stating the statuses are honest placeholders, not simulations.
findings.impact: Honest by design, but the section occupies a card that can never do anything; nothing in the panel tracks actual regulatory integration state.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — the intended docStatus vocabulary and its owner
findings.detail: The doc marks this UNVERIFIED and the source confirms the absence: there is no assignment site, no schema comment, and no DB.drivers seed carrying the field, so whether the intended values were 'expiring'/'expired' or something else, and which module should own the assignment, cannot be determined from the file.
findings.impact: A fix must decide the contract as well as implement it; the safest route the doc identifies is deriving docStatus from complianceScan() rather than adding a new field.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — whether document expiries realistically arrive during a session
findings.detail: The source comment at L12616 claims expiries actually arrive during a session. At SUBREQ_TIME_ACCEL_MIN_PER_TICK=1 with setInterval(tickEngine,1000), the nearest non-expired document (DRV-0105 vehicle_reg, 12 days) needs 5 simulated days ≈ 7,200 ticks ≈ 2 hours of real time to fall into the ≤7-day band. The arithmetic is verifiable; whether a session lasts that long is not.
findings.impact: The background scan is effectively decorative in a normal-length session, so the auto-suspend path is realistically exercised only by the seed data or by editing dates.

findings.title: update_doc_dates audit entry carries empty before/after objects
findings.detail: logAction supports a structured before/after diff (L3133-L3145) but saveDriverDocDates passes {} for both, putting the whole change into the human-readable summary string instead.
findings.impact: The Activity log cannot be queried or diffed programmatically for document-date changes; only the prose is searchable.

findings.title: Audit rows for incidents cannot be clicked through
findings.detail: logAction is called with entityType 'incident' (L13456, L13483), but resolveId()'s bucket list (L3270) covers riders, drivers, trips, subscriptions, payments and complaints — not incidents.
findings.impact: From the Activity log there is no way to jump from a safety audit entry to the incident it describes.

findings.title: before/after audit diffs are empty for two of three actions
findings.detail: incident_step passes before={} with after={step,done} (L13456, L13460) and precaution_suspend passes before={} with after={incident:incId} (L13472). Only close_incident populates both, with {status:'open'} → {status:'closed'}.
findings.impact: The structured diff logAction supports is unused for the two most frequent safety actions, leaving only prose to reconstruct what changed.

findings.title: Doc's KPI tile line numbers are off by one
findings.detail: The doc cites the tiles at L13400 (open), L13401 (critical) and L13402 (closed). Verified against source: #safety-kpis is fetched at L13399, the innerHTML assignment opens at L13400, and the tiles are at L13401, L13402, L13403 with the Compliance-navigating tile 4 at L13404 (which the doc gets right).
findings.evidence: 13401:    '<div class="kpi click" onclick="filterSafety(\'open\')" title="Show only open incidents">
findings.impact: Minor navigation drift; the corrected numbers are used throughout this fragment.

findings.title: The 'Normal' severity branch has no producer
findings.detail: The severity badge is a three-way ternary whose third branch renders 'Normal' for any value other than 'critical' or 'high'. All three seeded incidents are critical or high, there is no severity enumeration, no mapping from type to severity, and no UI to set severity at all.
findings.evidence: var sevB=inc.severity==='critical'?'🆘 CRITICAL':inc.severity==='high'?'High':'Normal';
findings.impact: A third severity level is rendered by the UI but unreachable by any code path or operator action.

findings.title: Three of four KPI bar widths are fixed constants
findings.detail: KPI 2 renders width:25%, KPI 3 width:33% and KPI 4 width:10%, none derived from data; KPI 1 uses Math.min(100, open.length*25), an arbitrary scale on which four incidents fills the bar.
findings.impact: The tiles carry a visual that reads as a proportion but conveys nothing.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — whether an SOS ingestion path was intended elsewhere
findings.detail: The doc marks this UNVERIFIED and the source is silent: DB.incidents has no writer anywhere in the file and nothing suggests a driver/rider app webhook was planned.
findings.impact: Whether the missing creation path is an omission or an out-of-scope backend concern cannot be settled from this file.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — whether severity was meant to be derived from type
findings.detail: The seed data is consistent with a mapping such as SOS ⇒ critical, but no code implements any type-to-severity derivation and severity is a hand-authored field on each record.
findings.impact: If severity is intended to be derived, every future incident would need it set by hand with no rule to check it against.

findings.title: All six growth cards are blank until the page is first visited
findings.detail: Neither renderGrowthPage() nor renderReferralProgram() appears in the boot setTimeout block (L14556-L14600); the only render path is the router branch.
findings.impact: Nothing on the growth page is warm at boot, so no growth figure can be surfaced elsewhere without navigating there first.

findings.title: New incentives append while new promos prepend
findings.detail: commitNewPromo unshifts so the newest campaign is first (L13554); addIncentiveRule pushes so the newest rule is last (L13718). Both lists are rendered in raw array order with no sort control.
findings.impact: Two lists on one page order new entries oppositely, so an operator who just created something has to look in a different place each time.

findings.title: Promos cannot be deleted or archived and the table has no empty state
findings.detail: Code uniqueness is checked once, at create (L13553); nothing prevents later mutation and there is no delete or archive action for promos anywhere. renderPromoList maps DB.promos and joins, so an empty array renders a header-only table with no placeholder row.
findings.impact: A mistaken campaign is permanent for the session, and a fresh install would show an empty table that looks broken rather than empty.

findings.title: renderGrowthPage() does not render the referral card
findings.detail: renderGrowthPage calls renderPromoList, renderIncentives, renderBulkMsg, renderCohorts and renderCsat. renderReferralProgram is invoked separately by the router branch at L8799.
findings.impact: Any future caller of renderGrowthPage alone leaves the referral config strip, KPI tiles, leaderboard and log stale.

findings.title: rider.referredBy is written and never read
findings.detail: grep of referredBy returns exactly one hit — the assignment inside processReferral. No consumer exists.
findings.impact: The attribution link between a referee and their referrer is stored on the rider record but nothing in the panel surfaces or uses it; only the referral log carries the relationship in practice.

findings.title: Seed referral row contradicts its own KPI delta label
findings.detail: DB.referralLog is seeded with REF-seed-1 (RDR-1041 → RDR-1075, 20/10 SAR, dated '18 Jul'), so 'Total referrals processed' reads 1 at boot while its delta line says 'this session'. Seed bonus rows BON-seed-1/BON-seed-2 similarly make 'Earned (real)' show one driver for INV-1 and INV-2.
findings.impact: Three headline counters start non-zero from demo data while labelled as session activity.

findings.title: The referee picker lists riders who are already referred
findings.detail: Both custom selects are built over every DB.riders key with no exclusion of the chosen referrer or of riders already present in DB.referralLog; the duplicate is caught only by guard 4 after submit.
findings.impact: The operator can complete the whole flow before learning the referee is ineligible.

findings.title: The referral-disabled message points to the wrong page
findings.detail: processReferral's first guard fails with 'Referral program is currently disabled in Settings.', but the ref-enabled toggle lives in the referral card on this Growth page (L1276), not in Settings.
findings.impact: An operator sent to Settings to re-enable the programme will not find the control there.

findings.title: Two modals open ungated and only refuse on commit
findings.detail: openProcessReferralModal (L3907) and openAwardIncentiveModal (L13688) perform no permission check; the gates live on commitProcessReferral (contact_users, L3920) and commitAwardIncentive (process_payouts, L13703).
findings.impact: An operator without the permission can select riders or a driver and type an amount before being refused, which reads as a failure rather than as a missing permission.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — actual delivery of sendSystemEmail
findings.detail: sendSystemEmail (L3578) writes to DB.emailOutbox; there is no transport in this static single-file app. Expected for a demo panel, but the two referral emails and the incentive-award email cannot be confirmed to leave the browser.
findings.impact: Referral and bonus notifications are recorded as sent in the outbox with no delivery mechanism behind them.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — runtime behaviour of the custom searchable select
findings.detail: customSelectHTML (L5336-L5382) builds the markup, but the runtime behaviour of positionCselMenu (L5383) and cselSetValue (L5427) — in particular whether already-selected values are filtered out — was not traced end to end for the source doc and is not confirmed here.
findings.impact: The severity of the referee-picker gap (#18) depends on this; it may be partially mitigated at runtime.

findings.title: #st-preview is an empty div nothing populates
findings.detail: The steering-offer modal renders an empty `<div id="st-preview">`; grep finds exactly one occurrence in the file, the markup itself. No code writes to it.
findings.impact: A cost-preview stub that was never built; the operator commits a bonus amount and cap with no projected-spend feedback.

findings.title: #zones-sub carries an id but is never written to
findings.detail: The page sub-line has id="zones-sub", matching the pattern of dynamic subtitles such as #all-pending-sub (L1326), but no JS assigns to it and liveSubtitles() does not cover this page.
findings.evidence: Where requests fail to match — the recruitment map
findings.impact: An inert hook for a live subtitle; the sub-line stays static English.

findings.title: A live steering offer cannot be cancelled or edited
findings.detail: Once pushed, an offer ends only when minutesLeft reaches 0 or spent reaches cap, both inside tickSteerOffers. No cancel, extend or amend control exists.
findings.impact: A mistyped bonus or cap runs to completion; the only mitigation is that the cap does genuinely close the offer.

findings.title: addTime collapses AM and PM into the same hour bucket
findings.detail: The hour is extracted with /(\d{1,2}):/ , which captures only the numeric hour, so '07:00 AM' and '07:00 PM' both increment bucket 7.
findings.impact: Harmless with the fixed 05:00-11:00 window and morning-commute seed data, but any afternoon or evening leg with a matching hour number would be counted as morning demand.

findings.title: Hours outside 05:00-11:00 vanish from the 'known demand' chart
findings.detail: The hours map is initialised with keys 5 through 11 only, and addTime increments only when `hours[h] != null`, so any scheduled trip outside that window is silently dropped with no indication in the chart or its footer.
findings.impact: The card is captioned as KNOWN scheduled demand from the subscription book, but it shows only the morning slice of it.

findings.title: KPI filters apply to only one of the two tables and persist invisibly
findings.detail: The _zonesFilter predicate is applied at L14143-L14146 to the Zone-health table only; the momentum table above renders its full zoneSubMomentum() output regardless. _zonesFilter is module-level and never reset by go(), and no chip or indicator shows that a filter is active.
findings.impact: Clicking 'Supply-starved zones' leaves the momentum list unfiltered with no explanation, and leaving the page with a filter set means returning to a silently filtered view.

findings.title: No map exists despite the page being framed as one
findings.detail: The h1 carries a 🗺️ icon and the sub-line calls the page 'the recruitment map', but zone records hold no lat/lng, polygon or geometry of any kind, and no canvas or SVG map is rendered.
findings.impact: The page's central metaphor is aspirational; spatial reasoning about adjacency or coverage is impossible from the data model.

findings.title: offer.sentTo is written and never read
findings.detail: commitSteerOffer stores steerableDrivers().length as sentTo on the offer record; no code reads it back — the modal recomputes the count each time it opens and the closing audit entry quotes accepted and spent instead.
findings.impact: The recipient count at the moment of sending is captured but never surfaced, so there is no record of how the audience size changed over an offer's life.

findings.title: Requests whose pickup matches no zone are silently discarded
findings.detail: zoneOfPickup does a naive lowercase substring match against zone names (aliasing on ' / '), returning null on a miss; zoneSubMomentum then skips the request entirely. With the five seeded subscription requests, 'Al Rabwah District' appears twice and matches nothing.
findings.impact: Two of five seeded requests are invisible to both the momentum table and the hourly chart, and the pipeline-value figure under-reports by the same amount, with no 'unmapped' row to reveal the loss.

findings.title: The hourly card never hides again once opened
findings.detail: showZoneHourly sets the card's display to '' on first use; nothing ever restores display:none, and the card is not cleared when the zone-health filter changes.
findings.impact: The card can keep showing a zone that the active filter has removed from the table, with no visual link back to a row.

findings.title: Two thresholds for 'demand outstrips supply'
findings.detail: This page and Predictive Signals treat demand/supply >= 3 as the shortage line; Executive Overview's expansion-ready list uses >= 2 and sorts descending by the same ratio.
findings.impact: The same concept produces different zone sets on different pages with no note explaining why.

findings.title: Unused subscription lookup inside the hourly loop
findings.detail: showZoneHourly computes a full subscription lookup for every upcoming trip and never references the result.
findings.impact: A per-iteration O(n) scan over the whole subscription book runs for no reason on every hourly-chart render.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — driverLiveState(id).busy semantics
findings.detail: steerableDrivers excludes drivers where driverLiveState(d).busy is truthy. The function is located at L7283 but its body belongs to the live-map module and was not read for the source doc; the meaning of 'busy' is taken from the call-site comment at L13983-L13984.
findings.impact: The exact eligibility population for a steering offer — and, via the same helper, for backup-captain candidates in Coverage — is not fully pinned down.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — whether zoneOfPickup resolves real-world pickup strings
findings.detail: Matching is a naive lowercase substring test with ' / ' aliasing. Only the five seeded subscriptionRequests (L2795-L2799) and the upcomingSubTrips route fields (L6177+) were traced, and no test suite exists in the file.
findings.impact: The silent-drop behaviour of #17 could affect an unknown proportion of real pickups, and the hourly chart's per-zone contribution from upcoming trips was not enumerated row by row.

findings.title: Zone names are interpolated raw into generated onclick handlers
findings.detail: Six sites build inline handlers by string-concatenating the zone name inside single quotes: L14020 (modal commit button), L14072 and L14079 (momentum row), L14155, L14163 and L14166 (health row).
findings.impact: A zone name containing an apostrophe would break every generated handler for that row. Latent — no seed zone contains one — and only reachable by editing source, since zones have no CRUD UI.

findings.title: A ledger term multiplied by zero
findings.detail: accountBalance('tax.vat_output')*0 in ledgerReconcile contributes nothing to the refunds comparison row.
findings.impact: Dead arithmetic that disguises the VAT-inclusive versus VAT-exclusive mismatch as an intentional comparison.

findings.title: A Paid payment renders in the same grey as an unknown status
findings.detail: statusBadge matches /done|resolved|closed/i to b-green, /trip|active/i to b-blue, /late|expir|pend/i to b-amber and /cancel|risk|refund/i to b-red, otherwise b-grey. The literal 'Paid' matches none of the four and falls through to grey, so the green branch can never be reached by any payment status.
findings.impact: The most common and most positive payment state is visually indistinguishable from an unrecognised one.

findings.title: Declared accounts that are never posted to
findings.detail: ACCOUNTS declares ar.rider (L19867) and expense.emergency (L19875); neither is ever used as an account key in a postLedger call. The emergency path posts to liability.driver and expense.compensation instead.
findings.impact: The chart of accounts overstates what the books actually track.

findings.title: Doc line references drift by one to four lines in several places
findings.detail: Spot-verification against source found: the refunds total is computed at L3206 and written at L3208 (doc says L3205-L3207); the refunds empty state is L3210 (doc L3209); the rider cell L3216, amount L3217, status L3221 (doc L3214, L3215, L3219); renderCreditNotes aggregates are L3925-L3927 equivalents at L15925-L15927 (doc L15924-L15926) and the credit-note amount is L15940 with the empty state at L15942 (doc L15938, L15941); issueCreditNote writes id at L15871 and noteNumber at L15872 (doc L15869, L15870); confirmCancelSub begins at L5549 (doc index L5545); getCancellationRule is defined at L5548 and called at L5527 (doc says L5533); postLedger begins at L19917 (doc L19918); PERMISSION_LABELS begins at L3225 (doc L3226). All handler names and all page/seed line ranges were confirmed correct. The corrected numbers are used throughout this fragment.
findings.impact: Documentation-only drift; no runtime effect, but line-anchored navigation from the doc lands slightly off.

findings.title: findInvoiceForRefund tests a field that does not exist
findings.detail: The matching clause tests p.sub===rel, but no record in DB.payments carries a sub field - the subscription link is stored in p.trip (e.g. PAY-5510 has trip 'SUB-1041'). The clause is permanently false.
findings.impact: One third of the intended matching logic never runs, pushing more refunds into the arbitrary-fallback branch.

findings.title: No filter, sort, search, export or pagination on the money lists
findings.detail: renderRefundsTable emits a plain tbl-scroll table with no max-height, no sort control, no filter and no export, rendering every row. renderCreditNotes likewise renders every key of DB.creditNotes with no controls, in oldest-first object-key order - the opposite ordering of the refunds table directly above it.
findings.impact: Both ledgers become unusable at real data volumes, and the two adjacent lists sort in opposite directions.

findings.title: payTable has no totals row
findings.detail: payTable renders six columns of payment data inside a max-height 380px scroller with no tfoot and no per-column sum, despite being a money table shown inside rider and driver 360 profiles.
findings.impact: An operator reviewing a rider's payments must add the column by hand.

findings.title: Refund seed comment contradicts the subscription seed
findings.detail: The comment above DB.refunds asserts the seeded refunds reference subscriptions 'already fully closed and outside today's active list', but SUB-0998 and SUB-0987 are both present in DB.subscriptions with status 'Cancelled'.
findings.impact: Demo-data artefact; the comment misdescribes the dataset it documents.

findings.title: The sub_before_first_trip cancellation rule is never read
findings.detail: DB.cancellationPolicy defines sub_before_first_trip with feePct 0, enabled false, locked true. getCancellationRule is called only for 'sub_mid_cycle' (L5527) and in the quick-ride path (L11832). The 'no fee before the first trip' behaviour is actually implemented by the used>0 test in cancelSub, not by the rule.
findings.impact: A configurable policy row shown in Settings has no effect on any calculation.

findings.title: Unreachable refunds empty state
findings.detail: The 'No refunds issued this session.' branch fires only when DB.refunds.length is 0, but two rows are seeded at L2882-L2883. The wording also says 'this session' although the rows are seed data, not session activity.
findings.impact: Cosmetic; the empty state can never be seen and its wording would be misleading if it were.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED payTable orphan-reconciliation branch
findings.detail: payTable renders a distinct empty state when reconcileEntity(ctxId) returns a row labelled 'Total paid' with severity 'orphan', warning that any refund calculated from the screen would be wrong. The doc marks this UNVERIFIED because reconcileEntity was outside its assigned scope and the branch was not traced.
findings.impact: It is unconfirmed whether the orphan warning - the one place the UI tells an operator not to trust a refund calculation - is ever reachable.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED provenance of the hardcoded finance figures
findings.detail: The doc marks as unverifiable (U1, U2) whether the seven hardcoded KPI figures were ever derived from a real dataset, and whether the static Revenue-by-plan percentages 20 / 18 / 15 / 18.1 are meant to mirror DB.plans[*].eyvarPct. The three per-plan values coincide with L2890, L2892 and L2894, but the table is static HTML with no binding, so the correspondence cannot be confirmed as intentional. Only their mutual inconsistency is verifiable.
findings.impact: The intent behind the demo figures cannot be established from the source, so it is unclear whether they encode a real business assumption.

findings.title: #escrow-count badge counts both statuses
findings.detail: setText('escrow-count', DB.escrowHolds.length) sits next to the header 'Subscription escrow holds' with class b-amber - the same amber used for the held state - so it reads as a held count but is a total count. With the seed it shows 4, not 2.
findings.impact: The badge overstates how much is actually still being withheld.

findings.title: A safety-net comment with nothing to override
findings.detail: The comment at L7022 describes the following block as the 'final authoritative versions' that 'override any stale duplicates', but grep finds no earlier definitions of payDriver, processAllPayouts, releaseEscrow, confirmApplyDeduction or renderPayoutsTable.
findings.impact: The comment implies a defensive redefinition pattern that does not exist, which could mislead a future maintainer into duplicating a definition.

findings.title: Doc line reference for postLedger is off by one
findings.detail: The doc's line-number index lists postLedger at L19918-L19933; the function declaration is actually at L19917. Every handler line number in this doc's index was otherwise verified correct against the source, as were the page div range L968-L1017 and all seed ranges.
findings.impact: Documentation-only drift; no runtime effect.

findings.title: Escalation KPI sub-line misstates its own metric
findings.detail: The tile reads 'repeat pattern detected' but counts every entry with status 'escalated' (L12242). Escalation is a manual operator choice made in the resolve modal (L12166) and is entirely independent of driverCashRiskCount.
findings.impact: The tile implies an automated pattern signal where the number is really a count of human decisions.

findings.title: No deduction creation path and no fee schedule
findings.detail: DB.deductions is seed-only: the only writes are the three seed literals at L2808-L2810 and the .status assignments in confirmApplyDeduction and waiveDeduction. There is no enumerated deduction-type constant - the type is a free string on each record - and no UI creates a deduction.
findings.impact: The penalty subsystem has no way to record a new penalty and no governed schedule of what penalties cost.

findings.title: No filtering or pagination on any of the five lists
findings.detail: None of the payouts table, escrow list, deductions list, cash queue or debt ledger has a filter, search, sort control or date range. The cash queue applies a hard slice(0,150) after a stable pending-first partition and truncates silently with no 'showing 150 of N' indicator, and its card header claims the list is 'sorted by most recent', which is only true within each partition.
findings.impact: Rows beyond 150 disappear from the cash queue with no indication, and no list can be narrowed at real data volume.

findings.title: Seeded audit entries contradict the seed data
findings.detail: AUD-0005 records 'Processed all driver payouts - 8,200.00 SAR total (3 drivers, cycle ending 22 Jun)' while the seed's total pending is 2,360.00 SAR. AUD-0004 records releasing escrow ESC-1035, which is not present in DB.escrowHolds. AUD-0001 is dated 20 Jun while the payout seed's lastPayout says 22 Jun. Notification seed N5 says 6,420 SAR awaiting processing for 3 drivers.
findings.impact: Demo-data artefacts; the audit log and notification tray tell a story the payout data does not support.

findings.title: Silver rating chip for every non-gold driver
findings.detail: The payout row builds the rating chip as dd.lvl==='gold' ? 'b-gold' : 'b-silver', so a standard or new driver gets a Silver-styled chip - contradicting the Level column immediately to its right, which correctly renders b-grey via lvlBadgeSm (L8902).
findings.impact: Two adjacent cells in the same row report different tiers for the same driver.

findings.title: The payouts table has no empty state
findings.detail: tbody.innerHTML = ids.map(...).join(''), so an empty DB.payouts renders a headed table with zero rows and no message. All four other lists on the page have explicit empty states (L8918, L8956, L12251, L12265).
findings.impact: An operator cannot tell an empty payout run from a rendering failure.

findings.title: Tips are displayed but never paid
findings.detail: simulateTip generates 2-10 SAR tips at trip completion and the driver 360 profile sums them as SUM of (t.tip||0) over the driver's trips (L4170), but no code path adds a tip to DB.payouts.pending. The comment at L12042 states tips go 100% to the driver.
findings.evidence: /* Tips go 100% to the driver - never split with platform commission */
findings.impact: Money the product says belongs entirely to the driver never enters the payout balance they are actually paid.

findings.title: Unused local and unused parameter in the payout flow
findings.detail: confirmPayDriver builds var rows = [['Net payout amount', ...]] at L7198 and never reads it. processAllPayouts accepts a btn parameter at L7037 and never references it.
findings.impact: Dead code in the two most sensitive payout entry points.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED runtime behaviour of the cash subsystem
findings.detail: DB.cashLedger and DB.driverCashDebt both start empty, and every row is produced by maybeGenerateCashEvent from the trip-completion simulation, which the doc marks as outside its assigned scope (U1). The generation itself is fully random - a five-branch probability ladder at L12109-L12122 plus Math.random for the tip, the rider confirmation and the reason - so no runtime value is statically determinable (U2). Whether driverCashRiskCount genuinely feeds Predictive Signals is also unverified (U3), as is whether playAlertBeep succeeds (U4).
findings.impact: All four cash KPIs, the queue and the debt ledger show zero or empty in a fresh session, so the subsystem cannot be assessed from a cold start.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED semantics of p.earned
findings.detail: releaseEscrow increments p.earned (L7066) but payDriver never decrements it (L7029-L7032). Whether earned is meant to be lifetime-gross or cycle-gross is documented nowhere in the file, so it cannot be determined whether the escrow increment is correct. The doc also leaves unverified whether DB.drivers[*].bank.iban is always present, since confirmPayDriver guards with a dash fallback (U5).
findings.impact: The Earned column may be double-counting or under-counting escrow money, and there is no specification to check it against.

findings.title: No export, search, filter, sort control or pagination on the wallets table
findings.detail: The page markup contains only a header, a KPI container and a single table. renderRiderWalletsList applies a fixed descending-balance sort and renders every wallet-bearing rider with no virtualisation. The panel has exportData/buildCSV and exportContacts elsewhere but nothing for wallets.
findings.impact: Safe at demo scale (2 seeded wallets) but unbounded in production, and Finance has no way to extract the wallet-liability list for reconciliation.

findings.title: No subs['rwallets'] key, so the toolbar sub-title is blank on this page
findings.detail: The titles map has rwallets:'Rider Wallets' but the parallel subs map has no rwallets key (it has wallets:'Driver payout management' for the driver-wallets page). The router sets tb-sub to subs[id]||''.
findings.evidence: var titles={…,rwallets:'Rider Wallets',…}  /* no matching key in the subs map at L2169 */
findings.impact: Cosmetic — the Rider Wallets page is the only finance page whose toolbar shows no explanatory sub-title.

findings.title: recordRefund is unreachable from the rider-wallets page
findings.detail: No button, link or handler inside #p-rwallets (L1020-L1029), renderRiderWalletsList or the adjust modal invokes recordRefund. Its only call site is commitCancelSub at L5562, and its confirmation gate spec at L17900 is exercised only through that path.
findings.impact: An operator on the wallets page cannot issue an actual refund to a rider's payment method; the only money movement available to them is a wallet credit, which creates a liability rather than returning cash.

findings.title: Refund ids derive from array length with unshift insertion
findings.detail: recordRefund builds id:'REF-'+String(DB.refunds.length+1).padStart(4,'0') and then unshifts the entry. The scheme is correct only while nothing is ever removed from DB.refunds.
findings.impact: Any deletion from DB.refunds causes the next refund to reuse an existing id, which would break the credit-note linkage that stores entry.creditNote against the refund.

findings.title: Seeded refunds do not reconcile with seeded wallets
findings.detail: DB.refunds seeds REF-0002 at 69.20 SAR for RDR-2087 (SUB-0998) and REF-0001 at 73.50 SAR for RDR-2055 (SUB-0987). Neither has a corresponding wallet transaction: RDR-2087's only seeded wallet credit is 17.30 SAR labelled 'Trip cancellation refund', and RDR-2055 has no wallet at all.
findings.impact: The demo data contradicts the code's own behaviour — commitCancelSub always writes both a refund line and a wallet credit for the same figure, which the seed does not reflect. Anyone using the seed to understand the money flow will draw the wrong conclusion.

findings.title: The 'Wallet transactions' KPI sub-label 'this session' is inaccurate
findings.detail: The third KPI's sub-label is a hard-coded literal in the tile array, while the value counts every transaction on every wallet including the two seeded WTX-seed records that predate the session.
findings.impact: The tile reads '2 · this session' on a fresh load when no transaction has occurred in the session at all.

findings.title: The debit modal's max attribute is a client-side hint set from an unformatted float
findings.detail: The amount input receives max="<w.balance>" only for debits, using the raw float rather than a formatted value. Nothing re-checks it in JS; the real guard is debitRiderWallet's balance test.
findings.impact: Not exploitable through this UI, but the attribute implies a validation that does not exist in JS and can render as max="17.299999999999997" for the seeded RDR-2087 balance.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — whether runtime-created reason codes carry a comp field
findings.detail: addReasonCode() pushes {code,ref:null,cat:'Other',target:'rider',tier:'T3',…} at L15117-L15129. The source doc did not establish whether the pushed object sets comp. If comp is undefined, compCheck's step-1 prohibition (which tests rc.comp===0) never fires for such a code, and rcCompCap would return null.
findings.impact: A reason code added at runtime through Settings could silently escape the per-scenario goodwill prohibition that all 40 seeded codes are subject to.

findings.title: Wallet transaction ids collide within the same millisecond
findings.detail: Both write paths build the id as 'WTX-'+Date.now(). processReferral issues two credits back to back at L3868 and L3869, which can land in the same millisecond.
findings.impact: Two transactions on different riders (or the same rider) can share an id, breaking any downstream reconciliation keyed on the transaction id.

findings.title: wallet.transactions[].balanceAfter is written and never read
findings.detail: Every credit and debit stores a balanceAfter snapshot on the WTX record. No renderer, report or reconciliation anywhere in the file reads the field.
findings.impact: The one piece of data that would let the audit-log's missing 'before' balance be reconstructed exists on the record but is never surfaced.

findings.title: createTicketFor hardcodes the opener's role as 'rider'
findings.detail: createTicket derives the opener role from resolveId (hit&&hit.type==='drivers'?'driver':'rider'), but createTicketFor writes role:'rider' unconditionally, even though openLowRatingTicket passes t.driver as the entity.
findings.impact: A ticket raised on behalf of a captain renders their opening message as a rider bubble, mislabelling who reported the issue in the transcript.

findings.title: DB.slaPolicy.breachEscalateTo is written and never read
findings.detail: The policy object declares breachEscalateTo:'ops_supervisor'. No reader exists anywhere in the file; slaSweep instead appends onCallName('primary') to the breach notification description.
findings.impact: The configured escalation target has no effect — breaches always route to whoever is on call, regardless of the setting.

findings.title: No search box and no pagination on the ticket queue
findings.detail: The Tickets card contains only #tk-filter-wrap (a 9-option status/SLA select), #tk-bulkbar and #ticket-list with max-height:560px and overflow-y:auto. renderTickets renders every matching ticket into that container.
findings.impact: Finding a specific ticket by id, subject or customer name requires scrolling the whole queue; at production volume the list is unusable.

findings.title: Reason-picker placeholder says 38 codes; the taxonomy holds 40
findings.detail: reasonSelectHTML passes the literal search placeholder 'Search 38 reason codes…' while DB.reasonCodes (L14667-L14722) contains 40 entries, all active:true.
findings.impact: Cosmetic; the count in the placeholder is stale relative to the taxonomy it describes.

findings.title: reasonCode.target is defined on all 40 codes and never read
findings.detail: Every entry in DB.reasonCodes carries target:'rider'|'driver'|'corp'. No renderer, filter, router or report reads the field.
findings.impact: The taxonomy encodes who a scenario is about but nothing uses it — driver-side codes are not routed, filtered or presented differently from rider-side ones.

findings.title: Seeded SLA ages are synthetic values chosen to demonstrate all three SLA states
findings.detail: backfillReasonCodes applies var ages=[190,26,1500,55,8] minutes by index modulo to compute openedAtMs, then sets firstResponseAtMs to openedAtMs+12 min when a non-bot agent message exists and resolvedAtMs to openedAtMs+40 min for Resolved/Closed tickets. Complaints are backfilled at a flat 360 minutes.
findings.evidence: var ages=[190,26,1500,55,8]   /* comment: so the seeded queue demonstrates in-SLA, at-risk and breached simultaneously */
findings.impact: Demo artefact — every SLA badge, breach notification and urgency sort on a fresh load reflects these constants rather than real ticket history, and they reset on each reload because SEED_EPOCH is Date.now().

findings.title: SLA tier 'hours' is a label with no business-hours arithmetic behind it
findings.detail: tiers[].hours holds '24/7' or 'business' and is rendered only as a display string by renderSlaPolicyForm. slaState computes elapsed time as raw wall-clock milliseconds with no calendar.
findings.impact: T4's 'business hours' promise is not enforced — a Low ticket opened on a Friday evening burns its 72-hour resolution budget over the weekend exactly as a 24/7 ticket would.

findings.title: Ticket ids are derived from array length
findings.detail: Both createTicket and createTicketFor build newId as 'TKT-'+(505+DB.tickets.length) and then unshift the record.
findings.impact: Removing any ticket makes the next created ticket reuse an existing id, breaking openTicketDetail, ownership keys (ticket:<id>), DB.scriptProgress and every cross-module link.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — showActorHistory was not read
findings.detail: The team-member modal's footer button calls showActorHistory(u.id) with the count DB.auditLog.filter(e=>e.actorId===id).length. The function definition was not read for the source doc, so its behaviour is unconfirmed.
findings.impact: Unknown — the '🕵 Activity (n)' affordance on the support-team modal cannot be characterised from this document.

findings.title: A resolved dispute can never be reopened
findings.detail: The confirmation gate states 'The dispute closes and cannot be reopened from this screen.' In fact nothing anywhere in the file sets a dispute's status back to 'open'.
findings.impact: A dispute resolved in error — including one resolved on inconclusive telemetry — is permanent. The gate's own consequence text ('The rider can escalate — a rejection is not the end of the matter') has no supporting mechanism.

findings.title: DB.arrivalConfig.riderGraceMin is defined and never read
findings.detail: The arrival config declares arrivalRadiusM, meetRadiusM, minDwellMin and riderGraceMin. arrivalEvidence uses the first three; riderGraceMin has no reader anywhere.
findings.evidence: riderGraceMin: 10   /* declared in DB.arrivalConfig L17605-L17610, never read */
findings.impact: The verdict engine has no notion of a rider grace period despite the configuration implying one, so 'the rider was late' is not a case the cascade can express.

findings.title: Dispute work-inbox entries are permanently high severity with no deadline
findings.detail: The inboxItems dispute branch hard-codes severity:'high' and dueMs:null. Disputes carry no SLA clock, no priority and no reason code of their own.
findings.impact: A dispute never sorts by deadline in the work inbox and never shows as breached, while permanently outranking items that do have real deadlines.

findings.title: Doc 13b's line numbers drift by 1–3 lines throughout
findings.detail: Verified against source: the Disputes card markup is L1369–L1372 (doc says L1368–L1371) and the Lost & Found card L1373–L1376 (doc says L1372–L1375); DB.disputes is at L14391 (doc L14390); renderDisputes at L14397 (doc L14396); DB.lostFound at L14448 (doc L14451, index says L14450); LF_FLOW at L14453 (doc L14456); advanceLF at L14468 (doc L14469, though the requirePagePerm line it cites as L14469 is correct). resolveDispute L14431 and renderLostFound L14454 are correct as documented.
findings.impact: Anyone navigating the source from the doc's line index lands a few lines off in the Lost & Found block; the corrected numbers are recorded in this fragment.

findings.title: DSP-07's hand-written evidence contradicts its own seeded telemetry
findings.detail: The seeded 'GPS trail' evidence line states 'Driver device at pickup point 06:54–07:12 (18 min on site)'. The arrived_rider_absent trace seeded for the same dispute has on-site pings at +8 and +22 minutes, which arrivalEvidence renders as a 14-minute dwell. Both appear in the same card.
findings.evidence: evidence:[['GPS trail','Driver device at pickup point 06:54–07:12 (18 min on site)'],…]
findings.impact: Demo artefact, but it undermines the card's own argument: the manual evidence and the automated verdict disagree about a fact the operator is being asked to decide on.

findings.title: Lost & Found records carry no machine-readable timestamp
findings.detail: The only time field is `reported`, a display string ('08:55', 'Yesterday', '22 Jun'). There is no openedAtMs, no advancedAtMs and no numeric clock of any kind on the record.
findings.impact: No age, no SLA, no ordering by recency and no escalation is possible for a lost item — the table cannot show which items have been sitting in 'searching' for days.

findings.title: Neither card has an empty state
findings.detail: renderDisputes joins its mapped array into #dispute-list and renderLostFound joins its rows into a table body. With an empty source array the dispute card renders a blank 480px box and the Lost & Found card renders a bare header row.
findings.impact: Contrasts with the ticket queue on the same page, which has 'No tickets match this filter.' An operator cannot distinguish an empty queue from a rendering failure.

findings.title: Resolved disputes stay in the list forever
findings.detail: renderDisputes maps the entire DB.disputes array in insertion order. There is no filter, no sort, no search and no archive; #dispute-count reports only the open subset while the list shows everything.
findings.impact: The 480px card grows monotonically and resolved items sit interleaved with open ones purely by array position, so the queue becomes progressively harder to work.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — a dispute referencing a missing subscription shows 0.00 SAR with no warning
findings.detail: renderDisputes guards with `sub ? subEconomics(sub).perTrip : 0` and resolveDispute repeats the same guard. A dispute whose sub key is absent from DB.subscriptions would therefore display '0.00 SAR at stake' and an 'Uphold — refund 1 trip (0.00 SAR)' button. Not reproducible with the seeded data, so the behaviour is inferred rather than observed.
findings.impact: A data-integrity problem would present as a legitimate-looking zero-value decision rather than an error, and the operator could resolve the dispute believing nothing was owed.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED — updateInboxBadge was not read
findings.detail: Disputes and lost items surface in the work-inbox badge via refreshInbox(). The definition of updateInboxBadge was not read for the source doc, so the exact contribution of these two queues to the badge count is unconfirmed.
findings.impact: Unknown — the only sidebar-visible signal that a dispute or lost item is waiting cannot be characterised from this document.

findings.title: A mass event with no matching tickets still creates and audits a hollow record
findings.detail: commitMassEvent filters affected tickets by window and reason code; when matched is empty it still unshifts the EVT- record, sets masterTicket to null (L16126), sends zero emails and writes a mass_event_declared audit entry (L16132) with '0 ticket(s) grouped, 0 rider(s) notified'.
findings.impact: The mass-event list accumulates empty incidents that read as real declared events in both the UI and the audit trail.

findings.title: DB.commLogs is not part of this module despite the name
findings.detail: DB.commLogs (seeded at L2749-L2762 with 3 trips and 6 entries) is keyed by trip id, read only by the trip 360° profile at L4246, and written only by the live-chat simulator (L11727) and the support-message sender (L11746). Nothing on p-contacts reads or writes it; it is a per-trip conversation transcript entirely separate from DB.contacts and DB.callSessions.
findings.impact: A collection that looks like the communication log contributes nothing to CPT, queue metrics or the channel mix, so real conversation volume is split across two unlinked stores.

findings.title: Mass-event status is write-only
findings.detail: commitMassEvent hardcodes status:'Open' at L16118. No code path anywhere reads ev.status or changes it, and the mass-event rows in renderContactsExtra render title, reason label, ticket count, master ticket and rider count — never status.
findings.impact: A mass event can never be closed, and the field implies a lifecycle the code does not implement.

findings.title: slaUrgency() is defined but unused on this page
findings.detail: slaUrgency (L14804-L14810) provides a 'breached first, then closest to breach' sort key. The Live SLA exposure list builds its rows as breaching.concat(atRisk), i.e. raw concatenation in DB.tickets order with no urgency sort at all.
findings.evidence: breaching.concat(atRisk) — no call to slaUrgency anywhere in renderContactsPage
findings.impact: The most urgent breach can sit below a less urgent one in the list an operator is meant to work top-down.

findings.title: The wrap-up note is captured and never shown
findings.detail: commitWrapUp stores note on the call session at L20305. The recent-call-sessions list (L20351-L20359) renders only caller, session id, reason label and durations, and exportContacts exports DB.contacts rather than DB.callSessions, so the note appears in no CSV either.
findings.evidence: sess.note captured from #wrap-note, never referenced by any render or export function
findings.impact: The operator's free-text record of what was agreed on a call is unreadable by anyone, including the operator.

findings.title: Three declared SLA/telephony policy fields are never acted on
findings.detail: DB.telephony.wrapUpSec (60, L20174) has no reader — there is no after-call-work timer. DB.slaPolicy.breachEscalateTo ('ops_supervisor', L14658) has no reader; breach notifications use onCallName('primary') instead (L14946). DB.slaPolicy.tiers[*].hours IS read, but only for display in renderSlaPolicyForm at L15136; slaState contains no calendar term at all, so the documented 'T4 follows business hours' assumption is declared, displayed and never enforced.
findings.impact: Three settings appear in configuration and documentation as if they govern behaviour; none does.

findings.title: A second DB.upcomingSubTrips seed can never execute
findings.detail: L6177 assigns a non-empty DB.upcomingSubTrips array. L6243 then reads DB.upcomingSubTrips = DB.upcomingSubTrips || [ ... ], whose right-hand literal defines four different UST-1..UST-4 records with different riders, times and statuses. Because the left operand is already truthy, the literal is never evaluated.
findings.impact: Four inert trip records mislead anyone reading the seed data about what the demo dataset actually contains.

findings.title: No dismiss, snooze, claim, bulk action, filter, sort or export
findings.detail: The page markup (L2068-L2076) contains one button of its own, one badge and one scrolling div. buildInterventionItems (L9450-L9533) emits exactly one action button per row and two navigation links; there is no whole-row handler, no pagination beyond max-height:360px with overflow-y:auto, and no user-changeable sort.
findings.impact: An operator cannot mark an intervention handled from this page; a row disappears only when the underlying record changes state somewhere else.

findings.title: The doc's boot-call line number is off by four
findings.detail: The doc records the boot call to renderInterventionsPage() at L14587 (§2.3 and §15.2). The source has renderInterventionsPage() at L14591, inside the same boot block that calls applyLanguage at L14596.
findings.impact: Cosmetic; corrected line recorded here.

findings.title: The intervention count badge is permanently red
findings.detail: The badge is written into the markup as 0 (L2075). renderInterventionsPage assigns only textContent (L10343) and never touches className, so the alert styling persists in every state including the zero/all-clear state.
findings.impact: A red 0 badge sits directly above a green '✓ All clear' message, training operators to ignore the badge colour.

findings.title: The page has no i18n at all
findings.detail: Verified by reading L2068-L2076: no data-i18n attribute appears anywhere in the page markup, and there is no nav.interventions key in LANG_STRINGS.ar. Every string — header, deprecation prose, card title, row labels, urgency bands, watch separator, empty state — is either hardcoded English markup or a JS string literal in the builder.
findings.evidence:
🚨 Interventions

Merged into the work inbox — one list, deadline-ordered, routed to your role
findings.impact: The page would remain entirely English under applyLanguage('ar'), consistent with the rest of the panel but with no sidebar label to translate either.

findings.title: The row DOM and its waiting timer update at different rates
findings.detail: tickEngine patches every .js-wait text node from DB.rideRequests once per second (L12576-L12579) without re-rendering the row, while the surrounding row markup is rebuilt only when renderDashboard runs — at most once per 60 ticks (L12614).
findings.impact: A row can show a live-ticking wait counter next to a status, tier and action button that are up to a minute stale.

findings.title: The unavailability reason is captured but never surfaced here
findings.detail: tripScenario builds t.unavailReason into sc.banner at L8301 ('<name> is unavailable — <reason>'). The builder discards sc.banner and sc.sub entirely, rendering only the terse scCfg label 'Driver unavailable' plus the urgency span (L9506).
findings.impact: An operator sees 'Driver unavailable' without 'Vehicle breakdown — flat tyre reported', and must open the picker to learn why.

findings.title: archivePlan() opens the confirmation modal before any permission check
findings.detail: requirePerm('manage_plans') sits on doArchivePlan() (L6166), not on archivePlan() (L6156). A user without the permission gets the full 'Archive <name> plan' modal with the danger button and is refused only after confirming. The same asymmetry does not exist for Activate/Deactivate, whose openers are also ungated but whose commits are.
findings.evidence: function archivePlan(){  /* no requirePerm */ … } vs function doArchivePlan(){ if(!requirePerm('manage_plans'))return; …
findings.impact: Cosmetic only — the write is still blocked — but it teaches unauthorised users that the action exists and produces a permission_denied audit entry after the fact rather than preventing the attempt.

findings.title: New surge-window multipliers are not clamped in JS
findings.detail: surge-cap is defensively clamped on save with Math.min(5, Math.max(1, parseFloat(val)||2.5)) (L12336). new-surge-mult carries HTML min=1 max=5 step=0.1 but addSurgeWindow() applies only parseFloat and an isNaN check, and saveSurgeSchedule() commits in-table edits with parseFloat(v)||1. Only currentSurgeMultiplier()'s Math.min(mult, capMultiplier) limits the effect at read time.
findings.evidence: capMultiplier: Math.min(5,Math.max(1,parseFloat(capEl.value)||2.5))  vs  multiplier from new-surge-mult with no clamp
findings.impact: An out-of-range multiplier can be written into DB.surgeSchedule and shown in the table as if valid; the cap is the only thing preventing it from being charged.

findings.title: No permission gate on entry to the pricing page
findings.detail: Neither the sidebar item (L538) nor the plans router branch (L8807) calls can() or requirePerm(). Every role can open the page and read commission rates, discounts, per-km/per-min rates, active subscription counts and the full surge schedule. Gating is entirely per-action.
findings.impact: Commercially sensitive margin data (Eyvar take rate per cadence, driver share) is readable by any authenticated role, including ones that cannot change it.

findings.title: renderRideTypesTable() is absent from the boot render block
