findings.detail: The boot block calls renderPlansFormSelects() (L14568), renderPlansTable() (L14569), renderQuickRidesTable() (L14570) and renderSurgeSchedule() (L14573) — but not renderRideTypesTable(). #ridetypes-tbody is populated only by the plans router branch (L8807). Note that renderQuickRidesTable is a different function belonging to the separate quickrides page.
findings.impact: Harmless in practice because the table is invisible until the user navigates to the page, which triggers the render — but the surge table beside it is booted and the ride-type table is not, which is an inconsistency waiting to bite if either is ever read at boot.

findings.title: Several doc line references drift from the source file
findings.detail: Corrected against source: approveRateCard() is defined at L21582, not L21603 as §16 states (L21603 is the guardAction wrapper that follows it). fareFor() is at L21467, not L21466. In renderRideTypesTable() the example-cell computation is at L12346 (doc says L12345) and the conditional Remove button at L12353 (doc says L12350). PRICING_EXAMPLES begins at L21616, not L21617. All other spot-checked references (page divs L1030/L1082, DB.plans L2889, DB.quickRideTypes L13908, DB.surgeSchedule L13883, DB.rateCardHistory L21463, cr() L12986, upd() L12987, REQ_NOW_REF L9555) matched exactly.
findings.impact: Documentation-only. Anyone following the doc's line numbers to audit the ungated approveRateCard would land on the guardAction wrapper and could conclude the gate is present.

findings.title: The surge live badge can drift from the simulated clock
findings.detail: #surge-live-badge is written only inside renderSurgeSchedule(), which runs on navigation, at boot and after each surge mutation. currentSurgeMultiplier() reads REQ_NOW_REF, a simulated clock seeded to Thu 25 Jun 2026 09:14 and advanced by the request tick loop (L9680). No tick handler re-renders the surge table, so a page left open shows a stale multiplier. Marked unverified: the drift depends on tick timing and is not directly observable from source alone.
findings.impact: An operator watching the badge to decide whether to change surge can be reading a multiplier from a simulated time that has since moved past a window boundary.

findings.title: The toolbar sub-line is hardcoded to '3 plan templates' and never recomputed
findings.detail: subs.plans = '3 plan templates' is written into #tb-sub by go() on every navigation to the page and nothing ever recalculates it. The in-page #plans-page-sub is recomputed correctly, so the two disagree as soon as a plan is added or removed. The static markup for #plans-page-sub also ships as '3 plan templates · 2 active · 1 draft'.
findings.impact: After creating a fourth plan the toolbar still says three. Low impact, but it is a visible wrong number on a pricing page.

findings.title: Two writers set the plans page sub-line with different wording
findings.detail: renderPlansTable() writes '<n> plan templates · <n> active · <n> draft' into #plans-page-sub (L5945). liveSubtitles() independently writes '<n> plan templates · <n> active · <n> not live' into the same element via the '#p-plans .ph-l p' selector (L21253), and it counts active with /active/i.test(status) rather than an exact match. Whichever ran last wins.
findings.evidence: set('#p-plans .ph-l p', plans+' plan templates · '+activePlans+' active · '+(plans-activePlans)+' not live');
findings.impact: The same count is described two ways depending on render order, and the two active-counting rules could diverge if a status containing 'active' as a substring were ever introduced.

findings.title: Feature-list drag reorder may be unreachable past the scroll boundary
findings.detail: #pf-list is a max-height:300px, overflow-y:auto scroller. pfDragStart/pfDrop implement no auto-scroll while dragging, relying entirely on native browser drag scrolling. Marked unverified: the behaviour depends on the browser and cannot be confirmed from source.
findings.impact: With more than about eight feature points, moving a bullet from the bottom to the top of the list may not be possible via the drag handle, and there is no alternative reorder control.

findings.title: No permission gate on entry to the plan editor
findings.detail: openPlanEdit() sets currentPlanKey and navigates with no requirePerm(), and the plan-edit router branch performs no check either. Any role can open the editor, read every rate and commission figure and type into the whole form; refusal comes only at savePlan() (L6118), doArchivePlan() (L6166) and toggleVehicleActive() (L6110).
findings.impact: Margin data is readable by any authenticated role, and an unauthorised user can invest a full editing session before being told they cannot save.

findings.title: renderPlanFeatures() runs twice on every page entry
findings.detail: The plan-edit router branch calls loadPlanEditForm() then renderPlanFeatures(); loadPlanEditForm() already calls renderPlanFeatures() itself at L6095 after refilling the buffer. The second call rebuilds a list that was just built.
findings.impact: Harmless duplicate work; it also discards any focus the first render set on a newly added row.

findings.title: The documented plan_features backing table has no consumer in this file
findings.detail: Section 2's helper copy and the code comment above PLAN_FEATURES both describe a plan_features table with (plan_id, sort_order, text_en, text_ar). In this single-file demo there is no persistence layer and nothing exports or serialises DB.plans; sort_order in particular has no counterpart on the feature object, which carries only {en, ar}. Marked unverified: a real backend contract cannot be confirmed from this file.
findings.impact: The declared data contract (four columns including sort_order and a plan_id FK) does not match what the app actually stores (an ordered array of two-key objects), so a backend built to the documented shape would need a translation layer.

findings.title: The editor ships with the weekly plan baked into markup, including a fictional plan_id
findings.detail: The static form carries Weekly plan / الباقة الأسبوعية / 7 / 5 / 1 / 20 / 0 / 80.0% / 1 / 0.95 / 1.10 / 1.35 / 1.60 with both Active boxes checked. #plan-edit-sub and subs['plan-edit'] both read 'Weekly plan · plan_id: 1' — real plan ids are string keys (weekly, biweekly, monthly, new1…), never 1. #fp3-name-en reads 'Weekly plan' while DB.plans.weekly.name is 'Weekly'. This is what is on screen at boot and whenever currentPlanKey is null.
findings.impact: Reaching the page with no plan selected shows a fully populated, entirely fictitious plan that looks editable; loadPlanEditForm() returns early at L6067 and leaves the placeholder in place.

findings.title: The empty-feature-list copy asks for something validation does not require
findings.detail: The #pf-list empty state reads 'No feature points yet — add at least one so the rider's plan card isn't empty.' validatePlanFeatures() iterates the array and returns null for an empty one, so the save proceeds. Only non-blank text in both languages on existing rows is enforced.
findings.evidence: renderPlanFeatures() empty branch: "No feature points yet — add at least one so the rider's plan card isn't empty."
findings.impact: A plan can go live with an empty rider-facing feature card despite the UI stating otherwise.

findings.title: The on-page formula box is hand-written and can drift from cr()
findings.detail: The .formula-box renders four lines of pricing formula as literal HTML with a note reading 'Example uses 10 km / 20 min.' The actual calculator is cr(), which hardcodes (20*pm)+(10*pk). Nothing generates the box from the function or asserts they agree, and the same 10km/20min figures are repeated in the column header (L1119) and the preview labels (L1086).
findings.impact: If the example trip or the formula changes, four separate pieces of markup must be hand-edited or the page will document a calculation it is not performing.

findings.title: The toolbar sub-line goes stale after a plan rename
findings.detail: loadPlanEditForm() writes the plan name into #plan-edit-sub and #tb-sub on entry (L6084–L6085). savePlan() refreshes #plan-edit-name-display and #plan-edit-sub after a rename but not #tb-sub, which keeps the pre-save name until the page is re-entered.
findings.impact: Cosmetic — two headings on the same screen show different plan names after a rename.

findings.title: #meta-reasons is written by nothing
findings.detail: A grep for id="meta-*" returns 12 elements; 11 are in renderSettingsMeta's map and the twelfth, #meta-reasons at L1796 in the Reason Codes & SLA pane, is not. A grep for the literal 'meta-reasons' across the whole file returns exactly one hit, the id declaration itself. It renders permanently empty. This is the mirror image of the renderOnCall/#oncall-body orphan: there a renderer exists with no element, here an element exists with no renderer.
findings.impact: The widest Settings pane silently lacks the 'Last updated by' line every comparable pane shows.

findings.title: An unknown tab key hides every panel
findings.detail: switchSettingsTab first clears .on from all 21 panels (L7315), then looks up #stab-<key> (L7316) behind an if(panel) guard (L7317). A key with no matching panel therefore leaves nothing visible - no toast, no fallback to General, just an empty right-hand column. No caller currently passes a bad key.
findings.impact: A typo in a future deep link would blank the Settings page with no diagnostic.

findings.title: Documented page-div range is two lines long
findings.detail: 16i and 16j cite the Settings page as #p-settings L1416-2050. In the source the export pane closes at L2044 and the three remaining closing divs are at L2046 (content column), L2047 (.settings-shell) and L2048 (#p-settings). The correct range is L1416-2048; L2049 is blank and L2050 is the Activity-log page's comment banner.
findings.impact: Documentation-only; corrected in this fragment's html_lines.

findings.title: Group headers are removed twice in reorderSettingsTabs
findings.detail: L21288 removes the three static group headers before building, and L21311 removes '.settings-tab-group-lbl' again just before nav.appendChild(frag). By L21311 the only labels in nav are the originals already removed; the six new ones are still inside the detached DocumentFragment and are unaffected. The second removal is a no-op in every reachable state.
findings.impact: Harmless, but a future reader cannot tell which of the two removals is load-bearing.

findings.title: The reorder design comment says twenty tabs
findings.detail: The block comment that records the rationale for the 6-group reorder says 'Twenty tabs had accumulated in the order they were built'. The file has 21 tab buttons (L1421-1443) and 21 keys across SETTINGS_GROUPS. The comment is one out of date with its own array.
findings.evidence: SETTINGS - REORDERED BY HOW OFTEN AND HOW URGENTLY THEY ARE OPENED. Twenty tabs had accumulated in the order they were built
findings.impact: Cosmetic; the comment is the design record for the grouping and now miscounts it.

findings.title: Three hand-maintained lists of settings keys
findings.detail: The data-tab attributes (L1421-1443), SETTINGS_GROUPS.tabs (L21271-21276) and renderSettingsMeta's map (L7340) are three parallel lists of settings keys that must be updated together, with nothing checking them against each other. The orphaned #meta-reasons element (L1796) is what a drift between list 1 and list 3 looks like.
findings.impact: Adding a tab requires three coordinated edits plus one to the L8819 router branch; a missed edit fails silently.

findings.title: Doc line numbers off by one for the tab button and applySiteBranding
findings.detail: The doc header cites the General tab button at L1422 and applySiteBranding at L7955-L7961. Source: the button is L1421 (L1422 is the Team & Roles button) and the applySiteBranding function declaration is L7954 (its body runs L7955-L7961). The same off-by-one affects the Team (doc L1423 / real L1422) and Permissions (doc L1424 / real L1423) tab buttons.
findings.impact: Navigating by the doc's line index lands one line off across all three Settings tab buttons.

findings.title: Empty favicon href on logo removal
findings.detail: applySiteBranding assigns f.href = g.logoDataUrl || '', so removing the logo sets rel=icon href to the empty string rather than restoring a default.
findings.impact: Browser-dependent tab icon after removal; some browsers resolve an empty href to the document URL and request the page itself as an icon.

findings.title: Language select is inert until Save
findings.detail: applyLanguage is called from exactly two sites: saveGeneralConfig (L7996) and boot (L14596). Changing the select without pressing Save does nothing, and there is no live preview.
findings.impact: An operator without manage_settings cannot switch the interface to Arabic at all, since the only trigger sits behind the permission gate.

findings.title: Support email accepts any string
findings.detail: cfg-gen-email is a plain text input with only the falsy-guard; the panel does validate email elsewhere (commitInvite L10536, commitEditTeamUser L10488 both require indexOf('@')>=0).
findings.impact: A mistyped support address is saved and audited as valid; inconsistent with the team-invite flow.

findings.title: Two separate logo settings in Settings
findings.detail: #stab-branding (L1706) with renderBrandingSettings() L18401 / saveBranding() L18445 covers the mark shown at the top of the sidebar, while this pane's general.logoDataUrl is the browser favicon. The doc marks the relationship between them UNVERIFIED from this pane.
findings.impact: Operators face two unrelated 'logo' settings with no cross-reference; uploading one does not update the other.

findings.title: Doc cites the Team tab button one line low
findings.detail: The doc header says the Team & Roles tab button is at L1423 with switchSettingsTab('team',this). Source has it at L1422; L1423 is the Permissions button.
findings.impact: Cosmetic doc drift; the pane range L1519-L1531 in the doc is correct.

findings.title: No 'last updated by' footer on the Team pane
findings.detail: renderSettingsMeta maps meta-<id> elements to settings entity ids; there is no meta-team entry and the pane markup has no .settings-meta div, unlike General, Cities, Gateways, Limits, Security and Notifications.
findings.impact: Team and permission changes are audit-logged but invisible from the pane itself; an operator must open the Activity tab to see who last changed the roster.

findings.title: openUserSwitchGuardless is an empty function
findings.detail: Declared with an empty body immediately after commitUserSwitch. grep finds no caller anywhere in the file.
findings.impact: None at runtime; a leftover that implies a guard-bypass path that no longer exists.

findings.title: PERMISSION_DESC.manage_team is overwritten at load time
findings.detail: L3256 declares 'Invite team members, change their role, and edit the role permission matrix itself.' L10516 - a bare statement sitting between a comment block and defaultPermissionsForRole - reassigns it to 'Add or edit team members, change roles, and grant or revoke any permission - including this one.'
findings.evidence: PERMISSION_DESC.manage_team='Add or edit team members, change roles, and grant or revoke any permission - including this one.';
findings.impact: The description shown in the UI never matches the one in the constant declaration, making the constant misleading to read.

findings.title: phone and photo are dead fields in this pane
findings.detail: Both are seeded on all five users (photo is null on all five). renderTeamTable renders neither, and neither the invite nor the edit modal exposes them. avatarHTML() at L10836 takes a hasPhoto flag but is not used by this table.
findings.impact: Contact data exists on the record but is unreachable from the roster; commitInvite does not even create the fields, so the shape of seeded and invited users differs.

findings.title: Roster has no empty state, sort, filter, search or pagination
findings.detail: renderTeamTable is a straight DB.teamUsers.map(...).join('') into the tbody, in array order.
findings.impact: Fine at 5 users; unusable as a roster grows, and an empty roster renders headers with no message.

findings.title: Accordion state is transient and there is no expand-all
findings.detail: var _pagePermExpanded={} is a module global mutated only by togglePagePermExpand. It survives re-renders within a session but resets on reload, and no control expands or collapses all 22 pages at once.
findings.impact: Reviewing the full 52-action grant state requires 22 individual clicks and cannot be captured in one view.

findings.title: Design comment says 12 permissions; there are 13
findings.detail: The GRANULAR PAGE PERMISSIONS comment block opens by referring to 'The original 12 permissions (PERMISSION_LABELS above)'. PERMISSION_LABELS declares 13 keys at L3226-L3238.
findings.evidence: The original 12 permissions (PERMISSION_LABELS above) are broad, whole-feature switches
findings.impact: Cosmetic; misleads a reader auditing coverage of the permission set.

findings.title: Doc cites the Permissions tab button one line low
findings.detail: The doc header says the Permissions tab button is at L1424. Source has it at L1423; L1424 is the next tab button in the list.
findings.impact: Cosmetic doc drift; the pane range L1534-L1549 in the doc is correct.

findings.title: Alerts fire off simulated ratings and 'sent' email is only a local row
findings.detail: The driver rating that triggers the rule comes from simulateRatingGiven() (L12034) inside the simulation loop. sendSystemEmail (L3578) only builds an entry and unshifts it into DB.emailOutbox, then re-renders the Email Log; nothing is transmitted. pushOpsNotification (L9661) unshifts into DB.notifications and updates the bell badge.
findings.impact: Demo-only behaviour: the alerting pipeline is entirely in-memory, so nothing reaches a real inbox or phone.

findings.title: Audit 'after' payload is a live object reference
findings.detail: saveNotificationConfig passes `n` - which IS DB.opsConfig.notifications - as the audit `after` argument rather than a copy. Any later mutation of that object changes what the historical audit entry appears to record. The same pattern appears in saveGeneralConfig (L7997) and saveSecurityConfig (L8029).
findings.impact: The audit trail for settings changes is not a stable historical record; every entry shows the current values.

findings.title: Doc line numbers for the tab button drift by two
findings.detail: The doc places the Alert Preferences tab button at L1439 and the 'System' nav group at L1437; the source has them at L1437 and L1436. Pane range (L1907-L1926), seed (L2571) and all function line numbers in the doc check out.
findings.impact: Navigation-only drift; no behavioural consequence.

findings.title: Inconsistent null handling for the threshold
findings.detail: renderNotificationConfig correctly uses `n.lowRatingThreshold != null ? ... : 2.5` (L8006) while lowRatingThreshold() uses `(n&&n.lowRatingThreshold)||2.5` (L15245). A stored 0 would render as 0 in the input but evaluate as 2.5 everywhere else. Unreachable today because saveNotificationConfig clamps to a minimum of 1.
findings.impact: Latent divergence between the displayed setting and the applied setting if the clamp is ever relaxed or the value is seeded externally.

findings.title: No throttling, dedupe or digest
findings.detail: Every trip completion whose driver rating meets the threshold immediately fires a notification and an email. There is no rate limit, no per-driver dedupe window and no hourly-summary option; the Planned card lists digest scheduling as not yet built.
findings.impact: A driver having a bad day generates one bell entry and one email per trip, and the ops bell can be flooded.

findings.title: Pane content is not internationalised
findings.detail: Only the tab button carries data-i18n (stab.notifications, L1437). Inside #stab-notifications no element has a data-i18n attribute - panel title, description, all four field labels, both status badges, the threshold note, the Save button and the whole Planned card stay English under applyLanguage('ar').
findings.impact: Arabic operators see an English-only pane, unlike the Security and General tabs.

findings.title: The configured 'alert' email is addressed to the driver
findings.detail: The pane is described as covering 'what the ops team itself gets alerted about internally' (L1911), but the email branch calls sendSystemEmail(t.driver, ...) - a check-in message to the rated driver, categorised 'transactional'. Ops receives only the in-app notification.
findings.evidence: sendSystemEmail(t.driver,'A recent trip rating needs your attention', ... ,'transactional');
findings.impact: Turning 'Email alerts' off actually stops an outbound driver-facing email, which is a customer-communication decision, not an internal-alerting one.

findings.title: Audit 'after' payload is a live object reference
findings.detail: logAction(..., before, s) passes the live DB.opsConfig.security object as `after`, so a later save mutates what earlier audit entries appear to say. Identical pattern in saveNotificationConfig (L8014) and saveGeneralConfig (L7997).
findings.impact: Security-setting history is not reconstructable from the audit log - every entry reflects current state.

findings.title: Clamped timeout is not written back to the input
findings.detail: saveSecurityConfig clamps to [5,240] but never assigns the clamped value back to #cfg-sec-timeout, so the field keeps showing whatever was typed until renderSecurityConfig runs again (next entry to the Settings page). saveOpsRadiusConfig (L8081) does write its clamped values back, so the two panes behave differently.
findings.impact: The operator believes 1000 minutes was saved when 240 was stored; no toast or field correction signals the clamp.

findings.title: Confirm-gate copy warns about the wrong consequence
findings.detail: GATE_SWEEP.saveSecurityConfig (L20780, d:true) lists 'Sessions already open are not terminated by this change' - a consequence of a setting that does nothing - and omits the one real consequence, that flipping require2FA immediately changes the Team & Roles table for every operator.
findings.evidence: c:['Weakening these affects every account in the panel, not just yours.','Sessions already open are not terminated by this change.'],btn:'Save security'
findings.impact: The confirmation step describes a non-effect and hides the actual visible effect.

findings.title: Doc line numbers drift for the tab button and Arabic strings
findings.detail: Doc places the Security tab button at L1442 (actual L1440), stabgrp.system at L1437 (actual L1436), sec.timeout_label Arabic at L7931 (actual L7932) and sec.planned_desc at L7934 (actual L7936). Pane range (L1976-L1994), seed (L2572) and all function line numbers verify correctly.
findings.impact: Reference-only drift.

findings.title: No authentication exists for either setting to act on
findings.detail: CURRENT_USER_ID is a hardcoded global ('USR-1', L2862) reassigned only by the demo user-switch paths (L3106, L21071). There is no login screen, credential store, token or session; the password fields in the My Account modal accept any non-empty 'current password' (changeMaPassword, L3036).
findings.impact: Both settings are configuration storage awaiting a backend; nothing in this file can enforce them.

findings.title: No SSO, IP allow-list, password policy, lockout or API keys
findings.detail: The pane contains exactly two controls. The Planned card names SSO/SAML login, IP allow-listing and per-role forced session timeout overrides as future work; there is additionally no password policy, no failed-login lockout, no API-key management and no session list here.
findings.evidence: SSO/SAML login, IP allow-listing for the ops panel, and per-role forced session timeout overrides.
findings.impact: The security surface of the ops panel is effectively unconfigurable.

findings.title: renderSecurityConfig uses || instead of != null
findings.detail: `if(t)t.value=s.sessionTimeoutMin||30;` means a stored 0 renders as 30. Unreachable given the min-5 clamp, but inconsistent with renderNotificationConfig (L8006), which handles the same case with != null.
findings.impact: Latent display/storage divergence if the value is ever set outside the clamped save path.

findings.title: step=5 is a browser hint only
findings.detail: The JS validation is parseInt plus a clamp; nothing enforces a multiple of 5. Typing 37 (or pasting it) saves 37.
findings.impact: Cosmetic - the stored value can be a non-multiple that the stepper UI would never produce.

findings.title: All matching runs on synthetic coordinates in a simulation loop
findings.detail: Driver and rider mapPos values are points on a 0-100 demo grid (e.g. DRV-0101 {x:60,y:55}, L2632); geoDistanceKm, estimateEtaMin and driverLiveState (L7256, L7273, L7283) operate on them, and nextOfferCandidate is driven by tickEngine (L12508), a per-second simulation.
findings.impact: Radius and ETA settings are tuned against demo geometry; real-world behaviour is unvalidated.

findings.title: Assorted doc line-number drift
findings.detail: Verified corrections: the Matching & Dispatch tab button is at L1425 (doc L1426) and the Operations group label at L1424 (doc L1425); the planVisibility seed is at L2574 (doc L2575); renderPlanVisibility starts at L8122 (doc L8121-L8126); DRV-0101's multiSubException and mapPos are on L2632 (doc L2650). The pane range (L1552-L1619), DB.searchPhases seed (L13925-L13929) and all other quoted function lines verify correctly.
findings.impact: Reference-only drift.

findings.title: Multi-sub toggle can desync on the modal path
findings.detail: onMultiSubToggle pre-reverts the checkbox to checked before opening the confirm modal, so Cancel leaves it visually on - correct only because the flag really is still on. No re-render from DB occurs on either the Cancel or the permission-denied path (which flips checkbox.checked rather than reading the flag).
findings.evidence: checkbox.checked=true; /* revert visually until confirmed, matching the "shows confirmation" step in the flow */
findings.impact: Minor - the toggle's displayed state is derived from DOM manipulation rather than from DB.opsConfig.allowMultiSubPerDriver.

findings.title: No give-up rule for a searching request
findings.detail: The phase ladder widens the radius indefinitely (last match wins), but nothing on this pane configures a maximum search duration, a cancel-after-N-seconds rule or an escalation to manual sourcing. The nearest equivalent (dispatchWindowSec / dispatchMaxCandidates) lives on the Reason Codes pane and is unseeded.
findings.impact: A request with no available driver keeps searching for as long as tickEngine runs, with no configured terminal state.

findings.title: No per-city or per-zone radius
findings.detail: nearestAvailableDrivers reads a single cfg.quickRideRadiusKm and a single cfg.subRadiusKm regardless of the rider's city; the only city-level control is the on/off active flag consulted by isCityActive.
findings.impact: A dense city and a sparse one must share the same search radius.

findings.title: Pane content is not internationalised
findings.detail: Only the tab button carries data-i18n (stab.dispatch, L1425). Inside #stab-dispatch (L1552-L1619) no element has a data-i18n attribute.
findings.impact: Arabic operators configure live dispatch through an English-only pane.

findings.title: Plan-visibility radios are only synced on page entry
findings.detail: renderPlanVisibility() (L8122) is called solely from the go('settings') render batch (L8819); savePlanVisibility() does not call it. The radios happen to match DB after a save only because the operator's own click set them.
findings.impact: If the flag were changed by any other path while the pane was open, the radios would show stale state until the page was re-entered.

findings.title: addCity confirm promises features that do not exist
findings.detail: GATE_SWEEP.addCity lists 'Operators must be scoped to it before they can see its data' and 'Pricing and policy for the city start from defaults' as consequences. There is no per-city operator scoping and no per-city pricing anywhere in the file — the city record has only name, active, launched, seed, custom and optional lat/lng.
findings.evidence: addCity:{t:'Add a city',s:'A new operating city becomes available for assignment.',
findings.impact: The confirmation dialog describes governance controls the operator does not actually have.

findings.title: Cities table has no empty state
findings.detail: renderCitiesTable builds rows with a bare .map().join(''), so an empty DB.cities produces a header with a blank body and no explanation. Contrast renderOpsLimitsTable, which supplies a colspan empty-state row.
findings.impact: Cosmetic; an emptied city list looks like a rendering failure.

findings.title: config_updated has no ACTION_LABELS entry
findings.detail: All cities mutations log the action key 'config_updated', which is absent from ACTION_LABELS. The Activity-log action-type filter is built from Object.keys(ACTION_LABELS), so these entries fall back to the raw key and cannot be selected in the filter.
findings.impact: Configuration changes are hard to find in the audit log.

findings.title: Doc line numbers for the cities pane are off by one to two
findings.detail: Verified against source: #cities-tbody is L1630 (doc L1629), #new-city-name L1635 (doc L1634), #city-suggestions L1636 (doc L1635), #city-map-preview L1639 (doc L1637), #add-city-btn L1641 (doc L1639), #meta-cities L1645 (doc L1644), and the pane div closes at L1647 (doc says the pane is L1622–1646). Function starts also drift: cityStats is L7445 (doc 7448), openCityDeactivateConfirm L7794 (doc 7792), applyCityToggle L7804 (doc 7803), KNOWN_CITIES L7819 (doc 7822).
findings.impact: Documentation-only; line citations must be corrected before being used for navigation.

findings.title: hasActivity is stale-baked into the inline handler
findings.detail: renderCitiesTable evaluates hasActivity = st.drivers>0 || st.riders>0 at render time and interpolates the boolean literal into the toggle's onchange string. If drivers or riders change without a table re-render, the deactivation confirm gate uses the stale value.
findings.impact: The high-impact deactivation confirmation can be skipped (or fired unnecessarily) after data changes.

findings.title: Map preview depends on an external OSM tile CDN
findings.detail: showCityMapPreview loads Leaflet tiles from https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/. It guards on typeof L==='undefined' so a missing Leaflet degrades gracefully, but whether the tile fetch itself succeeds in the deployment environment cannot be determined by reading the file.
findings.impact: An offline or network-restricted deployment silently loses the map preview; the selection flow still works.

findings.title: No edit path for any city field
findings.detail: The only editable per-row control is the Active toggle. There is no way to rename a city, correct its coordinates, or fix a wrong `launched` value from the UI, and seeded cities cannot even be removed.
findings.impact: A data error in a city record is permanent for the session.

findings.title: Toast and modal overstate what deactivation does
findings.detail: applyCityToggle's toast says sign-ups and ride requests are now accepted/blocked, and the deactivation modal says turning off 'immediately blocks new sign-ups'. No sign-up code path reads DB.cities — the only consumer of the active flag is isCityActive() inside nearestAvailableDrivers(). The panel description at the top of the pane states the accurate version.
findings.evidence: toast((c.active?'✅ '+name+' is now live':'⚠ '+name+' turned off')+' — sign-ups and ride requests there '+(c.active?'are now accepted':'are now blocked'),...)
findings.impact: An operator may believe deactivation stops registrations in that city when it only stops matching.

findings.title: config_updated has no ACTION_LABELS entry
findings.detail: All four gateway mutators log the key 'config_updated', which is not in ACTION_LABELS, so gateway audit entries cannot be filtered by action type on the Activity-log page.
findings.impact: Gateway configuration changes are hard to locate in the audit log.

findings.title: Disable toast uses success severity
findings.detail: toggleGatewayEnabled builds one toast for both directions and passes severity 'ok' regardless, so turning a gateway off renders in the success style despite the warning glyph in the text.
findings.evidence: toast(... '⚠ '+gw.name+' disabled — riders can no longer pay with it', 'ok')
findings.impact: Cosmetic; a negative state change reads as a positive confirmation.

findings.title: Gateways table has no empty state
findings.detail: renderPaymentGateways uses a bare .map().join(''), so an empty DB.paymentGateways renders a header with a blank body.
findings.impact: Cosmetic.

findings.title: Inconsistent risk weighting across the tab's actions
findings.detail: toggleGatewayEnabled and removeGateway are ungated and unconfirmed, while addCustomGateway (which creates an inert, disabled row) is registered danger:true in GATE_SWEEP.
findings.impact: Confirmation friction sits on the harmless action and not on the destructive one.

findings.title: No credentials, fees, currency or country fields exist
findings.detail: The gateway record has only id, name, type, matchPrefix, enabled, isDefault and custom. There is no API key, secret, merchant id, webhook URL, environment flag, MDR/fee, currency or country restriction anywhere in the file, and no fetch/XHR/SDK targeting any PSP. Whether a server outside this file is meant to consume DB.paymentGateways cannot be determined from the source.
findings.impact: Gateway choice cannot affect pricing or routing even in principle; the tab is a registry plus a live report.

findings.title: Type select is not cleared after adding
findings.detail: addCustomGateway clears only #new-gateway-name; #new-gateway-type retains the previous selection, so consecutive adds inherit the last type.
findings.evidence: addCustomGateway() clears the name input only (L7503); the type select keeps its value
findings.impact: Minor data-entry error mode; the type has no behavioural effect anyway.

findings.title: Add is immediate but the toast asks for a Save
findings.detail: addCustomLimit pushes the new row into DB.opsLimits directly and logs it, so the record already exists; the toast nevertheless says 'remember to click "Save all limits"'. For that row the subsequent Save is a no-op unless its value was edited afterwards.
findings.evidence: toast('✅ Custom limit added — remember to click "Save all limits"','ok')
findings.impact: Confusing mental model about when a limit is persisted.

findings.title: Applies-to select is not reset after adding
findings.detail: addCustomLimit clears #new-limit-label, #new-limit-value and #new-limit-unit but leaves #new-limit-target on its previous selection.
findings.impact: Consecutive adds can land in the wrong table.

findings.title: config_updated has no ACTION_LABELS entry
findings.detail: All three limits mutators log 'config_updated', which is not in ACTION_LABELS, so limits audit rows have no friendly label and cannot be selected in the Activity-log action-type filter.
findings.impact: Limit changes are hard to find in the audit log.

findings.title: removeCustomLimit has no confirmation
findings.detail: removeCustomLimit checks manage_settings, filters the row out and logs the whole removed object as `before`, but there is no confirm dialog — while addCustomLimit is confirm-gated.
findings.impact: One misclick removes a limit; the audit `before` snapshot is the only recovery path and it is manual.

findings.title: rider_request_cooldown is never enforced and ships disabled
findings.detail: Seeded value:30 seconds, enabled:false, enforced:false — the only limit in the array shipped switched off. Grep returns only the seed line.
findings.impact: No rate limiting between ride requests exists; enabling the row changes nothing.

findings.title: The promised future enforcement hook does not exist in this file
findings.detail: The DB.opsLimits contract comment says enforced:false rows are 'tracked/configurable now and ready for a future hook'. Grep confirms the five such keys appear only on their seed lines; whether a hook exists in a system outside this file cannot be determined from the source.
findings.impact: Five of eight built-in limits — the entire rider section — are configurable surfaces with no behaviour behind them.

findings.title: Client-side grace enforcement cannot be confirmed
findings.detail: The panel presents the grace period as a rider-facing free window. Nothing in this file enforces it; whether a rider-side app applies it client-side is outside the source and cannot be verified here.
findings.evidence: graceMin:2 with note 'Free for this many minutes after acceptance, to allow genuine mistakes.'
findings.impact: If no other system enforces it either, the documented free window does not exist in practice.

findings.title: config_updated has no ACTION_LABELS entry
findings.detail: saveCancellationPolicy logs the key 'config_updated', which is absent from ACTION_LABELS, so cancellation-policy audit rows cannot be filtered by action type on the Activity-log page.
findings.impact: Money-affecting policy edits are hard to isolate in the audit log.

findings.title: No empty states, and one Save button for two cards
findings.detail: Both tables use bare .map().join('') with no empty state. The single 'Save cancellation policy' button sits at the bottom of the Quick rides card but its selector covers both tbodies, so the Subscriptions card has no Save affordance of its own. The grace-period input also renders inside the Scenario cell rather than under the Fee column.
findings.impact: Discoverability risk — subscription edits can be made and left unsaved because no Save button is visible in that card.

findings.title: qr_before_assigned and qr_driver_fault are documentation, not code
findings.detail: cancelRequest() (the pre-assignment cancellation path) contains no fee logic at all, and driverDeclineOrTimeout() charges nobody. Grep returns only the two seed lines. The intended zero-fee behaviour is achieved by the absence of code rather than by code that enforces zero.
findings.impact: Correct outcome today, but nothing would stop a future fee path from bypassing these rules.

findings.title: Save toast overpromises
findings.detail: The toast claims the saved policy 'applies to the next cancellation immediately'. That is true for qr_after_grace, qr_rider_noshow and sub_mid_cycle, and false for graceMin and qr_after_arrival, which are never consulted.
findings.evidence: toast('✅ Cancellation policy saved — applies to the next cancellation immediately','ok');
findings.impact: The operator is told edits took effect when two of the editable fields did nothing.

findings.title: sub_before_first_trip is decorative
findings.detail: The zero-fee outcome for a subscription with no trips used comes from the hardcoded used>0 term in cancelSub's feeApplies expression, not from this locked rule. Grep for sub_before_first_trip returns only the seed line.
findings.evidence: {id:'sub_before_first_trip',appliesTo:'subscription',scenario:'Cancelled before any trip in the plan has been taken',feePct:0,enabled:false,locked:true,...}
findings.impact: The matrix documents intent that is implemented by an unrelated hardcoded condition; the two could drift apart without any signal.

findings.title: The scenario matrix is closed at eight rows
findings.detail: There is no composer, no add button, no delete path and no code that pushes into DB.cancellationPolicy. A new cancellation window would require a code change — the opposite of the self-describing extensible pattern used by DB.opsLimits on the neighbouring tab.
findings.evidence: DB.cancellationPolicy=[ ... ]; // 8 fixed rules, no push anywhere in the file
findings.impact: Policy changes that need a new scenario cannot be made by operators.

findings.title: The subscription fee has no ledger entry
findings.detail: confirmCancelSub credits only the net refund to the wallet; the mid-cycle fee is recorded only in the audit summary and the toast. It is a withholding rather than a charge, so it never posts to the double-entry ledger.
findings.impact: Cancellation fee revenue cannot be reconciled from the ledger.

findings.title: Unparseable fee input silently becomes zero
findings.detail: saveCancellationPolicy writes parseFloat(feeInput.value)||0 for both feeAmount and feePct, and parseInt(graceInput.value,10)||0 for graceMin, so any invalid entry disables the fee rather than being rejected.
findings.impact: A typo silently turns a fee off, and the save toast still reports success.

findings.title: breachEscalateTo has no reader
findings.detail: DB.slaPolicy.breachEscalateTo:'ops_supervisor' is defined at L14658 and a grep finds no other occurrence. SLA breach escalation instead embeds onCallName('primary') in the notification text at L14945. There is no UI for the field either.
findings.impact: A configuration value that reads as the escalation target does nothing.

findings.title: confirmDeadline is unvalidated free text
findings.detail: The evening confirmation cut-off is rendered as input[type=text] and saved as DB.commitPolicy[k]=i.value with no HH:MM parsing or validation - it is the only key in saveCommitPolicy exempted from parseFloat.
findings.impact: A malformed time string is accepted and propagated to every consumer of the confirmation deadline.

findings.title: rcCompCap() is a dead helper
findings.detail: rcCompCap(code) is declared at L14742 and never called; compCheck reads rc.comp directly at L15415.
findings.impact: None operationally; one more unused symbol in the taxonomy layer.

findings.title: The pane has no interface translation at all
findings.detail: No data-i18n attribute exists anywhere inside #stab-reasons (L1771-1822). All six card headings, all 22 column headers, the composer labels, the policy prose blocks, every SLA/comp/commit field label and hint, and every toast are English-only literals. The only Arabic the pane renders is the per-code labelAr content column and the bilingual option labels in reasonSelectHTML.
findings.impact: The most frequently opened settings tab is untranslatable while the nav button that reaches it is translated.

findings.title: The pane's 'last updated by' strip never fills
findings.detail: #meta-reasons sits at L1796 in the same visual position as its 11 siblings but is not in renderSettingsMeta's map. Contributing cause: this tab logs its saves under entityIds 'reason-codes', 'sla-policy', 'comp-policy' and 'commit-policy', none of which is a value in the map, so even adding the element id would need a matching entityId choice.
findings.impact: The widest settings pane gives no indication of who last changed it, while 11 narrower panes do.

findings.title: The reason code registry has no empty state
findings.detail: renderReasonCodesTable writes (DB.reasonCodes||[]).map(...).join('') straight into the tbody with no length check, so an empty registry renders as a bare header row with no message. The scroll box keeps its 520px max-height regardless.
findings.impact: Only reachable if the seed were emptied, but the pane would give no explanation.

findings.title: The referenced Call Center Communication Guide is not in the artifact
findings.detail: The panel description and 24 of the 40 codes cite guide section numbers (ref '1.1' through '7.3'). The guide itself is not present in this file, so the ref values cannot be checked against it.
findings.impact: The taxonomy's claim of completeness against an external guide is unverifiable from the source.

findings.title: The SLA tier form iterates a hardcoded key list
findings.detail: renderSlaPolicyForm builds its rows from ['T1','T2','T3','T4'].map(...) rather than Object.keys(DB.slaPolicy.tiers), so a fifth tier added to the data would exist, be assignable via the per-code tier select only if that list were also edited, and never appear in the tier editor.
findings.impact: The tier set is effectively fixed in two places at once.

findings.title: This pane's audit action keys have no friendly labels
findings.detail: edit_reason_codes, add_reason_code, edit_sla_policy, edit_comp_policy and edit_commit_policy are all absent from ACTION_LABELS (L2898-2910), so none of them appears with a human name in the Activity-log action filter.
findings.impact: Policy changes are hard to isolate in the activity log because the filter shows only the raw keys.

findings.title: Two stale reason-code counts in user-facing copy
findings.detail: The panel description says the registry is 'seeded from all 24 scenarios in the Call Center Communication Guide, plus 14 codes' and the reason picker's search placeholder says 'Search 38 reason codes'. DB.reasonCodes actually holds 40 entries, 24 with a guide ref and 16 without.
findings.evidence: seeded from all 24 scenarios in the Call Center Communication Guide, plus 14 codes for events this panel already generates
findings.impact: Cosmetic, but both numbers are quoted to operators as fact.

findings.title: 'and on generated documents' is aspirational copy
findings.detail: The pane description claims the mark appears on generated documents. Grep for DB.branding returns only the seed, applyBranding, renderBrandingSettings, saveBranding, resetBranding, maxUploadMB and handleLogoFile — no receipt, invoice or document generator reads it. The trip receipt modal builds its own markup without consulting DB.branding.
findings.evidence: The mark shown at the top of the sidebar and on generated documents.
findings.impact: The tab is described as controlling document branding that it does not control.

findings.title: Branding audit entries carry no before/after diff
findings.detail: saveBranding calls logAction with only four arguments, omitting the before and after objects that other settings handlers pass, so the audit-log diff renderer has nothing to show for the entry.
findings.impact: An audit reader can see that branding changed but not what it changed from or to.

findings.title: DB.branding.accent is never read
findings.detail: The accent colour is assigned at seed and again inside resetBranding, and is not exposed in the UI. Grep for 'accent' in the file returns only CSS accent-color declarations, an unrelated vehicle-model key, and these two assignments.
findings.impact: Dead configuration surface suggesting a theming capability that does not exist.

findings.title: Doc misattributes the reset gate spec and drifts on function lines
findings.detail: The doc places resetBranding's confirmation spec in GATE_SPECS at L20797–20799. In source, GATE_SPECS begins at L18245 and does not contain it; the spec is GATE_SWEEP.resetBranding at L20846–20847 (GATE_SWEEP begins at L20769). saveBranding also starts at L18445, not L18447, and guardAction('saveBranding') at L18459, not L18461.
findings.evidence:
resetBranding:{t:'Reset branding to default',d:true,
    c:['The uploaded logo is discarded and cannot be recovered from here.','Every operator sees the change.'],btn:'Reset'},
findings.impact: Documentation-only; the gate mechanism is correctly described, only its location and object name are wrong.

findings.title: edit_branding has no ACTION_LABELS entry
findings.detail: Both branding actions log the key 'edit_branding', which is not present in ACTION_LABELS. The Activity-log action-type filter is built from Object.keys(ACTION_LABELS), so branding changes cannot be filtered by action type.
findings.impact: Branding changes are invisible to the audit-log filter.

findings.title: No 'last updated' caption on this tab
findings.detail: renderSettingsMeta's element map contains keys for general, ops-radius, notifications, security, cities, limits, gateways, phases, plan-visibility, cancelpolicy and multi-sub — but no branding key. There is also no #meta-branding element in the pane markup to receive one.
findings.impact: The tab breaks the convention its siblings follow; there is no visible provenance for the current branding.

findings.title: 40-row cap with no show-all and no severity sorting
findings.detail: renderIntegrity renders s.rows.slice(0,40) and appends '…and N more.' with no control to expand. Rows come out in Object.keys order (all riders, then all drivers) with no sort, so a red 'no records' row can sit below 39 amber 'window gap' rows.
findings.impact: Actual alerts can be pushed off the visible list by expected, non-actionable rows; the only way to see them is the CSV export.

findings.title: Doc line numbers drift against source
findings.detail: Verified starts: reconcileEntity L18515 (doc 18517), integrityScan L18565 (doc 18566), rebuildAllHistory L18600 (doc 18605/18606), guardAction('rebuildAllHistory') L18607–18616 and exportIntegrity L18617 (the doc gives both an 18615 start), reconstructHistory L18668 (doc 18662), buildRiderHistory L18686 (doc 18689), buildFareBreakdown L18656 (doc 18654), saveDataWindow L20514 (doc 20516). Markup: #integrity-body is L1766 (doc 1767), #window-body L1759 (the doc header says 1762, its layout map says 1759), and the pane div closes at L1768 so the range is L1750–1768, not 1750–1769.
findings.impact: Documentation-only; the described behaviour is accurate, the citations need correcting.

findings.title: history_rebuilt and edit_data_window have no ACTION_LABELS entries
findings.detail: Neither key appears in ACTION_LABELS, and the Activity-log action-type filter is built from Object.keys(ACTION_LABELS), so neither the record-generating rebuild nor the window change is selectable in the filter.
findings.impact: The single most consequential action on the tab cannot be filtered for in the audit log.

findings.title: No 'last updated' caption on this tab
findings.detail: renderSettingsMeta's element map has no 'integrity' or 'window' key, and neither card contains a meta-* element, so the provenance caption used by the other settings tabs is absent here.
findings.impact: No visible record of who last changed the data window.

findings.title: provenanceChip call sites not enumerated
findings.detail: The doc marks this UNVERIFIED. provenanceChip(kind) is defined to label entity KPIs as 'billing aggregate' or 'panel records'; it does not appear inside renderIntegrity or renderWindowSettings, and its actual invocation sites on the entity profiles were not confirmed in this pass.
findings.evidence: provenanceChip(kind) returns '· billing aggregate' / '· panel records' with explanatory titles
findings.impact: If unused, the provenance labelling that the whole reconciliation design depends on is not actually shown to operators.

findings.title: The rebuild pathway is a demo generator
findings.detail: buildRiderHistory draws distances, durations, surge, cancellations, ratings, routes and payment methods from a seeded pseudo-RNG (fractional part of sin(seed)*10000), fabricates 5.00 SAR tolls at a fixed probability, and treats exactly 55% of the missing history as inside the window. Only the totals are made to match the stored lifetime figure, by scaling every component and forcing the last trip's fare.
findings.impact: Generated records are plausible-looking but fictitious at the line-item level; the gate text says so, and the records carry reconstructed:true, but they enter DB.trips and DB.payments alongside real ones.

findings.title: The window rationale is presented as policy but is not editable
findings.detail: DB.dataWindow.rationale is rendered in bold-prefixed prose under the months field as the governing rule, but no UI writes it and it is not versioned alongside the months value that saveDataWindow does audit.
findings.evidence: rationale:'12 months for year-on-year comparison + 1 month headroom. Must not be shorter than the payment provider’s dispute window.'
findings.impact: The stated justification can drift from the configured number with no record of either change.

findings.title: Audit entries carry empty before/after objects
findings.detail: Both logAction calls pass {} for before and after, so auditDiffHTML returns an empty string and no structured diff is stored or rendered.
findings.impact: The audit rows record a sentence but no machine-readable change record.

findings.title: Both audit keys are missing from ACTION_LABELS
findings.detail: legal_version_published and config_updated are absent from the ACTION_LABELS map that the Activity-log action filter is built from.
findings.impact: Neither legal action can be selected in the Activity-log action-type filter.

findings.title: Doc line numbers for the modal fields and the gate spec are off
findings.detail: The doc places #new-doc-version at L3828 and #new-doc-summary at L3829 (actual L3827 and L3828) and GATE_SPECS.sendReconsentReminder at L20807-20809 (actual L20857).
findings.impact: Line references in the doc's index need correcting before they are used for navigation.

findings.title: No document body and no per-user consent history
findings.detail: A version record holds only version, publishedDate and summary; there is no legal text, no link out and no diff. A consent record holds only version and acceptedAt, with no history of previously accepted versions.
findings.evidence: {version:'2.1',publishedDate:'01 Jul',summary:'Added subscription postponement policy and clarified cancellation fees.'}
findings.impact: The panel can state which version someone is on but cannot show what they agreed to or what they agreed to previously.

findings.title: Re-consent reminders have no de-duplication or cooldown
findings.detail: sendReconsentReminder recomputes the non-compliant pool and emails all of them every time it is pressed. Nothing records that a reminder was already sent, and there is no rate limit or suppression list — despite the confirmation gate warning that repeat reminders damage consent quality.
findings.impact: Repeated presses send repeated mail to the same customers, and there is also no guard against a 0-recipient send.

findings.title: Reminders log the generic config_updated action key
findings.detail: sendReconsentReminder emits logAction('config_updated','legal',docKey,...) rather than a legal-specific key, the same key used by gateway edits, broadcasts and push sends.
findings.evidence: logAction('config_updated','legal',docKey,'Re-consent reminder sent to '+nonCompliant.length+' non-compliant user(s) for '+doc.label,{},{})
findings.impact: Legal reminders cannot be separated from unrelated configuration changes when auditing.

findings.title: A broadcast re-renders the outbox once per recipient
findings.detail: sendSystemEmail calls renderEmailOutbox() after every single record it writes, and sendBroadcast calls it again at the end.
findings.impact: A broadcast to a large segment repaints the whole table once per recipient, freezing the pane while it fans out.

findings.title: Audience caption wording differs between HTML and JS
findings.detail: The static default of #bc-audience-count reads '0 rider(s) will receive this' while updateBroadcastAudienceCount writes '<n> recipient(s) will receive this'.
findings.impact: Cosmetic inconsistency visible until the first recompute, and misleading once driver segments are selected.

findings.title: Broadcasts log the generic config_updated key
findings.detail: sendBroadcast emits logAction('config_updated','settings','broadcast',...), the same key used by gateway edits, push sends and legal reminders, and that key is absent from ACTION_LABELS.
findings.impact: Customer-facing mass mailings cannot be isolated or filtered in the Activity log.

findings.title: Doc line numbers drift across the mail handlers
findings.detail: Verified positions: previewInboundMessage L7536 (doc 7538), replyToInbound L7549 (doc 7551), previewEmail L7578 (doc 7581), broadcastAudienceIds L7676 (doc 7674), updateBroadcastAudienceCount L7690 (doc 7686), GATE_SPECS.sendBroadcast L20850 (doc 20800). The pane also closes at L1904, not L1905.
findings.impact: The doc's line index needs correcting before it is used for navigation.

findings.title: renderSettingsMeta() call is a no-op for this tab
findings.detail: sendBroadcast calls renderSettingsMeta() but that function's map has no 'emails' or 'broadcast' key, so no 'Last updated by …' caption is ever produced.
findings.impact: The pane never shows who last acted on it, unlike the settings tabs that are in the map.

findings.title: Stale comment claims email broadcasts are riders-only
findings.detail: The push module comment justifies the two channels' different audience lists by stating 'email broadcast is riders-only today', but the email selector has carried a Drivers optgroup since L1885.
findings.evidence: target drivers (email broadcast is riders-only today).
findings.impact: The stated rationale for maintaining two audience implementations no longer holds.

findings.title: The Inbox is effectively a static three-row list
findings.detail: There is no search, sort, filter, pagination, delete or archive, and no UI or adapter that creates an inbound message. The contact-centre comment names onInboundMessage() as the intended entry point but nothing defines or calls it.
findings.impact: Real inbound mail cannot enter the panel; only the three seeded messages exist.

findings.title: Doc pane end and gate spec line are off
findings.detail: The #stab-push pane closes at L1973 (doc says L1974) and GATE_SPECS.sendPushNotification is at L20853 (doc says L20803-20805).
findings.impact: The doc's line index needs correcting before it is used for navigation.

findings.title: maxlength attributes are the only length enforcement
findings.detail: Neither the 40-character title cap nor the 120-character body cap is re-checked in sendPushNotification; both are browser-side attributes.
findings.impact: Any programmatic value assignment produces an over-length payload that is stored and displayed.

findings.title: Push sends log the generic config_updated key
findings.detail: logAction('config_updated','settings','push',...) shares its key with broadcasts, gateway edits and legal reminders, and that key is absent from ACTION_LABELS.
findings.impact: Push campaigns cannot be isolated or filtered in the Activity log.

findings.title: PUSH- ids are derived from array length
findings.detail: The id is 'PUSH-'+String(DB.pushOutbox.length+1).padStart(4,'0') rather than a monotonic counter.
findings.impact: Removing any record would make the next send reuse an existing id.

findings.title: renderSettingsMeta() call is a no-op for this tab
findings.detail: sendPushNotification calls renderSettingsMeta() but the map behind it has no 'push' key.
findings.impact: No 'Last updated by …' caption ever appears for the push tab.

findings.title: Search does not cover the message body
findings.detail: The filter tests p.title + ' ' + p.audience only, even though the body is the widest column rendered in the table.
findings.impact: Searching for wording that appears in a message returns nothing.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED audience-filter dependencies and vehicle-type domain
findings.detail: The doc could not confirm the thresholds inside driverOpenComplaints(id) and riderChurnRisk(r), nor whether every driver record uses exactly 'Economy'/'Comfort' casing or whether a Large/XL class exists that has no push segment.
findings.impact: Segment membership cannot be fully predicted from this documentation pass; a third vehicle class would be unreachable by push.

findings.title: Exporting the audit log mutates the audit log
findings.detail: exportAuditLog builds its rows first, then downloadCSV appends an export_data entry to DB.auditLog.
findings.impact: The exported file never contains the export that produced it, so consecutive exports are needed to reconcile the log.

findings.title: SNAP- ids are derived from array length
findings.detail: The id is 'SNAP-'+String(DB.dailySnapshots.length+1).padStart(4,'0'), which yields SNAP-0031 for the first capture against the 30 seeds.
findings.impact: Removing any snapshot would make the next capture reuse an existing id.

findings.title: Snapshot revenue figures are stored as strings
findings.detail: totalRevenue, quickRideRevenue and subRevenue are all written with .toFixed(2), producing strings on a record whose other fields are numbers.
findings.impact: Every downstream consumer, including the executive trend chart, must re-parse before arithmetic.

findings.title: Snapshots are memory-only with no schedule or retention policy
findings.detail: DB.dailySnapshots lives in memory; a reload discards captures and restores the 30 seeds. There is no timer, no boot-time capture, no retention rule and no size guard on any export.
findings.impact: The 'history you can trend' the card promises does not survive a page reload.

findings.title: The doc's exporter line numbers are systematically wrong
findings.detail: Verified positions: toCSV L7592, downloadCSV L7598, exportRiders L7607, exportDrivers L7611, exportSubscriptions L7615, exportPayments L7619, exportAuditLog L7623, exportInbox L7627, exportPushLog L7631, exportEmailLog L7634, captureDailySnapshot L7639. The doc lists 7595/7632/7600/7604/7608/7612/7628/7640/7648/7644/7645. The pane also closes at L2044, not L2047, and the footnote is at L2036.
findings.impact: The doc's line index cannot be used for navigation in this section without correction.

findings.title: The subscriptions CSV exports raw ids where the sibling path exports names
findings.detail: exportSubscriptions writes s.rider and s.driver directly, while exportRows('subscriptions') resolves both through nm2().
findings.impact: The same dataset exported from two places is not comparable without a manual id lookup.

findings.title: The unreachable export path hardcodes the frozen demo date into filenames
findings.detail: doExport composes its filename as 'eyvar_'+d.name+'_25Jun.'+fmt.
findings.impact: Any file produced by that path is stamped 25Jun regardless of when it was exported.

findings.title: Three of ten captured snapshot fields are never shown
findings.detail: The table renders 7 columns and the CSV exports 8; id, quickRideRevenue and subRevenue are computed on every capture and appear nowhere in this tab.
findings.impact: The revenue split between quick rides and subscriptions is captured on every snapshot and is invisible to the operator.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED payment type domain for the revenue split
findings.detail: captureDailySnapshot splits revenue on the exact strings 'Quick ride fare' and 'Subscription charge'. Whether DB.payments carries other type values was not confirmed in this pass.
findings.impact: Revenue of any other payment type is counted in totalRevenue but in neither split, and the discrepancy is invisible.

findings.title: All four pricing audit keys are unlabelled
findings.detail: rate_card_proposed, rate_card_approved, rate_card_self_approval_blocked and surge_suspended are absent from ACTION_LABELS, and all four use entityType 'pricing', a type used nowhere else in the file.
findings.impact: Price changes and surge interventions cannot be selected in the Activity-log action filter and their entity links do not resolve.

findings.title: Expired surge suspensions are never purged and none can be lifted
findings.detail: Suspension records carry no id and there is no cancel action — the module comment states expiry is deliberate — but nothing ever removes an expired record either; only the render filters on expiresAtMs > nowMs().
findings.impact: The array grows without bound for the session, and a mistaken suspension cannot be undone before it expires.

findings.title: proposeRateCard merges changes shallowly
findings.detail: The merge is a top-level assignment loop, so passing a partial object for a nested key such as classes would replace the whole object rather than merge into it.
findings.impact: Only the current single caller (which passes a full deep copy) is safe; any future partial change would wipe sibling keys.

findings.title: Several rate-card fields are declared and never read
findings.detail: currency, vatIncluded, surge.minMultiplier and capByCity.JED have no readers at all; commission.onDemand and every cancelFee/freeWaitMin/waitPerMin value are used only to build display strings; surge.appliesToPlanLegs is read only to colour a label while the exclusion itself is hardcoded in fareFor.
findings.impact: The pane presents configuration that looks operative but changes nothing, including the cancellation fee, whose real policy lives in DB.cancellationPolicy.

findings.title: The data-window control has no upper bound and reconciles twice per render
findings.detail: win-months carries min=1 but no max, and saveDataWindow accepts parseInt(...)||13, so 9999 months is stored. renderWindowSettings calls reconcileEntity() once per rider for the expectedGap count and again for the orphan count.
findings.impact: An absurd window is accepted silently, and every settings-page open runs a full double reconciliation pass over all riders.

findings.title: The proposal note is stored and never displayed
findings.detail: commitRateCardChange passes val('rc-note') to proposeRateCard, which sets draft.note. Nothing in renderPricing or either guard builder reads it.
findings.impact: The recorded justification for every price change is unreachable from the UI, including by the second person who must approve it.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED whether the pricing tab is a specification or a control
findings.detail: The ledger module explicitly states it is a model for the backend; the pricing module makes no such disclaimer, and its copy ('live', 'Every new trip prices under this card') reads as operative. There is no network layer in the file, so the behaviour is display-only as written.
findings.impact: The intent behind the whole tab is undocumented, so it is unclear whether the missing wiring is a defect or the design.

findings.title: Computed idempotency statistics and timestamps are discarded
findings.detail: idemStats returns operations, duplicated and suppressed but only suppressed is rendered; withIdempotency writes seen.lastAttemptMs on every retry and nothing ever reads it.
findings.impact: The pane cannot show how many distinct operations are registered or how many keys were retried, only a total attempt count.

findings.title: Journal entry ids are derived from array length
findings.detail: The id is 'JE-'+String(DB.ledger.length+1).padStart(5,'0') and entries are unshifted, so ids stay unique only because nothing ever removes an entry.
findings.impact: Any future deletion or trimming of the journal would silently reuse ids, in a collection where identity is the audit trail.

findings.title: The goodwill regex branch is redundant
findings.detail: The expense account is chosen as goodwill when /goodwill|apolog/i matches, compensation when /compensat/i matches, and goodwill otherwise — so the first branch and the fallback produce the same account.
findings.impact: Only a reason containing 'compensat' ever books to expense.compensation; the apparent three-way rule is a two-way one.

findings.title: The two money audit keys are unlabelled and unlinkable
findings.detail: duplicate_suppressed and ledger_rejected are absent from ACTION_LABELS, and both set entityId to the raw idempotency key or ref — a long pipe-joined string that resolveId cannot resolve, so auditEntityLink renders it as monospace text rather than a link.
findings.impact: Money-safety events cannot be filtered by action type and cannot be clicked through to the entity they concern.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED interaction between the money wrappers and guardAction
findings.detail: The four money functions are replaced by plain top-level assignment at script-eval time, while guardAction also reassigns window[name]; whichever runs last becomes the outer wrapper. commitWalletAdjust is guarded but recordRefund and creditRiderWallet are not, so no conflicting pair exists in this build.
findings.impact: The two wrapping mechanisms are uncoordinated; adding a gate to a patched money function later could silently reorder idempotency and confirmation.

findings.title: UNVERIFIED whether any seeded fare triggers the rounding rejection
findings.detail: postFareCapture computes net = r2(gross/(1+rate)) and vat = r2(gross-net) independently; for some gross values the two need not re-add to gross, in which case postLedger refuses the entry. Confirming whether any seeded or reconstructed fare hits this requires executing the file.
findings.impact: If it occurs, the affected trips are missing from the books with no visible signal beyond a red row in Refused postings.

findings.title: Coverage and gap detection disagree on a dangling user id
findings.detail: onCallNow returns covered:!!u, where u is the resolved DB.teamUsers record, while rotaGaps only tests !assign[slotKey]. A slot assigned to a user id that no longer exists is therefore covered:false in the head strip but not a gap in the uncovered-slots list, and its grid cell is not painted red.
findings.impact: The two coverage surfaces contradict each other for exactly the case that matters - a departed operator still on the rota.

findings.title: Every slot change rebuilds all 42 selects
findings.detail: setRotaSlot ends with renderRota(), which rewrites the whole pane in one innerHTML assignment - head strip, 42 custom selects, gap list and handover list. The dropdown the operator just used is destroyed under the click.
findings.impact: Filling a rota one slot at a time repeatedly discards and rebuilds the widget being used.

findings.title: Handover asks for confirmation twice
findings.detail: guardAction('commitHandover', ...) wraps the commit function rather than the modal opener, so the operator opens the handover modal, fills it in, presses 'Complete handover', and is then shown a second confirm dialog stacked on top of the first.
findings.impact: A two-step confirmation for an action whose modal already is the confirmation step.

findings.title: Handover rows show no timestamp
findings.detail: The handover record stores tsMs, fromId, toId and items[].type, but the rendered row shows only fromName, toName, day, block, item count, the transferred flag and the notes. The recent-handovers list therefore cannot be read chronologically beyond its newest-first ordering, and there is no click-through to the handed-over items.
findings.impact: A handover cannot be tied to a clock time when reconstructing an incident.

findings.title: The declared timezone is decorative
findings.detail: DB.onCallSchedule.timezone is 'Asia/Riyadh' and is printed in the pane's prose, but no conversion is performed anywhere; currentBlock uses the viewer's local getHours(). An operator in another timezone sees a different 'now' shift than the label promises.
findings.impact: Shift boundaries shown to a remote or travelling operator do not match the rota they are reading.

findings.title: The rota is deliberately seeded with 13 holes
findings.detail: rotaBoot skips night slots on even day indexes (sun, tue, thu, sat = 8 slots) and weekend escalation slots (fri, sat x 3 blocks = 6 slots), overlapping on sat night escalation, leaving 13 of 42 slots empty - 29/42 = 69% coverage, all 13 gaps high severity. The source comment states the intent: a fully covered grid would hide the feature that matters. The count is derived arithmetically from the rules and DB.teamUsers.length===5, not from execution.
findings.impact: Demo artefact; the headline coverage number is fabricated by design.

findings.title: The rota tab has no Arabic and no translatable strings
findings.detail: The tab button carries data-i18n='stab.rota' but no matching key exists in the Arabic dictionary, and there are zero data-i18n attributes inside #stab-rota. Day labels, shift labels, tier labels, gap warnings, the handover modal and every toast are English-only literals. The pane title 'On-call rota & shift handover' also differs from the nav-button label 'On-call & handover'.
findings.impact: An Arabic operator sees an untranslated tab label and a fully English pane.

findings.title: Unused local in openHandover
findings.detail: openHandover computes var me=meUser() on its first line and never references me anywhere in the function body; the modal is built entirely from held, next and DB.teamUsers.
findings.impact: None operationally.

findings.title: Last-updated strips silently reset once entries age out
findings.detail: settingsLastUpdated finds the newest DB.auditLog entry with entityType==='settings' and a matching entityId. logAction truncates the log to 500 entries, so once a section's entry falls past the cap its strip reverts to 'No changes recorded yet' even though the change happened.
findings.impact: A settings section can appear never to have been changed after enough unrelated activity.

findings.title: Nav height is not recomputed on tab switch
findings.detail: fitSettingsNavHeight is called only from the router branch and from a guarded window resize listener. switchSettingsTab does not call it, so a tab change that alters the page header or content height leaves nav.style.maxHeight at its previously computed value.
findings.impact: The nav rail can be left slightly too tall or too short until the next resize or navigation.

findings.title: scrollIntoView can move the page, not just the nav
findings.detail: activeBtn.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) scrolls the nearest scrollable ancestor chain, which includes #p-settings itself (overflow-y:auto) and not only the .settings-nav-col. Switching tabs can therefore nudge the page's own scroll position.
findings.impact: Minor visual jump when switching tabs on a scrolled page.

findings.title: The Activity pane is untranslated and its label collides with the page's
findings.detail: There are zero data-i18n attributes inside #stab-activity: the title 'Recent activity', the description and the button label 'View full activity log' are English-only, as is every string emitted by auditRowsHTML, auditEmptyHTML and showActorHistory. stab.activity also maps to the same Arabic string as nav.audit-log, so the tab and the standalone page are indistinguishable in Arabic.
findings.evidence:
Recent activity
Every configuration change made in Settings, newest first.
findings.impact: An Arabic operator cannot tell the in-settings preview from the full Activity Log page by name.

findings.title: The actor-history modal is unpaginated
findings.detail: showActorHistory filters DB.auditLog by actorId and renders every match through auditRowsHTML with no slice and no pager, so a busy actor can render up to the global 500-entry cap in a single modal body. Clicking the Who column inside the modal re-renders the same modal in place.
findings.impact: A large, slow modal with no way to narrow the result.

findings.title: The doc calls six live i18n group keys dead
findings.detail: 16j lists stabgrp.daily_ops, .money, .people, .comms, .platform, .records and .other as seven dead Arabic keys with no matching markup. In fact reorderSettingsTabs builds a fresh .settings-tab-group-lbl for each of the six SETTINGS_GROUPS at boot and sets data-i18n to g.i18nKey, so six of the seven are live at runtime; only stabgrp.other is unreachable, because every one of the 21 tab keys appears in SETTINGS_GROUPS so the leftovers branch never fires. The related claim that the markup has 3 groups is true only before presenceBoot runs.
findings.impact: Documentation-only: acting on the doc would delete six translations that are actually used.

findings.title: The doc's settings nav table is off by one
findings.detail: 16j section 8.2 places the Workspace group label at L1421 and General at L1422, and the Operations label at L1425. In the source the Workspace label is at L1420, General at L1421, the Operations label at L1424, dispatch at L1425, and reasons at L1430 rather than the 1431 the doc gives. The System label at L1436 and the Activity/Export buttons at L1442/L1443 are correct, so the table drifts and then re-syncs. 15-settings-shell has the correct numbers.
findings.impact: Documentation-only line drift within a single table.

findings.title: The empty-state copy is wrong on two counts
findings.detail: auditEmptyHTML('this session') renders 'No actions logged yet this session', but DB.auditLog ships with 8 pre-seeded entries dated 20-25 Jun which are not from this session; the state is also unreachable in practice for that reason. The sentence then enumerates three action kinds ('assignment, approval, or permission change') out of the many the panel logs.
findings.impact: Demo-data artefact in user-facing copy.

findings.title: The preview drops both the action key and the entity link
findings.detail: auditRowsHTML is called with compact=true, which renders only Time, Who and Action(summary) and suppresses the fourth column, auditEntityLink(e). The machine action key is not shown in either mode here, so an entry whose summary is terse cannot be traced to its record from this pane.
findings.impact: The preview can show that something happened without offering any route to what it happened to.

findings.title: Every logAction forces a full re-render of the audit view
findings.detail: L3149 ends logAction with if(typeof renderAuditLog==='function')renderAuditLog(). renderAuditLog rebuilds the filtered list, the whole table, the pager and the Settings preview branch regardless of whether either surface is currently on screen.
findings.impact: A bulk operation that writes many audit entries pays a full table rebuild per entry, and at the 500-entry cap with 200 per page that is a large DOM write per logged action.

findings.title: Free-text search covers neither action nor entityType
findings.detail: The filter predicate builds its haystack as (e.summary + ' ' + e.actorName + ' ' + (e.entityId||'') + ' ' + e.id).toLowerCase() at L9331. entityType and action are excluded, and entityType is not displayed or filterable either — its only consumer anywhere is settingsLastUpdated at L7336.
findings.impact: Typing an action key such as config_updated into the search box returns nothing unless the key also happens to appear in a summary sentence.

findings.title: Several doc line references are off by two to four lines
findings.detail: Verified against the source by reading L3133-L3151 and grepping for exportAuditLog. The 500-entry cap is at L3148 (doc §12 and §14 item 4 say 3146); the AUD- id assignment is at L3136 (doc §12 says 3137, which is actually ts); the forced re-render is at L3149 (doc §14 item 17 says 3147); and the exportAuditLog button in the Data Export tab is at L2031 (doc §5 and §15 say 2027, which is the Riders export button). The function-range header 'L3133-3151' is correct.
findings.impact: Cosmetic; corrected line numbers recorded here.

findings.title: The empty-state copy is misleading
findings.detail: auditEmptyHTML (L9306-L9308) reads 'No actions logged yet {ctx}. Every assignment, approval, or permission change you make will appear here.' With ctx = 'this session' it appears over a pre-seeded 8-entry array, and it enumerates 3 action kinds when 161 exist.
findings.evidence: 'No actions logged yet '+ctx+'. Every assignment, approval, or permission change you make will appear here.'
findings.impact: Cosmetic, but it sets an incorrect expectation about what the log records.

findings.title: The filter dropdowns are built once and never rebuilt
findings.detail: renderAuditFilterSelect (L9230-L9246) guards each build with a check that the csel-* id is absent, e.g. if(w && !document.getElementById('csel-audit-filter')). The actor list is snapshotted from DB.teamUsers on first render and never refreshed. (With 6 options the custom select's search box does not appear either, since customSelectHTML requires options.length > 6.)
findings.impact: A team member invited at runtime never appears in the actor filter, so their actions cannot be isolated — the same session in which the invite was audited.

findings.title: The pager has no windowing and the actor-history modal has no pagination
findings.detail: auditPagerHTML emits one button per page with no ellipsis or window (L9313-L9317) — at the 500-entry cap with 20 per page that is 25 buttons, growing linearly with the log. showActorHistory (L9271-L9280) renders auditRowsHTML(list, true) over the unfiltered, unsliced actor list and ignores AUDIT_SEARCH, AUDIT_FILTER_ACTION and pagination entirely.
findings.impact: The pager grows unbounded and a busy actor's history opens as up to 500 rows in a single modal with no filter.
